  made keep theirs.

2.43 **One click on a temperature opens its SetPoint** (Fritz, 2026-11-08: "Click on a Thermowell or Probe or Display of a
Temperature NOT in edit Mode, Bring up SetPoint Dialog"). Outside Edit layout, one click or tap on a **Temperature Probe** (its
reading or its Skynet Dial), a **Thermowell**, a **probe tee**, a **Probe or Thermowell built into a Vessel Device**, a Vessel's own
Probe spot, or a **Picture Widget** that shows a probe, opens the **SetPoint pop-up** of the Heating Element that holds that
temperature: the one whose Temperature Probe it is (older Hysteresis, PID and Deadband Devices too; a Vessel's own Probe goes to the
Vessel's Heater first). Two or more: a short list asks which. None: a short note says so (a simulated probe still opens its
Simulated reading pop-up). The pop-up shows the reading, whose Setpoint it is (ON or OFF, method), the Setpoint with − and +, then
**Set + ON**, **OFF**, **Set**, **Heating method…** (the Rule 6.19 pop-up) and **Cancel**. It still asks before it turns on
(Rule 2.33). Only Hysteresis, PID, Deadband and Precise hold a Setpoint: on On/Off or Duty Cycle, Set switches it to the first
allowed method that does. A Tap set by hand (When tapped) still wins. Operators and admins only. Double-click still opens Properties
(Rule 2.9).
- **BruControl Import:** checked, not changed. Its probes and Heating Elements are the Panel's own, so they get this click in the
  Panel; the Import keeps the probe it reads as each Heating Element's Temperature Probe. (thread "Open SetPoint dialog from
  temperature widgets", Help 160)
- **PV and SV on every probe's display** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, Panel Updates 41: "on 3 we will also need a SetPoint Field
  associated with the Temperture Probe visible to a users"; "the standard PV and SV can be intergrated into The Display"; "Forget visible
  option Make part of Digit Display Box. Keep all Digits an Dergee F or C fit on one line Inside the display."). On a running Tab every
  Temperature Probe's display shows **PV** (its reading) over a **green SV box** (its Setpoint), like a panel controller. **PV's color**
  (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "If the process is heating and the Temperature is Below the Setpoint , Blue, at Setpoint Between a Hys Green
  and PID (with smoothing Green) and if above Red. Opposite for Cooling. Dead Band Green in the Band and Blue if Heating and Red If Cooling.
  Duty Cycle Heating Red if On, Grey If Off, Cooling Blue if On, Grey if Off"; it replaced "Red when Heating Blue when cooling" the same
  day) comes from what uses the probe: Hysteresis Green within its Offset of the Setpoint, PID and Precise within half a degree C (one
  degree F), Deadband inside its Deadband, a Fermentor between its Heat and Cool Offsets; outside, Blue below and Red above. Duty Cycle,
  Direct and PWM: Red while a heater is ON, Blue while a cooler is ON, Grey while OFF. A probe nothing uses keeps its own Display color.
  A cooler is colored the same way (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, asked whether "Opposite for Cooling" swaps Red and Blue: "Go with A
  KISS"): Blue is always below the Setpoint, Red always above. Each line keeps
  its digits and °F or °C on one line inside the display (both made smaller together to fit). **No Visible switch.** One click on the SV
  box types a new Setpoint in place (no pop-up, Rule 2.44; Enter sets, Esc puts it back); a click on the rest of the probe still opens
  the SetPoint pop-up above. **One Setpoint, never two:** a probe a Heating Element, a Fermentor Control or an older Hysteresis, PID or
  Deadband Device holds shows and sets **that one's Setpoint** (two or more: the one that is ON, else the first); `Probe.setpoint` in a
  Process reads and sets it there too. A probe nothing holds keeps **its own Setpoint**: **Setpoint** in its Properties to start (empty
  shows ---), `.setpoint` in a Process, for Processes and Alarms. Like a Heating Element's, a Setpoint set on a Tab lasts until the
  Brain restarts. Not shown in Edit layout, on the Dial or Bar look, or when the value is hidden. Operators and admins only. **Both
  programs:** the BruControl Import has no running Tabs and BruControl probes have no Setpoint; its probes are the Panel's own, so they
  get PV and SV in the Panel. Help 160.

2.45 **Time and DateTime formats: pick how a time shows** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: BruControl's time Globals become Time or
DateTime Widgets, with more than one format, and the Importer carries the format over). A **Time Widget** and a **DateTime
Widget** (and a Code Value Widget holding a Time or DateTime) have **Shows as** in their Properties; a **Timer** has the same Time
formats in its **Digits** box (Rule 2.40). Time: hh:mm:ss (the standard look), hh:mm, h:mm:ss, mm:ss (all minutes, 90:00), Minutes
only, Seconds only, Days too. DateTime: mm/dd/yyyy hh:mm:ss (the standard look), with AM / PM, Date only, Nov 9, 2026, Monday,
November 9, 2026, Clock (2:30 PM), 24-hour clock, Day and clock, 2026-11-09 14:30:00. The letters are the same ones BruControl
and Windows use (yyyy MMM dd ddd HH hh mm ss tt; for a Time the biggest unit holds the whole time), so a Process can set **any**
format with **`.showas`** (`wgt_TM_Boil_BR.showas = "mm:ss"`, `tm_Boil.showas = "mm' min'"`); `""` puts back the Properties'
pick. Only how it shows changes: the value a Process reads is the same. Both programs: the BruControl Import keeps a Timer's
Format, and a Time or DateTime Global's Format rides along in its Globals list for when Globals are imported (each becomes a
Time or DateTime Widget with that format). Help 176.

2.54 **"✔ Saved" for 2 seconds** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "When something is saved but just stays on same screen Pop Up a
Quick "Saved" Dialog up for 2 seconds and then goes out on its own. Pump Profile was where I was testing"). Every **Save** that keeps
you on the same screen (a ☰ Menu tab such as a Pump, Valve, Mash, Boil, Water or Tab Background Profile, Default settings, the
Equipment Profile, the Recipe, Settings > Panel settings, Contact, Sending, Pop-ups, MQTT and voice, Simulator, Password rules, the
Probe index, the Brew Process, a Template, Schema.json, a Process saved in the editor with no problems) shows a **✔ Saved** box in the
middle of the screen, with what was saved under it, for **2 seconds**; it then goes away on its own. It is a notice, not a question
(Rule 2.44): nothing to click, and it never stops you working. It is the same notice box every short note uses (OakBarn Brewery,
2026-11-16: "There already is a small save that pops up at the Bottom ... Change its background and Middle of Screen for these types of
Info or Warnings and Larger. It was small and I did not even see it"): every short info, warning or "✔ Saved" shows big, in the middle
of the screen, on a strong background (green for ✔ Saved, blue for info, red for a warning or problem). A Save with a problem shows
the problem instead. The BruControl Import program's own notice keeps its look (Importer Sandbox, Rule 11.3). Help 33. **Both programs:** the BruControl Import's
Build page shares the Panel code. (A Rule 14.4 exception, OakBarn Brewery picked "Build it now".)
**Save, Undo and Close** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "Has a close button just move that next to the other buttons", "and Cancel
as Undo?", "Good"): on a ☰ Menu tab whose Save keeps you there, the three sit together at the top: **Save** saves, shows ✔ Saved
and stays open; **Undo** goes back to the last Save and stays open (it replaces Cancel, and asks first when there are changes);
**Close** closes, and asks first when anything is not saved. **All the buttons sit together, frozen in the upper right corner,
always in the same order: Delete · Save · Undo · Close · ✕**, so each one is in the same exact place on every screen (OakBarn
Brewery, 2026-11-16: "I like to have some buttons on any Dialog in same exact place on different Dialogs. A better Option would be to
move all the Buttons to the Upper Right and Freeze", "Do it now", "Delete Button also"; a Rule 14.4 exception). Close and the boxed ✕
are the Menu tab's own, at the far right corner where they always were. A screen without one of the buttons leaves it out; the
others keep their order. Done so far: Default settings, Equipment Profile (its buttons are now only at the top, frozen), Recipe, and the Pump,
Valve, Tab Background, Mash, Boil and Water Profile tabs.
*Changed 2026-11-18* (OakBarn Brewery, Dialog Sandbox item 1: "Follow rule 2.54 which Blickmann Model should do regardless so it would
be the same"): **every dialog** follows this order, the Blichmann Model (the Pump) too: every Properties and Add box, every ⬢ and ⬆
pop-up and every other dialog. The buttons sit together at the right end of the frozen top row: **Delete · Save · Undo · Close · ✕**.
In a dialog **Cancel is called Close** (it closes without saving and asks first when something was changed) and the boxed **✕** does
the same. Save is called **💾 Keep** in a pop-up opened from a dialog and **➕ Add Device** (or Add Widget) in an Add box. A dialog whose
Save closes it has no Undo (there is no earlier Save to go back to: Close lets the changes go). A dialog that had its buttons only at
the bottom gets them in a frozen row at the top. The buttons that are not one of these (COPY, Tick all, Convert ...) stay where they
were. Help 115, 128, 148. Both programs: the BruControl Import's Build page shares the Panel's dialogs.
2.55 **The purple + Add New button is for Profiles only** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "Need Add New Button to the Right Of the
Open DDLB on the pump profile with the Purple + Not Frozen but does same as Add New in the DDLB which can stay", "And a Rule: Any
Profile Like The Pump One gets the Add New Button For now that is only Profiles", "No may not use anywhere else is the rule now and
no need to fix now, sandbox"). A Profile screen (a ☰ Menu tab with an **Open** list, like the Pump Profile) gets a **+ Add New**
button, with a purple +, just right of its Open list. It does the same as **Add new ...** in the Open list, which stays. It is not
part of the frozen button group (Rule 2.54). **It may not be used anywhere else.** Built: the Pump Profile only (adding it to the other
Profiles was dropped, OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16). Help 36. **Both programs:** the BruControl Import's Build page shares the
Panel code.
2.56 **A reading stays on one line** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16, on the Boil kettle's "127.3 °F" with the °F dropped below the
number: "Yes That was coming soon regardless", "4 digits"). A number with its unit (a temperature, a value, a gravity, a flow, a PID
or Heating Element's "45 % ▸ 152" ...) is never split over two lines, up to 4 digits before the point (9999.9 °F). When it is
wider than its box, Skynet makes the value's font smaller until it fits; when the reading is short again, it goes back to its own
size. The box is never made bigger by itself (Design Rule #1: nothing the user set is taken away). Texts that
are meant to wrap are left alone: Text and Label Widgets, long strings, a String gGlobal (it is text, 2026-11-20), Alarm text and picture text. The Skynet Dial and Timer
Digits draw their own digits to fit (Rule 2.40). Help 138. **Both programs:** the BruControl Import's Build page shares the Panel code.

2.57 **Port means a board Port; a pipe end has an End Fitting** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "Ports could be confused with Arduino
Ports so use Inlet Fitting"; "Use Ports only for Arduino Type Ports in the Help   For IPs End Fitting or something akin."; "There
should be Inlet and Outlet fittings as they can be different on a Pump. Immersion Chiller, so every IP gets it own type End fitting.
Information only generally except for QDs."; "Yes Skynet can connect a TC to NPT and VICE versus  but the graphic is so small
noting need to be done except maybe a comment in the Property dialog of the IP that adapter is in the connection.   But Only for
imformation").
- In the dialogs, Hover Help and Help, **Port** is only a pin on an Interface (an Arduino, a Raspberry Pi ...). The connector where a
  pipe or hose joins a pump, a chiller or a valve is its **End Fitting** (TC1.5, FPT1/2, FMSSQD1/2 ...).
- Every IP has its own End Fitting (its IP Type, Rule 5.40). A pump has two: **Inlet IP Fitting** and **Outlet IP Fitting** (they can be
  different), one row each in every Pump dialog and in the Pump Profile.
- The End Fitting is **information only**, except a **Quick Disconnect**, where a hose end can be unhooked and moved (Rule 5.40).
  Two End Fittings that don't fit (a TC to an NPT) can still be joined: nothing is blocked and no adapter is drawn (it would be too
  small, and there is no warning ring); the IP's Properties say **Adapter: TC1.5 to FPT1/2** as a note.
- *Not yet (next step):* the vessel ports, the plain IPs and the chillers get the same End Fitting rows and wording; until then the
  vessel dialogs and their Help still say Ports, and the Panel's network and mail server port settings keep the word (they are not
  pipes). **Both programs:** the BruControl Import's Build page shares the Panel's dialogs; BruControl has no fittings to import.

2.58 **The New Schema Interview** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "Adding a New Schema Lands back on the Schema Page. Should land on
a short interview Page about the New Schema"; "Similar to the Skynet Schema Import"; changed 2026-11-19, PDF "Panel Update 5" #2 and
#3: "No way to create New"; the Tabs outline; "4. Equipment is taken care of in 3 above"). As soon as Add new Schema has made and
loaded the new Schema, a short interview opens: its steps across the top like the Skynet BruControl Importer, one page at a time,
◀ Back and Next ▶, with Close and ✕ frozen in the upper right (Rule 2.54). The pages:
1. **About**: the Name, and a one-line **What is it for?** that shows in the Schema list.
2. **Boards**: tick the real boards from the other Schemas that this one uses too, and **➕ Add a New board after Finish** (the Add
   Interface pop-up opens after Finish, then the Interfaces page, Rule 2.60).
3. **Tabs**: a box for each Tab, and **➕ Add New Tab** for more. Each Tab has:
   - its **Name** and **What is it for?**: **Brewing (Brew House)**, **Fermentation**, **Cleaning** or **Other** (the user names it).
   - for Brewing, a **Level** dropdown from **Stove Top (Extract)** to **All Grain with Mash Tun (3 Vessels)**. It starts on the
     **Skynet Brewer Level**: the Level picked last time (kept in the brewing defaults; All Grain with Mash Tun the first time).
   - an **Equipment Profile** dropdown: None, **➕ Create New** (the Equipment Profile Interview opens after Finish) or a profile
     the user has, filtered by what the Tab is for (a Fermentation Tab shows the fermenter profiles). Any number of Tabs may start
     from the same profile (changed 2026-11-19, Rule 2.62; was "One profile is on one Tab only").
   - **Import**: **Import All** (the whole Default Layout), **Import Vessels** (its vessels and equipment with their fittings) or
     **Import Manifold** (the valves, fittings and pipes between the vessels). Each one is a copy: the Tab keeps no link to the
     profile (Rule 2.62; was "Import All: the Tab follows the profile").
   - **Import Processes**: tick marks for the Skynet Processes of that kind and Level (a Stove Top has no Mash). A ticked one is set
     in Brew Process; an unticked one is left out (SKIP).
4. **Done**: a summary. (The old Equipment page is gone: the Tabs page takes care of it.)
A Skynet Schema Template or an Equipment Profile already asked about the boards, Tabs and equipment, so they get About and Done
only. **Nothing is changed until ✔ Finish.** Finish, and Close, land on the new Schema's first Tab, never back on the Schema page.
Units are not asked: they are a Panel setting, the same for every Schema. **Both programs:** the BruControl Import makes no Schemas
with Add new Schema, so nothing changes there. (thread "Open a short interview after adding a Schema", Help 202)

2.59 **Data is always metric; Units are for showing only** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17, Panel Updates Sandbox entry 9: "Remember
that switching units only affects display, not the data which is always metric"; "make sure everything like the defaults are set to
metric when stored. If we have any open defaults that are stored US Standard Now, convert them all"; "3 Vessel Schema ALL Metric
Data. we can work on the Display after"). Skynet keeps every number in metric: **°C, liters, kilograms (grams for hops), cm**.
Settings > Panel settings > **Units** (US or Metric) only changes what a box or a reading **shows** and what you **type**; switching it
never changes a saved number, so switching back and forth can never drift a number. What you type in US units is saved in metric.
- **Kept in metric now:** Mash, Boil and Water Profiles (Skynet's own too), Equipment Profiles and the Vessels in their drawings,
  Vessels on a Tab, Vessel Templates (the shipped ones too), and the Default settings (Batch Size, Hop Stands, Boil Start and
  Ferment temperatures). Recipes already were (Rule 17.16). A BeerXML map with `"units": "Metric"` imports liters and grams.
- **Older saves:** a Profile, Equipment Profile, Vessel Template, Vessel or Default kept in US units (each says so with its own
  US tag) is turned into metric **once** on the first start after the update; the old file is kept beside it (`.before_metric`).
  Skynet does this in the Background and needs no user input.
- **The 3 Vessel Sample** (and the Brain's starting Schema) is all metric: probes in °C, the HLT and Kettle elements' Setpoint and
  Offset (150 °F and -1 °F kept as 65.5556 °C and -0.5556 °C, so the Help examples stay true in US), the Recipe Globals (°C,
  liters, hop grams), the Vessels, the Simulator and the Brew Day Process. Names never change (Rule 3.2), so a Global named
  _Gal or _Oz now holds liters or grams.
- **The Rule (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "Keep backend data metric, display to user by choice in Skynet Settings"; "US would not
  understand C and Europeans not F"):** everything kept behind the scenes is metric; **everything a user sees and types follows
  Units**, on every page. **Tab temperatures (built 2026-11-19):** a Temperature Probe's reading (PV), its SV box, its Dial (with
  its Lowest, Highest, Cooler and Hotter ranges), the SetPoint pop-up, the Heating Element pop-up, the hydrometer's temperature,
  the "▸ Setpoint" of an older Hysteresis, PID, Deadband or a Fermentor Control, and in Properties the Setpoint and Offsets of a
  Heating Element, older Hysteresis, PID, Deadband, Fermentor Control, Cool / Warm Pump and gas burner (its Rise, Drop and Boil
  point), and a probe's own Setpoint. A turned temperature shows 1 decimal (the probe's Decimals for a reading); a number not
  changed is saved back exactly as kept. A **temperature difference** (an Offset, a band, a Rise or Drop, a Dial range) turns by
  9/5 only, never with the 32. The Hysteresis Offset list is every half degree in the Units.
- **A probe's own Units box ("Kept in"):** never dropped. It is the units that probe keeps its numbers in (its reading, Setpoint,
  Offsets and what a Process writes to it); it no longer changes what is shown. A probe kept in °F (older Schemas) keeps working
  and only shows in the Units. What is typed is saved in the probe's own units.
- **Temperatures in a Process (OakBarn Brewery's choice, 2026-11-19: "we need the use to be able to type 152. This can be
  triggered by the settings in Skynet Defaults US?Metric as how it inturpeded by the backend"):** a plain number set on, or
  compared with, a temperature is typed in Units (`HLT.setpoint = 152` is 152 °F in US). When the Process is saved it is kept in
  °C with its sign (`66.6667°C`), so a saved Process never changes meaning when Units is switched; when it is opened it is shown
  in Units again (`152`). An Offset (.onoffset, .heatoffset, .cooloffset, .deadbandoffset, .innerbandoffset) and a `+=` or `-=`
  are differences (9/5 only, no 32). A number typed with its sign (`152°F`, `66.7°C`) is always that. A plain number in a saved
  Process, a Sample or a Brew Day Process is °C. A number in a formula with a temperature (`= Strike + 2`) is left as typed (°C)
  and the save gives one warning; a setpoint hotter than boiling in °C gets one warning. A probe kept in °F is turned where the
  Process reads or sets it, so a Process always works in °C behind the scenes. The BruControl Import puts °F on the plain numbers
  of its scripts that are on °F probes (155 becomes `155°F`). *Not taken:* Processes in °C only, with °F typed by its sign
  (Claude's first recommendation).
- **Exceptions, kept in their own unit whatever Units says (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19):** (1) **Recipe items that come in their
  own unit**: "some recipes have grams vs ounces so we will need to set what the thing added use (some Yeasts come as Grams rather
  than Oz , although most are Packs. Additions can be either"; "Hops may be the same. I have always used OZ. But you could use
  grams as more accurate." Additions (Misc) keep their unit on each line; each **yeast** line has its own unit
  (Packs / g / oz / ml) and each **hop** line its own unit (oz / g), with an **oz → g** button (built 2026-11-19, Rule 17.18). (2) **A Vessel whose own screen has
  fixed units** ("A digiboil always opens in Metric after a power cycle"; "a user can switch the Digiboil and Brewzilla back
  to F. I would think that is most common for US Brewers"): a Manual vessel (DigiBoil, Brewzilla) has its own Temperature units,
  the units its screen shows. It starts as Units (°F in US Standard) and can be set to °F or °C in its Properties; its Hover Help
  says the screen comes back in °C after a power cycle. In °F its pop-up gives the set point in °C as well. No other Vessel
  has its own display units.
- **Recipe values and skn_Boil_Temp in a Process (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20, picked "Metric inside, Units in messages": "I think A
  because it follows the Rule"):** a Process reads every `skn_rcp_` temperature, volume, weight and ratio, and `skn_Boil_Temp`, in metric
  (°C, L, kg, L/kg), so `HLT.setpoint = skn_rcp_Strike_Temp` and `wait HLT_Probe >= skn_rcp_Strike_Temp` are right in US too. In a
  message (text joined with `+` in an `ask`, `print` or `show`, or a `print` of it alone) the number shows in the Units; `skn_rcp_Temp_Units`, `_Volume_Units` and
  `_Weight_Units` are the Units' words. A number added in a formula is °C (`skn_rcp_Boil_Start_Temp + 5`). The Brew Process page shows
  them in the Units. **Exception:** Recipe items in their own unit ("Other additions (Irish Moss, Yeast Nutrient ...) would have their
  own units that do not get converted for display ... they are for display to the user and no math is needed"): adjuncts, a hop's
  oz or g, a fermentable's Measurement, a yeast's Packs are never turned.
- **New items start in metric (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20: "Check any values anywhere stores as sae and convert to metric"):** a new
  Temperature Probe (any kind, a Thermowell, a probe tee, the probe of a Vessel Builder), the probes Build a Schema makes (with their
  Heating Element Setpoints, Offsets and Simulator numbers, kept in °C as in the 3 Vessel Sample) and a new hydrometer's temperature
  are kept in °C. They still show in the Units. A probe already saved keeps its own units (never changed by this).
- **Live readings (built 2026-11-20, Panel Updates live side; OakBarn Brewery's Rule: "Keep backend data metric, display to user by
  choice in Skynet Settings"):** a Pressure transducer, a Level (any analog input in psi, bar, kPa, gal, L, lb, kg ...), a Flow
  meter and a Vessel scale keep their numbers in the units their sensor is calibrated in (its Units, Weight units and Volume units
  boxes, "Kept in"; its range, pulses and counts per unit use them; never changed for the user). What is shown follows Units: US
  psi, gal, gal/min, lb; Metric bar, L, L/min, kg (a volume or weight unit already in the Units, such as qt in US or mL in Metric, shows as it is). **Pressure by the field** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20: "for a User it could be either depending
  on the field. AS an example, ICOA pressure is kPa from the Metar, while CO2 could be Bar or PSI"): each pressure sensor has a
  **Metric pressure in** box, bar (the start) or kPa, for what it shows in Metric; US is always psi. Display only: a Process works in
  bar. The boil temperature's air pressure keeps its own display (hPa in Metric, inHg in US, as METAR reports give it). On a Tab,
  its Data Display, its Dial (Lowest, Highest, Cool, Hot) and a Process message. **A Process works in metric** (bar, L, L/min, kg):
  it reads and sets the reading turned; a plain number set on or compared with one is typed in Units and kept in metric with its
  sign (US `wait Keg >= 12` is kept `0.8274bar` and opens as `12`); a number typed with its sign (`12psi`, `0.8bar`, `5gal`, `18.9L`,
  `10lb`, `4.5kg`, `2gpm`, `7.5Lpm`) is always that. A probe's temperature in a message is left in °C (Processes such as the 3 Vessel Sample write " °C" after it). A calibration (a
  scale's .calibrate) stays in the sensor's units. Every factor is a Skynet Constant. New sensors start metric (Level 0-100 L,
  Flow meter 450 pulses per L, Scale kg and L), except the 0.5-4.5 V Pressure transducer, which keeps psi because it is sold by its
  psi range. pH, %, SG, V and a Value Widget never turn. Help 241.
- **Still to come:** the live side of a user's own Schemas (turning older °F probes, their Setpoints, PID and alarms into °C).
- **Both programs:** the BruControl Import still makes its Vessels and Profiles in the Units picked; the Panel keeps them in metric
  when they are saved. Its probes stay in the units BruControl had until the live side is done. Its scripts: a plain number on a
  sensor kept in psi, gal, lb (any unit with a sign) gets that sign (`12` becomes `12psi`), as a °F probe's gets °F. (Panel Updates
  Sandbox entry 9)

2.60 **Every page has Close; a Menu tab goes back to where it was opened** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, PDF "Panel Update 5" #3:
"No close Buttons"; #4: "After Save of Add Interface should go to the Interface Board page"; #8: "Close goes back to Schema not the
dialog or Tab it was opened from").
1. The Devices (Interface Boards), Globals, Log, Import, Media, Settings and Config pages have **Close** and **✕** frozen in the upper
   right (Rule 2.54). They go back to the Tab the page was opened from.
2. **☰ Menu > ➕ Add Interface ...**: after **Save** the Devices page opens on the Interfaces part, so the new board is seen.
3. A ☰ Menu tab (Templates, Equipment Profile, Schema ...) opened from another Menu tab goes back to that Menu tab on Close; opened
   from a Tab or a page it goes back to that Tab or page, not always to the Schema tab.
**Both programs:** the BruControl Import's own pages keep their look; its Build page shares the Panel's ☰ Menu tabs, so Close goes
back the same way there.

2.61 **🐞 Report a problem: an easy way for testers to report bugs and French Help corrections** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19:
"I will have other testers so an easy way for them to report bugs as well"; a French-speaking tester will review the French Help).
Testers are not programmers, so:
  1. **One button, two kinds:** **🐞 Report a problem** (☰ Menu > About) and **🐞 Report** on every Help page (next to 🖨 Print, the
     panel's Help page and the Help window) open one small box: **🐞 A bug** or **🌐 The French Help** (lit up while the Help is read
     in French). Each has **GitHub** and **✉ Email**.
  2. **GitHub forms** in the public repo (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`): **Report a bug** (plain questions: what went wrong, what you
     were doing, what you expected, how often, pictures) and **French Help correction** (in English and French: the page, the French
     now, the better French, why). Both name buttons in English, as on the screen (Rule 11.11). A blank issue is still allowed.
  3. **Filled in for the tester:** the Skynet version (version.json), the screen or Help page, and the computer and browser in plain
     words (Windows, Edge). GitHub fills the form's boxes from the address it is opened with.
  4. **✉ Email for anyone without a GitHub sign-in:** the computer's own mail program opens with the same questions and details, to
     **support@oakbarnbrewery.com** (as Rule 11.10's broken link). Nothing is sent until the tester presses Send.
  5. The Brain gives its version to a signed-in browser only (`/auth/status`). No person is named in the forms or Help
     (Rule 11.5); the forms are not announced to testers until OakBarn Brewery releases them.
Help 205. **Both programs:** the BruControl Import ships in the same Setup and uses the Panel's Help window, so 🐞 Report is on its
Help pages too; its own screens have no ☰ Menu > About.

2.62 **Templates and Equipment Profiles are only for placing on a Tab: a Tab keeps ZERO link to them** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19:
"A profile is only to import to start a build. Nothing more."; "Once on a Tab, only the tab effects those things on a Tab."; "I want
ZERO connection after placed on Tab."; and, for every Template: "Templates are only for a Placement on a Tab for Building and nothing
else associated with a Tab or any of its chilcren (Pumps, Valves....)").
  1. **Copied, never linked:** an Equipment Profile (➡ Transfer All / Vessels / Manifold, the New Schema Interview's Import, 🗂 New
     Schema from this profile) and every Template (pump, valve, vessel, fitting, Device, Widget ...) is **copied** onto the Tab. After
     that nothing on the Tab, and none of its children (vessels, pumps, valves, pipes, IPs, fittings ...), reads from or writes to the
     profile or Template. A change to the profile never changes a Tab, and a change on a Tab never changes the profile.
  2. **Any number of Tabs** (in any Schema) can start from the same profile. "One profile is on one Tab only", the Tab that
     "follows" its profile's Default Layout, saving a Tab into its profile on every Save, a locked profile freezing its Tabs, and
     **Make it unique** are gone (before the first Public Production, the Old Ways policy).
  3. **The Tab's own Equipment numbers** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, picked "Copied onto the Tab"; "these act like default but can be
     changed either through the interview or on the Properties dialog anytime"): Brewhouse efficiency, System Loss, Cooling shrinkage,
     Grain absorption, Hop utilization and the vessel list a Brew Day reads are copied onto the Tab with the profile and are the Tab's
     own. They are changed in **Edit layout > Tab Settings > Equipment numbers**, with **⚙ Numbers** on the Tab's row of ☰ Menu >
     Equipment Profile, or by the Equipment Profile Interview. A Recipe's **Brew on** Tab, its Efficiency, 📝 Record a brew and Use the
     average (Rule 17.13) are all the Tab's.
  4. **One direction only: 💾 Save as a profile ...** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "Maybe a save of a Tab to Equiment Profile but that
     direction only") copies a Tab's equipment, pipes, hardware and numbers into a new Equipment Profile or over one picked. No link is
     kept.
  5. **The lock is on the Tab:** the **🔒 Locked** switch on a Tab's row (Operators and Admins) locks that Tab, and **lock_Equipment /
     unlock_Equipment** lock every Tab with equipment: its vessels, IPs, pipes and hoses can't change until unlocked. A profile's own
     lock only keeps that profile from being changed.
  6. A Schema saved before this change loses its link when it is loaded: a Tab that showed its profile's drawing keeps a copy of it, and
     takes a copy of the profile's numbers. Nothing on a Tab is lost (Design Rule 1).
  7. **Skynet valves and other User versions of a Skynet Device Template** (Rule 5.16) get a copy of the Template's fixed attributes
     and pictures when placed, with the list of which ones are fixed. A save keeps the valve's own (a screen still can't change them),
     so a newer or changed Template never changes it. Picking another **Orientation** is the user choosing another Template of the
     set, so that one's picture is copied then. Which Properties rows it shows is its own copy too (#10).
  8. **Pipe fittings** keep their own copy of their Template's bend, body thickness, size, upright and openings (`fit`), made the
     first time Skynet sees the fitting. A Skynet fitting no longer takes its Template's new picture, openings and shape when Edit
     layout opens (that was Rules 5.6 and 15.2 for fittings placed before 2026-11-02; Rule 2.62 wins).
  9. **Tab Profiles are copied too** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "NO LINK NO Connect Nada 100% Links gone"): a Tab Profile picked
     for a new Tab (Default settings > Tab Profile for a new tab), with **Copy Profile** in Tab Settings, or with **Copy onto it** on
     ☰ Menu > Tab Profile copies its background color into the Tab's own **Color** and its look (name and value colors, alignment,
     value style) into the Tab's own copy, which a new Device or Widget on that Tab starts with. The Tab never names the profile:
     changing or deleting a Tab Profile changes no Tab. A Tab saved before keeps what it showed (its own Color, else the profile's)
     and its link goes when the Schema is loaded.
  10. **A Skynet valve's Properties rows** (which attributes a user can set, Rule 5.16) are copied onto the valve when placed, with
     its fixed attributes. A Template changed later never adds or takes away a row on a valve already placed. A valve saved before
     gets its copy once, the first time it is saved after this change.
**Both programs:** the BruControl Import makes no Equipment Profiles; its import onto a Tab that is locked by lock_Equipment is stopped
with the same message. Help 28 and 188.

2.63 **Removing an Interface is safe** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-18: "I clicked remove on the Interface for BM Brewery Mega. It is
the host asking if I want to delete. I know I should not do this as it would mess up almost every Thing so a Remove needs lots of
steps to do so"; "When you Hover the Remove Button Large Warning Pop Up"; "Pop up does not cover Button"; Panel Updates entry 29,
approved 2026-11-20: "29 ... yes"). The browser's own OK box is never used for it. On the Devices page, Interface list:
- **Resting the mouse on Remove** shows a **large** Hover Help warning (red border, red ⚠ heading) with this Interface's own counts
  of Devices, Widgets and Processes that use it. It opens beside the button, never over it. It only warns; nothing is removed.
- **Remove** (Admins only) opens **one Skynet box** (buttons 🗑 Delete · Close · ✕ upper right, Rule 2.54). Nothing changes until a
  button is pressed. Nothing uses it: 🗑 Delete removes it. Something uses it: the box lists, by group with counts, the Devices on it
  (with their Ports), the Widgets and pictures tied to them, the Processes that use them, its 1-Wire Index slots and other items
  that name it.
- **▶ Move them** (recommended): every Device moves to another Interface (or ➕ Add new Interface) with its name and settings. A
  Device whose Port or 1-Wire Index is taken there stays and is listed with the reason. Nothing is restricted.
- **Remove anyway: one warning only** (no tick boxes, no chain of pop-ups). Typing the Interface ID lights up 🗑 Delete.
- A Schema backup is made first (Rule 9.17). **Nothing that used it is deleted** (Design Rule #1): its Devices keep every setting
  and show **⚠ No Interface** in red in their Interface box until moved; a Process stops at a line that uses one.
- **Changing the Board** of an Interface in use (question (c), OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20: "I'd make it simpler: show the counts and
  save, with no typed confirmation. KISS"): ⚙ Change > Save shows one box with what uses it (Devices, Widgets, Processes) and the
  Devices on Ports the new board does not have, with 💾 Save · Close · ✕. No typing. Those Devices keep their Ports until each is
  given a new one in its Properties.
- **The ⚙ Change pop-up** (entry 29 Parts 2-4): the **USB Port** is a dropdown of the ports Skynet finds on this Brain now (Windows:
  the number, COM3 shows 3; a Pi or Linux: /dev/ttyACM0), with what is plugged in when the port says so, and 🔄 Look again. A saved
  port not on this Brain stays, shown in red "(not found on this Brain)". When Skynet cannot read the ports it stays a text box.
  While the Simulator runs, a grey line shows the real port, used when switching back to Real boards; it may still be changed.
  The Interface ID balloon gets one line under its text: **Suggested Device Name: BM_Port_Type_Label_TabID** with the real ID in
  red. The USB Port and Answer Wait balloons have OakBarn Brewery's approved drafts A and B.
**Both programs:** the BruControl Import has no Interface list with Remove; its Interface step is unchanged. The Import Build page
shares the Interface pop-up: it lists the ports of the computer it runs on, the same as the Panel. Help 76.

2.64 **One Skynet confirm box for big deletes and changes** (OakBarn Brewery, Panel Updates entry 29, 2026-11-18: "I clicked remove
on the Interface ... It is the host asking if I want to delete"; 2026-11-20: "do 29"). The browser's own OK / Cancel box is not used
for a big delete or change. They all ask in **one shared Skynet box** (public/skyconfirm.js), the same everywhere (Rule 2.44):
- Its buttons are in the **upper right** (Rule 2.54): the action, named for what it does (🗑 Delete, 🗑 Remove, 🚚 Move in now,
  ▶ Proceed ...), red for a delete or a big change, then **Close** and **✕**. Close, ✕ and Esc change nothing. Close has the focus,
  so a stray Enter changes nothing.
- The question is the heading; the rest of the old message is the text under it, word for word.
- **One warning only:** one box, no second "Are you sure?", nothing to type or tick (only Remove an Interface keeps its typed ID,
  Rule 2.63). It is a modal dialog, so it is on top of everything (Rule 18.53).
- Used for: Delete a Tab, a Schema, a gGlobal, an Equipment Profile, a Profile, a Device Template, a Template,
  a User Process Template, a User Style, a Process (to the Recycle Bin) and a Process for good, a CSV set, a 1-Wire circuit or Index
  in use, a Help page, media files; Throw away the Build Tab; Replace in many Processes; Remove a user, an Approved Device, the
  Patron code; Turn Approved Devices Off; Make a new recovery code; the BruControl Import; Switch / load a Schema; Simulator or Real
  boards; Move in (Brain Move); Save the config file and Put back an old one. The small "leave without saving?" questions stay as
  they are. *Not* an item on a Tab (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-23): its Properties Delete goes at once and ↩ Put back (Ctrl+Z)
  brings it back (Rule 5.37). The **Delete key** (or **Backspace**, the Mac's "delete" key; 2026-11-24) does the same for the item picked in Edit layout (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-24: "If
  something has the focus can we delete it with the delete key?"): never while typing in a box or with a dialog open; a locked item
  (or equipment under lock_Equipment) stays, with one toast.
**Both programs:** the BruControl Importer's own pages are unchanged; the panel's BruControl Import button asked in this box until it
was taken out of the Panel (2026-11-21, Rule 11.3).
Help 28, 48, 119, 188.

2.65 **Find and Replace in every big text editor: Ctrl+F and Ctrl+H on one bar** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-21: "CTRL + F for Find
and CTRL + H also as Find and Replace on same Dialog"; picked "Add to Template + Help editors"):
- Every big text editor has the same Find bar above its text: the Process Editor and Schema.json (since PR #43), the Process
  Template editor (☰ Menu > Brew Process > 👁 View or ✏ Edit) and the Help text editor (✏ Edit page).
- **Ctrl+F** (⌘+F on a Mac) opens Find. **Ctrl+H** opens the same bar with the cursor in **Replace with** (one bar, never two
  pop-ups). Typing a highlighted word first puts it in Find.
- On the bar: match count (`3 of 12`), ▲ ▼ (Enter, Shift+Enter, F3), **Aa** (match case), **Whole word**, ✕ (Esc). Every match is
  lit; the current one is darker. **Replace** and **Replace all** type through the browser, so **Ctrl+Z** undoes them; nothing is
  saved until the editor's own Save.
- A read only text (a Skynet Process Template, or a Brewer) gets Find with no Replace row.
- The keys are taken from the browser only while that editor or its bar has the focus. They never take the copy, paste, undo or redo
  keys (Rule 2.32).
- **Changed 2026-11-22** (OakBarn Brewery, Panel Update 9, item 8: "CTRL + F Have the search box come up in the middle top of the
  screen. Besides the Tab you are on, all searches include the Help"; Fritz picked "Change Rule 2.65"): **anywhere else in the panel,
  Ctrl+F (⌘+F) opens the Skynet search box** at the top middle of the screen (it was the browser's own Find). Typing lists what matches
  on the Tab you are on (Devices, Widgets and Vessels, by Label or Name; a click lights it up) and the Help pages (by title and text; a
  click opens the page). Enter opens the first one; Esc or ✕ closes it. A search changes nothing. While a dialog is open Ctrl+F is left
  to the browser. Ctrl+H outside an editor stays the browser's (History), see Help 113. (public/skysearch.js, on top by Rule 18.53)
**Both programs:** the BruControl Import program's pages have no big text editor and no Tabs, so nothing changes there.
Help 30, 12, 113.

2.66 **The Recipe screens: no clutter, the same size buttons, plain pickers** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-22, Panel Update 9, items 20,
21, 24c, 25e, 29 and 33):
- Every Daughter Tab button on the Recipe tab is the **same size**, and the MASH one says **Mash and Sparge Profile**. The CLICK Here /

2.67 **A change to a Profile, a Template or a Setting is for new things** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-22, Panel Update 9, item 11: "No
Profile or Template or Skynet Settings change or affects already imported ones in a Tab or Recipe. They are on for new things only.
Exception: US/Metric changes display on the fly"): what is
already made keeps what it was made with. A new Template, Equipment Profile, Mash or Boil Profile, or a changed default, is used by
the next thing made from it; a Device, Widget, Tab or Recipe already made is not changed by it. **The one exception is Units**
(Rule 2.59): it is display only, so every screen shows the new Units at once (the values are kept metric and never change). To bring
a new Profile into something already made, pick it again there (for example Brew on, or a Recipe's Mash Profile).
**Both programs:** the BruControl Import makes new things only, so it follows this already.

2.68 **The Skynet Brew Timers** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-22, Panel Update 9 items 10d and 31: "There should be a skynet Boil Timer
and Mash Timer"; "Format hh:mm until 5 minutes left the hh:mm:ss"; "Skynet Boil Clock used for Hop Timer, Separate Whirlpool/ Chilling
Timer"; names picked "Rule words: wait_boil, skn_ timers", Rule 3.20). **`skn_Boil_Timer`, `skn_Mash_Timer` and `skn_Whirlpool_Timer`**:
- Skynet owns them. They **always count down**. A person sets only their **Labels** (☰ Menu > Default settings > Brew Timers; Boil
  Timer, Mash Timer, Whirlpool / Chilling Timer to start).
- Each **shows itself** at the top middle of every screen while it runs, and **hides** when it stops or reaches 0. It reads
  **hh:mm** until 5 minutes are left, then **hh:mm:ss**.
- A Process: `skn_Boil_Timer = 01:00:00` (the time left), `start skn_Boil_Timer`, `stop skn_Boil_Timer`, `reset skn_Boil_Timer`,
  `wait skn_Boil_Timer <= 00:30:00`, and `skn_Boil_Timer.running` (read only). They have no other attribute.
- `start` with nothing set first (or after `reset`) takes the **Brew Day value** from the loaded Recipe (or the ☰ Menu > Default tab
  while none is): the boil time; the mash steps' times added up; the Whirlpool Minutes.
- **Hop alerts run on the Boil Timer:** `start_hop_alerts` with no timer named follows `skn_Boil_Timer` while it runs (Rule 17.4).
- **Hop Stands hold on the Whirlpool / Chilling Timer:** the Skynet Chill and Whirlpool and Chill Process Templates set `skn_Whirlpool_Timer`
  to a stand's minutes, start it and wait for it (Rule 17.20, 2026-11-23).
- Fermenters' own timers ("each would need their own DateTime type") are not built. Panel only: the BruControl Import brings in no
  Skynet Brew Timer.

2.73 **Alt + key shortcuts work everywhere** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-24: "I want things to work universal so ALT + Z and ALT + R are
Out. and all the Firefox ones as well"). A Panel shortcut with **Alt** uses only a letter that no browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari),
no system (Windows, Mac, Linux, Raspberry Pi OS) and no common graphics overlay keeps for itself. **Allowed Alt + letter:** A, C, G, I, J,
K, L, M, N, O, P, Q, U, W, X, Y. **Never:** D, E, F (Chrome and Edge), F, E, V, S, B, T, H (Firefox menus), Z (NVIDIA overlay), R (AMD
overlay), nor Alt + Tab, Space, Esc, F1 to F10, Home or the arrows (Alt + Left / Right are the browser's Back and Forward). **Shift + Alt + letter** is free on all of them except T, I and A
(Chrome and Edge). **Shift + Alt + arrow** is free too (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-24: "Shift + Alt + arrow"), outside text boxes only. **Alt + number is never used** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-24: "What about alt + Number"): Chromium and Firefox on
Linux and the Pi switch browser tabs with Alt + 1 to 9, and on Windows Alt + number pad digits type characters (Alt + 0176 = °).
**Shift + Alt + number** is allowed, outside text boxes only. **Alt + ` (the ~ key) is never used** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-24: "alt + tilde"): GNOME switches
windows with it, on a Mac Option + ` types accents, and the key is ² on a French keyboard and ^ on a German one. **Alt + [** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-24:
"alt + [") is allowed but read by its place (the key right of P), since it is ^ on a French and Ü on a German keyboard; Help names
it that way. **Alt + =** ("Alt + =") the same: allowed by its place (the key left of Backspace; ´ on a German keyboard). **Alt + mouse click or drag is never used** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-24: "Can alt + Left Mouse Click work"): many
Linux desktops, and likely the Pi, move the whole window with it, so the click never reaches the Panel. Shift + click is safe. The older Alt held while
dragging (place without the snap, Edit layout) still works on Windows and Mac; on a Pi it may move the window instead. The allowed letters come first. **Ctrl + Alt + key is never used** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-24: "any conflicts with CTRL + Alt + Key"): on
European Windows keyboards Ctrl + Alt is AltGr and types characters (€, @), Linux and the Pi keep many (terminal, lock screen,
desktops), and on a Mac Control + Option is the VoiceOver key. The key is read by its place (`ev.code`), so a Mac's Option + letter, which types a symbol, works too. In use: Alt + P
(Picture picker, admins). Never while typing in a box, and never a key Rule 2.32 keeps. The full table, with what each combination does on Windows, Mac, Linux and the Pi, is
`docs/Skynet_Key_Combinations.md` (and `.csv`), and just the ones still free in `docs/Skynet_Keys_Available.md` ("Give me a second MD of list the keys that
are available on Skynet") (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-24: "make it an MD ... and available as a CSV"); a new
shortcut is added there too.

2.74 **Notes stay 2 seconds** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-24: "Nanny state up too long. Needs to be quick, maybe 3 seconds and then
gone"; "All nanny pop-ups 3 seconds"; then "Change Blue and Red Nanny to 2 seconds"). Every short note that pops up at the bottom of
the Panel ("… deleted. ↩ Put back (Ctrl+Z) brings it back.", "Moved to …", "Saved" …), blue or red (an error), in the Panel and the
BruControl Import program, stays **2 seconds**, then goes by itself, however long its words are. A new note never asks for another
time. The same for the small red **⚠** box in a dialog (Rule 18.28, was 5 seconds) and the **Hold the left button a moment, then
drag** hint on a Quick Disconnect hose end (was 3) (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-25: "Blue and Red notes need to be 2 seconds. Even 3
is too long"). A note with a button on it (**↩ Undo**) keeps its own time, so there is time to press it. *Was (2026-11-24):* blue
notes 3 seconds, red notes 5.

## 3. Names and file names

3.1 **Device names** follow `InterfaceID_Port_GeneralType@DeviceTypeID_Label_TabID`, **one underscore between the parts** (Fritz, 2026-11-05:
"Single Underscores between parts of name"; example `MB_A0_TEMP@10KNTC_Mash~Tun_SP`). **Spaces in the Label become `~`** (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "I like the ~ instead of a _ in
the label part of the name. Make that the rule"), so `_` only ever separates the parts: Label *Mash Tun* gives `Mash~Tun`. A taken name gets _2, _3 ... before the Tab ID.
**The Type part starts with the General Type and an `@`** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-11: "It is regarding Device Types. a on/off Pump is
DO:Pump I want the DO: to be in the Suggest Name"; "use @ symbol"): the Device Type shown as `DO: Pump` (Rule 18.18) is `DO@Pump` in the
name, because a `:` can't be in a name (Rule 3.4). An On/Off Pump is `BM_22_DO@Pump_Pump_BH`, a DS18B20 probe `BM1w1_1_HLT_BH`, a
Heating Element `BM_8_DO@H_Element_HLT~element_BH`. When the General Type and the Type ID are the same word it is written once (`PID`, `Hys`,
`DO`). A Process reads the `@` as part of the name, with no quotes. Older Schemas (Rule 15.2): once per Schema, a Device named in the
Suggested Name form gets its General Type@ when the Schema loads; its hidden key stays and every Process and setting that uses it follows.
The 3 Vessel sample and the default Schema are changed (Rule 15.3). Both programs: the BruControl Import names the same way. Every special
character and what it does in a name: docs/Special_Characters.md.
*Replaced:* `InterfaceID_Port_DeviceTypeID_Label__TabID`, two underscores before the Tab ID (2026-10-23). The panel suggests the name; an Admin may type another.
Full details (Type IDs, virtual ports, what happens to odd characters) are in the Device Library.
(2026-10-23, PR #97)
*Changed for 1-Wire probes (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "If we had an 1 wire Index IP like BM1w1_1 would be for the first 1 wire hooked
up to the First created On wire using An Interface and Port. The second one on the same circuit would be BM1w1_2. If a Second 1 wire was
created on the same board it would have probe index as BM1w2_n. Suggest name would be IndexId _Label_Tab"):* a DS18B20 probe is named
`IndexID_Label_TabID`, its **1-Wire Index ID** (Interface ID + `1w` + circuit number + `_` + probe number, Rule 6.37) then the Label and
the Tab ID: `BM1w1_1_HLT_BH`. It has no Port and no Type part (the `1w` says what it is), and the pin is not in it ("A user does not really
care about the PIN"). It starts with the Interface ID, so typing BM in the Process editor lists it ("This would work for predictive text and
show if BM was typed"). *Replaced:* `BM_700_TEMP@1W_HLT_BH` (virtual port 700 + probe number - 1). Older Schemas: once per Schema, a
probe in the old form gets the new name when the Schema loads; its hidden key stays and everything that uses it follows (Rule 6.37).
**A Heating Element's Type ID is `H_Element`** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-11: "Heating Element: DO@H_Element"; was `HE` from Fritz, 2026-11-07: "they are added from a DDLB so we know it is a Heating Element. So we
could Use MB_25_HE_HLT_BR"), e.g. `MB_25_DO@H_Element_HLT_BR` (with its General Type since 2026-11-11), whatever heating method it is using (Rule 6.19); the method is not in its
name or Label, since it can change while brewing. A Heating Element is wired straight to its port, going to an SSR (or a
contactor) or to a DAC. Elements named before keep `DO` (Rule 3.5). The BruControl Import names them the same way.
*Replaced:* a Heating Element on a relay had `DO`, like a plain relay (2026-10-23).
*Replaced:* the 2026-10-21 format `InterfaceID_Port_Type_DisplayName_TabID` from PR #61.

3.2 **The ID Rule** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "IDs for Interfaces, Tabs, and any other Item that has a User Set ID (Always a
Suggested Unique one on a New Build) 1 to 4 Char Unique Once saved, Never Changed even by an Admin. Used as first text with Name
(may change to Label on some) Example BH: Brew House for a tab DDLB."; letters and numbers picked the same day). Every **Interface ID**,
every **Tab ID**, and the ID of **any other item that has a user-set ID**:
- **Skynet always suggests a unique one** on a new build. The user may type another before the first Save. An **Interface ID**
  is suggested from its Name as it is typed (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15, Add Interface markup: "Suggest unique ID based on Name 2
  char then 3 and 4 if needed to be unique"): the first letters of its first two words (Hot Side = HS); when that is taken, 3
  characters (HSI, or the first letters of three words), then 4 only when every 3 is taken.
- **1 to 4 characters**: letters and numbers (A to Z, 0 to 9), **starting with a letter** (BH, MB2, F1).
- **Unique** among its kind (no two Interfaces, no two Tabs, the same ID).
- **Once saved, never changed, not even by an Admin.** The box shows it read only; the Brain refuses a changed ID. To use another
  ID, make a new item.
- **Shown first** in every list, before its Name (on some items its Label): **BH: Brew House**, **BM: Brewery Mega**.
The ID is part of every Suggested Device name (Rule 3.1), so a name never goes out of date. It is not the item's key: every
Interface and Tab also has its hidden Meaningless Key (Design Rule #2, Rule 3.10), and Processes follow the key, not the ID.
Other Rules, Help pages and Hover Help do not repeat these details: they say the ID **follows Rule 3.2** (OakBarn Brewery,
2026-11-15: "state that Tab IDs follow the Rule #"). Both programs follow it: the BruControl Import suggests the IDs, lets the
user change them on its Boards and Tabs page, and they are locked once the Schema is saved.
*Replaced:* Interface ID 1 to 4 letters, Tab ID exactly 2 letters, only an Admin can change either (2026-10-21, PR #61; restated
2026-10-27, PR #118; kept 2026-11-12).

3.3 **No spaces in Device or Process names.** Names must be unique. (2026-10-05, PR #25; 2026-10-21)
**No space at the start or end of any name or Label** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-11: "Hunt for Beginning or trailing spaces in a label
or name and not allow. This is an issue in BruControl I want to remove from Skynet"; "Put that in Naming and Label Rules"). A name
(Tab and Interface names too, though they may have spaces inside) is refused with a message; a Label is trimmed as soon as you leave its
box, again when it is saved, and every older Label once its Schema loads. Both programs follow this: a BruControl name or Label
brought in by the Import is trimmed the same way. See Rule 3.17.

3.4 **Allowed characters** in every name (Devices, Widgets, Interfaces, Tabs, Texts, pipes, vessels ...;
all names are treated the same, Rule 3.11): no control characters, no spaces at the start or end, no leading dot, no emoji, none of `< > : " / \ | ? *`, none of the Windows reserved
names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9). **File and folder names** follow the same list, and a
period only before the file ending (folders and Process names: no period). Only new or changed names
are checked, except `< > : " / \ | ? *`: under Rule 15.2 an older name with one of them is changed
once, each to a `~` (`Pump:1` becomes `Pump~1`, `_2` if taken); it keeps its hidden key, the old name
becomes its Label, and Processes, settings, saved values and the brew log follow (backups
`.before-safe-names.bak`; for a Tab, everything on it follows). (2026-10-23, PR #95; `< > : " / \ | ? *` added by
Fritz 2026-10-29, PR #134; every name 2026-10-29, Help 63)
**Plain names** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-11: the marks "Allowed in a name you type, but trouble are No No also"; "And any that
interfere with, Mac or Linux, MQTT are in the list"): a Device, Widget, gGlobal, Text, pipe, vessel or other item name has only
**letters, numbers, `_`, `~`, `@` and `°`**, and starts with a letter or `_`, so it works with no quotes in a Process and is safe on
Windows, Mac, Linux and MQTT. Tab and Interface names are shown names (Brew House) and keep only the list above; their IDs are plain.
An Integrated Instance keeps its `VesselName.DeviceName` (Rule 6.28). A Label may have any other mark (but see below): in the Suggested Name each other mark
becomes `~`, an accent is dropped and ß æ ø are spelled ss ae o (2026-11-20). Older names (Rule 15.2): once per Schema, each other mark becomes `~` (an accent dropped, `_2`
if taken) when the Schema loads; Processes and settings follow. Every mark and why: docs/Special_Characters.md.
**° is allowed** in a name (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-11: the degree mark, typed with Ctrl+D, "does no interference so should be allowed
even in a Name"): `Temp_°F`. **`@` and `~` are kept for the Suggested Name** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-11: "prevent @ and ~ being used
in a Label or name except when put there by the program in a Suggested Name", "AS they are reserved for Suggested Name Use Only").
**Changed 2026-11-24** (OakBarn Brewery: "And @ and ~ can be part of a name because Skynet adds them all the time"): a name typed by
hand may have `@` and `~` too. A Label still can't (below). **A Label can't have © ® ™ or
@ ~** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-11: "No Circle C or R in Labels"; © ® ™ are "Reserved for copyright and trademark notices of the
Skynet MIT License. Skynet is Open Source. Not Allowed in a name or a Label to avoid confusion with the Skynet MIT License", the
words of the small box and the Label Hover Help): while typing, © ® ™ are taken out and @ ~ become a space, and a small box says why; an older Label
gets the same when its Schema loads. Every other mark may be in a Label. **The words of the Process language** (Help 22, Reserved
words: `NULL`, `true`, `if`, `wait` ...) can't be a name either.

3.5 **Never rename an existing item by itself**, with one exception: **a clone follows its parent.**
A clone's name is always its parent's name plus `_Clone_N`; when the parent is renamed, the parent part
of each clone's name changes with it, and every Process follows (Rule 3.6). Each clone has its own
hidden key (Rule 3.10) but acts only through its parent's key. (2026-10-21; changed 2026-10-27)
*Replaced:* "Never rename an existing Device by itself. It would break Processes." (2026-10-21)

3.6 **When a name changes, every Process that uses it follows** the new name. The panel finds the
rename by the item's hidden key (Rule 3.10). A Process running at the time keeps working and uses
the new name from its next start. Renaming a Process changes the lines that start or stop it and
the Autostart list. **Clones follow too:** renaming an item changes the old-name part of each of
its clones' names (`HLT copy` becomes `Hot_Liquor_Tank copy`), unless that name is taken.
(2026-10-22, PR #73; keys and clones 2026-10-27)

3.7 **Every date in a file name follows ISO 8601**, safe for file names: `YYYY-MM-DD` for a day,
`YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS` (no colons) for a date and time. (2026-10-23, PR #93)
Note: the Panel Version name is not changed yet (see Open questions).

3.8 **Template names:** no spaces, unique. A Label is only on Tab items (empty Label = the name).
(2026-10-21)

3.9 **Generic names and shapes only.** Product photos with a maker's logo or name are redrawn as
generic shapes with generic names (for example Hop_Filter_Inline, not a brand name), because
Skynet will be open source. (2026-10-22)

3.10 **Every item with a name has a hidden key** (Devices, Widgets, variables, Texts, IPs, pipes,
vessels, fittings, Tabs, Interfaces, Processes, Templates, Profiles). It is given when the item is
first built (saved), is meaningless, unique and never changes. Nobody can see it (not on screen, not
in the Config Editor, not in a saved Schema file) and nobody can use it in a Process: Processes
always use names, and the panel ties each name to its key behind the scenes. Old Schemas get their keys
when they are loaded. **Exception:** picture and sound paths have no key; a later request covers
how the Graphic Picker handles a path. (2026-10-27)

3.11 **Once an item is built, its Name is locked** (🔒). It is changed only with the **✏ Change
name** button beside it, which opens the **Name Change** pop-up: the name now (read only), a box for
the new name, the **Suggested Name**, ✖ Cancel, 💾 Save and **💾 Update to Suggested** (Rule 3.16). The same pop-up renames
Processes and Schemas. (2026-10-27)
**All names are treated the same** (Fritz, 2026-10-29): a name is only there to find the item on the screen and, in the Process
Editor, to set its `.attribute`. **Skynet names are fixed** and are never changed (only while building Skynet). **Any name a Process
could use changes only with ✏ Change name** (Rule 3.6: the Processes follow). Exceptions: **User Template names** (only for picking
one; renaming changes nothing in a Process), and picture paths / graphic file names (handled later).
**A locked Name box says so** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-24: "On the Tab Property Menu, the Name has the focus but cannot be edited
here. The inner blue focus ring should be red and maybe lead by the name by the Do Not Enter icon. If anyone clicks into the field, it
would have a pop-up 'Do you want to change the Name of the Tab?' If yes, same as clicking the Change name button"): in every Properties
with a locked Name (a Tab, Device, Widget …), its name reads **⛔ Name 🔒**, its focus ring is red, and a click (or typing) in the box
asks **Do you want to change the Name of the Tab?** (Device, Widget, item). **✏ Yes, change it** opens the same Name Change pop-up as
✏ Change name; Close leaves it as it is.

3.12 **Interfaces are easy to find and add.** ☰ Menu has **🔌 Interfaces (boards)** and **➕ Add
Interface…**, and every Interface dropdown in a New Device box (any Tab, RIMS and kettle too) ends
with **➕ Add new Interface…**, which opens the Add Interface pop-up and comes back with the new
Interface picked. The pop-up explains the Interface ID: it becomes part of every Suggested Device
name, must be unique, and should be set once and left. (2026-10-27, thread "Make Interfaces easy to
add and simulate", Help 76)

3.13 **Own Device names get a warning.** When a name is typed instead of the Suggested Name, the panel
warns: a plain word like "Pump" becomes a reserved word in Processes and can cause problems in the
code; the Device name is only used in Processes and never shown on a Tab, so a unique, meaningful
name is better. OK keeps it, Cancel goes back. (2026-10-27, Help 76)

3.14 **Widget names** follow `wgt_Type_Label_TabID`, **one underscore between the parts** (Fritz, 2026-11-06: "Suggested names for
widgets wgt_Label_Tabid", "Widgets like gGlobals have types", "Your suggest name is good. wgt_DT_DateTime_1_BR"). Example
`wgt_DT_DateTime_1_BR`. The **Type** is a few letters for the kind of Widget, as gGlobals have gV_, gS_ ... (Rule 1.19):
**PIX** Picture, **TXT** Text, **LBL** Label, **VAL** Value, **CV** Code Value (Rule 1.27), **TM** Time, **DT** DateTime, **TMR** Timer, **AUD** Audio Widget (was SND Sound Player, Rule 7.26), **SW** Switch, **PSW** Process Switch (the Process Widget, a Switch Widget that is a Process subclass, Rule 1.31),
**PB** Push Button, **PL** Pulse Button, **LED** LED, **MV** Manual Valve, **TWV** Tap Water Valve, **ALM** Alarm (Basic and User),
**OVR** Override, **GPH** Graph (was CHT Chart, Rule 1.26), **SLD** Slider, **CHK** Checkbox, **LTB** Lighted Button (Rule 1.20) (Fritz picked PIX for Picture; the rest as suggested). Spaces in the Label become `~`, as in Rule 3.1 (`wgt_PIX_Kettle~Element`); a taken name
gets _2, _3 ... before the Tab ID. A new Widget is made on the 🔨 Build Tab (Rule 4.1), so its name has no Tab ID until Finish Build ...
> Move to Tab adds it. Its name **follows its Label and Tab** until a name of its own is typed (as a Device's does). Vessels, pipes,
fittings and Clones keep their own names. **Every Widget gets a Suggested Name and a Label, and the Label is never blank** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "All Widgets get a name and label"). Vessels, pipes, hoses and fittings keep their own name patterns (Pipe_1, Hose_1, Tee_1, Elbow_1); their Label starts as their Name in small letters (pipe_1, tee_1) and can be changed, but never left blank. A Widget made from a Template (a Chiller, Rule 5.41) gets its Suggested Name, Label and any preset .attributes from that Template. **Names already made never change by themselves** (Rule 3.5): w_Text_1, pic_Kettle,
alm_Hops, sw_1 ... keep working. The **BruControl Import** uses the same pattern when it brings Widgets in (Rule 15.4).
*Replaced:* pic_ + Label (Picture Widget, Rule 18.27), w_Text_N (Text Widget), alm_ + Label (Alarm), w_Value_N, w_Time_N,
w_DateTime_N, and the sw_, pb_, pl_, led_ hints. (thread "Add hover help to clean dialogs")

3.15 **Hidden names match what is shown.** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "if a Developer was using Skynet as Open Source, it might
be better to have all hidden names correspond in some what to a shown counter point or have their own meaningful name.") A setting's
hidden name (the one saved in the Schema, used by the code) is the name shown on screen, or a name that says what it is. First one:
an Interface's **Connection** (USB, Ethernet, WiFi or Simulator) is saved as `connection`, and the real Connection of a board in the
Simulator as `realConnection` (they were `type` and `realType`). An old Schema is changed over by itself when it is opened; nothing
else changes for the user. Both programs: the BruControl Importer writes `connection` too.

3.16 **The Suggested Name follows the Label** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "Rule All: A change in the Label Updates the Suggest
Name"; "All Change Name Dialog gets new Button").
- In every Properties box, typing a **Label** (or picking another Interface, Port, Device Type or Tab) changes the **Suggested Name**
  line at once. The Name itself stays as it is until it is changed (Rule 3.11).
- The Suggested Name always has its Device Type ID: a Device saved without one (the Three Vessel sample's built-in heaters and probes
  were) gets its usual one (HE for a Heating Element), so `BM_8_DO@H_Element_HLT~element_BH`, not `BM_8_HLT~element_BR`.
- **Every Name Change pop-up** shows the Suggested Name and has **💾 Update to Suggested** beside ✖ Cancel and 💾 Save: one click
  saves the Suggested Name. A Process or a Schema has no Suggested Name, so there the button is greyed out.
- **The Label's help balloon is made for where it is:** it names its own Label, shows its own Suggested Name with the Label part in
  red (`MB_22_HE_`**`HLT~Element`**`_BR`), says spaces become ~, and says what the ⬢ (font, size and colors) and ⬆ (a 2 line Text
  Box) beside it do. Help 180.

3.17 **Label Rules** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-11: "Put that in Nameing and Label Rules"). A Label is the name shown on the Tab, and
it is the Label part of the Suggested Name (Rule 3.16). It is never blank (Rule 18.28). It may have spaces and most marks, but:
- **No space at the start or end** (Rule 3.3; "an issue in BruControl I want to remove from Skynet"). It is trimmed as soon as you
  leave its box, when it is saved, and in an older Schema when it loads.
  To lay text out, use the codes `\n` (a new line) and `\t` (an indent, OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-12: "\t for indent!"), not extra
  spaces (OakBarn Brewery: "extra spaces are used as a poor man's way of spacing in a form or Box"). Help 22, Codes inside text.
- **No © ® ™**: "Reserved for copyright and trademark notices of the Skynet MIT License. Skynet is Open Source. Not Allowed in a
  name or a Label to avoid confusion with the Skynet MIT License." They are taken out as you type, and a small box says so.
- **No @ ~**: kept for the Suggested Name (Rule 3.4). Typed, they become a space, and the small box says so.
- In the Suggested Name each space or other mark becomes `~`, an accent is dropped and ° stays (Rule 3.4, docs/Special_Characters.md).
  **ß, æ, ø are spelled ss, ae, o** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20, option A, for the German, Danish and Norwegian Help to come):
  *Weiß Bier* gives `Weiss~Bier`, *Mæsk* gives `Maesk`, *Søl* gives `Sol`, not `~`, which stands for a space (public/letters.js). Names
  already saved never change (Rule #2).
- The same words are in the Label's Hover Help (Help 115).

3.18 **🏷 Suggested Names: convert all names at once** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-12: "There is a Button where all Names can be
converted to a Suggested Name, if you have not chosen to do so earlier" ... "build"). In Edit layout, Admins only, the **🏷 Suggested
Names** button lists every Device and Widget, on every Tab, whose Name is not its Suggested Name: Tab, Name now, Suggested Name,
each ticked (☑ Tick all, ☐ Untick all). **💾 Convert** gives each ticked one its Suggested Name, one at a time, so two that would
get the same name get `_2` (Rule 3.3, names unique). **Save layout** keeps them; Exit without Saving drops them. Every Process
follows the new names (hidden keys, Rule 3.10), and Clones follow their parent (Rule 3.5). Never changed: Integrated Instances
(VesselName.DeviceName, Rule 6.28), and items with no Suggested Name (vessels, pipes, fittings, Text, Processes, Schemas). Nothing
is converted unless the Admin presses Convert (Rule #1, never take away). **Both programs:** the BruControl Import's Build page
uses the same Edit layout bar, so imported names can be converted the same way after the Import. Help 46, 115.

3.19 **Rich Text Embedded Codes** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-10-29, the list of codes; 2026-11-15: "New pr and \degF and \degC good";
"maybe \dFC"). A short code that starts with a backslash, typed inside any text the panel shows (a Text, a Label, a Name, a Value, a
Process string, a `print` line, a pop-up), changes how it looks. The one list is Help 90, Rich Text Embedded Code:
- **Switches** (the first turns it on, the next turns it off): `\b` bold (`\B` too), `\i` italic, `\u` underline, `\s`
  strikethrough, `\L` large, `\S` small (three quarters size), `\_` subscript, `\^` superscript.
- **Color:** `\c{Red}` ... `\c`. A panel color name (the same one list as the color dropdowns, public/richtext.js NAMED_COLORS;
  capitals and spaces don't matter) or a #hex color. A name that is not a color stays as typed, so the mistake shows.
- **Signs and spacing:** `\n` a new line, `\t` an indent (Rule 3.17), `\deg` a plain ° (also for angles, a 45° elbow), `\degF` °F,
  `\degC` °C, `\dFC` °F or °C from the Default Temperatures unit (US °F, Metric °C; the letter only, the number is not changed),
  `\ohm` Ω, `\+-` ±, `\\` one backslash.
- **No `\F` or `\C` alone:** a folder path like `C:\Config` must never turn into °Config (Rule 7.23 uses paths everywhere).
- A code that is not on the list stays as typed. Codes work the same in both programs; the BruControl Import brings in no codes.

3.20 **`skn_` starts every Skynet name** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "yes the skn_ as any Skynet thing"; "KISS make them the
same"). A name Skynet owns, that a Process can read, starts **`skn_`**, lower case like the other starts (`gG`, `wgt_`):
Skynet internal Globals (`skn_Boil_Temp`, Rule 1.18), probe roles (`skn_Boil_Probe_1`, Rule 1.18, not built yet) and Skynet
Constants (`skn_const_L_p_Gal`, Rule 1.17). A group of Skynet names gets **`skn_<group>_`** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19:
"they could be skn_rcp_ so I will know what you are taking about"): `skn_const_` for Skynet Constants, `skn_rcp_` for Recipe values.
Recipe values are `skn_rcp_Strike_Temp` ... (Rule 16.4). *Replaced:* Recipe values were `rcp_` names (2026-11-20, before the
first Public Production, so no old way is kept).

## 4. Making things: the Build Tab

4.1 **Every new Device, Widget or copy of a Template starts on the 🔨 Build Tab, never on a regular Tab** (OakBarn Brewery,
2026-11-12: "When adding a new Device or Widget, automatically Start on the Build Tab and not a Regular Tab. It will be moved to the
Regular Tab at the End of the Build chain."). **Saving never ends a Build** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "IT is a bug because I was
Not finished Building. I want to add things to an existing Build and leave in Build Mode so needs to be fixed."; "Lets do A"):
- **💾 Save layout** saves the regular Tabs. The Build stays open on the 🔨 Build Tab and you stay in Edit layout, to keep adding to it.
- **An unfinished Build is kept on the Brain**, in the Schema, never run and never shown on Brew Day. It survives a restart and
  comes back on the 🔨 Build Tab the next time Edit layout opens. Leaving Edit layout (with or without saving) keeps it too. Its
  Devices keep their Ports: Available Ports never offers a Port a Device in the Build has.
- **A kept Build that comes back says so, with one click to 🗑 Discard Build** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "even if the Build was
  still in the Build mode after restarting, one click to discard"): Discard lets its Ports go, and **↩ Undo** shows for a few seconds
  after (Rule 2.53).
- **Only ✅ Finish Build ... ends it** (it was 💾 Save Build ...): **Move to Tab** (one Tab for the whole Build; the Tab picked in an
  Add box is only offered first, OakBarn Brewery: "Saving to the Tab (and I might have wanted to change the tab when saving) could be
  a nightmare for a User"), **As a Template**, **Throw it away** (asks first; its Ports go free), or **Keep building**. After Move to
  Tab, Save layout keeps it on that Tab. **Keep building** always goes back to building: a 👁 Preview left on is turned off, so
  things can be moved and changed again (2026-11-24, OakBarn Brewery: "Clicked Finish Build then Keep building as I wanted to change
  some stuff but still in non edit mode").
The Tab picked in its Add box (Rule 4.2) is remembered: its Suggested Name already ends with that Tab's ID, and its Properties' **Tab**
box shows that Tab (another Tab picked there changes the Tab offered first; it stays on the Build Tab).
*Replaced (2026-11-16):* "The end of the Build chain is 💾 Save Build ... > Move to Tab (Save layout opens it too): the Tab picked for
it is offered first and it moves there. When the new things on the Build Tab were picked for different Tabs, each goes to its own Tab
and the rest go to the Tab picked in Save Build."
- **Its spot on the Build Tab is its spot on its Tab** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-12: "Moving an Item on the Build Tab will be the
  Position on the Tab it is sent to when the Build is totally complete"): the Build Tab is at least the size of that Tab, and a build
  that goes to the Tab picked for it keeps its X and Y. Sent to any other Tab, it goes to the middle of that Tab, as before (Rule 4.3).
- **The Watermark is the Tab itself** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "the water paper template on a Build Tab should not be an
  equipment profile but the tab with all the widgets. The water paper is to help preplace items (devices and widgets)"): a faint copy
  of the Tab the build goes to, drawn the way Brew Day shows it (its background picture, every Device, Widget, vessel, picture, text
  and pipe on it, with their Labels), shows behind everything on the Build Tab, with "Goes to: Tab name" at the top left, so new
  items can be placed where they belong. Nothing in it can be clicked. It shows **as soon as the Build Tab opens**: the Tab the picked
  item goes to, else the Tab every new item on the Build Tab goes to (the Build's **Tab** box on the Edit layout bar: the Default Tab,
  else the Tab it came from, Rule 4.6). A Build for a Template has none (a Template goes to no Tab). **🗺 Watermark On / Off** on the
  Edit layout bar (only on the Build Tab) turns it on or off; this browser remembers the choice.
  *Replaced (2026-11-19):* "On the Build a shadow background like a water mark diagram of a selected Tab the item is going to only
  after the Tab attribute is set" (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-12): a faint drawing of that Tab (a dashed outline and Label for each of
  its items, its pipes) that showed only once the picked item's Tab was set.
- **It glows until clicked** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-12: "when first Moved to a Regular Tab ... we need the Border to glow red with a
  slow pulse so easy to find. As soon as clicked, the Border reverts to normal."): each item Finish Build moves onto a regular Tab has a
  slowly pulsing red glow around it until it is clicked (in Edit layout or on Brew Day). It is never saved; reloading the page ends it.
- **📁 Templates in the Tab list** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-12: "Also the Option in the Tab DDLB to send to Templates"): the Tab list
  in the Properties of a vessel, equipment or Tab_Fitting on the Build Tab ends with **📁 Templates**; picked, Finish Build ... shows
  **As a Template** first. Only these can be Templates (Help 55, What can be a Template), so a Device's or Widget's Tab list
  does not offer it (asked 2026-11-12, Open question 15).
- **A Chiller Bundle Equipment Template** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "I see the Equipment Template so use a Normal Build Tab to create a Bundled Immersion Chiller and save to Equipment Templates"; markup "Method to change the Menu Bar when the Build is for a Vessel Template, And Equipment Profile, An Equiment Template", option A: "Change Valves to Valves/Equpment and just add the Equipment Templates and Build new to the DDLB LIst"; "I think A is best choice if possible"; built as a Rule 4.1 and Rule 14.4 exception): the one exception to "Only these can be Templates". On a
  normal Build Tab, **one immersion chiller** (2 IPs) with the pieces that go with it, its **hoses** (plain or Quick Disconnect, the
  supply and the waste hose), **Ice Water Cans** (Rule 19.8), a **Sump Pump** (by hand, Rule 5.15a, or a pump Device on a controlled
  wall outlet) and **IPs**, is saved with **Finish Build ... > As a Template** as one Equipment Template. Anything else on the Build
  Tab (a Widget, a picture, text, another chiller) is named and stops it. **Add to Tab** (or Valves/Equipment) puts all of it on the
  🔨 Build Tab together, with new names where a name is taken and the hoses still joined. **A Template never keeps a Port** (Rule 6.1):
  a pump Device in a Bundle gets the next free Port of the Build's Interface when it is put down (Rule 4.2), or says to give it one.
- **Valves/Equipment** (markup option A): the **Valves** shortcut on the Edit layout bar is now **Valves/Equipment**. Its list has the
  Valves, then the **Equipment Templates** (one goes on the 🔨 Build Tab) and **🔨 Build new Equipment Template**, which starts a
  Build for an Equipment Template.
- **The bar while a Build is for a Template or an Equipment Profile** (the markup): while the 🔨 Build Tab is for a Template (Build
  new Equipment Template, a Clone of a Template, or 📁 Templates picked in a Tab list) or for an Equipment Profile (the Interview's
  🔨 Build), what can't go in one is greyed out: Select Widget Type, Add Widget, Picture, Text, Override, Boolean, Value, Code Value,
  Time, DateTime, Tab settings, New tab, Hidden Tab, Processes and Update Schema Version, and "Add Widget" in the hint under the bar.
  Finish Build ... then shows **As a Template** first.
*Replaced (2026-11-12):* "Every new Widget or copy of a Template is made on the 🔨 Build Tab first, then sent to a Tab. A new Device goes
straight on the Tab picked in its Add Device box" (2026-11-04, Fritz's Add Pump drawing; before that 2026-10-23, PR #97 and PR #99).
**A new Tab from the Add Device box** (Fritz, 2026-11-04; the general Rule is 18.14): picking **➕ Add new Tab…** in its Tab list pauses the Add Device box
