- **Place** (a switch for each spot, in Vessel Widget Properties): on = it is on the vessel and works (an IP joins pipes, hoses and
  fittings; the Probe and Element show their pictures, and the Element glows while its heater is on). Off = it is not there: nothing
  shows on a Tab and nothing (a pipe, a Process) can use or change it. *Changed (Fritz, 2026-11-05, Rule 19.4):* a Not Placed spot
  is hidden even on the Build Tab and in Edit layout; **👁 Show All** in the Vessel's Properties shows it.
  *Replaced:* "only in Edit layout a faint mark shows where it would go."
- **The spots are set by the Template and locked:** a user can't move an IP, the Probe or the Element Port.
  *Changed (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "Rule Change OK but Only during the Initial Build"):* **only during the initial build** in the
  Vessel Device Builder (Rule 19.5), **Pick** lets the user double-click the spot of a Drain, Tangential Inlet, Sparge Arm / Steam
  Slayer, Thermowell / Probe or Heating Element on the blank vessel. Near a preset IP it takes that IP; anywhere else it makes a
  **User IP** on that one vessel (Picked Drain ...). After the initial build no IP can be added or moved; once built and saved it is
  locked like every other IP.
- **IPs on a vessel** (Fritz, 2026-11-05): an IP is a TC, NPT or BSP outlet or inlet; the type does not matter, it is a place to
  connect another Device or Widget with its own IP (a Pipe, Hose, Fitting or anything with an IP).
- **The plan** (Fritz, 2026-11-05): more kettle Templates are built from the Main one with their Place sliders set to match real
  kettles, so a user picks the one closest to theirs; a user can change the Place sliders on their copy and add Devices and Widgets of
  their own, and Bundle them into a User Bundled Template (Rule 5.7).
- A Placed Probe or Element links a Device the Schema already has. *Waiting on Fritz's pick (Rule 5.7: "A Skynet Vessel Widget has
  no Devices, only built-in IPs"):* a Placed Probe making its own Device (Interface, Port, Probe Type), and the Element likewise.
- The Three Vessel sample's HLT, Mash tun and Boil kettle are **Vessel Devices** built from the Main Template (Fritz, 2026-11-07:
  "On the 3 Vessel sample, change all the vessels to" "Vessels Devices"): Center Bottom Outlet Placed on all three; a Thermowell
  with its probe built into the Left Element IP of each; the Heating Element built into the Right Element IP of the HLT and Boil
  kettle; the Left Sparge IP (the pipe in at the top) on the Mash tun and Boil kettle. Their probes and heaters keep their names
  and Ports, and a heater that is a heat controller (Hysteresis, PID ...) stays one, as on the RIMS tube.

5.32 **Sight Glasses are TC Pipe Fittings with a Length** (Fritz, 2026-11-05: "Create 2 Sight Glass Pipe Fitting, One Caged and one
not. Length attribute to stretch length"; thread "Add caged and plain sight glass fittings", Help 139).
- Two Skynet TC Pipe Fittings Widgets (Rule 5.25): **Sight_Glass** (plain glass) and **Sight_Glass_Caged** (a stainless guard round
  the glass), TC 1.5, an IP on each ferrule face (left and right), flow either way. Added from Elbows, Tees … and Add Widget > TC
  Pipe Fittings; names SightGlass_n and SightGlassCaged_n.
- **Length** (inches, ferrule face to ferrule face, 2 to 48, quarter inches; 6 when placed) stretches it along its pipe. Only the
  glass (and the cage) gets longer: the picture is drawn for its Length, so the ferrules and end collars keep their shape and size.
  Autosize to pipe makes it as thick as its pipe; with Autosize off, a typed Width sets the Length.
- Its **Label** starts filled in as **site_glass_n** (the next number) and is never blank (Rule 18.15; Fritz, 2026-11-05: "site_glass_1").
- Dropped on a straight pipe in Edit layout it cuts the pipe, as a tee's run does (Rule 5.25).

5.33 **The Tap Water Valve is a Manual Valve Widget with one IP** (Fritz, 2026-11-06: "Create Manual Valve Widget: a Tap Water
Valve that is a standard Manual House Hold Hose Bib with pix of one like you could buy a home dept"; his picture marks the IP at the
hose outlet; thread "Add hose bib Manual Valve Widget", Help 141).
- A **Manual Valve Widget** (Rule 5.15: only a click on its Tab opens or closes it; a Process asks for it by hand and waits) with
  the Skynet picture **Images/Skynet/Valves/Tap_Water_Valve_Hose_Bib.svg**: a brass household hose bib with a green cross handle,
  the wall side on the right, the spout turned down to a hose thread.
- **One IP only**, the center of the hose thread's outer face (the water comes in from the wall, which has no IP). This is not a
  ball valve, so Rule 5.24's two IPs do not apply; with one IP it does not cut a pipe it is dropped on (Rule 5.26).
- **Open, it is a tap water source**: flow pushes out of its hose outlet with no pump, tap water Blue (Rule 5.21). Closed, it
  blocks the hose on it.
- Added from Select Device Type > Valves and Select Widget Type > Semi_Widgets_Devices (**Tap Water Valve**), or by picking its
  Picture on any Manual Valve. Name ManualValve_n; its **Label** starts filled in as **tap_water_n** (Rule 18.15).
- Autosize to pipe as every Manual Valve (Rule 5.29 does not cover Manual Valves).
  *Changed (Rule 18.45, 2026-11-18):* it is a **Hose Bib**, sized by hand like a Pump, with its own short Hose or Pipe to its one IP.
  *Changed (Rule 18.49, 2026-11-18):* its one IP may be on any of the **8 spots** of its box, the wall side too, and it has an End
  Fitting (Outlet IP Fitting, MGH3/4 to start).
  *Changed (Rule 18.52, 2026-11-19):* it also has an **Inlet IP** on its wall side's thread; a pipe on it is the house water pipe,
  and a closed valve on that side stops its water.

5.34 **A Process connects a Quick Disconnect hose, and a person confirms it is there** (Fritz, 2026-11-06: "A process command to put a
QD Hose in a Vessel with a automatic need for confirmation that the hose is placed (similar to a Manual Valve) or a QD IP. Maybe
myQD_Hose.connect = qd_Ip_name or myQD_Hose.connect = vessel_Device_Name" ... "or vessel_Widget_Name" ... "Same as manually dragging
it to top Third of a vessel" ... "The connection confirmation needs to be for a connect process command or the manual dragging the
end"; thread "Add Process command to connect QD hose", Help 142).
- **The line:** `Hose_1.connect = QD_1` (a Quick Disconnect, or a plain IP), `Hose_1.connect = Mash_Tun` (a Vessel Widget or a Vessel
  Device), `Hose_1.connect = none` (taken off, loose). The hose is named by its Name (or its Label when only one item has it), and
  the place by its Name, with no quotes; the place must be on the hose's Tab. Only a Quick Disconnect hose (Rule 5.28) has .connect,
  and it is only set, with `=`.
- **A Vessel is its top third**, the same as dragging the end there by hand (Rule 5.28): the hose hangs over the rim and inside it.
- **The Process moves the drawing at once, then waits** (like a Manual valve, Rule 5.13): a pop-up says where to put the hose, the
  hose blinks, and the Process goes on when an operator or admin presses **Done**. A hose already there asks nothing. Override does
  not pass it.
- **Dragging the end by hand asks nothing** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "Right Click and hold the Yellow circle is all it should take to move it.  It unhooks without comfirmation and is locked or hanging open when Right Moude buuton release"; "If there is flow a warning,  No flow, no warning"): when the button is let go, the end stays where it is, on the IP, Quick
  Disconnect or vessel top under it, or hanging loose. (Until 2026-11-16 it asked "Is the real hose there now?".) Only a Process
  .connect line waits for Done. Locked onto an IP, Quick Disconnect or vessel top, the yellow ring flashes red and yellow for 2
  seconds; left in the air, it stays yellow.
- Predictive text offers .connect after a QD hose's name and, after `=`, the Quick Disconnects, Vessels and IPs on its Tab, then
  none; Check (Help 81) finds a wrong hose, a place not on its Tab, a vessel with no top, and `+=` or reading .connect.

5.35 **Valve Tees and Supply Manifolds: Long Tees with a valve built into each branch** (Fritz, 2026-11-06: "Long Tee with integrated
Motorized Valve and one with Long Tee with Manual Valve (and method to change valve type like a regular valve), a Double Supply
Manifold (2 long Tees with 2 Integrated Valves with IPs only at Valve ends and 2 one on each open end of the joined Tees. Both Manual
and Motorized Versions with ability to swap manual to motorized individually by valve. And a Triple Supply Manifold the same. Add to
Pipe Fitting"; "These have their own unique attributes ... the standard exceptions would apply if it fits"; thread "Add valve Tees and
supply manifolds", Help 146).
- **It breaks apart once placed** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-25: "And once this template is placed on a Tab, it becomes 3 devices and
  3 widgets"; "Any thing like the three valve supply tees needs to be individual Devices and widgets after placed because they need to
  be manipulated individually"). The Valve Tee and the Supply Manifolds are only a way to place them: as soon as one is placed (its Add
  box, the Setup interviews, a Template put on the 🔨 Build Tab), each tee becomes a TC Pipe Fittings **Long Tee**, joined end to end
  to the next IP to IP (Rule 5.26), and each valve its own valve joined IP to IP on its tee's branch: a **Motorized** one a **Skynet
  Motorized Ball Valve** Device (Vertical Right, or Horizontal when turned 90; same Name, Label, Interface and Port), a **Manual** one a
  **Manual Valve Widget** (Manual Ball Valve, side view, Rule 5.24). Pipes that were on its IPs go on the part now on that spot. One
  placed before this breaks apart the next time Edit layout opens (one note), kept with the next Save layout. The Add box has no
  Name (each part gets its own). What follows is how it is set up before it breaks apart.
- Three Skynet TC Pipe Fittings with valves built in: the **Valve Tee** (one Long Tee, Template Valve_Tee), the **Double Supply
  Manifold** (2 Long Tees joined end to end, Supply_Manifold_2) and the **Triple Supply Manifold** (3, Supply_Manifold_3). TC 1.5,
  Fritz's Long Tee drawing (Rule 5.25) with a valve on each branch, drawn to the Valve Standard (Rule 5.29).
- **IPs only on the two open ends of the joined tees and on the far end of each valve** (Rule 5.20): the Valve Tee has 3, the Double 4,
  the Triple 5. Flow goes any way through the tees; **a closed valve shuts its IP**.
- **Each valve is a valve Device built into the fitting** (a Skynet_Integrated_Device, Rule 5.2, like the RIMS tube's parts): it can't be
  taken out or deleted by itself; deleting the fitting deletes its valves. Rule 5.14 already says a valve in a fitting is a Device.
- **Manual or Motorized, each valve on its own**, the same way as a regular valve's **Valve type** (Rule 5.13): in the fitting's
  Properties each valve is **Manual** (turned by hand, no Port: a Process shows a pop-up and waits for Done) or **Motorized** (switched by
  its Port; one Interface for all the Motorized valves of the fitting, then each valve's Port; two valves can't share a Port). The
  picture follows (Manual ball valve or Motorized ball valve) and stays on the same spot.
- **A click on a valve on its Tab opens or closes it** (operators and admins). Open: the bolt (Motorized) or the green ring (Manual).
  Processes use the valve's own name (`<name>.state = true`); Motorized valves are on the Close all / Open all valve lists (Rule 6.15).
- **Added from** Edit layout bar > **Elbows, Tees …** > Valve Tees and Supply Manifolds, or Select Device Type > **Valves**: six rows,
  each fitting with all its valves Manual or all Motorized to start. Its **Add box and Properties are the Pump's drill-down**
  (Rule 18.29). It starts on the 🔨 Build Tab with its valves, and Finish Build ... moves it to the Tab picked in the Add box (Rule 4.1); its Properties open.
- **Names and Labels:** the fitting is ValveTee_n, Manifold2_n or Manifold3_n; its **Label** starts as **valve_tee_n**, **manifold_2_n**
  or **manifold_3_n** and is never blank (Rule 18.15). Each valve's Label is `<fitting Label> V1`, `V2` ...; its Name is the suggested
  name (Rule 3.1), e.g. `MB_22_DO@Valve_E_manifold_2_1_V1_BR` or, Manual, `M_L_Vlv_manifold_2_1_V2_BR`.
- **Orientation: three turns and Flip** (Fritz, 2026-11-06: "Supply Manifold No Flips just Rotate 3 Choices: Horizontal, Left
  Vertical 90, Right Vertical 90"; Fritz, 2026-11-07: "We need supply Manifolds to Flip Vertically Horizontally. Valves on Top or
  Valves on Bottom"): **Horizontal** (the valves hang down), **Left Vertical 90** (turned a quarter clockwise, the valves point left)
  and **Right Vertical 90** (a quarter the other way, the valves point right), with **Flip** on the same line: **No flip**, **Flip
  Vertical** (the valves on the other side of the tees: on top when Horizontal), **Flip Horizontal** (Valve 1 at the other end) or
  **Flip both**. The Valve Tee is the same. The Edit layout bar's turn buttons step through the three turns (no 45, an exception to
  Rule 5.5) and its Flip H and Flip V buttons flip it as it looks on the Tab. The valves and the IPs follow.
  No Autosize to pipe (it is drawn at the Valve Standard size) and no Clone. Dropped on a straight pipe in Edit layout, its run goes
  along the pipe (turned to one of the three) and the pipe is cut, as a tee's (Rule 5.25).
- **The valve ends match the tee ends** (Fritz, 2026-11-06: "The valve ends need to match the Tee ends in the graphic"): each valve is
  drawn on the tee's own grid, the same pipe as the tee's branch, a TC 1.5 ferrule at the top clamped to the branch ferrule, and the
  same ferrule at the bottom, whose face is the valve's IP. Drawn by the panel, so no picture was added to the Image Library.
- **Valve numbers** (Fritz, 2026-11-06: "When Building or editing a Manifold Supply the Valves need to be number corresponding to the
  Valve 1 in the dialog"): in Edit layout and on the Graphic of its Add box and Properties each valve shows its number (1, 2, 3), the
  same as **Valve 1**, **Valve 2**, **Valve 3** in the dialog and **V1**, **V2**, **V3** in its valves' Labels. Not shown in run mode.
  **Taken away** (2026-11-24, OakBarn Brewery: "And get rid of the yellow circle numbers"): no number is drawn on the valves, on the
  Tab or on the Graphic; Valve 1, 2, 3 count from the left as the fitting is drawn level.
- **Size: it takes the size of its pipes** (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "any Pipe Fitting, even if a device should size to the majority of the
  pipes or hoses"; Rule 5.36). This replaces "No Autosize to pipe (it is drawn at the Valve Standard size)" above: a Valve Tee or
  Supply Manifold is sized like a tee, its tees as thick as most of the pipes and hoses on its IPs; its valves grow with it. With no
  pipe on it, it keeps its size. It still has no Clone.
- *Standard exceptions used* (Fritz: "the standard exceptions would apply if it fits"): unlike the Vessel Device it is **not locked**
  once saved, so a valve can always be swapped Manual / Motorized. A Motorized valve's Port (and the fitting's Interface) is greyed
  out once saved (Rule 18.13); to wire it again, make it Manual, Save, then Motorized again and pick the Port.
  *Replaced (2026-11-06):* its valves' Interface and Ports were set in the fitting's Properties, not in a Pump-style Add box; Flip
  Horizontal, Flip Vertical and Rotate in 45 degree steps.
  *Replaced (2026-11-07):* "Orientation: no Flip, only three turns ... Flip says it has none".

5.36 **Every pipe fitting sizes to its pipes when saving** (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "Have any pipe fitting etc size to the pipe when
saving"; then "any Pipe Fitting, even if a device should size to the majority of the pipes or hoses"; thread "Size fittings to their
pipe on Save", Help 87).
- **The majority wins:** a fitting takes the size that **most of the pipes and hoses joined to it** have. On a **tie** (for example one
  1" and one 1/2", as on a Reducer, or two of each on a cross) it takes the **bigger** size. With no pipe or hose on it, it keeps its size.
- On **Save layout** every Tab is checked, and each time a Tab is drawn in Edit layout (so after 💾 Save in any Properties) that Tab
  is. Sized this way, about their bend (Rule 5.25):
  - every pipe fitting (Rule 5.14: elbows, tees, crosses, U, reducers, check valves, Sight Glasses, IP fittings, Straight Manual Valves; a Hose Bib is sized by hand, Rule 18.45):
    **always**, there is no switch (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "Always Resize pipes (no user Option)");
  - **Valve Tees and Supply Manifolds** (Rule 5.35; they have no Autosize switch, so they always follow);
  - **tees with a Temperature Probe** (Rule 5.30; no switch either, a Device dialog, Rule 18.10);
  - **valves and inline Devices** (Motorized and other valve Devices, Proportional Valves, flow meters and flow switches): each is drawn
    as it would be on a Tab whose 1/2" pipe is as thick as most of its pipes. With no pipe on it, the Tab's pipe size (Rule 5.11).
  - an **End Cap**, which gets **Autosize to pipe** (Rule 5.14 lists it as a pipe fitting): on an opening of a TC Pipe Fitting it
    takes the size of that fitting's ferrule (its box 1.5 x the fitting's pipe). On a Reducer (two sizes), a Valve Tee or Supply
    Manifold, or a vessel opening it keeps its size.
- **Pumps follow too** (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "Yes have Devices, Pipe Fittings, to default to a size ... I Think setting a Default Pipe
  size and have all the devices with Ips conform to that size is a better method"): a pump is drawn to the Pump Standard (Rule 5.27)
  for the size most of its pipes have, as a valve is. A Thermowell sits on a vessel and keeps its size.
- **The Default pipe size** (☰ Menu > Default settings, Rule 2.42): **anything with IPs that has no pipe on it** (a Device, pump,
  valve, pipe fitting, Valve Tee, probe tee ...) **takes the Default pipe size** instead of keeping its size, so a new pump or
  fitting already matches the brewery's pipes. A fitting sitting on a vessel opening with no pipe keeps its size. New pipes and hoses
  start at the Default pipe and hose size.
  *Replaced (2026-11-07):* "Pumps are not pipe fittings: they keep the Pump Standard size with the Tab's pipe size (Rules 5.11,
  5.27)", and "With no pipe or hose on it, it keeps its size".
- **A pipe size cascades** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16, Default Pipe Size Hover Help: "You can change a pipe size individually and the
  pipe size will cascade to auto size"; Panel Updates entry 12, built 2026-11-19): when a pipe's size is changed in its Properties and
  saved, every pipe joined to it takes the same size: pipes on the same IP, and through an elbow, tee, cross, U, coupling, check valve,
  Sight Glass or **valve** (Motorized, Proportional, Straight Manual Valve; OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "Should the size carry on
  through valves, like a manifold that stays one size? Yes") to the pipes on its other side, all the way down the line. It **stops** at
  a Reducer, a pump, a probe tee or other inline Device, a Hose Bib, a Valve Tee or Supply Manifold, a vessel, a hose (hoses never auto
  size) and a 🔒 locked pipe (it keeps its size). The fittings then size to their pipes as above. Only the size changes; the IP Types stay. A
  short note says how many pipes changed. Changing it back cascades back the same way. *Was (2026-11-16):* "Nothing cascades along
  the line yet".

5.37 **Grab pop-up: move it alone (🔓 Unlock its IPs), Swap places, and ↩ Put back** (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "I tried to replace the
Pump in the 3 vessel with a Blichmann Pump I added and it was not easy and never succeeded as the pipes followed the old pump. When we
grab a Device or Widget, maybe a Pop up to Unlock IPs so it moves independently of its pipes"; "That would apply to any Device, Pipe,
Fitting or Widget, but the Option to Unlock as the user may not want to, and maybe a way to restore back to any pipe movements";
"Not only the Pipes but locked fitting as well"; thread "Swap a pump without dragging its pipes", Help 153).
- **The pop-up:** in Edit layout, the first time a Device, Widget, Fitting (or Vessel) with pipes joined to it is dragged, it stays
  put and a pop-up asks: **🔓 Unlock its IPs** (each pipe end on it lets go where it is and is left a plain open end, its red dot, with no coupling (2026-11-24, OakBarn Brewery:
  "Unlock an end or Unlock IPs get rid of couplings"), so it then moves alone
  and the pipes and fittings stay), **Move it with its pipes** (Rule 5.19 as before), **🔁 Swap places with...** or **Cancel**.
  Unlocking is never done unless the user picks it. **Don't ask again** lasts until Edit layout is left. A Pipe joined to other
  things offers **🔓 Unlock its ends** (it moves alone) or Cancel. A locked item stays locked (Rule 2.12): no pop-up.
- **Shift + drag: move it with its pipes, no pop-up** (2026-11-24, OakBarn Brewery: "Left Mouse Key + a Key to move something with
  all connected pipes"; "If the entire manifold was connected, elongate the pipes connected to the vessels"; "add pipes at the end of
  a move if it did not just go down"): Shift held as the left button is pressed on an item, then a drag, moves it **and everything
  joined to it through its pipes** (fittings, valves, pumps and the pipes between them) together, with no pop-up. A pipe that runs to
  a vessel (or to something locked) keeps its end on the vessel and gets longer or shorter; moved across its line, a straight one gets
  a jog in its middle (two bends), so it still runs level and upright and stays joined; a note then names those pipes, warns that more
  pipes or fittings (elbows) may be needed there, and its **⟲ Revert** button puts the move back (the same as ↩ Put back; OakBarn
  Brewery: "the clean up would have to Warn that additional pipes or fittings may be needed ... something like Revert rather than
  Undo, but same as Undo"). ↩ Put back (Ctrl+Z) undoes the move. Shift +
  left click is free on Windows, Mac, Linux and the Pi (Rule 2.73).
- **🔓 Unlock its IPs in Properties** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-21: "Need unlock IPs on property dialog for things that have IPs";
  "The hose got connected to a Tee IP and I could not unlock"): an IP has no dialog of its own (Rule 2.9), so the title line of the
  Properties of anything with IPs (Device, Widget, Manual Valve, Hose Bib, fitting, vessel, a bundled vessel too) has **🔓 Unlock its
  IPs**, and a Pipe or Hose has **🔓 Unlock its ends**. It does what the pop-up's button does, at once: each pipe or hose end on it
  lets go where it is (an open end); ↩ Put back (Ctrl+Z) joins them again. It is greyed out when nothing is joined, when the item is
  🔒 locked (Rule 2.12: unlock it first) or when its Tab's equipment is locked (lock_Equipment). (Help 153)
  *Added (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-23: "The Unlock IPs on the dialog is good but add Move with Pipes option"):* beside it,
  **↔ Move with pipes** (not on a Pipe or Hose) is the pop-up's other choice: the next drag moves the item with its pipes (Rule 5.19)
  and does not ask. Greyed out for the same reasons, and when a 🔒 locked pipe or fitting would have to move with it.
- **🔍 Zoom box** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-23: "a keyboard Short cut to have an zoomed version of the Join where the mouse is for
  200 pixel square where Join area is zoomed inside the Dialog"; he picked A, the Z key, as Ctrl + Click already opens Properties,
  Rule 2.9): in Edit layout, **Z** (not Alt + Z, Rule 2.73) (not in a text box or dialog) opens a box in a top corner of the Tab area that shows the 200
  screen pixels around the mouse **3 times bigger** (on a smaller Tab area the box shrinks to fit). *Changed 2026-11-24* (OakBarn Brewery:
  "the zoom box needs to be bigger. Could be any manifold part. Top, bottom, right and left + 50 px and fill the work area"): the box
  **fills the work area** and zooms **2.5x** ("Can you also do zoom at 2.5"; was 3x). It is centered on the **whole manifold** under
  the mouse (the pipes, fittings, valves and pumps joined to the pipe, IP or fitting pointed at, not through a vessel, with **50 Tab
  pixels** all round) when that fits at 2.5x; otherwise on the mouse, and the view pans from the box's edges. A click, double-click or held press on an empty
  spot in the box never opens Tab settings ("inside the zoom Box, Click to open Tab Properties no longer works but only in the Zoom
  Box"); on the Tab itself it still does. *Changed (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-23: "be able to move within the dialog.
  Dialog moves now. It needs to stay fixed and move the joins together inside the Dialog"; "z does not work like the esc. Just
  change the text that you use the esc button to close and or have a close button upper right corner"):* the box **stays where it
  opened** (on the side away from the spot it shows) and keeps showing that same spot. **Work right in it:** every press, drag,
  click and double-click in the box goes to the Tab at the same spot, 3 times finer, so a pipe end or an item is dragged onto an IP
  inside the box (the grab pop-up, snapping and joins work as on the Tab). **Esc** or its red **✕** (upper right) closes it, and
  so does leaving Edit layout; its text says so. *Changed (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-23: "Try zoom x 2"; "I cannot grab the pipe
  inside the dialog after I release it"):* 3 times ("let's try 4 x", then 2026-11-24 "Back to 3 x"; was 3, then 2, then 4); a pipe can be grabbed and moved in the box again and again.
  *Added (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-24: "I want to be able to move the Inside of the scroll pattern to a different part of the whole
  manifold so when I get near an edge with the left mouse click held, it scrolls"):* with a mouse button held within 28 pixels of
  an edge of the box, the view moves that way (8 box pixels a frame, up to the edge of the Tab), and what is being dragged goes along.
  *Added (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-23: "ONLY INSIDE the Z Dialog, a double click on a red IP starts the Trace to another Ip. Trace
  would be red line. The a button to autoconfigure"; he picked "move the first onto the second": "has to trace back so no breaks
  in Ips"):* **only in the Zoom box**, a double-click on an IP starts a red **trace** and a click on another IP ends it (a
  double-click on an IP there no longer opens Properties). The red dot of an open pipe end with no coupling counts as an IP for
  the trace, at either end; it gets its coupling when the trace takes it (2026-11-24, OakBarn Brewery: "going from Valve Red IP
  to Pump Red IP would not lock trace. Going from Pump Red IP to Valve IP worked fine"). Only a red (open) IP starts or ends a trace ("Tracing should only be on red dots"): a
  double-click on or next to a green (joined) one goes on to the Tab as any double-click does, so the pipe there can be picked
  (2026-11-24, OakBarn Brewery: "I was trying to grab the smaller pipe to delete and it started tracing"). **🔧 Auto configure** moves the first IP onto the second and joins them,
  and traces the move back through what is joined behind it so no join breaks (Fritz: "the tee below the elbow ... would have to
  move right shortening the right pipe and lengthen the left pipe on the tee. The pipe to the elbow would have to shorten"): a
  straight pipe takes the part of the move along its own line by getting longer or shorter and passes on only the part across it
  to what is on its other end (fitting, valve, pump, an IP sitting right on another), and so on back; a pipe with a bend in it takes
  the whole move at its first bend (2026-11-24); two open ends (couplings) joined at a corner get the fitting the corner needs, an
  elbow (a tee, a cross ...) (2026-11-24, OakBarn Brewery: "On autoconfigure should have put in an elbow"); a hose just bends. When that
  **A red dot can be deleted** (2026-11-24, OakBarn Brewery: "trying to get the properties up so I can delete these coupling"): press
  it, then the Delete key, or two quick presses outside the Zoom box for its Properties and 🗑 Delete. *Changed (2026-11-24, OakBarn
  Brewery: "Used Delete and the Delete key. Pop-up says deleted but it is still there"):* the pipe (or hose) with that open end goes with
  the dot, since a plain end shows the same red dot; ↩ Put back (Ctrl+Z) brings it back. *Was:* the dot goes, its pipe stays, the end
  left plain.
  **Auto configure joins IP to IP** (2026-11-24, OakBarn Brewery: "why is the red dot not green on the elbow and valve?"): two IPs of
  things (not open pipe ends) brought onto one spot are joined by a pipe of no length (Rule 5.26), so both turn green.
  **Turn buttons in the Zoom box** (2026-11-24, OakBarn Brewery: "No way to orient"): while a fitting that can turn is picked, the
  Zoom box's title has ⟲ 90, ⟳ 90, ⇆ Flip H and ⇅ Flip V (Rule 5.5, a quarter turn at a time), and the box shows every change at once.
  **A deleted fitting leaves plain ends** (2026-11-24, OakBarn Brewery: "they are not needed with a new Join"): a pipe end whose
  elbow, tee or Device is deleted gets no coupling (no red ring); leftover red dots become plain ends when Edit layout opens.
  **A plain end shows the small red IP dot and joins** (2026-11-24, OakBarn Brewery: "Pipe end needs the red dot, cannot join a valve to
  a pipe"): in Edit layout a plain end has the same small red dot as an open IP (Rule 5.20; it is the end's drag handle). A valve, pump,
  fitting or other item with no pipes on it, let go with one of its IPs within 25 px of a red dot (a plain end or an open end's coupling),
  slides the last few pixels so that IP sits on the end, and the end joins it (the dot turns green); it is then not put into a pipe it
  lies over. ↩ Put back (Ctrl+Z) undoes it.
  would break a join (it reaches the second IP, a vessel or something locked, a pipe gets too short, or two ways back disagree),
  the second IP is tried onto the first. If neither works, nothing moves and one toast says it can't be done automatically without
  breaking a join or adding a pipe, hose or fitting, so do it by hand (delete or add pipes, fittings or joins). Nothing is ever
  added or deleted by it. Two IPs already joined by a pipe (a short one between them too) are left as they are, with a toast
  that says so: every join is a pipe, and taking it away would break the join (2026-11-24). **Cancel trace** or Esc takes the trace away; ↩ Put back (Ctrl+Z) undoes it. (Help 153)
- **Locked pipes and fittings:** an item that could not move because a locked pipe or fitting would move with it (the 🔒 toast)
  gets the pop-up instead, with Unlock its IPs only: it moves alone and the locked things stay where they are.
- **🔁 Swap places with...** (pumps, valves, Proportional Valves and Manual Valves): the other one of the same kind (any Tab, the
  🔨 Build Tab too) takes this one's X, Y, Width, Height, Tab and flips (the pump's Orientation), and every pipe end on this one's
  inlet or outlet goes on the other's inlet or outlet; this one goes where the other was. Nothing else on either one changes.
- **Dropped where something let go:** an open pipe end made by Unlock remembers where its IP was and which end (inlet, outlet ...).
  An item dropped with the same end within 14 pixels of that spot joins it again at once (Rule 5.27 keeps every pump's IPs in the
  same spots), and any other open end within 14 pixels of one of its IPs joins as on Save layout (Rule 5.19).
- **A Pump with no pipes always has free IPs** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "A Pump with No attached Pipes alwaus have free IPs";
  "If that does not work, assign inlet outlet IPs one of the 8 each"; thread "Let a new pump join existing pipes"): a Device or
  Manual Valve with no pipes on it, dropped with one of its IPs within 30 pixels of a let-go open end, slides that last bit so the IP
  is on it. A pump's Inlet and Outlet then each go on whichever of its 8 IPs (Rule 5.27) is where the old one's Inlet and Outlet
  were, so a new pump takes a Left (flipped) pump's pipes too; a Hose Bib's one IP the same (Rule 18.48). Then they join. No pop-up.
- **↩ Put back** on the Edit layout bar, and **Ctrl+Z** (not in a text box): undoes the last move, resize, unlock, swap or **delete**
  (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-23: "Could a simple CTRL + Z restore a Delete ?": an item deleted from its Properties, with no "Delete
  this item?" box), up to 30 steps, back to how pipes, fittings and items were. It starts fresh each time Edit layout opens. Other
  Properties changes are not in it;
  Exit without saving still undoes everything since the last Save layout.
  The "… deleted. ↩ Put back (Ctrl+Z) brings it back." note stays 2 seconds, then goes (Rule 2.74; 2026-11-24, OakBarn Brewery: "Nanny state
  up too long. Needs to be quick, maybe 3 seconds and then gone").
- **🗑 Delete Pipe / Delete Hose** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "Add Delete Button to Hose and Pipe Disconnect Dialog"): the
  pop-up of a pipe or hose has a red Delete button beside 🔓 Unlock its ends; ↩ Put back (Ctrl+Z) brings it back. Its top is frozen
  and it has no bottom row (Rule 2.51).
- **Shorten a let-go pipe** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "After a Pipe is disconnected to Move, able to Shorten"): a pipe end
  that 🔓 Unlock its ends let go (an open coupling) can be dragged along the pipe's own line to make it shorter or longer (never off
  its line, at least 10 pixels); its coupling goes with it.
- **Change a saved pipe's length, redraw a saved hose** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "Ability to change the Length of a Pipe once
  it has been saved. In the Build Mode, pipe Length need to be unlocked so the size can change after IPs Unlocked. Hose also need to
  be Redrawn after its IPs are unlocked"; Help 153): once an end of a pipe or hose is let go (🔓 Unlock its ends, or 🔓 Unlock its IPs
  on what it was joined to), that end has a round handle and can be dragged, saved or not: a **pipe** end along the pipe's own line
  (shorter or longer, as above), a **hose** end **anywhere** (the hose bends to follow; the round handles in its middle change its
  bends). The let-go end can be grabbed even where it sits on a pump, valve, vessel or fitting IP: it comes first. Dropped within 14
  pixels of an IP, that end joins it at once (only that end; the other stays as it is); anywhere else it stays open. Skynet does
  this in the Background and needs no user input. Nothing else changes: an end still joined, a 🔒 locked pipe or hose, and an end
  whose IP is 🔒 locked (No Unlock too, Rule 2.12) do not move. ↩ Put back (Ctrl+Z) undoes each drag; Save layout keeps it.
  *Added (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-23: "Tried to grab this and it ask me to unlock? It is not connected"):* an end with a **red ring**
  (on no IP, because what it was joined to is gone) is a let-go end too: it can be grabbed (no pop-up), it gets its coupling when
  grabbed, and dropped on an IP it joins it. Fittings still win (Rule 5.20).
  **Both programs:** the BruControl Import's Build page is the Panel's Edit layout, so it works the same there.
- **Deleting a pipe or hose takes its own IPs with it** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "I deleted a Pipe but the IPs where still on
  the Build"; "Check same issue for Hose"), from this pop-up or from its Properties: a coupling or IP point on one of its ends goes
  too when nothing else is on it (no other pipe, Quick Disconnect or End Cap, and not an opening on a vessel).
- **BruControl Import:** checked, not changed; it does not move things on a Tab. Schemas it makes get this in the Panel.

5.39 **Hand-set appliance vessels: the DigiBoil and the 65 L Brewzilla** (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "a DigiBoil Widget Vessel. It has its
own Heating but no control from Skynet at all"; "The 65 L Brewzilla Widget has 4 switches one Intergrated Bottom Drain Pump, 3
Heater"; thread "Add DigiBoil manual vessel widget", Help 158).
- Two Skynet Vessel Templates: **Kettle_DigiBoil** and **Kettle_Brewzilla_65L**. Each heats itself (and the Brewzilla pumps
  itself); Skynet does not switch any of it. Their parts are built in and never un-bundled (Integrated items):
  - **DigiBoil:** 2 manual switches, **Power** and **Heater**; one Manual valve in its outlet, the small silver **Spigot with BSP
    threads**; one manual **Temperature Set Point and Display Screen**.
  - **65 L Brewzilla:** 4 manual switches, the bottom drain **Pump**, **Heater 1**, **Heater 2**, **Heater 3**; one Manual valve in
    its outlet (the **BSP Spigot**) and one on the **out side of its pump manifold** (an IP of its own, Pump out); one manual
    **Temperature Set Point and Display Screen** that has an **On/Off button** and a **Run** hot spot.
- The switches and screen are its **Controls**, a Manual vessel Widget beside it (Name_Controls, for example DigiBoil_Controls).
  The valves are Manual valve Devices (Valve type Manual, no Port; DigiBoil_Spigot, Brewzilla_Pump_Out). A closed valve shuts its IP.
- **A Process sets them, a person does it:** `DigiBoil_Controls.setpoint = 152`, `.power`, `.heat`, `.heat2`, `.heat3`, `.pump`
  (`.power` is the Brewzilla screen's On/Off button) and `.run` (the Brewzilla Run spot) show what was asked on its Controls,
  pop up what to do by hand, and the Process waits for ✔ Done (like `ask`, Rule 16.5). Already set that way: no pop-up.
- **°C pop-up:** both screens go back to °C every time they are turned off. When the panel works in °F (its Controls' units), the
  set point pop-up gives the °C too: "Set the DigiBoil temperature set point to 152 °F (that is 66.7 °C)". In °C only the °C shows.
- **`open_valve Name` / `close_valve Name`**: a Process command for **any one valve**. A Manual one (a Manual valve, a Manual
  Valve Widget, a built-in Spigot or Pump out valve, a Supply Manifold's Manual valve) pops up "OPEN ... by hand" and waits, as
  in Rule 5.13; a motorized one is switched at once. `Valve.state = true` still works as before.
- A click on its Controls in run mode records what you set by hand (a switch, a valve, a new set point, what its screen reads).
- **Schema Templates (Rule 16.6):** a new heat choice, **Its own, set by hand**: Skynet makes no probe or heater for that vessel and it
  does no Brew Process heating job. The OakBarn Template uses the DigiBoil and the 65 L Brewzilla this way. The older
  Kettle_DigiBoil_Electric and Kettle_Brewzilla_Electric Templates stay for brewers who switch theirs from Skynet.
- Older Manual vessel Widgets (no appliance) work as before: no pop-up.
- **BruControl Import:** checked, not changed. BruControl has no DigiBoil or Brewzilla items; its Manual valves import as before.

5.40 **IP Type: the connector on each end of a pipe or hose** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "Need 2 additional Defaults with
associated IPs Pipe Connector and Hose Connector"; "4 Choices Triclamp, NPT, BSP, or QuickDisconnet"; "Pipe and Hose
Attributes as to IP Type that are set by the selected Defaults"; "On Both End").
- Every pipe and hose has an **IP Type at start** and an **IP Type at end**. Both are in its Properties, under its size.
- **Sized IP Types** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "IPs Types will need to be expanded to have size  TC1.5  TC3/4   TC2  ....   NPT
  to MPT1  MPT1/2  MPT 2"; "FPT1.   A list of the sizes and type in Defualts with a TickBox to show in the List.  Have sizes from
  1/8 to 6 " ( and if there are odd Metrics Those too."; "Do A with all Unclicked in the Default"): an IP Type is a type and a
  size in one code, real sizes only (public/iptype.js): **Tri-Clamp** TC1/2, TC3/4, TC1.5, TC2, TC2.5, TC3, TC4, TC6 (sized by
  the clamp); **FPT** (female) and **MPT** (male) pipe thread 1/8" to 6"; **BSP** 1/8" to 6"; metric **DN6** to **DN150**;
  stainless **Quick Disconnect** **FMSSQD** (female) and **MSSQD** (male) 1/2" to 3" ("Hose FMSSQD1/2 wher they are on a Pipe
  or Pump and a MSSQD1/2 on the other end").
- **Camlock** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "add camlocks and 1/2 to the Ends"; "no need for image"): **CAMF** (female coupler)
  and **CAMM** (male adapter), 1/2" to 6". A CAMF fits a CAMM of the same size. Tick boxes only; no drawing of their own.
- **Default settings > IP Types** has a tick box for each. **None are ticked to start.** An IP Type list shows the ticked ones,
  the ones already used in the Schema (Never Take Away), and its own. A sample Schema may name its own (`ipAllow`); the 3 Vessel
  sample allows TC1.5, TC2, FMSSQD1/2 and MSSQD1/2, and its pipes and pump are TC1.5.
- **Ends that fit by themselves** ("Pipe and hose changes are always auto"): a pipe end on a pump's In or Out, or on a Stove Top
  Vessel's Bottom Outlet, takes the IP Type that mates with it (MPT1/2 on an FPT1/2 port), greyed out in the pipe's Properties.
  A hose's Quick Disconnect end is FMSSQD where it is on a pipe or a pump and MSSQD on its other end. On a Tri-Clamp pipe or pump
  the real adapter goes there (OakBarn Brewery: "Adapter is what I use"; "And that is the most common TC to QD": TC1.5 to
  MSSQD1/2); until it is added, the fit warning shows (Rule 5.43).
- **A pipe divided in two keeps everything** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "Maybe a comment in the Help about auto setting fittings
  like elbows that the pipe is devided in two pipes and all the IPs and other properties are set and proties inheietrd"; "Good
  check that auto always works"): a tee, cross, pump, valve, probe tee or Manual Valve on a pipe cuts it, and every piece keeps
  every setting the pipe had (size, IP Types, color, Flow Color, lock); only its Name, Label and Show label are its own. A new pipe
  drawn on to a pipe (a corner at an elbow) takes that pipe's size, its IP Type at the joint and its color. Skynet does this in the
  Background and needs no user input (Rule 11.13). Checked by test/pipesplit.test.js for every kind of cut.
- **Auto typed to the join** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16, IP Type Hover Help: "When Pipes are Joined, the IPs are auto typed to the
  join. Once locked, they stay until unlocked. Generally, it is done automatically after your first pipe join"; "When Hoses are
  Joined, the IPs are auto typed to the join"; Panel Updates entry 12, built 2026-11-19): when a pipe end is joined to an IP where
  another pipe end already is (dragged on, a moved pipe dropped on, or joined again on Save layout), the end just joined takes the IP
  Type of the end already there; a hose end joined to a hose the same. It happens only at the join, so the type then stays until the
  end is let go (🔓 Unlock its ends) and joined again, and one changed by hand in Properties stays. A 🔒 locked pipe keeps its own.
  **A hose joined to a pipe changes neither** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, picked "Keep today: adapter note"): the hose's Quick
  Disconnect end is FMSSQD as above, the pipe keeps its type, and the Adapter note shows (Rule 5.43). So the sentence "when a Hose is
  joined to a Pipe, the Pipe IP End Type becomes the Hose End IP Type" is not in the Hover Help.
- **No mismatch:** two pipe ends on the same IP whose types can't be joined directly (another type, or MPT to MPT, FPT to FPT)
  are joined with an adapter, as in the real brewery, so there is no mismatch and no warning ring (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17:
  "There can be no mismatch because an adapter would be used so no need for Orange Ring"). The IP's Properties say **Adapter: ...**
  as a note, information only (Rule 2.57). Different sizes of one type meet at a reducer. Nothing is blocked.
  *Replaced (2026-11-17):* an orange ring in Edit layout marked such ends.
- Older Schemas: once (ipSizesKept), each old plain type becomes its size (a pipe or hose end from its own size, threads male; a
  pump from its Ports, female; a Stove Top outlet female), then the ends above are fitted.
- A size the connector is not made in is not offered with it: Tri-Clamp is not made under 1/2", so a 1/4" pipe offers only
  NPT, BSP and Quick Disconnect.
- **Defaults (Rule 2.42):** ☰ Menu > Default settings has **Default pipe IP Type** (beside Default pipe size; Tri-Clamp unless
  you change it) and **Default hose IP Type** (beside Default hose size; Quick Disconnect unless you change it). A new pipe or
  hose takes it on both ends. A Quick Disconnect hose (Rule 5.28) is always Quick Disconnect on both ends.
- New things only: changing the Default never changes a pipe or hose already made. Once per Schema, each pipe and hose made
  before this Rule took the Default IP Type of that day on both ends.
- **Drawn as its type** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "Connectors: Graphic match Type"): each end of a pipe or hose is drawn as
  its IP Type, across the end and turned with it, its size following the pipe: Tri-Clamp a ferrule and clamp band, NPT a tapered
  thread, BSP a hex nut on a thread, Quick Disconnect a cam lock with its two arms. Not drawn where the end sits on a fitting, a
  Quick Disconnect Widget or an End Cap (drawn already), or at a QD hose's free end (its yellow ring is there).
- **Quick Disconnect hose ends move at any time** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "QD Ends can be disconnected and moved even when not
  in Build Mode"; "QD ends: Hoses only and only grab one end at a time"): a hose end whose IP Type is Quick Disconnect can be
  grabbed and moved outside Edit layout like a QD hose's free end (Rule 5.28), one end at a time; the other end stays. Pipes never
  do, whatever their IP Type.
- **Unhooking a hose end: a warning only when liquid flows** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "Right Click and hold the Yellow circle is all it should take to move it.  It unhooks without comfirmation and is locked or hanging open when Right Moude buuton release"; "If there is flow a warning,  No flow, no warning"): holding the left mouse button a moment (the right button until 2026-11-24, Rule 2.9), or a finger, on the
  yellow ring is all it takes; with no flow there is no pop-up and the end moves at once. With a pump on the hose On, or liquid
  flowing in it, a warning (frozen top, Rule 2.51) says "Turn the pump Off before you unhook it" and the end does not move. Skynet
  keeps checking (every half second) and the warning closes by itself once nothing flows; then hold the ring again. **✖ Exit**
  closes it. It only warns: it never turns anything On or Off (Rule 2.44). Letting go after a drag never opens Help.
  A hose end left in the air is open: what pushes into the hose (a Tap Water Valve that is On, a running pump) pours out of it, so
  the hose shows flow (and moving it warns). On a plain IP at the open end of a pipe, flow goes on into that pipe. Any open pipe or
  hose end can flow; only End Caps and closed valves stop it. Where flow pours out of an open end, a water splash is drawn (Skynet's
  own art, made in code, in the flow color with white details). A hose end put on the open end of a pipe goes in the way that end
  faces, with a U when needed, as a real hose does (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17).
  (Replaces the 2026-11-14 pop-up that asked about gravity draining and needed **Yes, unhook it**.)
- **Pumps:** the **Inlet IP Fitting** and **Outlet IP Fitting** in every Pump dialog are the IP Types of its In and Out IPs (OakBarn
  Brewery: "Add Connection Type for the In and Out IPs as above on a Pump"; 2026-11-17, Rule 2.57: one row each, named Inlet and
  Outlet IP Fitting). A pump starts with what its older Ports pick says (TC is Tri-Clamp, FPT or MPT is NPT, BSP is BSP), or else the
  Default pipe IP Type; pumps already made took it once. The Pump Profile has the same two rows.
- **BruControl Import:** BruControl has no connector on its pipes, so imported pipes and hoses take the Defaults.

---


5.41 **A Chiller is the same as a pipe, no more, no less** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "A chiller is not really a Device but a
Special Widget with IOs"; "a chiller could be hooked up quite a few different ways in a manifold and would need to be flexible as
where the flow supply came from, like a permanently open valve"; "Treat a Chiller like a pipe. IPs at the Inlets Outlets. No on/off,
simply flow. It would need a source for flow"; "Chiller same as a pipe, no more, no less"; thread "Make the Chiller a flexible
Special Widget", Help 14).
- A **Chiller** (Plate chiller, Counterflow chiller, the Copper Counterflow Chiller, an Immersion coil or a Chillzilla) is a
  **Widget** with no Port (Rule 1.2). It has **IPs at its inlets and outlets** and nothing else.
- **No On / Off.** It has no On / Off state, and a Process never turns it on or off.
- **Flow simply passes through it, the same as a pipe:** it flows when a **source** upstream pushes flow in (a running pump, or
  an open Tap Water Valve, Rule 5.33), and stops when nothing does. Where the flow comes from is up to how it is piped, so it can
  be hooked up any way in a manifold, including from a valve that is always left open.
- **Each path is its own pipe.** A plate or counterflow chiller has two paths that never mix, **Wort In to Wort Out** and **Water
  In to Water Out** (4 IPs), each with its own source. An Immersion coil has one path, **In to Out** (2 IPs). A **Chillzilla is a counterflow chiller**
  with 4 IPs (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15), not an immersion chiller.
- **Nothing a pipe doesn't have:** no Size, Units or Dead space in its Template, and no built-in Thermowell. A probe for the chilled
  wort goes in the pipe beside it (a probe tee, Rule 5.30).
- The Brew Day's **Chiller cooling water** job (Rule 16.3) picks the **source** of the water (the valve or pump that feeds Water In),
  never the Chiller.
- **BruControl Import:** BruControl has no chillers, so nothing is imported as one; the Importer's Build page is the Panel's, so a
  Chiller works the same there.
- **3 Vessel sample** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "Replace with Chiller Widget and no on/off in 3 vessel"; "A Chiller is normally
  manually placed into a Brew Kettle and chilling water (Tap or Chilled Water depending on the User) and the outlet dumped down a drain
  or outside"; "Have the Tap Water valve by Pass the chiller. Have a manual Tap Water Valve go to one side of the chiller and open Hose
  on other side"): the old Chiller water On/Off Device is gone. A **manual Tap Water Valve** (Rule 5.33, "Chiller water") and an open end,
  "Drain or outside", wait for the chiller. **No Chiller Widget is on the Tab** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "Remove Chiller widget
  from 3 Vessels. It will be placed and removed with Process code and we need to re draw the hoses to it"): a Process places it in
  the Boil Kettle and draws its hoses, and takes it away again. A **motorized Tap Water
  Valve** on Port 30 bypasses the chiller and feeds the pump's suction line through a tee. The Brew Day Process asks the brewer to
  open and close the Chiller water tap.

5.42 **The Chiller Overlay: a Process places a chiller in a vessel and takes it off again** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "A Chiller
is normally manually placed into a Brew Kettle"; "Could almost be an Overlay type when placed on the screen and maybe a command to
move it to the Brew Kettle"; "a snippet of Code where a Skynet Chiller Template is chosen and it is superimposed on a Device vessel
from a DDLB with the brew Kettle as the Default"; "place_Chiller = template, vessel"; Help 200).
- `place_Chiller = Immersion_Chiller, BK_Vessel` draws that **Chiller Template** (a chiller that goes into a vessel: an immersion chiller
  with 2 IPs, In and Out, such as Immersion_Chiller; never a plate or counterflow chiller, a Chillzilla included) **over that vessel**, on top of it, with **two hoses**: In from the Tap Water Valve on the vessel's
  Tab (Rule 5.33; one with "chill" in its Label first) and Out to the Tab's drain IP ("Drain" or "outside" in its Label). Flow
  passes only while that tap is open (Rule 5.41). A chiller already placed on that vessel is taken off first.
- `remove_Chiller = BK_Vessel` takes that chiller, its IPs and its hoses off; `remove_Chiller` alone takes off every one a Process placed.
  A chiller a person built and moved in by hand is never taken off by a Process, and `place_Chiller` says that vessel already has one.
- **Moving an Immersion Chiller by hand on a live Tab** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "Immersion Chillers on a Tab Can be Free Floating
  but later moved to a Vessel similar to hand a QD Hose on a Live Tab"; built as a Rule 14.4 exception: "B Now"): the same as a Quick
  Disconnect hose end (Rule 5.40). A **left-button hold of a moment** (the right button until 2026-11-24, Rule 2.9), or a finger, on the chiller picks it up, with no pop-up; while water flows
  through it a warning says so and it does not move (the warning closes by itself once nothing flows). Let go over a vessel (no other
  chiller in it) and it **drops into that vessel**, in its lower middle, the same spot `place_Chiller` uses, and flashes red and yellow
  for 2 seconds; let go anywhere else and it stays there, **free floating**. Its own hoses (a bundled supply and waste hose, or Quick
  Disconnect hoses to a supply on the Tab; OakBarn Brewery: "Immersion Chillers can be a bundled item with their own flow supply or
  connected with a QD Hose an different existing one one a Tab. and the waste hose") stay on its In and Out IPs and follow it; a
  chiller is a pipe (Rule 5.41), so moving it changes no flow. Only an immersion chiller (2 IPs) moves; a plate or counterflow chiller
  (a Chillzilla too) or a jacketed coil stays put, and so does a chiller joined by a rigid pipe, a locked one, or for a Viewer. A
  right-click that does not move it opens its Help, as before. The Equipment Profile keeps a chiller in a vessel with that vessel
  (Rule 19.6). A **Chiller Bundle Equipment Template** (the chiller with its hoses, Ice Water Can and Sump Pump) is made on a Build
  Tab (Rule 4.1). Placing a Bundle, or moving a chiller already on the Tab, with a Process line waits in the Process Updates Sandbox,
  entry 8 (Rule 14.5).
- **Only the drawing changes; the Process does not wait.** An `ask` line after it waits for the brewer.
- The chiller's **Suggested Name and Label come from its Template** (`wgt_CHL_Immersion~chiller_BH`, Label Immersion chiller; Rule
  3.14); its hoses get the next free Hose_n with Label hose_n.
- The **Process editor** lists the Chiller Templates after `place_Chiller =`, then the Vessels with the **Brew Kettle first**. The
  Process Check reports a missing Template, Vessel, Tap Water Valve or drain IP before the Process runs.
- **3 Vessel sample:** the Brew Day places the Immersion chiller in the Boil kettle 15 minutes before the end of the boil and takes
  it off after chilling.
- **BruControl Import:** BruControl has no chillers; the Importer does not run Processes.

5.43 **Only real things on a Tab or in a Process** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "Any fittings are not samples as only real world
thinks go on a tab or Process unless as Virtual."): everything on a Tab or named in a Process stands for a real thing in the
brewery, unless it is marked Virtual (Rule 6.2). So there are no sample-only fittings: every fitting is a real Skynet library item
a user can add (Rule 5.14), and a sample Schema uses those same items. Skynet never draws or assumes a part that is not there:
where two IP Types can't be joined, the user adds the real adapter, or the fit warning stays (Rule 5.40).

5.44 **A pipe that crosses another pipe with no joint never looks joined** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20: "When a Pipe crosses a
different pipe with no connect"; "The red looks like a cross fitting"; thread "Show pipe crossings without a joint"): where two
pipes cross in the middle of both, with no IP, tee or cross there (Rule 5.25: such a pipe does not join the other), the
**up-and-down pipe passes in front** and the **level pipe goes behind it**, with a thin dark edge on each side of the front pipe, so
the crossing can never be taken for a cross or a tee. When both pipes lean the same way, the one higher in the Layer Order (Rule
1.29) is in front. Only the drawing changes: the pipes, their IPs, flow and Layer Order stay as they are, and clicking still picks
the pipe under the pointer. Hoses bend and lie where they fall, so a hose is left as drawn. Help 124 (and French).

5.45 **Water that stands still, and flow never past a closed valve** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20, Panel Update 7: "It could also
show in the pipe up to the valves, but the flow is stopped. The flow does not move"; "Looks like a leak. The end is not open but
connected to a Pipe. This is a Bug."; "Flow past a Closed Valve = bug"):
- **Still water:** from a Tap Water Valve that is On (a Hose Bib included) or a running pump's outlet, every pipe or hose the water
  can reach that has no flow (it ends at a closed valve or an End Cap; a Quick Disconnect with nothing on it is open and sprays, Rule 5.28) is full but not moving.
  It shows the flow dashes in the flow color, standing still; moving flow still moves. Still water goes through open valves,
  fittings and pumps that are off, as flow does, and stops at a closed valve.
- **A water splash only on a truly open end** (Rule 5.40): a loose pipe or hose end within 25 px of an IP (as Save layout rejoins,
  Rule 5.19), or anywhere inside a Tee, Elbow or other Tab_Fitting, is in that IP: flow goes on through it as if joined, and no
  splash is drawn. A loose end lying on another pipe or hose, or on a widget, gets no splash either. Only an end out in the air
  gets one. The saved drawing is not changed.
- **Never past a closed valve:** a pipe joined to a valve goes on the valve's IP on its own side, never on the far IP, where it
  would run under the valve and show flow on the other side. The 3 Vessel 1 Pump sample and the default Schema had the Manifold
  Valve's two pipes the wrong way round (fixed; its Tap water now flows Right to Left, from the tap side to the manifold).

5.46 **A Tap water valve with a pipe on its tap side gets its water along that pipe** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-21, word for
word: "Flow is wrong and spurts even when hose bib is turned off = bug"). A Valve Device with **Tap water** on (Help 31) is fed the
same way as a Hose Bib's Inlet (Rule 18.52 #7, "if another valve is on that side, it must be open"):
- **Nothing joined on its tap side:** the house plumbing is not drawn, so it always has water. Open, it pushes water out of its Out
  side, as before.
- **A pipe on its tap side:** it has water only along an open way from a source (an open Hose Bib, a running pump, another Tap water
  valve that has water), a plain IP end, an open end in the air, or an open valve whose other side has nothing joined. A vessel's port
  is not a supply. A closed Hose Bib or a closed valve on that side means no water: open or not, nothing comes out of it, no flow and
  no water splash.
- **With water:** the pipes from the source to its tap side flow toward it while water goes on out of it; when every way out is
  closed they stand still (Rule 5.45).
- Example, the 3 Vessel 1 Pump sample: on the Brew House the Firehose Valve and Manifold Valve Clones are fed by the Hose Bib through
  a Tee. Before, the Firehose Valve sprayed out of its Quick Disconnect with the Hose Bib closed, and with the Hose Bib open its water
  stood still under the valve. On the Water Tab both valves are fed from the plain Tap Water Supply IP, so they work as before.
Help 31 (and French). Checked against both programs: the BruControl Import brings pipes in as they are and draws no flow; nothing
changes there.

## 6. Devices, connections and safety

6.1 **One Interface Port, one Device** (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "That means the is a Limit of One Interface Port to one Device. Another
Major difference from BruControl"; reworded by OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09). **No two Devices ever share a Port on an Interface,**
whatever their Device Types. A heater's ways of control are one Heating Element's heating methods (Rule 6.19), not more Devices. The
Available Ports lists never offer a Port that is assigned, and saving a Device on a used Port is refused and says which Device has it.
- **Once a Port is picked, it is taken:** it can never be picked again. It never shows up on a list to be picked, because only free,
  fitting Ports fill any pick list.
- **A Template, Device or Integrated Device can NEVER change its Interface or Port.** Once set, they still show in its Properties,
  greyed out: you can see them but not change them.
- **Quibbling exception: Integrated Instances and Clones:**
  1. An Integrated Device inherits its Properties from the Template and then becomes independent, but it still follows this Rule. As
     long as a Template, a Device or an Integrated Device uses an Interface and Port, that Port is never available to be used ANYWHERE.
     See Rule 6.28, Last One Rules.
  2. Clones are simply duplicates of the Parent, except: see Rule 6.28, Last One Rules.
- **BruControl:** the Import makes heating controls on one port one Heating Element (Rule 6.19); anything else still sharing a port
  (for example a pump's on/off and its PWM speed) is listed in the Import notes so the brewer can keep one.
*Replaced:* (2026-10-23, PR #97) "Exception: outputs of different Device Types may share a port (for example Hysteresis and PID on
one heater). The last one turned on wins and the others turn off."

6.2 **Virtual ports:** hydrometers 200, 201 and up. *Changed 2026-11-19:* OneWire probes no longer have virtual ports 700-799; each has a 1-Wire Index (Rule 6.37).
Analog pins use BruControl numbers (A0 = 54, A5 = 59). (2026-10-23, PR #97)

6.3 **Connection ranking per board** (2026-10-26, PR #108, still open):
- Arduino Mega: USB best, Ethernet OK (a network failure is a safety risk), WiFi poor. There is no "other
  Arduino-type board" (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "List Boards Only"): the Board list is every board Skynet names, never "Other"
  (2026-11-19, Rule 6.35: every standard Arduino board and every BruControl board). Another Arduino-type board is rated like the Mega; a
  board with WiFi built in is rated like the ESP32.
  *Replaced:* "the Board list is Arduino Mega, ESP32 and Raspberry Pi." (2026-11-15)
- ESP32: USB best, Ethernet good, WiFi good **as long as no heating is on a pin**.
- Heating on Ethernet or WiFi is allowed, with a warning. A lost link turns the board's outputs off
  after a set delay.
- **Lost Comm (s) is a must-fill box on the Interface dialog** (named Lost Link until OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "Lost Link (s)
  Change to Lost Comm") (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "Make it a Mandatory Field on a New
  Interface, edited on the Interface Dialog. Set all Interfaces and existing Templates to the recommended setting"): 3 to 600
  seconds, 10 to start. Every Interface and Sample Schema has it set to 10. It is not on the Default tab.
*Replaced:* Fritz first said "Mega by USB only" the same day, then changed it to this ranking.

6.4 **Switching Schemas turns every output off** before and after the switch (manual valves are
not touched), and warns if Processes are running. (2026-10-21, PR #66)

6.5 **Never run real JavaScript inside a Process.** C-style spellings (`;`, `{ }`, `++`) are fine.
(2026-10-21, PR #58)

6.6 **Remote access is by Tailscale only.** Never open a port on the router. (2026-10-04, PR #8)

6.7 **Digital input push buttons** (Pulse mode) have a 3 second lockout by default. (2026-10-04,
PR #4) The default is ☰ Menu > Default settings > **Push Lockout (s)** (0.1 to 60, 3 unless changed; 2026-11-14, Rule 2.42); it is
used when a new button is made, and each button changes its own in its Properties.

6.8 **Firmware for the boards**: ready firmware for boards that are not on the standard Arduino IDE
is now a go (2026-10-27, thread "Build firmware for non-Arduino-IDE boards"). Every firmware keeps
the same message language (docs/DEVICE_PROTOCOL.md) and the lost-link watchdog.

6.9 **RTD chip-select (CS) pins on an Arduino Mega:** an RTD Device (PT100 / PT1000 on a MAX31865
board) may ONLY use **D14-D17, D22-D39, D41-D43, D47-D49 or D53** for its CS pin. Those pins are not
PWM, counter, SPI (50-52), OneWire (40) or Ethernet shield (4, 10) pins. The pin list offers only
these, and the panel refuses any other pin. Thermocouples are not covered (yet).
(2026-10-27, thread "Limit RTD CS pins on the Mega")

6.10 **Pin D10 on an Ethernet Mega:** the Ethernet shield uses pin D10, and a pin is hard wired to its
equipment, so moving it is real work. On a Mega on Ethernet no Device may use D10 (the pin list
doesn't offer it). Before a Mega Interface can be changed from USB to Ethernet, the panel checks
pin 10: if a Device uses it, the panel says that Device and its wiring must move to another free
pin first, and refuses the change until pin 10 is free. (2026-10-27, thread "Limit RTD CS pins on
the Mega")
On a Mega **not** on Ethernet (USB, WiFi bridge) D10 is **kept by a warning only** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "On a Mega, we
want to reserve pin 10 on USB Connection until it is the last one available and if picked Give warning about Ethernet no longer
Available as an Option because of PIN 10 being used. The reservation is not a fixed thing but a warning to the User"; then "It can be in
order but can it be a Different color on the DDLB?"): the Port list keeps D10 in number order, in **another color** with "Reserved
for Ethernet: see Help" beside it, and picking it shows one warning that Ethernet is no longer a choice while D10 is in use.
The true PWM pins have their own color in the Port lists too (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "Different color for PWM Pins"):
PWM pins blue, D10 orange with "Reserved for Ethernet: see Help" (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "Only pin 10 gets ethernet
warning and Reserved for Ethernet: see Help"). Help 46.
Help 69.

6.11 **SD cards are not supported. Never insert an SD card** in a Mega's Ethernet shield. Pin D4 is
the shield's SD card pin: it is NOT blocked, but picking D4 for a Device on a Mega shows the warning
"SD Card Not Supported. Never insert an SD Card!". The Ethernet sketch (firmware 0.5) holds D4 HIGH,
checks the slot every 10 seconds, and when a card is in, the panel shows "SD Card Not Supported.
Remove the SD Card!" to everyone and on the Devices page. (2026-10-27, thread "Limit RTD CS pins on
the Mega") The D4 warning and the "SD card pin" tag go on every board that takes an Ethernet shield, not only the Mega (OakBarn
Brewery, 2026-11-19, from Arduino's Ethernet shield notes: "Digital pin 4 is used to control the slave select pin on the SD card";
not on a board whose Ethernet is a module without an SD slot).

6.12 **Firmware order and add-ons** (Fritz, 2026-10-27/28): 1 Raspberry Pi GPIO program, 2 board
profiles with ready-made firmware for Uno, Nano, R4, GIGA, Opta and the others, loaded from inside
Skynet (board on the Brain's USB, the Brain uploads, terminal-style box and serial monitor, Admin
only), 3 Pi Pico. Every board is a daughter board (Interface) of the Brain like a Mega 2560; the Brain
holds all logic. **Each add-on (OneWire, RTD, thermocouple, ADS1115, load cells, steppers, Ethernet)
goes to every Arduino board**: one shared Skynet firmware, built with only the add-ons that
Interface's Devices use so small boards fit. (thread "Build firmware for non-Arduino-IDE boards")

6.13 **Raspberry Pi GPIO pins:** an Interface with Board "Raspberry Pi" runs `firmware/Pi_GPIO`.
Pins are GPIO (BCM) numbers 2-27. GPIO 4 is kept for DS18B20 probes, GPIO 7-11 for SPI (RTD and
thermocouple boards), GPIO 2-3 for I2C (ADS1115). No analog pins and no stepper motors on a Pi: the
panel refuses them. On the Brain itself (address 127.0.0.1) the rating is Best. Same protocol and
lost-link watchdog as every other board. (2026-10-28, Help 78, PR #119 open)

6.14 **Database and .API on every Device and Widget** (Fritz, 2026-10-30, Help 98). Every Device and Widget
with a value has a **Database and .API** box at the end of its Properties:
- **Send to the database**: Off, On demand, On value change (at most 10 a second, the last change never lost),
  **When Clicked** (each time someone sets it on its Tab), When a Process starts, At a date and time (once), At clock time (every day at that time), **Every second, Every minute, Every hour, Every day (at Midnight)** (shortcuts,
  Fritz 2026-11-06, listed just above the Every N choices), Every N ms /
  seconds / minutes / hours / days, Every 00:00:00. The **At clock time** box shows only when **At clock time** is
  picked; the Every choices have no clock time (Fritz, 2026-11-04). **What to send** is its main value unless another attribute is picked.
  `send_db Name` in a Process sends it now, whatever the setting, **even when it is Off** (Fritz, 2026-11-05: kept
  `send_db Name`, no `send_Now` command).
- **Database Groups** (Fritz, 2026-11-05, rewritten 2026-11-06). **A Group is how a set of Devices and Widgets is sent to the
  Database or not.** A Process command starts sending a Group, and another Process command stops it:
  **`start_db_group Group_Name`** and **`stop_db_group Group_Name`**.
  - **A single Device or Widget can belong to more than one Group** (Fritz, 2026-11-06). The Database and .API box shows the
    item's Groups and a **👥 Groups…** button (Fritz, 2026-11-06, a dialog change he commanded, Rule 18). It opens the **Group
    list**: a list box of the existing Groups with **➕ Add new Group…** at the top (Rule 18.14: it makes the Group, comes back and
    selects it); ✔ marks the Groups the item is in. **A click on a Group opens the Group dialog with all its members. A
    double-click on a Group adds this Device or Widget to it** and opens the Group dialog with its members. The Group dialog also
    has ✏ Change name and ➕ Add / ➖ Take this item out. The Group list's 💾 Save keeps the choice; it is saved with the Properties.
  - **An item assigned to a Database Group is only sent to the database while a Group it belongs to is started.** It is sent by
    its **own** Send to the database setting (Every 1 minute, On value change, When Clicked ...), so the item sets *how often*
    and the Group sets *when*. An item in no Group is sent by its setting all the time, as before. Every Group is stopped when
    the Brain starts.
  - **On demand is always true still** (Fritz, 2026-11-06): `send_db Name` (and Log now, and the API) sends the item at once,
    whatever its Groups, even when they are stopped. **`send_db_group Group_Name`** sends every item of the Group **once, now**,
    started or not.
  - **Example (Fritz):** you want a Mash Temperature Probe sent to the database **every minute**, but only during the Mash. Set
    the probe's Send to the database to **Every minute** and add it to the Group **Mash** (👥 Groups…, double-click Mash). At the beginning of the Mash a
    Process line `start_db_group Mash` starts the Group, and the probe reports to the database every minute. At the end of the
    Mash a Process line `stop_db_group Mash` stops it. The database only has that probe's data during the Mash.
  - A Group has a **meaningless hidden key** (the items point to it) and a **Group Name**. **✏ Change name** changes the Group
    Name and **every Process** follows (`send_db_group`, `start_db_group`, `stop_db_group`; Update All, like Rule 3.11).
  - **In a Group is no longer a Send to the database choice, and Once is gone** (Rule 15.2): each Schema's Once items and In a
    Group items become **On demand** still in their Group, so `send_db_group` still sends them as before.
- Each reading is kept with its **time stamp** and the item's **hidden key** (Rule 3.10), so a renamed item keeps
  all its readings under today's name. The key never leaves the Brain. The database is SQLite on the Brain
  (free, SQL). An outside database (offload, reports and CSV from it, a "Database Not Available" pop-up) is later.
- **.API**: Off (the start), **Read Only (Get: outside programs like Node-Red can read it.)**, **Read & Control (Get & Put:
  outside programs like Node-Red can also control it.)** (Fritz, 2026-11-06, renamed from Get only / Get and Put; elsewhere in these Rules Get only = Read Only and
  Get and Put = Read & Control). Only items with .API on are in `/api/items`, MQTT and Home Assistant; only Read & Control can be
  changed from outside.
- **Safeguards so a bot can't take over:** board readings (inputs, probes), names, Tabs, Interfaces, ports and
  pictures are never changed from outside; a Manual Valve Widget has no .API (only a click turns it); ten wrong
  API keys in 10 minutes shut that address out for 15 minutes; every outside change is written in the Processes
  console.
- These two settings are always user settable, also on a User version of a Skynet Template (an exception to
  Rule 5.16).
- **`Name.Attribute DBSend`** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "Name.Attribute DBSend and send_db Name have both") sends that one
  attribute to the database now; `Name DBSend` is the same as `send_db Name`. Help 98.

6.15 **Close all and Open all valve lists** (Fritz, 2026-10-30). Every valve a Process switches (Electro_Mechanical, such as a
Motorized Ball Valve) has two switches, **On Close List** and **On Open List** (Fritz, 2026-11-05, renamed from Close all list / Open all list), both **on to start**.
`close_all_valves` and `open_all_valves` in a Process (and PreBrew's house cleaning) use them; `all_pumps_off` turns every pump off.
**`all_heaters_off`** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-21: "new command heaters_off and turn off all heaters"; named to match all_pumps_off)
turns every heater off: every Heating Element on any method (a PWM or analog one goes to 0; its PID, Hysteresis, Duty Cycle or
Deadband stops with it, so it can't switch back on), every older Duty Cycle, Hysteresis, PID or Deadband control (disabled), and
every gas burner (its Solenoid Gas Valve closed and its igniter off, as a Flame Out trip, Rule 6.33). It is the same list as step 1
of Emergency Off (Rule 6.41; one shared piece of code), with no reminder pop-up. Nothing turns back on until a Process or a click
turns it on. Help 100.
**A tap water valve is always on Close all and never on Open all**: its Properties show On Close List on and On Open List off,
both greyed out (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "Tap Water Valves have the Open attribute as false and greyed out"), and the Brain puts it back
on every save. A Schema from the BruControl Import is put right the same way when it is opened. **The last step of Clean is
open_all_valves** (only the valves On Open List, so never tap water). A Manual valve is on neither list. (thread "Build the Standard Skynet Brew Process", Help 100)
**The Manual valve reminder** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20: "Close all Valve command that closes every valve that has the close toogle
set. Tap water are always close with this command. Followed by Nanny 'Have you closed all Manual Valves'"; "Open all valves command
that opens all valves except tap water one. with nanny 'Have you opened all Manual Valves'"): after `close_all_valves` closes its
list, the Process shows **one** pop-up, **Have you closed all Manual Valves?**, and waits for ✔ Done; after `open_all_valves`, **Have
you opened all Manual Valves?**. Skynet can't turn a Manual valve, so this one reminder is asked for (it is not a nanny pop-up). Only when the
Schema has a Manual valve (a Manual valve Device or a Manual Valve Widget); with none, the Process goes straight on.
The On Close List and On Open List switches still pick the valves (Rule 1, Never Take Away). Help 100.

6.16 **Moving from BruControl needs no new hardware (Windows Brain only)** (Fritz, 2026-11-03). Every way a BruControl
Windows PC connects to its boards has an equal way in Skynet, so a brewer moving from BruControl keeps the same boards, shields,
wiring and cables: the same board types (Arduino Mega 2560, Adafruit Grand Central M4, ESP32, ESP8266, Feather M0, Arduino Due, and
the BruControl UniShield / UniFlex built on them), the same links (USB on the same COM port, Ethernet, WiFi), and the same pin
numbers (BruControl numbering, Rule 6.2). Which pin does what is set from the Brain, never by editing firmware, so anything wired
for BruControl works as it is. The only change allowed is **loading Skynet firmware onto the board once**, over its USB cable, from
inside Skynet (no Arduino IDE), with WiFi or network settings set the same way. Skynet does not copy BruControl's private firmware
language. This Rule is for a Windows Brain only, because BruControl runs only on Windows. Gaps and plan: docs/BruControl_Connections.md.
(thread "Match BruControl's Arduino connections on Windows")

6.17 **Deadband Device, as in BruControl** (Fritz, 2026-11-05: "Add Deadband", "look at BruControl's Deadband Control"). A
Deadband is its own control output Device (Type ID **DBand**), next to Duty Cycle, Hysteresis and PID. It reads an Input and,
every **Calc Time**, steps its output % toward the **Setpoint**:
- within **± Deadband Offset** of the Setpoint the output is left alone (the whole Deadband is twice the offset);
- within **± Inner Band Offset** (outside the Deadband) it moves by the **Inner Band Drive**;
- further out it moves by the **Outer Band Drive**.
Below the Setpoint the output goes up, above it goes down; **Reversed** turns that round (cooling). It starts at the **Initial
Output** when Enabled. On a PWM pin (PWM output on) the pin follows the output %; on an on/off pin it is on for that % of each
**Output window** (a Duty Cycle). The Skynet way (Rule 15.1): the output is a **%** (0-100), not BruControl's 0-255, so Import
changes the Initial Output and the two Drives to % and says so. Like the PID it counts as a heater, is On while Enabled
(Rule 7.9) and can share a heater's port (Rule 6.1). Starting values: Deadband Offset 0.5, Inner Band Offset 2, Initial Output 0,
Inner Band Drive 1, Outer Band Drive 5, Calc Time 10 s, Output window 2 s. (thread "Add Deadband control", Help 126)

6.18 **API_Name: the name a Voice Command says** (Fritz, 2026-11-06: "a new string field associated with API. API_Name. This
field must be Unique. It is what a Voice Command would use. It would only be on the Database and API Popup"). Every Device and
Widget with a value has an **API_Name** String, **only on its Database and .API pop-up**, below .API.
- It **must be Unique** in the Schema; capitals and extra spaces don't count (`Red Pump` = `red  pump`). Saving one that is
  already used is refused and says which item has it. Spaces are allowed; `< > : " / \ | ? *` are not; at most 60 characters.
- It **may be blank, with a warning** that a Voice Command can't be used for that item (Fritz, 2026-11-06: "It can be blank,
  but with a Warning that you could not use a Voice Command").
- A Voice Command says it: an API_Name **Red Pump** is switched by "Turn on Red Pump" (Fritz, 2026-11-06). Home Assistant (Alexa,
  Google Home, Siri) names the item by its API_Name (its Label when blank); `/api/items/<name>` finds an item by its Name or its
  API_Name. It opens nothing by itself: the item's .API (Rule 6.14) still says what outside programs may do.
- It replaces the "Voice Name" planned on 2026-10-30 (unique, starting as the Label): an API_Name starts blank.
- It is not the item's Name (Rule 3.1): Processes keep using the Name. The BruControl Importer (Rule 15.4) carries it over later.
  (thread "Add unique API_Name for voice commands", Help 144)
- **.API is the one switch for the web API, MQTT and voice** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "We need to build for all three. API seems
  to be the place to do it unless there is a need for a separate MQTT and Voice"; "even if they are not true api, the sorta act like
  it"): **Off** = not shared anywhere; **Read Only** (Get) = the web API, MQTT and voice read it (Home Assistant, and so Alexa, Google
  Home and Siri, gets it); **Read & Control** (Get and Put) = they can also change it, with the web API's safeguards (board readings
