  and Manual Valve Widgets never; a Widget that switches a Device needs that Device's Read & Control too). There are no separate MQTT
  and voice ticks per item any more; Settings > MQTT and voice lists the shared items with their .API. Silencing a shared alarm and
  stopping Processes are always allowed; starting a Process only when ticked there. A gGlobal is never shared (Rule 1.33). Both
  programs: the Panel (lib/mqtt.js, lib/itemapi.js); the BruControl Import has no MQTT.
- **Every Voice Command is Unique** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-18: "That could be an issue with any voice command so in the next PR
  add Voice Command must be Unique"): an API_Name is Unique across **every Device and Widget**, a Hose Bib (Rule 18.49) too, in the
  Panel and on the Brain. What a Voice Command says is the API_Name, else the Label, else the Name; a Label that more than one shared
  item has (or that is another item's API_Name) can't tell them apart, so each of those is called by its own Name, which is always
  Unique (Rule 3.1). No pop-up: the API_Name's blank warning stays the one warning. A Hose Bib with .API on is shared with MQTT and
  voice too (asked for by hand, Rule 18.49). Help 144.

6.19 **One Heating Element, the heating method picked** (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "The way I want to handle this is ONE device, but a to
select the heating method via process or on the Device when clicked"). One physical heating element is **one Device**: a Heating
Element (a Digital Out with Kind = element, on its own or built into a Vessel Device, RIMS tube or Integrated kettle). How it heats
is its **heating method**: **Direct**, **PWM**, **Duty Cycle**, **Hysteresis**, **PID**, **Deadband** or **Precise**. **Direct** is full on or
off (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "On/Off Change to Direct").
- **Adding one: a row for each method** (OakBarn Brewery's markup "Update Panel", 2026-11-15, Panel Updates Sandbox entries 3 and 4;
  built 2026-11-17, "Ok lets get all the decided ones done first"). Select Device Type > Heating Element (and the Edit layout bar's
  Heating Element list) has the header Hover Help "Heating Element. Direct On/Off, PWM, Duty Cycle, Hysteresis, and PID are control
  Methods of a Heating Element. These are all a single Element Device that can use any of the Methods, but choosing Duty Cycle one
  creates a Heating Element Device that first presents the Duty Cycle Attributes." and the rows **Heating Element: DO On/Off (relay,
  SSR, contactor)**, **PWM (0 to 100%)**, **DutyC (Duty % per Cycle)**, **HYS (Target and Offset)**, **PID (Holds a Set
  Temperature)**, **Precise (Holds to 0.1 Degree)**, **Deadband (Steps its %)**, then **RIMs Tube** and **Vessel Device Template**.
  Each row makes ONE Heating Element starting on that method, and its Properties open with that method's Settings on top. The
  separate Duty Cycle, Hysteresis, PID and Deadband control Devices are no longer added ("Question 3. Yes One Port One device
  Rule"); ones already in a Schema keep working. Deadband stays a Method ("Yes to all recomendations").
- **PWM is a Method too** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "It is Both. I actually wrote a script to control a Heating element using PWM
  values"): its **Power %** (`.power`), set by hand or a Process, goes out while it is ON. The PWM row offers PWM Ports first.
- **The Port picked decides** how a % reaches the element (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "question 4 2 rows"): one PID row and one Precise
  row, no "Pseudo PID" row. On a **PWM Port** the % goes out as PWM; on a **plain Port** the element is fully On for its % of each Output
  window (the "Pseudo PID"). **Changed (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, "Hardware Controller decides"):** the % goes out as PWM only when
  the element's **Hardware Controller** (Rule 6.29) is **DAC / 0-10 V** and its Port is a PWM Port; an Optical SSR, Contactor or
  Mechanical relay gets the plain-Port way on any Port, so an SSR on a PWM Port (the 3 Vessel sample's HLT element on D8) never gets
  fast PWM. A DAC / 0-10 V on a plain Port says it needs a PWM Port. The **Heating Element: PWM** row starts on DAC / 0-10 V. A
  Heating Element saved sending PWM before this gets DAC / 0-10 V when it loads, so it works as before. The Heating Element's PWM switch
  follows the Hardware Controller and the Port when it is added or its Properties are saved (it is no longer a switch in the method dialogs). Each method's Settings say which: a PWM Port goes to a PWM-to-0-10 V module and a 0-10 V
  power controller, not straight to a zero-cross SSR; a plain Port quickly wears out any mechanical switching device (mechanical
  relay, relay module, contactor, timer switch), so use an SSR, with the Electrical Warning (Rule 6.20).
- **Precise** (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "a method of precise control built if possible using offsets to get to .1 F or .1 C"; for a
  still's column, which a BruControl PID could not hold): a calm PID that holds a Setpoint to 0.1 degree. It shares the PID's
  Setpoint, Kp, Ki, Kd and Max output, and adds **Hold output %** (the % it needs to stay at the Setpoint; it starts there),
  **Smoothing** (seconds it averages the probe over) and an exact Output window (the part of a window too short to switch is
  carried to the next). Its I part does not grow while the output is at 0 or Max or the reading is already heading for the Setpoint, and its D part works on the smoothed
  reading. Its Properties say whether its probe can see 0.1 (a DS18B20 sees 0.11 °F steps, a PT100 0.05 °F; a thermistor on an
  analog pin cannot). Every **Temperature Probe** also has a **Two-point calibration** (ice water and boiling water at your
  altitude; the Calibration offset is added after it), and the boards set DS18B20 probes to their finest (12-bit) steps.
  Help 156.
- **Built in Elements too** (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "The only thing that seems to be missing is the Element Method Field and the
  Hotspots to switch Methods on the Screen when running"): an Element built into a Vessel Device, RIMS tube or kettle is a Heating
  Element with the same Heating method field, allowed methods and spots. One still saved as an old separate control Device (the
  Three Vessel sample's HLT_Heat was a Hysteresis) becomes one when the Schema loads, starting in that method; its name, settings
  and Processes stay (Rule 3.5). A RIMS tube's Control picks the method its Element starts with.
- **Only Heating Elements, today** (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "Heating Elements are the only thing I can Think of that could have a
  different method of control. The hard wiring from the Arduino to the end hardware prevents other hardware from having different
  methods of control"). The Rules about Devices with more than one Control Method (4.4, 6.19, `.method`) stay general, so another
  kind could be added later only if Fritz says so.
- **Properties (and its Build):** under *Heating method*, its **main method**, the one it **starts with** (Direct for one that has
  none), the **Temperature Probe** it reads (Hysteresis, PID, Deadband and Precise need one) and that method's settings, then **tick boxes
  for the other methods it may use**. **Only the main method and the ticked ones are allowed** (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "we ask the
  primary Control Method, and then have check boxes of other available Methods. Only Checked Methods are allowed. If a Method is
  Checked, it needs a Hot Spot or Icon on the Screen Display of the device to switch between methods"): its pop-up, its spots,
  its Method Clones, the Process editor and the Brain offer only those; a Process asking for another gets a plain error. One with
  nothing ticked has one way of control. **Direct is always allowed and always has its spot; it is not a tick box** (Fritz,
  2026-11-08: "It should not be a choice. Always displayed"). The other methods' settings are kept.
- **One click on it while running** opens its pop-up (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "One Click on the dispayed device"): one button per
  method (the one in use marked; the ones that need a probe greyed out without one), and **one click on a method switches to it at
  once**, the method's main setting with − and + (Duty cycle % or Setpoint), then **Set + ON** (ON for Direct), **OFF**, **Set**
  and **Cancel**. *Changed 2026-11-08 (Rule 2.33):* one click on the Element itself now turns it ON or OFF at once; the pop-up opens
  from a method spot or its Temperature Probe's SetPoint pop-up (Rule 2.43, **Heating method…**).
- **In Duty Cycle the % is its On and Off too** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-08: "Duty Cycle % is good. 0 turns it off. Above zero
  turns it on if it was off"): set from the pop-up, a Process or the .API, a Duty cycle % of **0 turns the Element Off**, and **above
  0 turns it On** if it was Off. Loading a Schema never turns it on. In another method the Duty cycle % is only a kept setting.
- **The SV box: change the Duty cycle % or the Setpoint right on the Tab** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, Panel Updates 40: "Heating
  Element in Duty Cylce, Click % and User Input"; "with 2 so a Setpoint can be changed on a Tab by a user"; picked "Show only the %").
  On a running Tab the Element's display shows what it is doing and, on the same line, a **green box** with the number a person sets,
  like the SV of a panel controller: in **Duty Cycle** its **Duty cycle %** (only the %, no Setpoint); in **Hysteresis, PID, Deadband
  and Precise** **SV** and its **Setpoint** with the probe's °F or °C (0.1 degree). Direct and PWM have none. **No Visible switch**: it is
  part of the display (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, for item 3: "Forget visible option Make part of Digit Display Box"), all on one line.
  **One click on the box** types a new number in place (no pop-up, Rule 2.44): Enter sets it (or clicking away after a change), Esc puts
  it back. A new Setpoint never turns it On or Off and never switches the method; a new Duty cycle % follows the bullet above (an Element
  set to Ask before changing by hand asks before a % turns it On). A click anywhere else on the Element still turns it On or Off. A
  Method Clone shows the box of its own method. Not shown in Edit layout, on the Dial or Bar look, or when a Data Display value is
  picked (the user's own choice wins). Operators and admins only. A Process that runs may set the number again. **Both programs:** the
  BruControl Import has no running Tabs; its Heating Elements are the Panel's own, so they get the box in the Panel. Help 150.
- **The Heating method section** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10, Integrate 5; Method Settings 2026-11-15): **Current Method** (a dropdown
  holding only the methods in use), **Short Label** (a switch) and a red **⬢** that opens the Current Method's own Settings (OakBarn Brewery,
  2026-11-15: "a Icon that pops current properties methods") on one line; then **Method Settings**, a **⬢** button for each method
  with ✔ Used or Not used under it (*replaced 2026-11-15:* the row of **Enabled** switches); then **Control Method**, a balloon for each method in use, the Current Method **Red** and the others
  **Yellow**, the same balloons as under the Element on its Tab. **The balloons work together:** one click on a balloon in the dialog or on
  the Tab makes it the Current Method in both places at once, and the one before turns Yellow. The dialog opens on the method the Element
  is in now. The explanations are in hover help, so the dialog stays clean.
- **One settings dialog for each method** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "When a user switches from Hysteresis to Duty Cycle there would
  need to be Property Dialog for the Hysteresis attributes and one For Duty Cycle to set the parameters for the new method. One for each
  method. Include a Use Method Boolean so it allows the method to be selected in a Process or DDLB. Is set to [No], Hide all the
  Attributes on that Property sheet. Standard Close Frozen on the dialogs"; "And also the process commands to change a method"): each
  method's ⬢ opens its own dialog, **"Duty Cycle Settings"** and so on, with its title, ✖ Cancel and 💾 Keep frozen at the top and no
  bottom row (Rule 2.51); Keep puts its settings in the Properties, saved with them. At its top is **Use Method**, a switch: **On**, the
  method may be picked in the Current Method dropdown, by its balloon (dialog and Tab), by a Method Clone and by a Process; **Off**, it
  may not, and **every other setting on that dialog is hidden** (the settings are kept). **Direct** and the **Current Method** are always On
  (greyed); a new Current Method keeps the one before in use. Use Method is the same setting the Enabled switches were (saved as
  methodSpot_<method>), so nothing saved changes. Direct has nothing to set. The Temperature Probe and the Setpoint are shared by the
  methods that use them. **Processes:** `.method = "X"` and the short `.DutyC` ... may only pick a method in use: the Process editor offers
  only those and its check shows a plain error before brewing; the Brain refuses it if it runs anyway. Switching Use Method On never turns
  the Element On. The Heating Element Properties have the frozen top too, with no bottom row. **Both programs:** the BruControl Import
  uses the same dialogs and switches Use Method On for each joined BruControl control. Help 150.
- **Ctrl + Click opens a method's Settings on a running Tab** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "I tried double clicking on the Little
  Method Balloons for a Heating element to bring up the dialog for Duty cycle for that element"; "CTRL + Left Click could do something";
  *changed 2026-11-17* after trying the double-click: "Maybe the CTRL + Click is the way to Bring Up Properties Dialog"; "Other
  Properties only on Build"; picked "A"). Outside Edit layout:
  - **Ctrl + Click** (**⌘ + Click on a Mac**, where Ctrl + Click is the right-click and gives Help, Rule 2.11) on a **method button**
    under a Heating Element opens that method's Settings for that Element (for example "HLT Heater: Duty Cycle Settings"); on the
    **Heating Element picture** (on its own, built into a Vessel Device, or a Picture Widget that follows one) it opens the Settings of
    the method it is in now; on a **Method Clone**, the Settings of the Clone's method.
  - **It turns nothing On or Off and never switches the method.** A plain click acts at once, as always (no waiting). A double-click on a
    running Tab is two plain clicks (*replaced 2026-11-17:* the double-click that opened the Settings, and the short wait it needed).
  - It is the same dialog as the method's ⬢ in the Properties, with its title, ✖ Cancel and 💾 **Save** frozen at the top (Rule 2.51).
    Save saves it to the Schema at once (no Edit layout); a new Offset, Delay, Kp ... works at once, the Element stays On or Off in the
    same method, and a new Setpoint is sent at once too. **Admins only** (it changes the Schema); others get a short note.
  - The everyday quick changes stay one click (Rule 2.44): a Temperature Probe's SetPoint pop-up (Rule 2.43), a PWM or analog out's
    number pop-up, and the Heating Element pop-up (Heating method…). **Every other Property is changed only in Edit layout.**
  - **Phones and tablets:** nothing new (no Ctrl key; holding a finger gives Help, Rule 2.11).
  - **Only Heating Elements for now.** The code keeps one list of what answers it (CTRL_CLICK in public/app.js), so other Devices can
    be added later, one at a time, when OakBarn Brewery says so.
  - **In Edit layout** Ctrl + Click opens Properties, the same as a double-click (Rule 2.9).
  - **Both programs:** the BruControl Import has no running Tabs; its Build page is the same Edit layout, so Ctrl + Click opens
    Properties there too. Help 150.
- **The Hysteresis rows** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10, Integrate_4; in the Hysteresis Settings dialog since 2026-11-15): **Temperature Probe** and **Setpoint** on one line; **Direction**
  (Heating, greyed) with **Offset** beside it, picked from a list of every half degree its Hardware Controller allows (Rule 6.29);
  **Predictive** with **Delay** beside it. Each of the two lines has a small wave drawing: the temperature (red) going between the
  Setpoint (blue) and the Offset (yellow). Data Display calls the probe reading **Temperature**. A Device built into a Vessel Device
  shows its layer as **Inside Vessel Device Layer**.
- **Direction and the sign of the Offset** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "Plain English and not a Who's on First Confusion where
  + = - and - = +"): the Direction is greyed and says which way the Hysteresis works. The sign of the Offset says where it turns On:
  **On at Setpoint + Offset**, every time. A Heating Element is **Heating** with **Offset (-)** (the HLT element: -1, On at 149 °F with
  a Setpoint of 150 °F); anything that only cools is **Cool** with **Offset (+)**; the Fermentor Control (Rule 6.30) is
  **Bi-Directional** with **Heat Offset (-)** and **Cool Offset (+)**. Dialogs show and take these signs; the Rule 6.29 ranges are
  shown with the same sign (Optical SSR -0.5 to -3 °F).
- **One sign everywhere** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "We need to think in plain terms No Debit a Credit Confusing", see "Plain
  terms" at the top): the saved Schema, the Brain, a Process, the .API and the dialogs all use the same sign; nothing is turned
  around in the background. A Process writes `HLT_Vessel.BM_8_DO@H_Element_HLT~element_BH.onoffset = -1` to heat and `+1` (or `1`) to cool; a
  Fermentor Control's `.heatoffset` is minus and `.cooloffset` plus. After `.onoffset =` the predictive text offers **(-) Heat** and
  **(+) Cool** (only the ones that fit the Device) and writes the sign. A Heating Element (or a Fermentor's Heat) given a plus, or a
  Fermentor's Cooling given a minus, gets a plain error. A Cool / Warm Pump may take either: plus cools, minus warms. **Both
  programs:** the BruControl Import turns BruControl's sign around (in BruControl a plus heats), in its Devices and in its Process
  lines (`.onoffset = 2` becomes `-2`; a calculation is listed in the Import notes to check by hand).
- **Overlay colors follow the Direction** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10): the Overlay choices are None, Lightning Bolt, Flashing
  Lightning Bolt, Corner Badge Bolt, See Through Lightning Bolt, Green Glow Ring, Red Glow, Orange Glow and Blue Glow. Something that
  **heats** (a Heating Element, the Heat of a Fermentor Control, a Cool / Warm Pump with a minus Offset) has no Blue Glow and no Green
  Glow Ring. Something whose Direction is **Cool** (the Cooling of a Fermentor Control, a Cool / Warm Pump with a plus Offset) has
  no Red Glow and no Orange Glow, and has Blue Glow and Green Glow Ring. Anything else has every choice but Blue Glow (**Blue is kept
  for cooling**). A choice already saved always stays in its list. A Heating Element starts with **Red Glow** (saved as no overlay), so
  the other Red Glow is not in its list.
- **Its own On / Off in its Properties** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "There are 2 On Off Type on offs ... we need something to
  correspond on the Property Dialog. A small Icon of the Element as a Toggle"): on the Current Method line, a small picture of the
  Element is a Toggle. One click turns the Device **On or Off** at once, the same as one click on it on the Tab (Rule 2.33). On / Off is
  the Device itself (the old BruControl *Enabled*); **Direct** is a method, the Element simply On or Off, so a Direct Element that is On is
  at 100 %. The picture shows On or Off as it is now.
- **One-click method spots** (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "with the Tartan Main Panel Port 42, that will be integrated into a vessel, it
  need only one click to select Duty Cycle or a click somewhere else to select PID"; "Those hot spots only need to be there when
  there is more than one control metod"): every allowed method (the main one and each one ticked) gets a small button under the
  Element on its Tab, or under its picture on a Vessel Device when it is built in, whenever **two or more** are allowed. **One
  click** on one switches the Element to that method at once; the one in use is **red**, the others **yellow** (Fritz, 2026-11-07).
  **The method box** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "an invisible box where the Methods ... can reside ... dynamically resize to how
  many Ticked"): the buttons sit in an invisible box just below the picture, **only as wide as the methods allowed**, with its middle
  under the middle of the picture. **Short method names** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "an Option to shorten the Names in the
  Ballon"): a switch in its Properties, **Short method names on its buttons**, shows **DO** (Direct), **DutyC** (Duty Cycle), **HYS**
  (Hysteresis), **PID**, **DeadB** (Deadband) and **PREC** (Precise), the same short words a Process uses. **There is no Turn Off
  button** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "Delete the Turn Off. Clicking the Heater Image does that"): one click on the picture turns it
  Off. *Replaced:* a dark Turn Off button at the end of the row while it was ON (2026-11-08 to 2026-11-09). One click on the picture of an Element built into a Vessel Device turns it
  ON or OFF at once, like a Pump (Rule 2.33); a click on its box (tile) opens its pop-up (ON, OFF, its method). A spot clicked while the Element is OFF only switches its method: picking a
  method never turns it On, with no pop-up (changed 2026-11-08, OakBarn Brewery: "Selecting a Different Method when a Heating Element
  does not turn it on, On off is By the On Off Buttton"). Any number of Elements may be ON at once (Fritz,
  2026-11-08: "I use more than a single element as they are on different AC Circuits").
  With only the main method, none show. The
  BruControl Import makes the first joined control's method the main one and ticks the others (port 42: Duty Cycle main, PID
  ticked), and explains this on its first page. This needs no Clone (Rule 4.4).
- **A Process:** `hE_1.method = "PID"` (Direct, Duty Cycle, Hysteresis, PID, Deadband, Precise, or DO, DutyC, HYS, PID, DeadB, PREC), or the
  short way on a line of its own (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "MB_25_HE_HLT_BR.HYS or MB_25_HE_HLT_BR.DutyC"): `MB_25_HE_HLT_BR.HYS`,
  `.DutyC`, `.PID`, `.DeadB`, `.PREC` or `.DO` switches it to that method, the same as `.method =`. Its settings
  by the same names the separate Devices had (`.setpoint`, `.dutycycle`, `.kp` ...). **It is turned On or Off, never "Enabled"** (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "I prefer on and Off rather than
  enabled"; "So even a Hystersis element would be Turned On or Turned Off and not use enabled"): `hE_1 = on` (or `= true`) turns it ON
  in its method. `.value` is a PID, Deadband or Precise output %; `.pv` the smoothed reading Precise holds; `.output` is its pin now (read only).
- **`.setpoint` is the Setpoint; `.target` is the same** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: ".target for backward Compatibilty but
  .setpoint is perferred. Both do exactly the same. Relabel Target to Setpoint in any Dialog."): the temperature a Heating Element,
  a Cool / Warm Pump (Rule 6.21) or an older Hysteresis, PID or Deadband Device holds is **`.setpoint`**, read or set by a Process,
  a Code Value Widget or the .API. The older **`.target`** (BruControl's word, older Processes) does exactly the same and always
  keeps working, but the Process editor offers `.setpoint` only. Every dialog calls it **Setpoint**, never Target. Help, Rules,
  examples, Process Templates and the 3 Vessel sample use `.setpoint`. The Schema file keeps the setting under its old key
  (`target`), so nothing saved before changes. A Stepper Motor's `.target` (where it moves to) is not a Setpoint and stays.
  **Both programs:** the Importer turns BruControl's Target into the Setpoint and writes a script's `target` as `.setpoint`.
- **Picking a method never turns it On** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-08: "Selecting a Different Method when a Heating Element does not
  turn it on, On off is By the On Off Button. When a Heating element is On, It simply switches to the new control method and stays
  on"). A method spot, the pop-up's method buttons or a Process `.method` only change the method, with no pop-up; turning it On or
  Off is its picture, a Clone, a Duty cycle % (below) or a Process.
- **Changing the method while it is ON** goes on at once in the new method, **except to Direct**, which turns it **OFF** first, so it
  never jumps to full power by itself.
- It is On while ON (Rule 7.9), whatever its pin is doing; it shows what it is doing (60 %, 45 % ▸ 152, ON ▸ 152, idle ▸ 152).
- **The BruControl Import** (Rule 15.4) makes BruControl's two (or more) heating controls on one port (Duty Cycle, Hysteresis, PID,
  Deadband) **one Heating Element**, starting in the first one's method. Each old name still works in a Process, made safe
  (`HLT PID` -> `HLT_PID`): `HLT_PID = true` switches it to PID and turns it ON. A second one placed on a Tab becomes a Clone of
  it. A heating control alone on its port stays as it is.
- Older Skynet Schemas with two heaters on one port keep working as they are (Rule 6.1, older Schemas).
- **`.method` is the one Process word for choosing the method of control** of **every** Device that has more than one (Fritz,
  2026-11-07: "We need to add something in the Process method for things that have more than on method of control to chhose the
  one you want to use"). Today that is the Heating Element; any later Device with more than one way of control uses `.method` too.
  In the Process editor, typing `name.method =` lists that Device's methods (for example "PID", "Duty Cycle"), and `.method`
  shows its choices beside it. A Device with only one way of control has no `.method`.
  (thread "Pick the heating method on one Element", Help 150)

**The Methods hotspot, and a display that does not jump** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20, Panel Update 8, items 2, 3, 5):
- **Methods hotspot** ("Get rid of clutter. This area of any graphic (just Outside the Vessel, adjacent to the side of a vessel same
  pixels high and wide as the Red area ... so it would work with any graphic (skynet or User) and as a is a one click hotspot toggle the
  Methods to be in View or Not"): a Heating Element's method buttons (Rule 6.19) **start hidden**. A strip as high as the Element's
  picture where the Element goes in, from the Element's end plate out to 10 px past the Vessel wall and never thinner than 25 px
  (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-21: "Hotspot too small increase to purple area"; it was a 10 px strip outside the wall), or beside the
  picture of an Element on its own Tab spot, shows them with **one click** and hides them with the next. It works with any Vessel picture, Skynet's or the user's. Only
  this screen remembers it (each phone or PC picks its own); nothing turns On or Off, and every role may use it. Not in Edit layout.
- **PID % is always two digits** ("have the % as 2 digits always unless 100%"): 00 % to 99 %, then 100 %.
- **Hysteresis idle, Heat and Cool are the same width** ("have idle, Heat and Cool all the same size so it does not jump"): what an
  Element is doing sits in a box as wide as the longest word it can show, with even-width digits, so its SV box never moves.
Help 150.

6.20 **Electrical warning** (Fritz, 2026-11-08: "WE wi;; give a General warning about electricty and that we are not
Electricians and can give no electrical advice. Consult a Licensed Electrician."; "OaKbarn Brewery or Skynet"). Wherever
Skynet talks about wiring, heating elements, SSRs, contactors, DACs or AC circuits (a Heating Element's Properties and the hover
help on its Heating method, Help 137 and 150, the BruControl Import's Heating Element note), it shows:
**"⚠ Electricity can kill. OakBarn Brewery and Skynet are not electricians and can give no electrical advice. Consult a Licensed
Electrician."** Any later page or dialog about wiring gets the same words. In a help balloon (the Heating method's) the warning comes
**first**, with a red warning triangle, in **red bold** words, then the rest of the help (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10, "Heat Method Hover
Help").
In **every Help page** the warning shows the same way: red bold words under the red warning triangle (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10:
"If Possible in any Help use the Red Text and the Icon for any Electricity Can Kill"; "And Oakbarn is fine here as well", so the
warning keeps its OakBarn Brewery words, an approved OakBarn entry under Rule 11.6). A paragraph that starts with
"⚠ Electricity can kill" is drawn this way by the Help page (public/help.js).
**The gas half** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "a disclaimer that we are not plumbers or Electricians"; 2026-11-14: "Text is good"):
wherever Skynet talks about gas burners, gas valves or gas wiring (a gas burner's Flame Out safety in its Properties and its balloon,
Help 197, the Process snippets, the BruControl Import's burner question), it shows, the same way (first, red bold, red triangle):
**"⚠ Gas can explode or kill. OakBarn Brewery and Skynet are not Electricians, Plumbers or HVAC experts. Consult a Licensed
Electrician, Plumber or HVAC professional."** (public/flameout.js GAS_WARNING). A paragraph that starts with "⚠ Gas can explode or
kill" is drawn in red by the Help page too.

6.21 **One Cool / Warm Pump, its method picked** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-08: "Cool and Warm pumps: One Port, One Device, with a
Method field"; "the suggested type is plain, e.g. MB_D5_CPMP_Cool~Pump_FR"). A pump that a temperature switches (a glycol pump that
cools a fermenter, or a pump that brings warm water) is **ONE Pump Device on its port** (One Port, One Device, Rule 6.1), never a
pump plus a separate Hysteresis Device. Its **Device Type ID is CPMP** (Cool / Warm Pump), so its suggested name reads plainly, for
example `MB_D5_CPMP_Cool~Pump_FR`. It has a **Method** field, as a Heating Element has (Rule 6.19), with a pump's own methods only:
**Direct** (On/Off: a click or a Process) or **Hysteresis** (its Temperature Probe, `.input`, and a Setpoint: a **plus Offset cools** (On above the Setpoint), a
**minus Offset warms**). A Process changes it with `.method` and reads `.setpoint`, `.onoffset` and `.ondelay`, the same words a
Heating Element uses. Methods that switch a motor many times a minute (Duty Cycle, PID, Deadband, Precise) are not offered for it.
- **Both programs:** the Panel shows the Method, Probe, Setpoint and offsets in the Pump's Properties and the Brain runs it like a
  Heating Element's Hysteresis. The BruControl Importer makes a BruControl pump that had a Hysteresis (or another control) on its port,
  alone or beside its on/off output, one CPMP Pump that starts in that method, with its settings and probe, and lists it in the report.


6.22 **Dual Throw: a second Port that is always the opposite** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "Add it", after the BruControl compare;
as BruControl's Dual Throw output, its DualThrowPortNum and DualThrowDelay). A Digital Out (a plain output, a Motorized valve, a
Pump; never a Heating Element or a Manual valve) may have a **Dual Throw second Port** on the same Interface and a **Dual Throw
delay** in milliseconds. **ON** = its own Port on and the second Port off; **OFF** = its own Port off and the second Port on. The
Port that goes off goes off first; the other one comes on after the delay, so the two are **never on together**. It is for a valve
with an **Open wire and a Close wire**, or a motor that turns forward on one relay and backward on another.
- **One Interface Port, one Device (Rule 6.1):** the second Port is taken by its Device. It drops off every Available Ports list, and
  it can't be the Device's own Port.
- **Where:** the ⬢ **Pin attributes** pop-up beside the Interface (with Invert and One-shot), on a Digital Out's and a Motorized
  valve's Properties and in the Add box. None (the default) = no second Port. Invert (Active Low) inverts both Ports.
- **OFF is a state, not "no power":** when everything is switched off (Rule 6.4, another Schema), a Dual Throw Device goes OFF, so
  its second Port comes **on** (a valve is driven closed). Only a lost link (the board's own safety) turns both Ports off.
- **Both programs:** the Panel's Brain switches the two Ports; the BruControl Importer keeps BruControl's DualThrowPortNum (-1 =
  none) and DualThrowDelay and lists each one in the Import notes. Help 167.


6.23 **Predictive Hysteresis: no overshoot, never more starts** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "I think of it as smoothing the
overshoot. Maybe make all the Hysteresis Predictive unless that could hurt a compressor type hardware"). Every Hysteresis (the
Hysteresis Device, a Heating Element's Hysteresis method, a Cool / Warm Pump's Hysteresis) is **Predictive** unless its **Predictive**
switch is turned off. After it turns off, the heat (or cold) already on its way keeps the reading going past the OFF point. Skynet
watches how far it coasts each time (averaging the last runs) and turns off that much **before** the Setpoint, so the reading settles at
the Setpoint instead of going past it.
- **Safe for a compressor:** the ON point moves down by the same amount, so the swing between ON and OFF, and how often it starts, stay
  the same as without Predictive. The **On delay** (the shortest time off before it may start again) is always kept. The early OFF is
  never more than half the On offset.
- **What it costs:** the low point of each swing is lower by the same amount (for cooling: the high point is higher).
- It learns again after its method changes. Switch it off for the plain BruControl way (`predictive` off in its Properties).
- **Both programs:** the Panel's Brain runs it; the BruControl Importer leaves every imported Hysteresis Predictive (BruControl's own
  Predictive Hysteresis switch is not copied: Skynet's way is on). Help 168.


6.24 **Calibrations and Smoothing on every reading, in plain boxes** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "adding those calibrations are good as they are
similar to other programs and not proprietary to BruControl"; "build a Calibration with Measured Voltage vs PWM %"). A Temperature
Probe, an Analog In and a Flow meter have a **Calibrations** list. Each calibration works on the result of the one before, top to
bottom (layered, as BruControl's): **Linear Offset**, **Linear Multiplier**, **Linear Divider**, **Floor**, **Ceiling**, **Thermistor
(Steinhart-Hart)**, **Celsius / Fahrenheit / Kelvin** conversions and a **Lookup Table** (reading, value pairs).
- **Plain boxes, never typed code:** ➕ Add calibration, a dropdown for its kind, a box for each number, ↑ ↓ to change the order, ✕ to
  remove, and a switch to turn one off without losing it. A probe's Properties show them as one line (More calibrations) with the ⬢.
- **Where they start:** a probe and a flow meter (its rate) start from their own reading (after the probe type's formula and its
  offsets); an Analog In with calibrations starts from its raw 0-1023 reading (instead of its Signal settings), as in BruControl.
- **Smoothing** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "Smoothing might be added to more things than a Counter"; "my 10K NTC would be better
  with smoothing as they sometimes jump"; BruControl's Avg Weight): **Smoothing %** (`avgWeight`) is how much each new reading counts;
  the shown value moves that many % of the way to it, 100 = none. On every Temperature Probe, Analog In, Flow meter (the rate; the
  Total never), Scale (weight and volume; Auto tare still works) and Counter. Empty = **25 % for a thermistor (NTC) probe**
  (BruControl's default), 100 % for everything else. A Counter gets a **Rate** (`.rate`): counts per second over its **Sampling
  Period** (1 to 10 seconds, empty = 1, as BruControl's Counter Input), then smoothed; the Count never is. A Process, an Alarm and the
  Tab see the smoothed number; `.raw` is the reading before smoothing. The Importer keeps Avg Weight as Smoothing %. Help 171.
- **Measured volts** on a PWM output and an Analog output: pairs of its setting (a PWM output's %) and the volts measured there with a
  meter, because a DAC seldom gives exactly 10 V at full and each one is different. It shows `≈ 7.0 V` beside the value, a Process
  reads `.volts` and sets one: `My_DAC.volts = 7.5` sets the % the pairs say gives 7.5 V.
- **Both programs:** the BruControl Importer keeps each Analog In's and probe's calibrations in order, with its Text Format (Decimal
  Places, Prefix, Suffix as Units). A PWM output's BruControl calibrations are not copied (BruControl counts it 0-255, Skynet in %) and
  are listed in the Import notes. Help 169.

**A smooth temperature on the screen** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20, Panel Update 8, item 4: "Smooth the Temperature so it does not jump on the screen";
"It was jittery and distracting. More smoothin in simulation mode"): a Temperature Probe's reading on the screen is the average of
its readings from the **last 5 seconds**, or the **last 15 seconds** when its board is in Simulation. Only what is shown: the Brain,
the heating methods, Processes, Alarms, the Database and the .API use the real reading (Smoothing %, Rule 6.24, still smooths that).
A jump of 2 degrees or more shows at once. Help 171.

6.25 **One Hydrometer Device, a Template for each kind** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "Add all the Hydrometer Types as Hydrometer
Templates, Tilt, Tilt Pro, ISpindel and I know there or others. Almost all have a Method so you can connect more than 1. Tilt has you
purchase a difference color. There may be a need to add all the properties of the different Types to the General Hydrometer
Properties but Grey it if not applicable to the type"). The Hydrometer is one Device (Type ID **Hydro**, a virtual port 200, 201 ...,
Rule 6.2). Its **Template** (Tilt, Tilt Pro, Tilt Pro Mini, iSpindel, GravityMon, Floaty, BrewBrain Float, RAPT Pill, PLAATO, Other)
picks which of its settings it uses; every setting is in its Properties and the ones its Template does not use are **greyed out**.
- **Connection** (not "Method", which is the Control Method of Rule 6.19): Bluetooth, Wi-Fi to Skynet, or the maker's cloud, as its
  Template allows.
- **More than one:** a Tilt is told apart by its **Tilt Color**, every other kind by its **Hardware ID** (its Name or chip ID). Both are
  **mandatory** for their kind (OakBarn Brewery: "for a Tilt Color and Id are mandatory") and never shared: one Hydrometer per Tilt
  Color (any Tilt kind), one per Hardware ID. **Never by IP address** (OakBarn Brewery: "No tracking by IP Address"): a router may
  change it. A hydrometer the Brain hears that no Hydrometer has yet is offered in the Hardware ID box, so nobody looks it up.
  **A Tilt's Color can't be left blank** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "if you select Tilt as type, and you leave color null and exit
  the field A Pop up that states Color for a Tilt cannot be left blank, choose a Color"): leaving the Tilt Color box blank pops up
  "The Color for a Tilt cannot be left blank." and goes back to the box, in the Panel's Properties (the Rule 18.28 pop-up) and on the
  Importer's Hydrometers page. The Color is a drop-down list. On the Importer page, picking a Tilt type goes straight to its Color, and the
  box a type does not use (Tilt Color or Hardware ID) is greyed out.
- **SG, °Plato and °Brix all the time** (OakBarn Brewery: "List SG, Brix, and Plato all The time and on a graph choose which to display
  but easy to switch right on the graph"): `.sg`, `.plato`, `.brix`; its Gravity units pick what its value shows. On a Graph a
  Hydrometer's line has an SG / °P / °Bx switch (each screen keeps its own pick).
- **Smoothing** (Smoothing weight %, as an Analog Input's): Tilts start at 20 %, the others at 100 % (none). **Lost signal** after a
  number of minutes (Tilts 15, others 60): it shows No signal and `.lost` is true. Original Gravity (`.og`) gives `.abv`.
- **Database and .API** as every other Device (OakBarn Brewery: "Database for readings would be handled like any other database").
  One that talks through the web (Wi-Fi to Skynet or the cloud) has **.API On (Read Only), greyed out** (OakBarn Brewery: ".API may
  need to be on and greyed out for any that talk via a web interface only").
- **Read by hand is a Process command, not a Device** (OakBarn Brewery: "Glass and Refractometer Readings are external to the Program,
  but there could be a command to Take a Reading that acts like a Wait until a Reading Question is answered"): `take_reading Name`
  (Name: a Hydrometer, a Value Widget or a gGlobal). A pop-up asks **Refractometer** or **Glass** (a tick box each). A Refractometer
  goes to the SG box and Save at once; a Glass sample first counts down its minutes to cool, then the same SG box pops up. **Send to
  Database now** is a tick box; unticked, Save is Exit (No Database). **Pause** (only a person) hides it, and it pops up again in 5
  minutes. The Process waits until it is saved.
- **Both programs:** the BruControl Importer makes a Hydrometer Input a Tilt with its Tilt Color on the same port, and its
  Hydrometers page lists the same Templates with Tilt Color and Hardware ID. Help 170.
- **Bluetooth** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "Two PRs", Bluetooth the second): a **listener** near the fermenter hears the adverts
  and sends them as they are to `POST /api/hydrometer/bluetooth` (same rules as Wi-Fi: your own network, or the API key). Two
  listeners: an ESP32 with `firmware/ESP32_Hydrometer` (works with any Brain, Windows too), or a Raspberry Pi's own Bluetooth
  (`firmware/Pi_Bluetooth`). The Brain reads the adverts itself: a Tilt (any Tilt kind) by its Tilt Color, a RAPT Pill by its Hardware ID
  (its Bluetooth address, offered in the Hardware ID box once heard). Only Hydrometers whose Connection is Bluetooth take them. A real
  reading stops the Simulator's pretend one for 10 minutes. The makers' clouds come later.

6.26 **Data Display: pick which value shows** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "Not only Primary. Just have a DataDisplay and able to
pick which one. If there was a script command, we just write our Process to do it either way or have two different ways to do it to
make it back compatible with BruControl"). A Device with more than one value (PID, Deadband, Hysteresis, Duty Cycle, a Heating Element
run by a method, Flow meter, Scale, a PWM or Analog output with Measured volts) has **Data Display** in its
Properties: the first choice shows them all, as before, or one of its values (for example a Flow meter's Rate or Total). BruControl had
a Primary Value and a Show Secondary Value switch; Skynet lists every value. A Process changes it: `Flow_1.display = "Total"` (its key
or its words, any capitals; `""` puts back its Properties' pick). A Flow meter's `.value` follows it (BruControl's Primary Value: its
Total when Total is picked), so BruControl scripts work either way. **Both programs:** the Importer turns Show Secondary Value off into
the main value's pick and lists it in the notes. Help 174.

6.27 **Board settings and Board Talk** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "You could add the Board things also as it is possible
sometimes to use communications to the board to find or fix a problem. There was no real explaination on how to communicate or what
to send and what is reply meant"; changed 2026-11-15, Add Interface markup). Each Interface has **Board settings** (its ⚙ Change
dialog, both programs), each with its own Hover Help:
- **On** (Off = never opened; saved as `enabled`). When a board is Off none of its Devices work; a board must be On and in
  communication with the Brain to do any action.
- **🔌 Test Communication** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "Change Pause Communication To Test Communication. Have a Step by Step how
  to test with a sample responses and maybe a way to send specific code for common Comm Errors. Plain not technical"): a step by step
  pop-up: 1 is the board On and talking (what the Brain sees now), 2 👋 Say Hello (sends HELLO; a Skynet board answers with its name
  and program version within 5 seconds), 3 sample answers in plain words, 4 what to check when there is no answer (USB or network).
  Nothing on the board is turned On or Off. A new Interface is tested once it is added.
- **Answer wait** (seconds without a word from the board before the Devices page says "no answer"; 2 to 600, default 10;
  BruControl's Response Timeout).
- **Lost Comm** (Rule 6.3): a safety, with the reminder that the user, watching the brewery, is the primary safety.
- **Diagnostic logging**: normally Off; every line, with plain words, to a file a day in the data folder's logs/boards. Used only to
  find a problem, by someone who knows what the log means: Skynet gives no communication help, the log is only the means for the
  user or another person to find it.
- **Network port** (Ethernet / WiFi), which must match the program on the board (Skynet's: 4100).
- **No Baud** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "Baud would come from Board Type ... If not delete"): every Skynet board program talks at
  115200, so the Brain always uses it.
**Board Talk** (💬 on the Devices page, admins) is a window with every line to (→) and from (←) the board, each with its time and
its meaning in plain words, Hide PING, ⏸ Pause communications (only PING is sent, so the board keeps its outputs; what the board says
is shown but not used; Talk again sends every setting and output), and a box to send a line (sent even while paused). Help 177 lists
every line in plain words (public/boardtalk.js, the same words as the window; the details are in docs/DEVICE_PROTOCOL.md). BruControl
Import: Enabled and Response Timeout (ms to seconds) are kept; Baud is not copied (Skynet's programs use 115200); Logging is listed in
the notes, not turned on (it writes every line); Refresh Interval is not copied. Help 76, 177.
*Replaced:* Pause communications and Baud (USB speed) were boxes in the Interface dialog (2026-11-09 to 2026-11-15).

6.28 **Last One Rules** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09, its own draft: "All for One, One For All"): **The last Device with the same
Interface and Port controls the action.** How can there be more than one Device with the same Interface and Port (Rule 6.1)? There
cannot be, but there are two cases that may look like more than one:
1. **A Clone** (Rule 4.4).
   a. A Clone is an exact copy of its Device and is like the Borg.
   b. A Clone and its Parent have one set of Properties. Change one and it changes the other. They are **totally dependent** and just
      a reflection of each other. You can consider them one, except for the **Last One Rules!** Whoever in this group turns something
      On, all of the group turn On. Because of this, think of the Device and its Clones as ONE. In this Rule, **Device** means the
      Device and all its Clones, unless a Clone is the topic (**Last One Rules!**).
2. **An Integrated Instance** on a Vessel Device (Rule 6.1).
   a. It has the Properties it inherited from where it was made, but unlike a Clone it becomes totally independent, except for the
      **Last One Rules!** It is more like Bob of the Bobiverse (We Are Legion) than the Borg.
   b. An Integrated Instance of a Device has its own independent Properties that have no link to the original Device or Template,
      except that they share the same Interface and Port.
3. In both cases the Interface and Port cannot be used to make a new Device, and neither one can change its Interface or Port.
4. **LAST One Rules!** And most important for the On or method action of something like a Heater: whenever a Device commands
   something to turn On, all its Instances are turned Off. Whenever an Instance commands something to turn On, the Device and the
   other Instances are all turned Off. **Only one, the Device or one Instance of the same Interface and Port, can be On at one time**
   (that is really why they are not truly independent and not really separate: all just one happy family). The last one turned Off
   turns the Port Off, so every one on it is Off. Help 180.

6.29 **Heat Hysteresis by what switches it** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "Heat Only Hysteresis: Offset Range from .5 to 3 is allowed
for heating elements with Optical SSRs"; for a Contactor, OakBarn Brewery OK'd the suggestion of 2 to 5 with an On delay of at least
60 seconds: "Right track"). A Heating Element (Rule 6.19, on its own or built into a Vessel Device) has a **Hardware Controller**: **Optical
SSR** (solid state relay, the start), **Contactor** or **Mechanical relay**. Its **Hysteresis** (Offset with a minus, Rule 6.19) may only use:

| Hardware Controller | Offset | On delay |
|---|---|---|
| Optical SSR | -0.5 to -3 °F | any |
| Contactor | -1 to -5 °F | at least 10 seconds |
| Mechanical relay | -1 to -5 °F | at least 10 seconds |
| DAC / 0-10 V | -0.5 to -3 °F | any |

With a °C probe the numbers are converted (-0.3 to -1.7 °C; -0.6 to -2.8 °C). A Contactor's contacts wear each time they close, so it
heats less often and longer. A Heating Element only heats, so a plus Offset on it is refused (Rule 6.19).
- **Picking a Hardware Controller sets the On offset and the On delay** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10, with a table): Optical SSR
  **-0.5 °F and 0 seconds**, Contactor **-1 °F and 10 seconds**, Mechanical relay **-1 °F and 10 seconds** (the offset converted for a °C probe).
  So a Contactor or Mechanical relay may hold -1 to -5 °F with an On delay of at least 10 seconds. The reason is in the balloons of Hardware Controller and On offset; no
  range line is written in the dialog.
- **Properties:** Hardware Controller is under Heating method, its range in its balloon; when Hysteresis is Enabled but is not the Current
  Method, its On offset and On delay still show. **Save refuses** a number outside the range and says what is allowed.
- **A Process or the .API** setting `.onoffset` or `.ondelay` outside the range gets the same plain error. The Brain never runs a heat
  Hysteresis outside its range, whatever was saved.
- **Both programs:** the Panel's Properties and Brain check it; the BruControl Import starts every heating element as an Optical
  SSR (BruControl does not say what switches it), brings an Offset outside -0.5 to -3 °F to the nearest end, and lists each one
  in the Import notes. Help 181. The Fermentor Control's Heat follows it too (Rule 6.30).

6.30 **The Fermentor Control** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "an integrated Fermentor control that heats and Cools with Hysteresis";
"Has three integrated devices 1. Heater 2. Cooling 3. Temperature Probe"; "flashing a Light Bulb is not good either"; fermentation is
exothermic "Only in the beginning"). A Fermentor Control holds the beer at **one Setpoint** with **Hysteresis on both sides**:
1. **Its three Devices:** the **Heat** (a Heating Element, a Light or a plain Digital Out: heat mat, heat wrap, ceramic heat
   emitter, lamp), the **Cooling** (a plain Digital Out for a freezer or fridge, a Pump for glycol, or a Motorized valve for glycol;
   never a Manual valve) and the **Temperature Probe** that reads the beer. Heat only or Cooling only is allowed; the probe is a must.
2. **Heat comes on** at Setpoint + **Heat Offset (-)** (below the Setpoint, -1 °F to start), **Cooling** at Setpoint + **Cool
   Offset (+)** (above it, 1 °F to start), Rule 6.19; both stop at the Setpoint, a little before it with Predictive Hysteresis (Rule 6.23, learned for each side).
3. **Never both On.** One must have been Off for the **Changeover wait** (300 seconds to start) before the other may start (once
   the other side has run; a fresh start waits only its own On delay).
4. **Short-cycle protection on both sides:** an **On delay** (the shortest time Off before it starts again: Heat 60 s, Cool 300 s
   to start) and a **Shortest run** (once on, it stays on at least: Heat 60 s, Cool 120 s). Turning the Fermentor Control On starts
   each side's On delay, so a freezer just plugged in is never started at once. The Mode or Off stops a side at once.
5. **Mode:** Heat & Cool, Heat only, Cool only. Heat and Cool are equal (fermentation makes heat at the start, needs heat at the end).
6. A Heating Element as its Heat runs in **Direct** while the Fermentor Control is On; its offset and On delay are kept to its
   **Hardware Controller** range (Rule 6.29).
7. **No reading:** both Off, and it shows No reading.
8. **Built into a Fermentor Vessel Device** (Rule 5.31) by the Vessel Device Builder (Rule 19.5, question 14): the Heat and Cooling
   are built in **without a spot** and keep their own names, called VesselName.DeviceName in a Process (Rule 5.31, Help 180);
   the probe is on its spot. The Fermentor Control itself is called by **its own plain name** (the vessel's Label): `FV1 = on`,
   `FV1.setpoint`, `FV1.mode`, `FV1.heatoffset`, `FV1.cooloffset`, `FV1.changeover`, `FV1.heatdelay`, `FV1.heatminrun`,
   `FV1.cooldelay`, `FV1.coolminrun`; `FV1.doing` (Off, Idle, Heating, Cooling, Waiting to heat, Waiting to cool, No reading) is
   read only. It has no Port of its own.
9. **One click** turns it On or Off (Rule 2.44); **a click on its probe opens its Setpoint** (Rule 2.43).
10. **Both programs:** the Panel's Properties, Vessel Device Builder and Brain; the BruControl Import makes ONE Fermentor Control
    from a heating Hysteresis (a plus OnOffset in BruControl) and a cooling Hysteresis (a minus OnOffset in BruControl) on the same probe, keeps the two
    outputs' names and Ports, takes the Setpoint, offsets and the longer of the two On delays, and lists it in the notes. Help 182.

6.31 **Sleep, Windows Update and restarts** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-12: "With a New Build, most people will likely start right on a
PC Computer and not the Pi as the "Brain", so we need to fix the Sleep Issue and What Happens during an Update and Restart, or even a
User Introduced Restart"). The Processes and controls run in Skynet Brewer on the Brain, never in the browser, so closing a browser
never stops a brew. On every Brain (Windows, Mac, Linux, Pi):
1. **Kept awake while brewing:** while any Process runs or anything is On, Skynet asks the computer not to sleep (the screen may go
   dark). Nothing is asked when nothing is brewing.
2. **Off before it stops:** however Skynet is closed (☰ Menu, the window's X, Ctrl+C, Windows shutting down or restarting), every
   output is turned Off first. A power cut or a crash is covered by each board's Lost link (Rule 6.3).
3. **Nothing comes back On by itself:** after a restart everything starts Off and no Process carries on where it was (a Process set
   to start when the panel starts still starts from its top). Woken from sleep during a brew, everything is set Off and every
   Process is stopped, so a board that talks again is never told to turn something back On.
   **The Resume button** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-12: "Resume Button"): for **15 minutes after the stop**, the notice has
   **▶ Resume** (Operator or Admin). One click turns back On what was On (outputs, PWM, controls, running timers) and starts each
   Process again **at its step** (no step: the line it was on) with its variables; a Stepper never moves by itself. After 15 minutes
   the button is gone.
4. **A notice on every screen:** after a stop or a sleep during a brew, it says when, what was On, and which Process was on which
   step and line; when Windows has an update waiting to restart, a yellow notice says to restart before brewing. ✕ closes it on
   every screen (Operator or Admin).
5. **Setup:** "Start Skynet Brewer by itself each time you sign in to Windows?" (a Startup folder shortcut, no admin rights). Skynet
   never changes Windows settings itself; Help 190 says how to set Active hours, sign-in after an update, the laptop lid and power
   return.
6. **Both programs:** the Panel does all of this; the BruControl Import controls nothing, so it needs none of it (its Build page
   runs no board and shows no notice). The same Setup asks the question for both. Help 190.

6.32 **The Brain runs in the Background; Standby** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "Windows PowerShell remains open after Skynet Panel
is closed"; "Maybe Change that the Brain is in the Back ground and somewhat separate on a Computer ... the Skynet Panel acts like a
remote Browser Connection at all times"; "If Pi is Powered, Admin Only can restart"; "Only Admin User can put Brain in standby or
remove that status"). The Brain is the program that runs the boards, Processes and controls; every panel window, phone and computer
is only a browser showing it.
1. **Windows: no window stays open.** Skynet Brewer (Skynet_Brewer.bat) shows its black window only for the first-time steps
   (Node.js, USB board support), then starts the Brain in the Background with no window (lib/startbrain.js) and closes. The Brain
   still gets Windows' shut down, restart and sign out message, so everything goes Off first (Rule 6.31). What it writes goes to
   data\brain.log (a new one each start, the last one kept as .old). It did not start: the black window stays open with the last lines.
   The Brain must keep running after the program that started it ends (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: the panel window opened, then
   "Failed to fetch": Windows had ended the Brain together with Skynet Brewer). On Windows it is started through cmd's `start /b`
   (lib/brainstate.js spawnInBackground), so it runs on by itself and keeps its hidden window; the same when the Brain starts itself
   again (Standby, Start).
   The panel window is opened by the program that was double-clicked, never by the Brain in the Background (OakBarn Brewery,
   2026-11-14: "Full installer only starts the Brain": a program with no window can't bring a window to the front). **Skynet Panel**
   (Desktop and Start menu) opens the panel window; the Brain is started first if it is not running. The Setup's last page starts the
   Brain and opens the panel. Double-clicked again while it runs: only the panel window opens. Start menu > Skynet Brewer > **Stop the Skynet Brain** stops it
   the normal way (lib/stoppanel.js). Skynet never changes Windows settings: no service, no admin rights.
2. **Close** is only on the Brain's own computer (Rule 2.25).
3. **Put the Brain in Standby** (☰ Menu, **Admins only**, on any other screen and on a Pi): the same tick box warnings and Back as
   Rule 2.25. Every output Off, every Process stopped (a brew is written down, Rule 6.31), and the Brain starts again in Standby: **no
   board connected, no Process, no MQTT, nothing can be changed**, and every screen shows only "The Brain is in Standby" (who, when).
4. **Only an Admin starts it again**, from **any** screen, near or far (Tailscale too): ▶ Start the Brain on the Standby page. Anyone
   else sees "Sign in as an Admin". The Brain starts the normal way, everything Off; a brew that was stopped gets its notice and Resume
   (Rule 6.31). Standby is kept in data\standby.json, so it **stays in Standby after a restart or a power cut** until an Admin starts it.
5. **Both programs:** the BruControl Import also runs in the Background with no black window, and its own Close Importer button stops
   it. It controls nothing, so it has no Standby. Help 95.

6.33 **Flame Out safety for gas burners** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "WE could have a sfety built in if the temperature decrease
while a Gas Burner is on"; 2026-11-14: "Yes to both", "Also in Skynet have the software backup of decreasing Temp (with smoothing for
false feedback)"). A **gas burner** is a Heating Element with **Gas burner** switched On (a burner on a gas valve) or a **Solenoid Gas
Valve** (DO@Valve_Sgas, with its Temperature Probe picked). While its gas valve is **really open** (Direct: while On; a control
method: while its pin is on), the Brain watches its probe about once a second:
- **Smoothing:** the reading is averaged over **30 seconds**; one wild reading (more than 5 °F in one second, or a probe error) is
  thrown away; one that stays 10 seconds is real.
- **No rise:** after **5 minutes** of burning the average must have risen **1 °F** (0.5 °C); it rests within 3 °F of the **Boil point**
  (212 °F to start; lower at altitude).
- **Drop:** once the pot has started warming after the valve opened, a fall of **1 °F** (0.5 °C) below its highest trips it.
- **Pause:** **10 minutes** (the burner pop-up's **⏸ Pause Flame Out**, or `name.flameout = "pause 10"`), for the lid, cold water or
  doughing in; it watches again by itself.
- **A trip** turns the gas Off and the burner's **Igniter** Off, sets `.flameout_tripped`, and shows **"Burner may be out: check the
  flame. Gas is turned off."** in red on every screen, beeping and spoken once, until closed. **Nothing turns back on by itself**
  (as Rule 6.31); turning the burner back On clears `.flameout_tripped`.
- **Flame safety** (the brewer picks it; Skynet cannot check it): **Thermocouple gas valve (UL or CSA listed)**, the real flame safety
  (a pilot heats a 0 to 30 mV thermocouple; the valve shuts all gas by itself; it is switched by 24 VDC (preferred, only a valve
  labelled 24 VDC) or by a true 24 VAC step-down transformer, through a relay on a Digital Out), or **None (plain solenoid valve)**.
  These standing pilot valves are made for **low-pressure** gas (propane about 11 inches of water column); most brewing burners use a
  high-pressure regulator, so Help and the balloon say plainly to have a licensed gas professional match the valve, regulator and burner.
  Three ways in Help 197 (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "Baso $$$$ so not for Home Brewer"; "high pressure propane is more standard
  for a Home Brewer"): 1. high pressure + 24 V solenoid only (None: cheapest, only the slow Flame Out); 2. low pressure + 24 VAC VR8200
  type valve (real flame safety, the best for the money, heats more slowly); 3. high pressure + a high-pressure thermocouple safety
  pilot valve (for example BASO H19, costly) + 24 V solenoid (real flame safety).
  **Recommended: the UL or CSA listed way (2 or 3).** **For Information Only** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "Big Caveat with this one.
  For Information Only. One Way some Hpme Brewers do it with high pressure and then recoomend th UL Way"; "No mention of Skynet or
  Aokbarn only to say were are NOT..."): a high-pressure daisy chain some home brewers build (a K-type thermocouple in the flame, a
  stand-alone temperature controller's relay in series with the brew controller's relay ahead of a 24 V high-pressure gas solenoid, a
  timed ignition bypass of 10 seconds to start (OakBarn Brewery: "10 sec might be good starting point"), at most 3 tries a minute
  apart). Help 197 shows it under a big caveat, never as recommended, supported or endorsed by Skynet or OakBarn Brewery, which are
  named there only in the gas warning. Flame safety list: **Flame-out cutoff (K-type thermocouple and controller, not listed)**, whose
  note says it is not listed and not recommended.
  Flame Out stays On as the software backup either way, and the dialog says which: "a backup", or "a helper, not a flame safety device".
- **Flame Out** is **On to start** for every gas burner and for the Schema Builder's gas burners; it can be switched Off.
- Process words: `.flameout` (On / Off / "pause 10"), `.flameout_paused` (minutes left, 0 ends a pause), `.flameout_tripped` (read
  only). Help 197 has two Process snippets (gas burner control, and the software backup in Process words), each with the gas warning
  (Rule 6.20).
- The gas warning (Rule 6.20, the gas half) starts the Flame Out section's balloon.
- **Not a UL safety** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "it is not a UL Safety and should not be relied on. Monitor the Burner."): the
  Flame Out's Properties note, its balloon, the burner pop-up and Help 197 say "This is not a UL listed safety and should not be relied on. Always monitor the burner." (the same words
  in the BruControl Import's burner question).

6.35 **Every standard Arduino board; the Mega is the standard; 3.3 V warnings** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "I want all standard
Arduino Boards added. Brew Control had a lot but no Opta which I have and would like to intergrate"; "I also have a Grandcentral";
"Plan Skynet for a Mega and the warnings if you use a 3.3v board instead"; "Make those Warnings"; "you could have a mixed system of 3.3
and 5v I do").
- **The Board list** (public/boards.js): Arduino Mega 2560, Uno R3, Uno R4 (Minima or WiFi), Nano, Nano Every, Leonardo, Micro, Due,
  GIGA R1 WiFi, Nano ESP32, Adafruit Grand Central M4, Adafruit Feather M0 (WiFi), Arduino Opta (Rule 6.36), ESP32, ESP8266 and Raspberry Pi. No "Other".
- **The Mega 2560 is the board Skynet plans and wires for**; it is first in the list and its Port lists do not change. Every other
  board can be used: its own Ports, true PWM Ports, counter Ports, analog Ports (with BruControl's numbers on the Mega and the Grand
  Central), SPI, OneWire and I2C Ports, and its own Connection choices. A Port a board does not have is refused (the Pi already was,
  Rule 6.13). Uno R4: interrupt (counter) Ports D0-D3, D8 (the ones Arduino's Minima and WiFi pinouts share, each its own), and Help says its Ports give at most 8 mA
  (no warning pop-up). From the makers' pinouts (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, answers 1-9: yes): Leonardo and Micro A6-A11 (= D4, D6,
  D8, D9, D10, D12; one pin, two names, so one Device); Grand Central counter Ports D0-D3, D6, D7, D14-D19, D23, D28, D32, D33 (one per
  interrupt) and PWM on D20, D21 too; Nano ESP32 D1 offered last for outputs (a 499 ohm resistor in its line) and one warning for A4-A7
  on WiFi (the second ADC can't read while WiFi is on); ESP32 GPIO16, GPIO17 offered last with one warning (not free on WROVER boards);
  Raspberry Pi GPIO 12, 13, 18, 19 (hardware PWM) read "Best for True PWM: see Help" in blue. ESP32: GPIO 6-11 never offered, GPIO 34-39 inputs only; ESP32 and ESP8266 start-up pins offered last.
- **Rule 6.10 on every Ethernet shield or module**: D10 is not offered on any board connected by an Ethernet shield or module, not only
  the Mega (an ESP32 with its own jack has no shield). Rule 6.9 (RTD CS pins) and 6.11 (SD card pin) stay Mega only.
- **3.3 V warnings, one each, per board**: a Device put on a Port of a 3.3 V board (Due, GIGA, Nano ESP32, Grand Central, Feather M0,
  ESP32, ESP8266, Raspberry Pi) shows one warning, once, when it is put there: 1 a Digital Input (wire it to 3.3 V, never 5 V), 2 a 0-5 V
  analog sensor (voltage divider, 3.3 V sensor or ADS1115), 3 a relay output (many 5 V relay modules do not switch from 3.3 V; the
  electrical warning, Rule 6.20, follows it). Then the brewer decides (one warning is enough). 5 V and 3.3 V boards may be mixed: each
  board is its own Interface, and the warnings go by the board each Device is on.
- **The BruControl Import** picks the Board from BruControl's board type for every board in the list (Grand Central, Feather M0,
  ESP8266, Due, Uno ...); any other is left "(pick the board)".
- **Firmware**: the Skynet program on the board is written and tested for the Mega. The shared firmware for the other boards (Rule
  6.12) is written with every board in this list in mind (pin maps, 3.3 V and 5 V, PWM and analog differences). The **Arduino Opta**
  is in the list (Rule 6.36).
  *Replaced:* "The Arduino Opta is not in the list until its program is planned and Fritz agrees (Panel Updates sandbox)." (2026-11-19)
Help 206 (and French), Help 3, 69, 76.

6.36 **The Arduino Opta** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "Opta can be built now as well"; "OPta would run anything it can based on the
Pins"; Panel Updates entry 34 step 1; Arduino's pinout AFX00001/2/3, Skynet_Private Plans/Board_Pinouts/).
- **In the Board list** (Lite AFX00003, RS485 AFX00001, WiFi AFX00002), after the Feather M0. Its Ports go by name: **Relay 1-4**
  (R1-R4; D0-D3 on the board, Normally Open, at most 250 V AC and 10 A) and the inputs **I1-I8** (A0-A7 on the board, each 0-24 V
  digital or 0-10 V analog). It runs on 24 V. No D10 (Ethernet is built in, so no Port is kept for it), no OneWire, SPI or I2C Ports.
- **Like a Mega** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "Make the Temperature Probes or other Things like heater control just like how a mega
  does it as you cannot directly attach a probe to any pin and it will work. You need something besides the Mega (even one wire is
  external circuit. If it requires an expansion Module, then add that in the Help"): every Device can go on an Opta. A relay takes any
  output, an input takes any reading; only a reading on a relay is refused (an output on an input already is). Ports read *relay* or
  *input: digital or 0-10 V*.
- **One warning saying what has to be added** (Rule 6.20 one warning): a temperature probe, by probe type (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19:
  "Do the best for 10KNTC Probes ( and support for all th eprobes on our Skynet Probes. JUst add the addition Cu=ircuits."; Help 206
  table): 10K NTC, PT1000, thermocouple = a 0-10 V transmitter on I1-I8; PT100 = the Opta Analog Expansion A0602 or a transmitter;
  LM35, TMP36 = only a 5 V supply; DS18B20 = no OneWire on an Opta (keep it on a Mega, swap the probe, or a DS18B20-to-RS485 module once
  RS485 is built); PWM or Pseudo PWM on a relay (an SSR on the Opta Digital Expansion D1608S, or On/Off by
  Duty Cycle or Hysteresis; with the electrical warning); a stepper (a stepper driver with its own controller); an ADS1115 (no I2C pins:
  0-10 V straight to I1-I8, or the A0602). Otherwise a relay gives one warning (Normally Open, 250 V AC, 10 A, with the electrical
  warning) and an Analog In one 0-10 V warning. Help 206 names the modules.
  *Replaced:* "A relay takes a Digital Out, a Duty Cycle, a Hysteresis, a PID or a Deadband, On/Off only: never PWM or Pseudo PWM" and
  "Refused on an Opta: every temperature Device (DS18B20, RTD, thermocouple, NTC) and the stepper" (2026-11-19, before merge).
- **Connection:** USB, Ethernet (built in), WiFi (Opta WiFi only); rated like a Mega, WiFi like an ESP32 (Rule 6.3). RS485 and
  Bluetooth later. Expansion modules (D1608E, D1608S, A0602) later.
- **Firmware:** the Opta's own program is step 6 of the firmware plan, after the Mega and the Grand Central (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19:
  "No, I will be testing with a Mega and Grand central").
- **The BruControl Import:** BruControl has no Opta, so nothing changes there; its Build page shares the Board list and the Port lists.
Help 206 (and French).

6.37 **1-Wire circuits and the 1-Wire Index** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, Panel Updates entry 37: "A One wire circuit is Board and Pin
Related. You could have two different One Wire circuits on the same Board").
- **A circuit** is one data pin on one Interface with its pull-up resistor; an Interface can have several. Each is kept on the Interface:
  its number, **Pin**, **Powered by** (Board 5V or External supply) and **Resolution** (12-bit by default; 11 or 10-bit per circuit,
  "C ... yes"). A circuit number is never used again after its circuit is deleted ("Ok about delete and renumbering as it just does not
  matter"). A circuit's pin can't be used by anything else (Rule 6.9's blocked pins).
- **The 1-Wire Index** of a DS18B20 probe is its circuit and its number there: Index ID `BM1w1_2` = Interface BM, circuit 1, probe 2.
  It starts the probe's name (Rule 3.1). The Index holds the probe's ROM id (Devices > 🌡 OneWire Probes), so a probe is replaced by
  giving its Index the new ROM id.
- **Adding a probe** ("1. Create an Index for a new One Wire Cicuit 2. Choose an Existing Circuit to add an additional Probe"): the
  probe's **1-Wire Index** box offers **➕ Create an Index for a new 1-Wire circuit** (a short interview: Pin, Powered by, Resolution;
  the probe gets Index 1) and every circuit the Interface has, with its next Index (any free Index can be picked). The first 1-Wire probe
  on an Interface starts with the interview ("the First 1 Wire to a Board sets the first index"). With one circuit, its next Index is
  already picked. **➕ Add 1-Wire circuit** on the Devices page runs the same interview.
- **Soft limit, one warning** ("We do not restrict the excess, but give a warning once exceeded"; Rule 6.20 one warning): about 6 probes
  on Board 5V, about 12 on an External supply. Past it, one warning; the probe is still added.
- **The boards:** the Mega sketch lists its 1-Wire pins in `ONEWIRE_PINS` (D40 to start) and reads every circuit without waiting; the
  panel sends `CFG OW <pin> <bits>` for each circuit when the board connects, and the board reports `T <ROM id> <°F> <pin>`
  (docs/DEVICE_PROTOCOL.md). A Raspberry Pi has one circuit (GPIO 4).
- **Older Schemas** (once per Schema, Rule 15.2): every DS18B20 probe on the old one-list Probe # goes on circuit 1 of its Interface with
  the same number, and the Interface gets circuit 1 (its usual 1-Wire pin, Board 5V, 12-bit). The 3 Vessel sample and the default Schema
  are changed (Rule 15.3).
- **Both programs:** the BruControl Import puts each BruControl probe on circuit 1 of its Interface (BruControl has one 1-Wire bus per
  Interface), named the same way.
Help 234 (and French).

6.38 **On Press: a DIN push button does one thing** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, Panel Updates entry 31: "A Physical DIN push button
that triggers a Process similar to a Process Widget without writing code ... This would only do One Thing. So not like Override but acts
like one. I had a Blue LED Push Button Din that Advanced like an Override button can ... If not, push ignored. I had a Red one That
canceled all alarms. I had a yellow one that did a 20 second firehose."). Every Digital Input Device has an **On Press** row, **None** to
start (it does nothing more than before). The other three:
- **Run a Process**: starts the Process picked in its **Process** row and lets it run to its end in the background, as a Process
  Widget's Start does (Rule 1.31). A press while it runs is ignored; a press never stops it.
- **Advance (Override)**: an Override button on the wall (Rule 2.26), set to **Any** or one Process. It works only when a Process it is
  set to is held in a wait or sleep; otherwise the press is ignored. A button set to Advance counts as an Override button for that
  Process, so no Override pop-up comes up for it by itself.
- **Cancel all alarms**: every Alarm sounding now is turned Off, as a tap on it does (an Alarm Chain goes on to its next waiting step,
  Rule 7.16).
- A press is the input counting up (from the board or the simulator's Simulate: press), so its lockout (Rule 6.7), debounce and on delay
  count first. What each press did is written in the Console. A Process rename is followed (Rule 1.31's way).
- **Both programs:** a BruControl DIN comes in with On Press None (BruControl has no such setting); nothing else changes.
Help 235 (and French).

6.39 **PID Auto-tune** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16, Panel Updates Sandbox entry 25: "And you can set up Autotune for the
Precise?"; started 2026-11-19, "Sure"). A Heating Element's **PID** and **Precise** Settings each have one **🎯 Auto-tune** button
(they share Kp, Ki and Kd, Rule 6.19, so one tune serves both). It opens a pop-up with the electrical warning (Rule 6.20) and one line
saying it turns the element On and needs water over the element and the probe in the water (in the pop-up, not a second pop-up: one
warning), the **Highest temperature** (the Setpoint + 10 °F, 5 °C, to start), **▶ Start**, **■ Stop** and what it is doing now.
- **How:** a relay auto-tune with a bias, run by the Brain (lib/control.js, public/autotune.js): the element goes up below the Setpoint
  and down above it (a band of 0.5 °F, 0.3 °C) for 5 swings; the bias moves until heating and resting take about as long. The first
  swing (the warm-up) is not used, the last 3 are averaged, and the Tyreus-Luyben rules (calm, little overshoot) give Kp, Ki and Kd;
  the bias it ends on is the Hold output % for Precise. It uses the element's Max output %.
- **Safety:** it stops, and the element turns Off, above the Highest temperature, after 30 seconds with no probe reading, after
  3 hours, on ■ Stop, or when the element is turned Off. It never starts with no probe reading or a probe already above the Highest.
- **Use or Keep old:** done, the element turns Off and the pop-up shows the Old and New numbers side by side; **✔ Use new numbers**
  saves Kp, Ki, Kd and Hold output % at once, **Keep old** changes nothing. Nothing is changed by itself.
- **Read only for a Process:** `.autotune` (what it is doing: Warming up to the Setpoint, Swing 2 of 5, Done, Stopped: why),
  `.autotune_kp`, `.autotune_ki`, `.autotune_kd`, `.autotune_hold` (the last numbers found). Only the Brain sets them.
- **Admins only** (as the Method Settings). It runs on the Brain, so it goes on with the pop-up closed. Numbers are in the probe's
  own units (the 3 Vessel sample's probes are °C, Rule 2.59).
- **Both programs:** the BruControl Import program has no running Brain, so it shows no Auto-tune button; it shares the method
  dialogs, nothing else changes there.
Help 237 (and French); Help 156 points to it.

6.40 **Shut down the Brain's computer** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20, Panel Update 7: "We need a method to shut down a Brain when
you exit but reserved only for admin users And maybe a Skynet Setting to avoid option until set to Shut Down Brain Option is True in
settings so no annoying Do you want to shut down the Brain every time an Admin closes the browser"; "Only Admin users are allowed to
set Skynet Settings").
1. **Shut Down Brain Option** (Settings > Panel settings > The Brain, a switch): **Off** to start. Only an Admin changes it (every
   Skynet Setting is Admins only: the Brain refuses a change from anyone else, and the Settings page is greyed for them).
2. **☰ Menu > ⏼ Shut down the Brain's computer**: shown only to an **Admin**, only when the Option is On; on any screen, and as a
   button on the Standby page (Rule 6.32). With the Option Off nobody sees it and the Brain refuses it.
3. It is a ☰ Menu choice, **never asked when a browser closes**: a browser can't tell the Brain a window was closed (a phone that
   lost WiFi looks the same), and closing a window never stops the Brain (Rule 2.25).
4. **The same box as Close and Standby** (Rule 2.25): what happens, brewing (what is On, which Processes run), other screens named,
   one tick box each, **Back** changes nothing. Then the normal stop (every output Off, every Process stopped, a brew written down,
   Rule 6.31) and the computer turns off. Every screen shows "The Brain's computer is shutting down". Standby stays as it was.
5. **How** (lib/brainoff.js): Windows `shutdown.exe /s /t 10` (no admin rights); Raspberry Pi and Linux `sudo -n systemctl poweroff`,
   which the Pi and Linux installers allow without a password and nothing else (/etc/sudoers.d/skynet-brewer-poweroff); Mac System
   Events "shut down". Checked **before** anything stops: a computer that refuses leaves everything running and says why (Pi: run
   the installer again once).
6. **Both programs:** the BruControl Import program controls nothing and never shuts down the computer; nothing changes there.
Help 95, 9 (and French).


6.41 **Emergency Off** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20, Panel Update 8, item 20: "Stop All could be an Emergency Off where it shuts every thing down: Heaters, Pumps,
Valves close. But that could be a SkyNet Button"; "And maybe fashioned after a real world graphic"; "Emergency off now"):
1. **Where:** a Skynet button at the top right of **every page**, Skynet's own drawing of a real Emergency Off button: a **red
   mushroom head on a yellow round plate**, no words in it (Rule 7.25). It is in the Image Library (On_Off/Skynet_Emergency_Off.svg,
   Skynet Picture number 238); the top bar draws it itself, so it shows even without the Skynet Media Setup.
2. **One click, no pop-up** (Rule 2.44). Brewers and admins (a viewer can't switch anything).
