3. **What it does, in this order:** every Process stops (as Stop all); then the **heaters** (Heating Elements Off; Duty Cycle,
   Hysteresis, PID and Deadband disabled); then the **pumps** and motors; then **every other output** (PWM and analog outputs at 0,
   Switches Off); last the **valves close**, so a pump never runs against a closed valve. **Manual valves** are turned by hand and stay
   as they are. Timers, Alarms and sounds are left alone. The Console says how many things it switched.
4. **Both programs:** the BruControl Import program controls nothing, so it has no Emergency Off.
5. **The big one** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-23, Panel Update 12, item 1b: "Hover over Emergency stop for 2 seconds Pop Up to 400 Px or
   so"): the mouse resting **2 seconds** on Emergency Off pops up a **400 px** Emergency Off under it (OakBarn Brewery's own picture at
   400 px, public/icons/Emergency_Stop_400.png). One click on it does the same as the small one; it goes when the mouse leaves both,
   with Esc, or once clicked. It is a pop-up, so it is on top (Rule 18.53). A phone or tablet has no hover, so it has only the small one.
Help 244.
## 7. Pictures

7.1 **All Skynet pictures are SVG only.** (2026-10-22) Fritz's PNG drawings are redrawn as SVG and
only the SVG ships. (2026-10-22)

7.2 **Skynet pictures live in media/Images/Skynet/<group>/** and are read only in the panel. User
pictures go in media/Images/<group>/. The groups are Alarms, Vessels, Pumps, Valves, Chillers,
Motors, Lights_LEDs, Hop_Infusion, Other_Equipment, Miscellaneous and On_Off. (2026-10-22, PR #80)

7.3 **No .svg may be deleted, renamed or replaced from the panel**, not even a user's own.
(2026-10-21)

7.4 **Skynet drawing style:** flat grey #808080, black outline, see-through background. (2026-10-23)

7.5 **Keep the two-picture (On and Off) code** until Fritz says to delete it, even though On overlays
now exist. Ask before deleting any On picture files. (2026-10-22, PR #81)
*2026-11-05 (Fritz):* every Skynet **Open valve picture** is retired to Delete/ (Rule 15.3); the two-picture code stays for a
user's own pictures. Pump On pictures stay in Skynet, but nothing that ships uses them (Rule 7.8). Help 129.

7.6 **Sounds** go in media/sounds; pictures in media/Images. (2026-10-20, PR #48)

7.7 **The Image Library is never added to automatically.** A new picture goes into
docs/Image_Library.md (and the Image_Library folder) only when Fritz says to commit it.
(2026-10-27)

7.8 **Skynet Standard: On overlay when On / True is the preferred way** for on/off Devices and
Widgets, and for heaters (Rule 7.9). Two pictures (on and off) are still allowed where needed. This
is new in Skynet; BruControl never had it. In Properties the overlay comes right after the picture
and the second picture comes last, marked optional. (2026-10-27, Help 58)
**Skynet valves have no Open picture** (Fritz, 2026-11-05: "I generally want to get away with changing the background picture for
switching from Off to On. Better to use the Overlay in all the sample Schema."): a valve keeps its one picture and its On overlay
shows open (the bolt on a motorized valve, the green ring and tick on a Manual Valve Widget). The sample Schemas and the default
Schema swap no pictures: pumps, valves and burners keep their Off picture with the bolt overlay, a heating element glows red
(tint). Help 129.
**On overlays have no border and are smaller** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "On Overlays no Border and smaller", "# 1 applies to all
overlays"): a picture with an On overlay shows **no green box** round it while it is On, and the overlay (a bolt, a badge or the
user's own) is drawn at about half the size of the picture, in its middle. A glow (tint) colors the picture itself and the Green glow
ring goes round it, so those two stay the picture's size. The same on parts built into a Vessel Device.
**A Heating Element's Overlay: Glow, None or a picture** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "In Overlay None should mean None. Default to
the Glow (what None was regardless). And Have None as none"): **Glow** is the start (it glows while On: a Skynet element shows its
glowing on picture, one built into a Vessel Device glows orange). **None** means nothing at all changes on the picture while it is On.
A bolt or other picture is drawn small on top of the glow. *Replaced:* None glowed anyway, and an Element built into a Vessel Device
also showed the bolt. Help 179.

7.9 **Heaters are On while Enabled.** A PID, Hysteresis or Duty Cycle counts as On from Enable to
Disable (not only while its output fires): its overlay or On picture, a vessel's heater glow and a
Picture Widget that turns on with it all follow Enabled. A PWM output is On above 0 %.
(2026-10-27, Help 58, Help 74)

7.10 **Background pictures are .backpath, .backpath_2 and .backpath_3** (Fritz, 2026-11-02, thread "Rename image paths to
backpath", Help 25). Every Device and Widget with background pictures has three paths: **.backpath** (Image Path 1),
**.backpath_2** (Image Path 2) and **.backpath_3** (Image Path 3), e.g. `my_Widget.backpath = "Images/Skynet/Pumps/xxx.svg"`.
**.background** picks which one shows: **1** = .backpath, **2** = .backpath_2, **3** = .backpath_3; **0** or **any number over
3** = no background; **blank** sets .background to **0**. Setting a path does not change .background; `my_Widget.image =
"path"` is the shortcut that sets .backpath and .background = 1. All three can be changed in Properties (except on a User
version of a Skynet Template, Rule 5.16) and by a Process; changing 2 or 3 in Properties pops up the one-picture heads-up.
Under Rule 15.2 the old names **imagePath_1, _2, _3** are changed everywhere (Schemas, Processes, samples, predictive text,
the BruControl importer); an older item with a picture and a blank background gets .background = 1 so it still shows.
**Exception, a User pump** (Fritz, 2026-11-04, Rule 18.19): one path only, its Image Path; a Skynet pump drawing has none
(its Graphic is set). **Only what BruControl had** gets the three; a new Skynet Device or Widget has one path (`.path_image`, `.path_audio`, Rule 7.26). **At most 3:** no item has more than 3 background pictures; an older item with a 4th or more keeps only the first 3
(stacked BruControl copies with more than 3 are handled when the importer is built). **Not every item has a backpath:** most
Widgets have none; the Graphic Widget is the one that normally does.
*Replaced:* imagePath_2 and imagePath_3 worked as in BruControl and a blank background showed imagePath_1 (2026-10-27).
Before that, after a BruControl import imagePath_2 and _3 were locked (2026-10-05).

7.11 **Picture Widget: Turns on with** picks what turns it on: any on/off Device or Widget (output,
switch, input, alarm, sound player, timer, true/false variable) or a heater (on while Enabled).
**None** = a still picture, and its On pictures (Picture when on, On overlay) are greyed out. The
pictures are picked from the Picture list. (2026-10-27, Help 74)

7.12 **The Alarm Widget has two subclasses**, picked when it is made and never changed (Fritz, 2026-11-02, thread "Make the
Alarm Widget a Template", Help 107):
- **Basic Skynet Alarm:** a set Skynet bell picture that can't be changed, in three versions (Together, Back only, Fore only;
  Images/Skynet/Alarms/Alarm_Basic*.svg; Fritz will send his own drawings to replace them). It is drawn in layers, bottom up:
  **Layer 4 Back** (colored by **.back**), **Layer 3 Fore** (the bell, colored by **.fore**; never the text), **Layer 2 Set
  Graphic** (a short list of Skynet pictures, **None first**; a new one starts at **None**, OakBarn Brewery 2026-11-14), **Layer 1 Active overlay** (on top while **.active** is true,
  None first). Back and Fore use the standard color list. Standard Label attributes and the standard Alarm attributes.
  **Bell** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "rename a Alarm Hop because we will use different fore and back for Flavor and Aroma
  Hops"): **Basic** (Alarm_Basic*.svg, with its black lines; empty = Basic) or **Hop** (Alarm_Hop*.svg: an original line
  drawing, bell and sound waves in the Fore and Back colors only, no black lines). The hop is never part of a bell: it is the
  separate Set Graphic Alarm_Set_Hop_Cone.svg (Layer 2, fixed greens, see-through outside the hop). Alarm Hop replaces
  AlarmBitter.png (copyright, Rule 9.12).
- **User Alarm:** its own background picture (Image Path 1), a Set Graphic that is any picture (Layer 2), an Active overlay,
  and **.backcolor** (.back) behind it. Standard Label and Alarm attributes.
An Alarm made before 2026-11-02 keeps working as before.

7.13 **Pump Cover Overlays** (Fritz, 2026-11-02, thread "Draw SVGs for common brew pumps", Help 111): a pump picture is drawn in
layers, bottom up: the **pump picture** (a Skynet no-cover pump drawing), the **Cover overlay**, then the **On overlay**. The cover
has a see-through background and shows on and off. **One cover for each color, and every cover fits every Skynet pump** (Fritz,
2026-11-05: "1 of each Color that I ask For and User created ones that just change the color using RGB. All Covers can overlay any
Pump"). A cover is a color, not a drawing: each Skynet no-cover pump drawing has one cover outline and one cover shape
(Images/Skynet/Pumps/Covers/), and Skynet fills the shape with the cover's color. The **Skynet colors** are the ones Fritz asks for:
**Red, Yellow, Blue, Green, Purple, Orange and White** (White is RGB 250 250 250, #FAFAFA). The **User Cover** is the same cover in
any color the user sets (standard color list or Custom RGB). A new color needs no new drawings. A Pump Device has **.cover** (None,
Red, Yellow, Blue, Green, Purple, Orange, White, User; **None is the default**) and **.coverColor** (the User cover's color).
*Replaced (2026-11-05):* each pump had its own cover file in every color (about 96 files); those are in Delete/.

7.14 **Every new Alarm meets the new Alarm standard** (Rule 7.12: a Basic Skynet Alarm or a User Alarm). **Old Alarms**
(made before 2026-11-02, in the samples and Schemas) **are changed to the new Basic format one by one**, using Basic Alarm
Widget formats Fritz will make; nothing is converted until then. The list of old Alarms is docs/ExistingAlarms.md (not
the OakBarn Schema). (Fritz, 2026-11-02, thread "Build the Basic and User Alarm Widgets")

7.15 **Powered valves and pumps show a lightning bolt when On** (Fritz, 2026-11-04, with a drawing, thread "Center pumps and
valves on pipes", Help 58 and 121). The Skynet On overlay **Lightning bolt, red and yellow** (Images/Skynet/On_Off/Overlay_Bolt.svg,
steady, not flashing) sits over the middle of the picture while it is On (a valve open, a pump running, a Proportional Valve above
0 %). Every new motorized valve, Proportional Valve and Pump Device starts with it, and the Skynet valve Templates have it set.
**Lightning bolt, flashing red and yellow** (Overlay_Bolt_Flash.svg) is a choice in the On overlay list, not the default (Fritz,
2026-11-04: "the flashing Bolt is good, but the default should be the single bolt that is not flashing"). Once per Schema, each one
that had no On overlay gets the steady bolt, and one that got the flashing bolt from the first version is changed to the steady one
(Rule 15.2); one with another overlay keeps it, and picking (none) or the flashing bolt afterwards stays. A Manual valve has no power,
so it has none. New pumps from the pump picker keep the Green glow ring (Rule 18.13; Fritz: leave it, the default may change later or
go into Panel Defaults). **2026-11-14:** the On overlay a new pump or valve starts with is ☰ Menu > Default settings > **Pump
Overlay** (Green glow ring) and **Valve Overlay** (the steady bolt) (Rule 2.42). Pumps and valves already made keep
theirs.
*Replaced:* the flashing bolt was the default (2026-11-04, PR #179).

7.16 **The Alarm Chain: one Alarm does the work of many stacked ones** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "Since we can Change the
Path of an Alarm as well as the audio file One Alarm could do what all the alarms did. I had to Stack Them and it was a pain to
work with so many"). An Alarm Widget (Basic Skynet or User) has an **Alarm Chain** of up to 20 **steps** (Alarm Widget
Properties > Alarm Chain; each step's red ⬢ opens its pop-up). Each step has a **Step name** and can change the **Fore color**,
**Back color**, the **Set Graphic (Layer 2)**, the **Active overlay (Layer 1)** and the **Sound file** (a User Alarm also its
**Background picture**, Image Path 1). **Every choice starts on No Change, which skips that adjustment** for that step: the Alarm
keeps what it has. A Process picks a step with **`alm_Brew.step = 2`** or by its name, **`alm_Brew.step = "Strike"`**;
**`alm_Brew.step = 0`** puts back what its Properties say. `.setgraphic` changes Layer 2 from a Process. A Hop Alarm's steps can
each have a **time on its timer**: when the timer reaches it, the Alarm goes to that step and sounds (once). **A Timer's Alarm
Chain is kept in the order its steps go On** (a count-down timer: the most time left first), and a **new step is put into its
place** as soon as it is saved (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "Auto Order the Alarm Chain of a Timer by when the Alarm is set to On
or Active", "if a new alarm is enetered in the chain auto reorder takes place"). Steps with no time keep their order after them.
Both programs: the BruControl Import makes Alarms with no chain (its stacked alarms are listed for the user to join by hand). A BruControl Timer's 2 alarms that are on are joined to their
Alarms: the Alarm becomes a Hop Alarm on that Timer, the first time is its own time, and a second time is a step on its Alarm
Chain (in Skynet one Alarm can hold up to 20 timed steps).
Help 172.

7.17 **Alarm Email Notification: an Alarm can send an email** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "Alarm e mail notification could be
built in but have user what e mail server on his computer he wants to use. The almost always default to the Microsoft internal
server when I only use gmail"). An Alarm Widget (Basic Skynet or User) has **Email Notification** (a switch, Off to start) and
**Email to** (in the Alarm Widget Properties, below the Sound boxes). With it On, each time the Alarm goes off Skynet sends one email (at most one a
minute for each Alarm). **Email to** takes one or more addresses with commas between them; left empty, the email goes to every
user who has an email in My account. The email is sent through the **mail server the user picks** in Settings > Sending codes and
Alarm emails (Gmail, Outlook.com or any other, with an app password); Skynet never uses a built-in or Microsoft one. A Process can
turn it on or off with **`alm_Brew.email = true`** / **`false`**. If no mail server is set up or the email fails, the Process log
says so in plain words. Both programs: the BruControl Import keeps each Alarm's Email Notification switch (BruControl's own mail
settings are not copied; the user picks the mail server in Skynet). Help 175.

7.18 **Alarm Priority: every Alarm in one logical line** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "We could set a priority attributes on
Alarms ... All 1 go before the first 2. Then within all the 1s, 1.0 goes before 1.1 goes before 1.2 ... If there is a Conflict
between two (two 1.1 random pick one then follow with the other)", "and maybe 2 decimals as you could then insert without
renumbering"). Only one sound plays at a time. Every Alarm has a **Priority**, a number from 0 to 99 with **up to two decimal
places** (1, 1.1, 1.15, 2 ...): **the lower one plays first**, and an Alarm can go in between two others without renumbering. An
Alarm with no Priority of its own has **its Kind's number** (Brew Flow 1, Hop 2, Pre-Hop 3, General 4, Sound only 5; the Sound
Player is 5). **The same Priority:** the one that went On first plays first, so a playing Alarm is never cut off by one of the
same Priority; **two that go On at the same moment** follow the same rule: **the first one On plays first** (1a), then the next (1b), even within the same second (in a Process, the order of their lines). *Replaced* (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "First one on is priority"): two within a second were picked at random. A lower
Priority still cuts in at once (a Hop Alarm stops the music). It is the same whether an Alarm was set On by a Process, by its
Alarm Chain (Rule 7.16) or by both. **Alarm Chain steps wait their turn:** a timer step that comes due while the Alarm still
sounds the last step waits (the Alarm shows "+1 step waiting") and follows as soon as the last one is tapped off; a Process's
`.step` still changes it at once. **A sound that does not Repeat lets the next one play** once it has played to its end, while
its Alarm still shows On. Set in Alarm Widget Properties > Alarm > **Priority**, or by a Process: **`alm_Brew.priority = 1.15`**
(`""` puts back its Properties' number). `.waiting` (read only) is how many Chain steps wait. *Replaced:* between two of the same
Kind the newest one played (PR #24). **Brew Flow first** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "Alarm order. Change the Rule. I may change it after I get the
Oakbarn sample back and create a conflict to see what we should do"): the Kind numbers are **Brew Flow 1, Hop 2**, Pre-Hop 3, General 4,
Sound only 5. *Replaced:* Hop 1, Brew Flow 2 (2026-11-09). An Alarm with its own Priority keeps it. This may change again once the
OakBarn sample is back and tested. Both programs: the BruControl Import gives each Alarm its Kind's number. Help 21 and 172.

7.19 **Alarm Digital Outputs: an Alarm can switch 2 Devices** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "Ok, we can add that but add 2 Items to
contol I assume it was one in BruControl", "And if blank those do nothing"). An Alarm Widget (every kind) has **Digital Output 1** and
**Digital Output 2** (optional; None to start, Rule 18.33). Each picks a Device with an ON / OFF state (a warning light, a horn, a relay;
a Duty Cycle, Hysteresis, PID or Deadband by its ON / OFF). It goes **ON while the Alarm is active and OFF when the Alarm stops**. A
blank slot does nothing; a Device that has no ON / OFF state is skipped with a note in the Console. Both programs: the BruControl Import
puts BruControl's one Digital Output in slot 1 (an Alarm imported before keeps it there too). Help 178.

7.20 **A sound can be a web link to an MP3** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "Yes. And is there a place we can store the mp3 for free";
"We could give that as an option if people do not want the audio files on their computer"). Every sound box (an Alarm's Sound file, an
Alarm Chain step, the Sound Player, the sound before a hop alert, and a Process's `SoundPlayer path = "..."`) takes a file in the media
folders on the Brain **or** a web link that starts with `https://` (or `http://`) and points straight at the sound file. The browser
plays the link from the web, so the file never has to be on the Brain. **When a sound can't play** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "We will Do a Text to Speach MP3 for a Missing
Alarm Sound"): a link with no internet, a wrong link, or a file that is missing. An Alarm then plays the **Missing Alarm Sound**, a
voice clip on the Brain (`sounds/Skynet/Alarm_Sound_Missing.mp3`, a Text to Speech voice made by OakBarn Brewery), or the Skynet beep (`sounds/alarm_beep.wav`)
when that isn't there either, and shows a warning that says why; an Alarm is never silent. A Sound Player plays OakBarn Brewery's own
song *Find The File - Connecting* (Treblo, `sounds/Skynet/Find_The_File_Connecting.mp3`) once instead, with the same warning (OakBarn
Brewery, 2026-11-10: the song for music, the voice for Alarms); the sound before a hop alert is skipped and the alert's voice still speaks. **The beep, the Missing Alarm Sound and the Find The File song come
with the main Setup and the panel zip** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "Keep the Beep"; "Song and clip also with the brain"), so they
are on the Brain even without the Skynet Media Setup (an exception to Rule 9.12). Help says a file on the Brain is the safest choice for Hop and
Brew Flow Alarms. **The free home for MP3s** is a GitHub Release (tag `Skynet-Sounds` on the Skynet project, not set as the latest
release, so Releases > Latest stays the Setup); only files with the right to share go there (Rule 9.12). Both programs: the BruControl
Import keeps a sound that is already a link as it is and never copies it. Help 186.

7.21 **The Alarm attributes** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13, README markup "Skynet Brew Panel 1 a", pages 15 to 19: "Common
Attributes to All (SkyNet and User Alarms. Alarms can have additional attributes only applicable to them"; "Your Alarm spec is not
built yet go wit your recomendtions"). What a Process can use on an Alarm Widget (a Basic Skynet Alarm, a User Alarm or a Pre-Hop
Alarm), in OakBarn Brewery's words. **Common to all:**
1. **`.path`**: its sound file (.wav or .mp3, .mp3 preferred). A wrong path plays no sound (Rule 7.20 then plays the Missing Alarm
   Sound). Audio only plays while the Alarm is On. The older `.sound` still works.
2. **`.label_fore` and `.label_back`**: the colors of its Label (the same as its Label Attributes' Fore Color and Back Color).
3. **`.x` and `.y`**: its place on the Tab; **`.h` and `.w`**: its size (the same as `.x_hPosition`, `.y_vPosition`, `.height`, `.width`).
4. **`.visible` is automatic**: `AlarmName = On` shows it, `AlarmName = Off` hides it. It is not on the Properties dialog and a Process
   can't set it (it can still read it). In Edit layout a hidden Alarm shows faint so it can be placed. Hidden Locked still works.
5. **`.toggle`** (hidden, never set by a Process): a click on the Alarm's picture turns it Off, or On, which changes `.state`.
6. **`.loop`**: true plays the sound and repeats it; false plays it one time.
7. **`.state`**: its On / Off. `AlarmName = On` and `AlarmName.state = On` are the same.
8. **`.skynet_Layer_2`**: its Layer 2 picture (its Set Graphic), above the base picture and under Layer 1 (the Active overlay):
   `AlarmName.skynet_Layer_2 = "Name of Skynet Picture"`, or `AlarmName.skynet_Layer_2 = Skynet_Picture_Number` (its fixed number,
   Rule 7.22; `.skynet_Layer_2.path` and `.skynet_Layer_2.file` work as Rule 7.23 says). Picked on the Properties dialog or by a
   Process. The older `.setgraphic` still works.
**Each kind:**
- **(1) Brew Flow** and **(2) Hop Drop**: a Basic Skynet Alarm; `.fore` and `.back` color its bell. **A Brew Flow Alarm holds its
  Process:** `AlarmName = On` (or `.state = On`) in a Process is followed by a hidden `wait AlarmName = Off`, so the Process goes on
  only once the Alarm is tapped Off (or another Process turns it Off). Stop and Override end the wait as on any wait.
- **(3) Pre-Hop Drop: a Combination Alarm and String Box Widget** (☰ Add > Pre-Hop Alarm). **`.background`** picks one of **three
  Skynet watermarks** (1, 2 or 3; the pictures are Skynet's and can't be changed, only picked by a Process: `AlarmName.background = 3`).
  **`.fore` and `.back`** color its text, **`.string`** sets its text (Rich Text codes work), and **`.playtime`** is how many seconds it
  stays On; then it turns itself Off. A click turns it Off sooner. Empty or 0 = it stays On until it is tapped.
- **(4) User Alarm**: `.background` 1, 2 or 3 picks one of **your own three pictures** (Image Path 1 to 3, changed on the Properties
  dialog or by a Process). **`.fore` and `.back`** color its text, **`.string`** and **`.playtime`** as the Pre-Hop Alarm.
**Priority:** the spec's `.alarmchain` number is the Alarm's **`.priority`** (Rule 7.18), because Alarm Chain is already the steps
(Rule 7.16). Kind numbers: Brew Flow 1, Hop 2, Pre-Hop 3, User 4, Sound only 5. The three Pre-Hop watermarks are placeholder drawings
(`media/Images/Skynet/Alarms/Alarm_PreHop_Mark_1.svg` to `_3`, Skynet Picture numbers 195 to 197) until OakBarn Brewery sends its own; they are not in the Image Library.
Both programs: the BruControl Import's Build page is the Panel's, so it has the same attributes; imported BruControl Alarms have no
Alarm Widget kind yet (Rule 7.14) and keep their own `.visible`. Help 195.

7.22 **Skynet Picture numbers** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13, ReadMe markup "Skynet Brew Panel 1 a" page 16: "for all skynet Pictures,
a Leading ID Number will be created and remains Unique and not changeable ever. That Number besides the Name will be in all DDLBs for
these types of Graphics. A Printable list will also be available"). Every picture in media/Images/Skynet has a fixed **number**
(lib/skynetpicids.json, a Meaningless Key, Design Rule #2): it never changes and is never given to another picture, even when the
picture is renamed (its row keeps its number) or taken away (its row stays, marked retired). A new Skynet picture gets the next number
(`node tools/skynet-picture-ids.js`, which also writes docs/Skynet_Picture_IDs.md; a test fails while a picture has no number).
Every picture list shows a Skynet picture as **number · file name** (24 · Overlay_Bolt.svg), and so do the 🖼 picker and the Media page.
**The printable list:** Media page > 🔢 Skynet Picture numbers (each picture, its number, file name and group; 🖨 Print). A Process can
give a Skynet picture by its number wherever a picture goes: `alm_Brew.setgraphic = 24`. Both programs: the BruControl Import's Build
page uses the same lists. Help 193.

7.23 **Two-part paths: .path and .file** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13, ReadMe markup "Skynet Brew Panel 1 a" page 17: "All Paths will
have two fields .path and .file ... When selecting a file the Path and file are combined so Generally the DDLBs will only contain the
File Name. The path on a property dialog can be edited on a User Audio or Graphic but normally the default would be used.
UserAlarmBackground = "File Name.svg" would construct the real path using the Default path. UserAlarmBackground.path = "Full Path"
would require a Full Path"; "Two-part paths (.path + .file) build as it simplifies the entry in process").
- **Four default folders:** **Skynet Graphic** `Images/Skynet` and **Skynet Audio** `sounds/Skynet` (never changed: the Skynet pictures
  and sounds live there), **User Graphic** `Images` and **User Audio** `sounds` (Settings > Panel settings > Default folders; not a
  Skynet folder).
- **Properties:** every picture and sound list shows **only the file name** (with its number, Rule 7.22; the folder only when two
  files have the same name). The **Folder** line under it shows the folder: greyed for a Skynet picture or sound, typed for your own
  (normally the folder it is in is used).
- **In a Process:** a file name alone (`alm_Brew.backpath = "Bell.svg"`) gets its folder: the User folder (and the folders in it) first,
  then the Skynet folder (and its groups); found nowhere, it is the User folder and the name, and the Process check lists it.
  **`.path`** is the whole path and **`.file`** only the file name (`alm_Brew.backpath.path = "Images/Hops/Bell.svg"`,
  `alm_Brew.backpath.file = "Bell_Red.svg"`; .file keeps the folder when the file is there). Every picture or sound attribute has them:
  .image, .backpath, .backpath_2, .backpath_3, .imageon, .imageoff, .imageoverlay, .setgraphic, an Alarm's .sound, a Sound Player's
  sound (`SoundPlayer_1.path`, `SoundPlayer_1.file`) and a Graphic gGlobal (`gG_Pic.path`, `gG_Pic.file`). **The item's own
  .path / .file** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "yes" to this mapping; ".path is the full path including the file. We might need .path_2
  and .path_3 and .file_2 and .file_3"): on a Device or Widget `.path` / `.file` are Image Path 1, `.path_2` / `.file_2` Image Path 2,
  `.path_3` / `.file_3` Image Path 3; on an Alarm or a Sound Player `.path` / `.file` are its sound. A web link and a word such as
  none are kept as they are. The 🖼 picker in the Process editor inserts only the file name when no other file has that name.
- Each path is still kept whole inside Skynet (folder and file together), so nothing that already works changes.
Both programs: the BruControl Import's Build page uses the same dialogs and the same Process reader; the pictures and sounds it copies
into Images/User and sounds/User are found by their file name. Help 194.
**A Tab's background lists only the Tab Background folder's Skynet pictures** (2026-11-25, OakBarn Brewery: "If there are ever any
Skynet pictures they will be very simple background and be in a Tab Background folder"): media/Images/Skynet/Tab_Background/ (none
yet). Your own pictures all show.

7.24 **File Not Found picture** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "if a Path is missing it just does not display. Maybe we can create an
Image that says File Not Found when the path does not work"; "Looks good use it"):
- When a picture's file is missing (moved, renamed, or not on this Brain), Skynet shows the **File Not Found** picture
  (`public/File_Not_Found.svg`: a torn picture with a red ✕) in its place, at its size, so the item is still seen and can be fixed.
- Its Hover Help says **File Not Found:** and the path it looked for. Nothing in the Schema is changed; put the file back, or pick
  another picture in Properties.
- **The picture shows by itself once its file is there** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: after the Media Setup ran with the panel
  open, File Not Found stayed until the panel was closed and opened again). The panel looks again for each missing picture when
  its window comes back to the front, when pictures are added from the panel (File Move, Get Skynet pictures), and every 20
  seconds while one is missing; no closing, no F5. Skynet does this in the Background and needs no user input (Rule 11.13).
Both programs: the BruControl Import's Build page shows it too.

7.25 **Help pictures stay sharp** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "All of the graphics in the Hover Help ... are very poor and hard to read"):
- Pictures in `media/help_pictures` (Help pages and Hover Help) are **never swapped for a traced SVG copy** (Settings > Pictures,
  lib/vectorize.js). A traced copy turns small words into blobs. They show the picture itself, whatever Settings > Pictures is
  set to, unless a **hand-made SVG** of the same name sits next to it; then that drawing is used, since it is sharp at any size.
- Help pictures are not traced at all, so no copies are made for them.
- **Words in a Help picture are real text, never part of the graphic** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "And any text has to be
  text and not just part of a grahic"; 2026-11-20: "remove all text that is part of a graphic and add as text (maybe smaller and
  always translate because German, Danish, Norwegian, and Italian are coming"): the picture is a hand-made SVG whose words are
  &lt;text&gt;, so they stay sharp at any size and are translated. A drawing that has pictures in it (a pump, a board) is an SVG with the
  picture inside (`<Name>_Art.png`, the PNG with its words taken out) and its words on top as &lt;text&gt;; the Brain puts the picture
  inside the SVG as it sends it.
  - **Every word is translated:** each Help language has the words of the Help pictures in `help/<lang>/_pictures.json`, English
    text → its text in that language (French now: `help/fr/_pictures.json`). The Help page and the Hover Help balloon ask for the
    picture in the language picked in 🌐 Help language, and the Brain sends it with its words in that language. A word much longer
    than the English is drawn smaller so it fits where the English was. A new or changed picture word gets its French in the same PR:
    a test (test/helppicfrench.test.js) fails and names it, and `node tools/helppics-french.js` lists them. A new Help language
    (German, Danish, Norwegian, Italian) adds its own `_pictures.json`; nothing else changes.
  - **Words printed on a real item stay as they are** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20: "Do not worry about parts of a graphic that are
    model or anything in the real world cannot be translated as it is fixed and printed on the label of the item"): a board's name and
    pin names (MEGA 2560, GND, D23), a model or brand (SSR-40 DA, Blichmann), or what is printed on an SSR or a pump stay in the
    picture, or as a word whose "translation" is the same English. Only Skynet's own words are translated: titles, labels, callouts,
    notes and warnings.
  - **A screenshot of the panel stays as it is shot** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20, "lets keep a for now"): the screens, buttons and
    labels are English in every Help language (Rule 11.11), so the words in a screenshot are what the user sees on the screen. Any word
    Skynet adds to a screenshot (a note, a callout) is real text on top of it, translated like any other picture word; the marks
    (a red box, red dashes) have no words. This covers the Step by Step screenshots, Greyed_Do_Not_Enter, and the two **Tab size
    pictures** (`Tab_1600x900_on_1920x1040_Screen.png`, `Tab_1920x1040_on_1920x1040_Screen.png`, in the Width and Height of a New
    Tab Hover Help), so this is not an exception. A whole-screen picture uses ⟪imgw:path⟫ in Hover Help, drawn as wide as the
    balloon (⟪img:⟫ stays at most 240 px).
- **Any Help picture taken from a PNG or a PDF is redrawn** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "Good rule on drawing any pix from a Png
  or pdf"), never cut out and shipped as it is. A picture cut from a markup PDF is only as sharp as it was pasted into the PDF
  (most are 96 dots per inch). The PNG may stay next to the SVG (Rule #1, Never Take Away); the SVG is what shows.
Skynet does this in the Background and needs no user input (Rule 11.13). Both programs: the BruControl Import makes no traced copies, so it already shows
the pictures themselves (and the hand-made SVGs). Help 7.


7.26 **Only what BruControl had gets three backgrounds; a new Skynet Device or Widget has one path** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20, Panel Update 8, item 8: "New Rule
Change: The 3 background rule does not apply to anything that BruControl did not have. Note A Graphic Widget will have 3 backgrounds
because it could have been a global in Brucontrol. New Skynet Devices and widgets only have one path and attribute. On the new
attributes will be .path_image and .path_audio"). A change to Rules 7.10 and 18.50 #4:
- **Three backgrounds** (.backpath, .backpath_2, .backpath_3 and .background, Rule 7.10) only on the items BruControl had. The
  **Graphic (Picture) Widget** keeps its three, because a BruControl Global with a background picture comes in as one (there is no
  Graphic gGlobal, Rule 1.19).
- **A new Skynet Device or Widget** (one BruControl never had) has **one path and one attribute** for each thing it shows or plays:
  **`.path_image`** for its one picture and **`.path_audio`** for its one sound. The first is the **Audio Widget**.
- **The Audio Widget** ("Create an Audio Widget that plays a sound with repeat and a path (only one) Similar to alarm but likely hidden
  99% of the time so visible would default to no. Not an Alarm but boolean Process Command to turn on and Off. It could have a graphic
  path that a Picture could be selected (only 1)"; "I forgot about the sound Player but Audio Widget conforms more for a name"): the
  Sound Player with its new name. One sound (`.path_audio`, the older `.path` works too), **Repeat sound** (`.loop`), one optional
  picture (`.path_image`), and On / Off from a Process (`wgt_AUD_Music_BH = On`). **A new one starts hidden** (Visible Off). It is not
  an Alarm: it has the lowest sound priority (5) and pauses while an Alarm sounds. Type letters **AUD** (Rule 3.14). The Process word
  `SoundPlayer` (the built-in one every panel has) is not changed.
Help 21.
7.27 **The Skynet Audio folders, their drawings, and an Audio Widget that shows only while it plays** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-22,
Panel Update 9, items 1 and 2):
- **Folders:** `media/sounds/Skynet` has six subfolders, **Songs, Text_to_voice, Fanfare, Beep, Nature, Go_to_work**, and a
  **Patron** folder with the same six. Every Skynet sound that was loose in `sounds/Skynet` is in **Songs**. On start the Brain makes any
  folder that is missing and moves a loose Skynet sound into Songs (a copy already in Songs wins; Rule #1, nothing else is touched).
  A bare file name still finds its sound in any subfolder.
- **Pictures:** each folder has its own picture on a light (250,250,250) background: `Images/Skynet/Miscellaneous/Skynet_Audio_<folder>.svg`
  (Skynet pictures 239 to 244, Rule 9.12, Media_Licenses). Since Panel Update 10 (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-23: "These are for the media
  catergorys") they are OakBarn Brewery's own pictures (Adobe Firefly), kept inside each .svg as a small JPEG: Songs a music note,
  Text_to_voice a man shouting, Fanfare a bugle, Beep a desert bird ("no resemblence" to any cartoon), Nature a koi pond, Go_to_work
  brewers marching off to work. The same file names, so nothing else changes.
- **The Audio Widget** shows its own picture (`.path_image`) or, with none, the drawing of the folder its sound is in. It is on top
  (Layer 1) while it plays and hidden when stopped: `.play = true` plays it and shows it, `.play = false` stops and hides it.
- **The one exception** (to Rules 1.29 and 6.15, which give every Widget `.visible`; OakBarn Brewery: an exception to any Rule): an
  Audio Widget has **no `.visible`, `.hidden` or Hidden Locked** for a user or a Process. A Process line that sets one is an error that
  says to use `.play`.
**Both programs:** the BruControl Import's sound swaps (Sandbox/Importer/Sound_Swaps.md) point at `sounds/Skynet/Songs`. Help 21, 186.

## 8. Sign-in and roles

8.1 **Roles:** viewer, operator, admin. Any new screen that changes things is Admin-only or
Operator-only. Only Admins edit Schemas or move pictures. (2026-10-04, PR #8; 2026-10-21)

8.2 **First Admin setup** works only from your own network or Tailscale. The recovery code screen
must be impossible to miss: a big code, copy, download and print, and a required "I saved it" tick.
(2026-10-04, PR #11)

8.3 **Password rules** are set by the Admin in Settings > Password rules. Old passwords keep working.
(2026-10-21, PR #53)

8.4 **Password key** (Fritz, 2026-11-05): every new-password box (Admin setup, Forgot password, Settings > My account,
Settings > Users > Add user) has Skynet's own **key** button that makes a strong password following the Password rules
(Rule 8.3), fills it in both boxes and shows it so it can be written down. Skynet has its own key because a browser's
"Suggest strong password" key needs the browser signed in and syncing, and the clean window never syncs (Rule 9.8).
(thread "Restore generate password Key on fresh install", Help 10)

8.5 **Passwords are never kept; what must be read back is locked; OakBarn Brewery never emails about passwords** (OakBarn Brewery,
2026-11-14: "Reword all about Password to the way it works", "Can we encrypt all passwords, reset codes and e mails"):
- **Never kept:** passwords, recovery codes, sign-in codes and sign-ins are saved only as a one-way scramble (a salted hash); nobody can
  turn one back into the password.
- **Locked (encrypted):** what the Brain must read back to send a message: the email account's app password, the Twilio token, and each
  user's email address and mobile number. They are locked with a key kept on the Brain (data/seal.key), so a file or backup copied
  without it cannot be read. Plain ones from before are locked when the Brain starts. Moving the Brain (Rule 9.9) takes the key along.
  Messages the Brain sends go over a locked connection (TLS).
- **The Brain's data folder is the Brain's own:** at each start the Brain locks its data folder so only the computer account that runs it
  (and the computer's Administrators and the system) can open it; other people signed in to that computer with their own account cannot
  (Windows: its permissions; Pi, Linux, Mac: owner only). Inside Skynet, only Admins change things (Rule 8.1).
- **A password is reset only on your own Skynet:** the recovery code (made when the first Admin account is set up, Rule 8.2; a new one
  each time it is used), an Admin in Settings > Users, or the reset-password tool at the Brain itself.
- **OakBarn Brewery never emails anyone about a password.** An email that says it is from OakBarn Brewery and asks to reset a password,
  sign in or send a code is a scam (phishing). This warning is on the sign-in page, the recovery code screen and its saved file, Help 10
  and oakbarnbrewery.com. A Skynet panel's own emails (sign-in codes, alarms) come from the user's own email account as "Brew Panel".
Both programs (the Importer signs in the same way). (thread "Let users build their own Pump Templates", Help 10)

8.6 **Approved Devices** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "Is there a Key that we can add so only an Official skynet Panel can access the
brain", "Set that up and I will see how painful for a user but internet safety may trump that"). A key hidden in the Panel cannot
work (the Brain sends the Panel to every browser, so anyone could read it); instead each phone, tablet or computer must be approved:
- A right password (or sign-in code) from a device not approved yet does **not** sign in: the device waits on **Settings > Approved
  Devices** until an Admin **Approves** or **Refuses** it, then signs in again. A stolen password alone gets nobody in.
- **Always approved:** the Brain's own computer (never through a proxy, Rule 6.32). **Approved by themselves:** the device that makes
  the first Admin account, a device that uses the recovery code (Rule 8.5), and, while no device is approved yet, the first Admin to
  sign in from your own network (so a Pi with no screen never locks everyone out).
- **Remove** a lost or sold device: it is signed out at once. **Rename** gives it a plain name. Each device has its own device cookie
  (a long random number); only its hash is kept, in data/devices.json.
- **On** by default; an Admin can turn it Off (a password alone then signs in). Last resort at the Brain:
  `node tools/reset-password.js --devices-off`.
- Programs and gadgets with the API key (voice control, hydrometers) are not devices and are unchanged.
OakBarn Brewery tries it to see how much trouble it is for a user. Both programs (the Importer's Build page signs in with its own
one-time key, so it is not asked). (thread "Let users build their own Pump Templates", Help 10)

9.1 **Every code change ships as a pull request (PR)** on GitHub. (2026-10-21)

9.2 **Zips of the whole panel are sent only when Fritz asks** for one (no data/ or node_modules
inside). (2026-10-21 09:17Z)
*Replaced:* from 2026-10-03 a zip came with every change.

9.3 **The release zip carries no config/, media/ or scripts/ folders.** Samples ship in defaults/
and are copied only into a missing folder, so unzipping over an old copy and choosing "Replace all"
is safe. (2026-10-05, PR #39)

9.4 **Never edit version.json in a PR.** A GitHub Action writes it on every merge. The version name
is `PR<number>_Skynet-v.yyyymmdd_hh_mm`. (2026-10-21, PR #65; 2026-10-22, PR #86)

9.5 **New pictures go in a fresh PR off the default branch.** (2026-10-22)

locks them before a production zip. (2026-10-21)

9.7 *Replaced (2026-10-28):* "When Fritz closes a chat, rewrite docs/Unresolved_PRs.md" (2026-10-27).
Fritz dropped it: open PRs are on GitHub and Claude doesn't forget them, so no Unresolved PRs
document is kept.

9.8 **Four update choices on an existing install** (Fritz, 2026-11-06, replaces the single Start Fresh question; Modified Fresh
Start added 2026-11-13): when an installer (the Windows Setup .exe, the Mac .command, the Linux / Pi .sh) finds the panel already
installed, it asks what this update does. The program files are always updated. The Windows Setup shows a page with four round
choice buttons; the Mac and Linux / Pi installers show the same four as a numbered list:
1. **Start Fresh: delete everything, nothing saved** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "A fresh start should be a real Fresh Start
   with nothing saved" ... "and the Import"; "the Fresh Install should also delete the Media files"): as below, and now also the
   `backups` folders, the whole `media` folder (every picture and sound, the Skynet ones too: the Media Setup runs after it) and
   everything in the Import folder.
2. **Modified Fresh Start** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "a Modified Fresh Start like the Fresh Start now where some files are
   kept"): after a warning it deletes the Schemas, Tabs, Devices, Widgets and own Templates (`config`), users and the brew log
   (`data`) and Processes (`processes`). **Kept:** the Default settings (`brewDefaults`, put back into the new layout on the next
   start), own Mash / Boil / Water Profiles, Equipment Profiles, saved Recipes, own pictures and sounds, the `backups` folders and
   the Import folder.
   Both Fresh Starts run `lib/freshstart.js`, the same file in every installer.
3. **Update the program and reset all users**: after a warning (No, go back, is the default) it deletes every user, password,
   sign-in and the recovery code (`data/users.json` and `data/sessions.json`), and on Windows the user name and password the
   clean window remembers. Schemas and settings (`config`), the brew log and saved values (`data`), Processes (`processes`) and
   `media` are kept. The panel opens at Admin setup.
4. **Update the program and keep everything** (the original No: recommended, already picked, and what a silent or
   unattended update does).
With 3 or 4 the installer still offers to replace single folders ("Keep all of them as they are?").
**Except the Full Setup** (Rule 9.20, 2026-11-17): it shows none of these four choices. It is always a full install that
overwrites everything; its only question is backup or no backup (2026-11-18); see Rule 9.20.
*Replaced:* "it first asks **Delete all users and Schemas and Start Fresh?** (No is the default)." (2026-11-02)
**Start Fresh** (Fritz, 2026-11-02): choice 1 shows a second warning that **all existing data will be deleted**, listing what goes,
with **No (back out, nothing deleted)** as the default. Confirmed, it deletes `config` (Schemas, Tabs, Devices, settings),
`data` (users, passwords, sign-ins, recovery code, brew log, saved values) and `processes` (Processes) for good, with no
backup, and the panel starts again from the samples with Admin setup. **Kept:** `media` (pictures and sounds, Rule 7.3) and
the `backups` folder. (thread "Add Start Fresh option to installer", Help 18)
**Fresh is fresh** (Fritz, 2026-11-05): Start Fresh on Windows also deletes the clean window's own browser profile (Rule 2.36,
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\SkynetBrewer\AppWindow`), which holds the user name and password the browser saved. Admin setup always opens
with **empty** boxes: it is marked as a new account and, for as long as setup is open, any box you have not clicked, typed or
pasted in is kept empty, even when a browser fills it in later. Skynet's clean window never syncs with a Microsoft or Google
account (Edge signs new profiles in by itself and synced the old login back in). Saving your password still works: it is
kept only in Skynet's own window and fills in on Sign in as before.
(thread "Make Start Fresh admin setup truly fresh")

9.9 **Move to a new Brain** (Fritz, 2026-11-03): someone who runs the Brain on a Windows, Linux or Mac computer can move it to a
Raspberry Pi later (or any Brain to any other), with **☰ Menu > Move Brain** (Admins), in three steps:
1. On the **old** Brain, **Make a Brain Move file**: one file, `Skynet_Brain_Move_<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS>.skynetmove`, with every Schema
   (and its saved gGlobal values), panel setting, Profile, Recipe, Template, Process, picture and sound in the media folder, the
   logins and recovery code, and the brew log. It is **locked with a Move password** (typed twice, at least 6 characters), because
   it holds the logins and the hidden keys (Rule 3.10). Making it changes nothing on the old Brain. Browser sign-ins and other media
   folders are not in it.
2. On the **new** Brain (a normal fresh install), **Bring in the file** with the same password: it is checked first (a wrong
   password or a damaged file changes nothing), then **Move in now** stops the panel and, as it starts again, puts the old Brain's
   files in place. The new Brain's own config, data, processes and media are **kept** in `backups/before_brain_move_<date>`, never
   deleted. Everyone signs in with the old Brain's user names and passwords.
3. **USB ports**: each old USB port (COM3) is changed to the new Brain's (/dev/ttyACM0) in **every Schema at once**, Simulator
   boards included. A board the old Brain saw is found by its serial number and picked for you. It can be used any time, not only
   after a move. Ethernet and WiFi boards keep their address.
   *Changed 2026-11-20* (Panel Updates entry 29 (e)): **Change to** is the **same USB Port list as the Interface pop-up** (Rule
   2.63): the ports on this Brain now with what is plugged in and its serial number, on Windows the number alone (COM3 shows as 3),
   the old port always in the list (red **not found on this Brain** when it is not here, Design Rule #1), and **🔄 Look again** at
   the bottom of the list, which keeps what was already picked. Move in now asks in the Skynet confirm box (Rule 2.64).
(thread "Move a computer Brain to a Pi", Help 119)

9.10 **The Windows Setup .exe is signed** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09): Smart App Control blocks unsigned programs, so the
release build signs the Setup .exe and the Uninstall .exe inside it with Microsoft Artifact Signing (Azure), using six GitHub
settings (three secrets, three variables). The steps are in [Code_Signing_Setup.md](Code_Signing_Setup.md). Until all six are
set, or if signing fails, the Setup .exe is built unsigned and the release is still made; the release notes say which.
(thread "Sign the Setup .exe with Azure")

9.11 **The Setup and its start files stay clear of what virus scanners distrust** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09, after
Malwarebytes called the unsigned Setup .exe "Malware.Ransom.Agent.Generic", a guess, not a real find): the Setup .exe has
its Details filled in (company, description, a version number that goes up with each build, original file name). The
.bat start files never use PowerShell's `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` (not needed for a one-line command) and download only
into the user's own TEMP folder, never the shared Public folder. What Setup and the start files do for the brewer does not
change. Signing (Rule 9.10) is the real cure; until it is on, a scanner may still guess wrong, and the file can be
restored and reported to the scanner's maker as a false positive. Both programs (the Importer ships in the same Setup).
(thread "Stop antivirus flagging the Setup")
Virus check (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-12: "Can a exe be sent to the virus check within github"): after every Release is
made, a Windows computer at GitHub scans every .exe on it with Microsoft Defender (first proving the scanner works on the
harmless EICAR test file). Clean: the Release notes get a "Virus check ... nothing found" line. Anything found: the
Release goes back to a Draft (hidden from the public) and GitHub emails OakBarn Brewery; nothing is deleted.
Then VirusTotal (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-12: "Can skynet have that free account", key in the VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY secret)
has about 70 scanners look at every .exe; it only reports (counts and links at the top of the Release notes, a warning
if any flag a file) and never hides the Release. Skipped until the key is saved.
(thread "Turn on code scanning for Skynet repo")

9.12 **The Skynet pictures and sounds are their own add-only Setup** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "remove all the graphics and
have separate exe loader for them ... we might only want to add more graphics (Never Change or Delete!)", "All Media Files"):
everything in media/ (pictures and sounds) is left out of the panel zip and the Skynet Brewer Setup, and ships as
**Skynet_Media_Setup_<date>.exe** (Windows) and **Skynet_Media_<date>.zip** (Mac, Linux, Pi, by hand), on the same GitHub
Releases page. They only ADD: a file already there by that name is never changed, nothing is deleted (Rule #1), and the user's own
pictures and sounds are never touched. **Get Skynet pictures** (Help 59) is add-only too. A redone drawing is a new file with a new
name. The Setup's last page, the ReadMes and Help 183 say where to get it. **No copyrighted media** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10; made exact 2026-11-18: "No Copywrite stuff in any Skynet Media",
"My own will be under the MIT Liencence and Public", "CC BY and CC By SA are fine. we will put the credit in a Read me"):
Skynet ships only these pictures and sounds:
1. **Its own** (made by OakBarn Brewery or for Skynet), under the MIT License.
2. **Public domain** ones, CC0 included.
3. Ones under **CC BY** or **CC BY-SA**, with the credit the license asks for in the README (**Media credits**) and in
   Media_Licenses.csv. A changed copy of a CC BY-SA picture or sound stays CC BY-SA (it cannot become MIT).
4. **Fonts** under the **SIL Open Font License 1.1 (OFL)** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20: "A for font rule"), such as Google Noto,
   for showing a Help language whose letters a device may not have. The OFL license file ships next to the fonts, and each font
   has a row in Media_Licenses.csv. A font is never sold on its own and keeps its own name if changed, as the OFL asks.

Nothing under a non-commercial (NC) or no-changes (ND) Creative Commons license, and nothing under any other license.
**Exception** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-18, "Yes"): the BruControl Import's clinking beer mugs icon (Google Noto Emoji, Apache
License 2.0) stays, with its credit in the README's Media credits.
Every picture or sound that is not Skynet's own has a row in
[Media_Licenses.csv](Media_Licenses.csv) with its source, license and what the license asks for. A questionable file is replaced by one OakBarn Brewery makes, or by a free one OakBarn Brewery approves.
*2026-11-17 (OakBarn Brewery: "Every thing with a possible copywrite violation needs to be listed and changed to a Non copywrite version"):* the pictures that might be copyrighted (the Riptide-style Pump_<color>_Rip pictures, BurnerFlame, the Burner No Flame and BigMacRElement PNGs, brewery_main.png, the Help 180 Bob screenshot and Musketeers clip art, and the valve photos in Delete/) were taken out of the public repo and replaced by Skynet drawings; the list is in docs/Image_Library.md, Removed for copyright. They are still in the Git history. Every picture Skynet ships has a row in docs/Image_Library.md. AlarmBitter stays (OakBarn Brewery's own).
Both programs (the Importer ships in the same Setup; it already copies imported pictures and sounds into User folders).
**Exception** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10, "Keep the Beep", "Song and clip also with the brain"): the three fallback sounds,
sounds/alarm_beep.wav, sounds/Skynet/Alarm_Sound_Missing.mp3 and sounds/Skynet/Find_The_File_Connecting.mp3, also stay in the
panel zip and the Skynet Brewer Setup (in defaults/media, copied in only when missing), so an Alarm or Sound Player can always
sound. Every other sound and picture is only in the Media Setup.
(thread "Shrink the Setup .exe and remove dead code", Help 183)
*2026-11-17 (Rule 9.22):* the Skynet Media Setup .exe is retired: the Update Setup brings the pictures and sounds added since the last
one, the Full Setup has them all. The Media zip stays (Mac, Linux, Pi, by hand). Still add-only.

9.13 **The extra Sample Schemas are their own add-only Setup** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "separate the Sample Schemas in a
separate exe and only leave the 3 vessel as the only Sample Schema as Skynet Panel ships"; "leave the new exe empty of schema
because we may fix those before adding and I would do That one at a Time. That would also be the basis for someone imported a
Schema from another Brewer"): the panel zip and the Skynet Brewer Setup ship **only the 3 Vessel 1 Pump sample**

in `Sandbox/` (Rule 16.8) and are added **one at a time**, each only after it is brought up to the current Rules. Like the Media
Setup (Rule 9.12) it only ADDS: a sample already there by that name is never changed, nothing is deleted (Rule #1), and a redone
sample gets a new name. The panel lists `sample_schemas` after the 3 Vessel sample under Add a Sample Schema (Rule 10.6); a name
already in `samples/configs` wins. **A Schema from another brewer** goes in the same folder (its `sample.json`, `config.json` and
`processes/`) and comes in the same way. An update of the panel never touches `sample_schemas`. The three samples older versions put in `samples/configs`
(two-vessel-one-pump, brewzilla-brew-day, oakbarn-brucontrol) are **moved, never deleted**, to `backups/old_samples_<date>` on an
update; nothing else is touched (a user's own Schemas are in `config/schemas`, never in `samples`). **Videos:** Help 83 links
