sample Schema exe Have tick boxes for which samples will be imported. No All Tickbox. Rule Never Delete a Sample Available if a
change is need add a new Sample with the same Name but at #2"): the Sample Schemas Setup shows **one tick box per sample** so the
brewer picks which samples are imported, and has **no All tick box**. A sample that is available is **never deleted**: when a change
is needed, a new sample is added with the **same Name and #2** at the end (then #3 ...), and the old one stays. The tick boxes are
built with the first sample put in the Setup (it holds none yet). (thread "Move Sample Schemas to own Setup", Help 184)
*2026-11-17 (Rule 9.22):* the Skynet Sample Schemas Setup .exe is retired: the Update Setup brings the Sample Schemas added since the
last one, the Full Setup has them all. The Sample Schemas zip stays (Mac, Linux, Pi, by hand). *Replaced:* "a redone sample gets a
new name" and "An update of the panel never touches `sample_schemas`": a changed Skynet sample now replaces its older copy (a Schema
made from it is the user's own and is never touched).

9.14 **Official Skynet: the program on a Brain is checked on every start, and a change is reported** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-12:
"can we set something so that the skynet code on ones sent from Skynet Official updates cannot be modified once on a Brain?", "WE
still want it open source but maybe once on a user computer core code cannot be accessed", "Warn the end user is a good idea for
non official updates", "Explain the Offical Updates in the Help"). Skynet stays open source (MIT): the code stays public on GitHub.
1. **The list:** every merge, GitHub writes `skynet_files.json` next to `version.json` (tools/make-file-list.js): the fingerprint
   (SHA-256) of every **core** program file: `server.js`, `importer.js`, `package.json`, `lib`, `public`, `templates`, `firmware`,
   `install`, `samples`. Never edited by hand. Not core, never checked or touched: `config`, `data`, `media`, `processes`, `help`
   (Admins edit Help pages), `sample_schemas`, `node_modules`, `backups`. (Text files are compared without carriage returns.)
2. **Every start** (lib/official.js) the panel compares its core files with the list of its own version from **OakBarn Brewery's
   GitHub** (always oakbarn/Skynet_Brewery, never the repository named in `version.json`); without the internet, with the list that
   came with it, and says so. **Official** = an OakBarn Brewery version and every core file the same. **Changed** = an OakBarn
   Brewery version with core files changed, missing or added. **Not Official** = someone else's copy (a fork), or no Panel version.
3. **Warn the end user:** the Menu Bar version shows **✓ Official**, **⚠ Changed**, **⚠ Not Official** or **⚠ Not checked**; when
   not Official, a red bar on every screen (Details, Help, ✕ until the next check); **☰ Menu > About > Official Skynet** names the
   Changed, Missing and Added files, with **🔍 Check again**. The check never stops anything: a running brew carries on.
4. **Repair** (Admins, when Changed): the official file of the same version for every changed or missing one, from OakBarn Brewery's
   GitHub, each checked against the official list before use; the replaced and added files are **moved** to
   `backups/changed_files_<date>`, never deleted (Rule #1). Without the internet: run the Setup of that version again.
5. **Read-only:** Official and unchanged, the core files are made Read-only, so an editor can't save over one by accident. Not in a
   developer's copy (a `.git` folder). The Windows Setup (install and uninstall) and the Mac and Linux / Pi installers take
   Read-only off the core files first; `unzip -o` on a Pi replaces them anyway.
6. **Honest limit:** whoever is the administrator of a computer can change any file on it, the check included. It finds and
   reports changes; it can't make them impossible. Replaces the old "+ changes" after the version (the `code` fingerprint in
   `version.json`, which covered only `lib`, `public`, `server.js` and `package.json`).
7. **Help 191** explains Official Skynet updates, Repair, the virus checks on every Release (Rule 9.11) and how anyone can check a
   Setup .exe for free at virustotal.com (named, not linked: Rule 11.10). Both programs: the BruControl Import's files are core
   files of the same Setup, so the same check covers them; the Panel shows it. The Importer's Build page shows no badge and runs
   no check of its own.
8. **Retired program files** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-18, after an update: About said "2 added program files"): a core file that
   Skynet no longer uses is moved to `Delete/` in the repo (Rule 15.3) and its path is added to `RETIRED` in lib/official.js. An
   update only adds and replaces files, so an older copy can stay on a Brain. On every check, each retired file still there (and
   not in this version's list) is **moved** to `backups/retired_files_<date>`, never deleted (Rule #1), so it is not counted as
   Added. Skynet does this in the Background and needs no user input.

9.15 **The installers work from and into a folder with any name** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-12, after a brewer on Ubuntu
24.04 ran the Linux installer from `Brassage bière/.../Skynet Brew Panel`): spaces, accented letters (é, è, ü), apostrophes,
`$`, `%` and quotes in the folder name never stop an install, an update or the panel. Every path is kept whole (in quotes), and
each file the installer writes (the start file, the Skynet Brewer menu entry and Desktop icon, the start-by-itself service) gets the
path in that file's own way of quoting. Applies to the Linux, Raspberry Pi and Mac installers and to the panel itself. Both
programs: the BruControl Import is Windows only and is installed by the same Setup .exe; nothing changes there.

9.16 **Every pull request runs the Skynet tests** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "do that on 369"). GitHub runs the whole test suite
(`npm test`) on every pull request to the default branch and after every merge (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`). It shows on the pull
request as the check **Skynet tests**: green = every test passed, red = one failed (its log names the test). The branch ruleset can make
it required before a merge, so the name **Skynet tests** never changes. It changes no code and needs no secrets. Both programs: the
BruControl Import's tests are in the same suite.

9.17 **A Schema backup every time a change is saved; nothing is ever written over** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13, README markup
"Skynet Brew Panel 2a": "Only make a Backup after Build Mode and Changes saved"; "the Schema name and Name_yyyymmddThhmm.BacUp"; "If we
save a Back up every time a change is made and saved, the daily backup is not needed. That was a feature I wanted in BruControl";
on a Schema import with a name already taken: "Use the Rule, just cannot overwrite a file"):
- **Every saved change** (Edit layout > Save Changes and every other layout save, a restore) first keeps the Schema as it was, with its
  saved values, as `<Schema name>_yyyymmddThhmm.BacUp` in `config/schemas/backups/<id>/`. **Back up this Schema now** makes one at
  any time. There is **no daily backup** any more. A backup is never written over (a second one in the same minute gets `_2`) and
  none is ever removed. Help says only that Skynet does this in the Background and needs no user input (Rule 11.13).
- **Schema.json page:** no copy on opening; a copy is made before every save or restore (`config/backups`).
- **An import never writes over a Schema:** a Schema whose name is taken is added as `Name #2`, `#3` ... (the same as Rule 9.13).
- **An import never writes over a Process either** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "Change the way in skynet to something different as I
  think that is all background and never seen by a user Name(1) is more standard to the Windows World"): an imported Process with the
  same name as one you have but other text comes in as `Name_1` (`_2` ...), and the imported Schema's Process lines and Process
  Widgets point to it. `_1` stands in for Windows' `(1)` because a name can't have ( ) (Rule 3.1, docs/Special_Characters.md).
- **Both programs:** the Panel's Schemas; the BruControl Import saves its Schema files to the Import folder and never writes over one.

9.18 **The Processes folder is `processes`** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13, README markup "Skynet Brew Panel 2a": "Rename to Skynet
Terms. That is part of the No Bructrol Rule"). It was called `scripts`, BruControl's word. Everywhere: the panel's folder, the
release's `defaults/processes`, each sample's `processes/` (Sample Schemas and a Schema from another brewer, Rule 9.13), Brain Move
files (Rule 9.9), File Move, the installers, and the MQTT topic `<base>/processes/running`. A panel from an earlier trial version
that still has only `scripts/` gets it renamed to `processes/` once, on its next start, so no Process is lost; the installers'
Start Fresh and start-over also clear an old `scripts/` folder. Help says only that Skynet does this in the Background and needs no
user input (Rule 11.13). Only the BruControl Importer still says "scripts" where it means BruControl's own Scripts.

9.19 **Uninstall deletes everything** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13, after an uninstall left `C:\Brewing\Import` with its
BruControl files and `BrewPanel\data\brewlog.db` behind; picked "All of C:\Brewing, after a warning"). The Windows uninstall
works like Start Fresh (Rule 9.8), with nothing saved:
1. One red warning lists what goes. **No** stops and nothing is deleted; to keep something, copy it somewhere else first.
2. Skynet is stopped first, because Windows can't delete a file a program has open, like the brew log (OakBarn Brewery: "To get
   rid of the DB you need to be sure node js is stopped"). The uninstall and the Setup (every update, Start Fresh and Modified
   Fresh Start) ask the panel to stop by itself, the normal way with every output Off first (Rule 6.31), with a key the panel
   writes in `data\stop.key` each time it starts and only on this computer (`lib/stoppanel.js`, `POST /ui/localstop`); the
   BruControl Importer is closed the way its own Close button does. Only Skynet's own Node.js is stopped, never another Node.js
   program, and nothing is killed. If it is still running after 15 seconds, the user is asked to close it (Retry / Cancel).
3. Deleted: the panel folder (`C:\Brewing\BrewPanel`: program, config, data, processes, backups, media), the Import folder and
   everything in it, the shortcuts, and Skynet's own small folder in the user's AppData (the Skynet window's and the Importer's
   remembered sign-ins and settings). The Brewing folder itself goes only when nothing else is left in it.
4. If a file still can't be deleted, a notice says to restart the computer and delete the Brewing folder by hand.
5. **Helper programs are not removed** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "Add a Comment about not removing auxiliary programs like
   Tailscale if you installed them"): Node.js, Tailscale and any other program the user installed stay, because other programs
   may use them. The red warning, Help 19 and install/ReadMe.txt say so and point to Settings > Apps.
Both programs (the Importer is in the same Setup). The Mac and Linux / Pi installers have no uninstall.

9.20 **A Full Setup with the pictures and sounds inside** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "Set GitHub to have 2 different Skynet
Panel Installs. The ones we have now but a new one that is a Full install that also has the media embedded so a new install does
not need the media exe separate"). Every Release also carries **Skynet_Brewer_Full_Setup_<date>.exe**: the same Skynet Brewer
Setup (same pages, choices, Uninstall and Rules) with every Skynet picture and sound of the Media Setup inside it. It adds them the
Media Setup's way (Rule 9.12): a file already there by that name is never changed and nothing is deleted. It adds them after a
Start Fresh, so a Fresh Start gets them back with no second Setup. Its welcome page says it is the Full one, and its file Details
say "Full Setup". The plain Skynet Brewer Setup, the Media Setup and the Media zip stay on every Release as they are (Rule #1,
Never Take Away; the Media Setup and zip are made new only when media changed, Rule 9.21): the plain Setup is the small one for updates. Built by tools/build-release.sh from the same SkynetBrewer.nsi
(`-DMEDIA_SRC`); signed the same way when signing is set up (Rule 9.10); scanned by Microsoft Defender and VirusTotal like every
.exe on the Release (Rule 9.11). Size: about 12 MB (the plain Setup about 5 MB); GitHub allows up to 2 GB per Release file, and
VirusTotal takes files over 32 MB through its large-file upload. Ships only the media already in Media_Licenses.csv (no new
media). Both programs (the Importer is in the same Setup; nothing changes there). (thread "Add a Full Setup with media included",
Help 19 and 183)
**No choices: the Full Setup always overwrites everything** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17, Panel Updates Sandbox entry 10, word for
word: "Somewhere in a sandbox we had about a full install not having any options always a full install and will overwrite any
installed folders or files. If the Install can see a previous install the one warning is allowed that explains this is the Full
install and will OVERWRITE everything. If Only an Update, get that Update. and then a link to the Update and clicking it closes the
install. also a Close and Do Not install Option that closes the installer."; "It is annoying to have to click the Fresh every
time."). The Full Setup does not show the four update choices of Rule 9.8. On a new computer it just installs. When it finds Skynet
already installed it shows **one warning page**: this is the Full install and it will OVERWRITE everything, with a link **Get the
Update Setup** (opens the download page and closes the Full Setup), a **Close and Do Not Install** button (closes it, nothing
changed) and **Install**. Install runs the same Start Fresh as Rule 9.8 choice 1 (`lib/freshstart.js fresh`), then adds the Skynet
pictures and sounds. Before that, the old `config`, `data`, `processes`, `media`, `backups` and Import folders are **moved, never
deleted**, to `<Brewing folder>\Skynet_Backups\Before_Full_Setup_<date>` (outside the panel folder, so the overwrite cannot reach
them). The plain Setup (the Update Setup) keeps its four choices. *Replaced:* "the same Skynet Brewer Setup (same pages, choices,
Uninstall and Rules)": the Full Setup now has the warning page instead of the choices page.
**Backup or no backup** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-18: "On a Full Install, add question about Back up if previous installtion
installed and ask Abort and get Just Update or Install with Backup Yes or Install No Backup"): the warning page now has one choice,
two round buttons: **1. Install with no backup**, already picked (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-18: "I do not generally want a backup
for a Full install"; "It made a backup without asking"), skips the move, so the old folders are deleted for good by the Start
Fresh; **2. Install and back up my old folders first** does the move to `Skynet_Backups\Before_Full_Setup_<date>` above. "Abort and get Just Update" is the **Get the Update Setup** link; **Close and Do Not Install** stays (Rule #1,
Never Take Away). Still the one warning: no second pop-up for choice 1, the page itself says the folders are deleted for good. A
silent Setup never reaches the page. *Replaced:* "No choices" and "Before that, the old ... folders are moved" (always): the move is
now choice 2, and no backup is the default.
*2026-11-17 (Rule 9.22):* the Full Setup also has every Skynet Sample Schema, added the same add-only way.

9.21 **The Media Setup and Media zip are made new only when Skynet pictures or sounds are added** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15:
"Unless we add additional Skynet Media files, the Media exe and Zip do not need updating"). On every merge the release workflow
looks at the last Media Setup on a published Release. If nothing in `media/` (and nothing in the Media Setup's own script,
`install/windows/SkynetMedia.nsi`) changed since it was made, the new Release carries **that same Media Setup and Media zip,
unchanged, with their own older date in the name**, and its notes say so. If a picture or sound was added (or anything in `media/`
changed), both are made new with the new date. Media stays add-only (Rule 9.12): a changed drawing is a new file with a new name, so
any change means new media. The Media Setup and zip are still on every Release, so the Latest Release always has them (Rule #1,
Never Take Away). The plain Skynet Brewer Setup and the Full Setup are made on every merge as before, and the Full Setup always
carries every picture and sound (Rule 9.20). OakBarn Brewery can force a new Media Setup with **Actions > Panel version > Run
workflow > rebuild media** (for example once signing is set up, Rule 9.10, so the Media Setup gets signed). If the last one cannot be
found or downloaded, it is made new, so a Release is never missing it. Both programs (the Importer is in the same Setup; nothing
changes there). (thread "Rebuild Media Setup only when media changes", Help 183)
*2026-11-17 (Rule 9.22):* there is no Media Setup .exe any more; this Rule now decides only whether the Media zip is made new.

9.22 **The Update Setup brings the new Skynet pictures, sounds and Sample Schemas; no separate Media or Sample Schemas Setup**
(OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "If there are new skynet Media files since the last Update exe, can they be included in the update and
added to the media on the brain"; "Add New Skynet Schema same as media. WE could get rid of both the Schema Uodate and the Media
updates"; **why:** "THat is the correct way to handle it.. No extra steps for a User."). The plain Skynet Brewer Setup (the Update
Setup) and the panel zip carry, besides the three fallback sounds of Rule 9.12, every file **added** to `media/`, and every
file **added or changed** in `sample_schemas/`, since the last published Release that has an Update Setup. Pictures and sounds go in `defaults/media`, and the
panel copies in only the ones the Brain does not have yet on its next start (lib/seed.js). Sample Schemas go in `sample_schemas/`,
where a **changed Skynet sample replaces the Brain's older copy of it** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17, about Skynet Templates: "Since they are only used on a New Schema, they would not affect any User Schema"; the same holds for a sample). A Schema the user already made from a sample is their own copy and is never touched. Skynet Templates (`templates/`) are program files, so every update already replaces them; User Templates (`config/templates`) are never touched. Pictures and sounds stay add-only: a file already there is never changed (Rule 9.12). Only Skynet's own
media already in docs/Media_Licenses.csv is ever in `media/`, so nothing copyrighted ships. The **Full Setup** (Rule 9.20) has every
Skynet picture, sound and Sample Schema. So the **Skynet Media Setup .exe and the Skynet Sample Schemas Setup .exe are retired**
(allowed before the first Public Production, Rule Old Ways; their scripts are in Delete/install_windows/). The **Media zip**
and **Sample Schemas zip** stay on every Release for Mac, Linux, Raspberry Pi and by hand; the Media zip is still made new only when
media changed (Rule 9.21). Both programs (the Importer is in the same Setup; nothing changes there). (Help 183, 184)

9.23 **Only the newest two Releases stay on GitHub** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-18: "we need to clean that every 25"; "Ok if it can
do that only keep the last one and the new one"). After every merge, once the new Release is made and virus checked, the release
workflow (.github/workflows/panel-version.yml, job keep-newest) deletes every older Panel version Release, so the Releases page has the
new one and the one before it. Only published Releases count: a Release the Virus check hid as a Draft (Rule 9.11) is never counted
or deleted, so the last good one always stays. The **tags stay**, so the Official Skynet check (Rule 9.14) still works for an older
install; only the Release pages and their downloads go. The Skynet-Sounds Release (Rule 7.20) is never touched. The number kept is
KEEP in that job. Both programs (the Importer is in the same Setup; nothing changes there). (Help 19)

9.24 **The Skynet Language Fonts: an add-only Setup of their own** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20, Panel Updates entry 45: "if you
clone the checked install and only add the font package, the second exe has been checked already"; "Ok then add Chinese, Japanesse,
Korean, Thai and Hindi to the Font Package"; "lets do no bold and simplified"). The fonts for a Help language (Rule 11.16) are **not**
in the panel zip, the Update Setup or the Full Setup, so the main Setup stays small. Every Release also carries
**Skynet_Language_Fonts_Setup_<version>.exe** (Windows) and **Skynet_Language_Fonts_<version>.zip** (Mac, Linux, Pi, by hand), built
by tools/build-release.sh from the same release (install/windows/SkynetLanguageFonts.nsi): Google Noto Sans, **Regular only**, for
**Chinese (Simplified), Japanese, Korean, Thai and Hindi**, as WOFF2 web fonts cut into small pieces (about 10 MB), each with its OFL
license file (Rule 9.12 point 4). Fetched from npm (Fontsource) at exact versions; with no npm at build time they are simply not made
and the Release goes on. Like the Media Setup of Rule 9.12 it **only adds** (a font already there is never changed, nothing is
deleted) into the panel's `fonts` folder, which is not a core folder (Rule 9.14). This is the one add-on .exe left after Rule 9.22.
Fonts an Admin adds with **🔤 Add Font to Brain** are the user's own (data/fonts), never touched by a Setup. (Help 242)

9.25 **The Skynet Music Pack is an optional download, not in the Setups** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-18, Panel Updates entry 30:
"These may need to be in a separate file", "a Get Music Pack"; 2026-11-20: "an Add On music pack", "subfolders on images and audio
of Patron in Addition", "Do not need to be to fancy ... do not need any warnings or nanny"). Public domain marches and bugle calls
are a **GitHub Release of their own** (tag `Skynet-Music-Pack`, never set as the latest release), one MP3 per file. They are
**never put in `media/`** in the code, so Rule 9.22 does not put them in the Update or Full Setup and the Setups stay small.
**☰ Menu > Get Music Pack** (Admins) asks GitHub which files the Release has and copies the ones the Brain is missing into
`media/sounds/Skynet_Music` (lib/musicpack.js). It only ADDS: a sound already there by that name is never changed, nothing is
deleted (Rule #1), and a damaged download (wrong size or fingerprint) never lands. Every file has a row in Media_Licenses.csv and
the pack's credit is in the README's Media credits (Rule 9.12).
**More packs later:** each Add-On pack is one more Release and one row in PACKS in lib/musicpack.js. A **Patron** pack lands in a
`Patron` subfolder of its own (`media/sounds/Skynet_Music/Patron`, and `media/Images/Skynet/Patron` for Patron pictures), next to
the normal folders. Who may get a Patron pack is Panel Updates entry 27 (on hold). A sound or picture that came in a pack is an
ordinary file: there is no lock and no warning, and a user may copy one out and use it as their own.
Both programs: the BruControl Import is not changed (it never brings in the pack). (Help 243)

9.26 **The everyday Windows installer says Update** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-22, Panel Update 9, item 4): the Setup that every release
makes is **Skynet_Brewer_Update_<version>.exe**, and its first screen says Skynet Brewer Update. It is the same program as before
(it installs a new panel or updates one, Rule 9.22). The **Full Setup** keeps its name. The release check finds the newest release by
either name, so an older Setup still updates. Help 18, 19, 183, 184, 191.

## 10. Testing

10.1 **Updates keep logins.** Installing a new version never removes users, passwords, sign-ins or the
recovery code, unless the person installing picks **Update the program and reset all users** or **Start Fresh**
in the installer and confirms its warning (Rule 9.8; Fritz, 2026-11-06). There is no Testing mode switch. (Fritz, 2026-11-03, thread "Keep logins
after installing a new .exe")
*Replaced:* "Testing mode is on: every newly merged version wipes all logins, so Fritz starts fresh with
Admin setup. It stays on until he is in real use." (2026-10-04)

10.2 **Fritz's test bench** (week of 2026-10-20): a Pi, a Mega, an ESP32, one Tilt, a couple of
valves, a 12 V LED as a burner and another as an electric element. Firmware has never run on real
hardware, so expect first real-hardware bug reports. (2026-10-20)

10.3 **Simulation (test mode) touches no hardware.** Turning it on or off stops all Processes and
turns outputs off. (2026-10-05, PR #22)

10.4 **One switch for Simulator or Real boards**, for the whole panel (every Interface at once): the
🔌 Real / 🧪 Simulator button beside ☰ Menu (Admins), ☰ Menu > Switch to Simulator / Real boards,
(Settings > Simulation is gone, Rule 10.10). Timers run as before. **A wait on a reading** (temperature, boil start,
level, weight, flow) **is pretended reached** after a set time (60 clock seconds to start, Simulator bar
> ⚙ Settings, can be switched off); a wait on a button or switch never is. (2026-10-27, Help 77)

10.5 **A new empty Schema starts with no Interface** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "A Schema does not need an interface default.
Users can add devices. Those devices have the Interface on them"). Add the Interfaces on the Devices page. It starts with the Look
picked in ☰ Menu > Default settings > Look of a New Schema (Rule 2.42). A Skynet Schema Template made with no real Interface still
gets a pretend Mega for its Devices, on the Simulator. A copy of a Schema keeps its Interfaces.
*Replaced:* a new Schema that was not a copy started with a pretend Mega named New_Mega_2560_N, on the Simulator (2026-10-27, Help 76).

10.6 **A Sample Schema always comes in as a new Schema** (Schema dropdown > Add a Sample Schema, the
☰ Menu > 🗂 Schema tab, or Settings): it never writes over one of yours. Every Interface in it gets
Connection Simulator (its real connection is kept to switch to later), and the panel switches to
Simulator mode and says so, so nothing real is switched. (2026-10-28, thread "Add sample Schemas to
the Schema list", Help 83)

10.7 **The Simulator bar** (yellow 🧪 SIMULATION bar) can be hidden with **▴ Hide** on the bar or ☰ Menu >
🧪 Hide Simulator bar, per screen. **Hidden, the bar is gone completely** (no strip), so the browser window is free for
the Panel; a small 🧪 on the ☰ Menu button says it is still Simulation. In Simulator mode **☰ Menu > 🧪 Show Simulator
bar** brings it back (changed 2026-11-04, Fritz: "keep the browser window as free as possible for the Panel"; it was a
thin 🧪 SIMULATION strip that always stayed). Hiding changes no setting. **In the Process Editor the bar is off** (2026-11-23, Panel Update 11, item 1a: "Hide the Yellow bar"); ☰ Menu > Show Simulator bar brings it back until the Process Editor is left (Rule 2.70).
**Each time the Simulator is switched on, the bar opens at 25× speed with Auto skip on**; after that
the user's choices stay until the next switch on. (2026-10-28, thread "Improve the Simulator bar
defaults", Help 85)

10.8 **The Sample Schemas can be cloned to a User Schema** (Clone a Schema lists
them after the user's own Schemas, as 🧪 Sample; the panel ships only the 3 Vessel sample, the others come with the Sample Schemas
Setup, Rule 9.13). The clone is a normal User Schema, always loaded at
once, on the simulator (Rule 10.6). The OakBarn Brewery sample is not offered for now. (2026-10-28,
thread "Improve the Simulator bar defaults", Help 85)

10.9 **Sharing Schemas between brewers** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "A place to add a file from another Brewer and an method in
Skynet to export a Schema with a Notice about copywrites but no checking of an export or import between brewers"; "That is between
the Brewers"): the Schema list (Menu Bar dropdown and ☰ Menu > 🗂 Schema) has **Export to share ...** (the same as Schema.json >
Save as .json file) and **Import a brewer's Schema ...** (the same as Schema.json > Open a Schema file). **The place for a file from
another brewer is the Import folder** (`C:\Brewing\Import`), or any .json file picked on the computer; it always comes in as a new
Schema (no Schema is written over). Every one of these dialogs, and the 🗂 Schema tab's **Share with other brewers** part, shows
the notice: *"Skynet does not check what is in a Schema file, going out or coming in. The pictures, sounds, names and anything
else in it, and any copyright on them, are between the brewers."* **Skynet does no checking** of a shared Schema. A shared Schema
can also be added as a folder in `sample_schemas` (Rule 9.13).
**The kinds of files** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "More info about type of files and that media files (if not all are Skynet)
need to be shared as well. Skynet cannot set up to send those files as they may contain copywrite material and then a Link to a Step
by Step on how to tansfer files and maybe even a methos where a user can click a User File to send. Also a caveat about being on the
latest Version of Skynet as items may have been aded."): **Share with other brewers** says what a shared Schema is made of (the
Schema file (.json); the brewer's own pictures and sounds, which the file only names; the Processes (.txt), which are not in the file)
and lists the loaded Schema's own pictures and sounds (not Skynet's, which come with every Skynet), each one a click to save it on
this computer. **Skynet never sends a file itself**, as they may hold copyrighted material: the brewer sends them. A ⚠ caveat says both
brewers should be on the latest version of Skynet, and **❓ Step by step: how to send the files** opens Help 203. The 🗂 Schema
tab's buttons are **Create New Copy of Schema** (was Clone) and, under Add a Sample Schema, **Add This Schema Template** (was Add). Both programs: the BruControl Import saves its Schemas in the same
Import folder; nothing changes there. (thread "Move Sample Schemas to own Setup", Help 44)

10.10 **Every Simulator setting is ONLY on the Simulator bar** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "All Simulator Bar settings should be
ONLY!!! on the Simulator Bar"). Speed, the skip buttons and Auto skip are on the bar itself. **⚙ Settings** on the bar (Admins) opens
the rest: "Skip to next event" lead, Auto skip watch time, Pretend readings are reached and its seconds, the Time jumps table and
the Process timeline, with Save at the top and the bottom. They are not in Settings or on the Default tab. Switching the Simulator on
or off stays on the 🔌 Real / 🧪 Simulator button and the ☰ Menu (Rule 10.4). (Help 85, 20, 77)

10.11 **When a change touches Schemas, check only the 3 Vessel Sample** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, on whether a removed Template
was on the 3 Vessel Sample: "Only any thing that affect a 3 Vessel Sample. Rule. Check only things that affect the 3 Vessel sample
and no other schema or tab"). When a change could touch what is already on a Schema (a Template taken out, a renamed item, a new
setting), Skynet checks and fixes only the **3 Vessel Sample** (samples/configs/three-vessel-one-pump). No other Schema, Schema
Template or Tab is searched or changed for it. **Both programs:** the BruControl Import has no Sample Schema to check, so nothing
changes there.

10.12 **No Switch to Simulator while brewing** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-23, on the Panel Update 12 Simulator question: "We want to
be able to switch to a simulator except on a Brew Day and Actively brewing"). While a Flow, Sub or Repeat Process runs (a Looper runs
all the time and does not count), ☰ Menu > 🧪 Switch to Simulator is grayed, and its balloon names the running Processes: stop them
first, or wait until the Brew Day ends. Any other way in is refused with one message. Switching back to the Real boards is never
blocked. There is no way to step out of brewing into the Simulator and back (OakBarn Brewery, asked about it for troubleshooting:
"Likely a Bad Idea to allow it"); a Process log with exact line numbers and a list of issues to fix before the next Brew Day are in
the Panel Updates sandbox instead. **Both programs:** the BruControl Import has no Simulator, so nothing changes there. (Help 85, 77)

10.13 **The Process Error Log: Fix before next Brew Day** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-23, after he set stepping out of a brew into the
Simulator aside: "Likely a Bad Idea to allow it.  Maybe a Log with exact location in a Process with Line mumbers and a way for a user
to keep a log of issue that need to be fixed before the next bre day"; "I think just and error log with the line # of the error, what
the error was and a way to fix it if evident"; "Do a combination of A and C.  Log it, and if it was fixed, the fix.  and the Check
button could be used to check it in a simulation mode just for the checking"; on how much a Check runs, "I think B is best and use
the Pop up Override to run from just above the error"; "Go ahead and build it"). Panel Updates entry 55.
- **☰ Menu > 🔧 Fix before next Brew Day** (everyone reads it; Brewers and Admins add, check and tick off), with the number open.
- **Every Process error is written by itself:** the time, the Process, the **line number** (the line in the file, as in the Process
  Editor, blank and comment lines counted), the line's own text, what the error was, and **how to fix it when evident**
  (public/errorfix.js; nothing when the error's own words already show how). A Process that does not start is written the same way.
  The same error on the same line again is one entry with a count. A Process saved while it ran is marked, as its lines may have moved.
  **Look** (OakBarn Brewery, Error Text PDF 2026-11-25): the Process and line in red, the error in red on its own line, and when the
  error lists the names that are allowed ("(they are: ...)"), a light blue **Possible Suggested Replacement at Line N:** on the next
  line, then the list. The whole message is kept (up to 4000 characters), so the list is not cut short.
- **The fix is kept:** when the Process is saved with the error's line changed, the entry keeps the line as it was and as it is now.
- **🧪 Check** runs the saved Process in a **check-only simulation** (lib/checkrun.js): its own Engine on a copy of the Brain that
  reads every Device, Widget and gGlobal as it is now; what it sets stays in the copy (and is listed), nothing goes to a board, the
  database, the screens or the saved Schema, and a running brew is never touched. It starts **just above the error** (the statement
  before it, unless that is a wait, step or label) with the variables the Process had at the error, and stops at the **next wait or
  step** (also a sleep, an ask, a manual valve or reading ask, a lock), at the end, or at an error; 5000 statements or 5 seconds with
  no wait end it too. **▶ Override** goes on past that wait, like the Override pop-up (Rule 2.26), up to the next one. A Check with no
  error moves the entry to **Fixed** with its fix.
- **✔ Fixed** and **↩ Open again** by hand; **Delete**. **➕ Add an issue**: a person's own issue, with the Tab (or the open Process).
- **Kept on the Brain** (data/errorlog.json): open entries until fixed or deleted, fixed ones 90 days, at most 500.
- **Recommendations taken** (OakBarn Brewery said build it before these were asked): the Add an issue box is in this list's window;
  open ones are kept until fixed, fixed ones 90 days; Brewers and Admins add and tick, view-only accounts read.
**Both programs:** the BruControl Import has no Processes running and no ☰ Menu, so nothing changes there. (Help 247, 33)

10.14 **Resume after an error: the brewer decides** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-25, after a Brew Day stopped on an error: "Can we have
the Brew day Progress if the error is not critical with a resume?"; on who decides, "any error may be able to be fixed during a Brew
Day so I would say leave up to the User to Resume. I have had to replace Pumps and Valves, but BruControl would just start over and I
had to continue without the software. If I could have resumed, I could still follow the Process and resume again if it hit the same
error later"; "I might even be able to swap a Heater!"; "I could just re route through the RIMS!").
- A Process that stops on an error **leaves everything as it is** (nothing is switched Off by the error) and keeps the line it stopped
  on and its variables. The error still goes on the Process Error Log (Rule 10.13).
- A red pop-up on **every screen** (with the Brain notices, Rule 6.31) shows the Process, the line number, the line and the error.
  **The first time an error happens it always waits for a brewer** (Skynet can not see a pump swapped or a path re-routed). The
  choices (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-26: "1: Fix hardware 2: Fix Process code 3. Ignore same Error in any Process, Skip this Line and
  Proceed"; "Resume does not work. It needs to start one line past 77 (line 78)"):
  1. **🔧 Fixed hardware: try line N again**: the same line runs again (a pump, valve or heater fixed or swapped), as often as needed.
  2. **✎ Fix Process code**: the Process Editor opens at that line; Save, then Try again runs the saved Process from that line. A
     line still open on the Error Log shows in the editor with a **red background and bold yellow text**, and goes back to normal
     colors when its entry is Fixed (a 🧪 Check with no error, or ✔ Fixed) (OakBarn Brewery: "Put the Error in Red Background BOLD
     Yellow text in the editor"; "And after a check with no issues normal Text colors").
  3. **▶ Resume at the next line**: that line is left out and the Process goes on at the next one.
  4. **⏭ Ignore this error in any Process and go on**: the line is left out, and from then on the same error (the same words) in any
     Process, on any line, is left out by itself with no pop-up (still printed and on the Error Log) until the Brain restarts. Its
     **one warning** shows when it is pressed: you are responsible, stay with the brew and watch it. It takes effect only after
     **✔ I take responsibility** is clicked (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-26: "Maybe Have to Click a Key that they take Resposibility");
     **Cancel** leaves it stopped with the choices again.
  The pop-up and the Error Log show a plain **Why:** line under the error when Skynet can tell why it failed (OakBarn Brewery,
  2026-11-26: "if you can add plain text to the error and why it failed, do so"; public/errorfix.js).
  **✕** leaves it stopped. Operators and Admins pick; view-only accounts see it. Starting the Process over lets the pop-up go. The
  variables come back as they were. A Check run (Rule 10.13) and a Code Value Widget's code have no Resume.
- The "Next time this error happens" dropdown (Auto with a 5 second pop-up / Auto with no pop-up, 2026-11-25) is **replaced** by
  choice 4 (OakBarn Brewery picked it 2026-11-26; Design Rule #1 is suspended until Production).
**Both programs:** the BruControl Import runs no Processes, so nothing changes there. (Help 247)

## 11. Help pages

11.1 **Every new feature gets a Help page** (or an update to one) when it merges. Help pages are
Markdown files in help/ on the Brain, numbered for order. Next free number: **159** (143 is the BruControl Importer's, 144 API_Name, 151 Panel Looks, 152 Skynet Dial, 153 Move alone, Swap and Put back, 154 Properties hot spots, 155 Default settings, 156 Precise heating, 157 Schema Templates, 158 DigiBoil and Brewzilla by hand). (2026-10-04,
PR #16)

11.2 **New Help headings and ☰ Menu tabs** are added to the right-click Help map. (2026-10-21,
PR #57)

11.3 **BruControl differences are only in the Importer Help** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "BruControl Differences only in the
Importer Help. Skynet Help and Hover Help take all references to Brucontrol Out. They can be added from the Skynet Pane Help when we
update it for the Importer Help so keep the extracted help in a Sand Box."; "Hold off on the Import Help until we finish the SkyPanel
Help").
  - **BruControl is a forbidden word in the Skynet Panel** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-21: "Wrong. BruControl is a forbidden word in
    Skynet Panel and Only used in th eImported." [the Importer]). The word is never shown anywhere in the Panel: screens, menus,
    balloons, messages, pop-ups, Help, Hover Help, the README, Template notes and the sample Processes. It is used **only in the
    Importer** (its own pages, its Build page, its Help). Where the Panel must point to the Importer it says **the Importer**.
    Code comments, these Rules and the docs for builders may still say BruControl (no one sees them in the Panel).
    *This replaces the 2026-11-10 exception* that let a Panel page name the Import screen or "the BruControl Import program"
    (Help 1, 44 and 67): that exception is gone.
  - **Skynet Panel Help and Hover Help say nothing about BruControl:** no comparisons ("like BruControl's ..."), no "From BruControl"
    sections, no BruControl words for things, no history of how BruControl did it.
  - **The Importer's own Help pages** (Help 143 and 165) stay in `help/` for the Importer but are **not listed or searched in the
    Panel's Help** (`IMPORTER_HELP` in lib/help.js). The Import screen's Help (Help 8) is Panel Help and has no BruControl part.
  - **Nothing taken out is lost:** every BruControl sentence and section taken out is kept in `Sandbox/help/BruControl_Help_Extract.md`,
    with where it was and what is there now. It is the starting point of the Importer Help.
  - **The Importer Help** (Help 143 and 165, plus what is kept in the extract) is the Skynet Panel Help with the BruControl comments
    added. It is **on hold until the Skynet Panel Help is finished**.
  - **Importer updates go to the Sandbox for now; one Big Merge later** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-12: "For the Most Part, Put Updates to
    the Importer in a Sand Box. We will do a Big Merge to move things over to the Importer."; "I might say add this note only in the
    importer version, then that goes to the Importer SandBox"). The Skynet Panel version is polished first (Help, Hover Help, the
    README); its model for the Importer version comes later. Until the Big Merge, anything said to be for the Importer version only
    (a note, a BruControl comparison, a difference) is written in the **Importer Sandbox**, `Sandbox/Importer/Importer_Notes.md` in the private Skynet_Private repo (Rule 13.7), with
    where it goes, and is not put in the Importer yet. **But when OakBarn Brewery says to update both the Importer and Skynet** (OakBarn
    Brewery, 2026-11-12: "I may also tell you to update Both Importer and Skynet, an ten it does not go to the importer sandbox, but to
    the Importer itself"), the change goes straight into the Importer itself as well as Skynet, not into the Sandbox. BruControl text taken out of Skynet text goes to
    `Sandbox/help/BruControl_Help_Extract.md` as before. Example: the README (GitHub front page) is the Skynet version, with no
    BruControl (2026-11-12); its BruControl text is in the extract, ready for the Importer's own Read Me.
  - **A BruControl Read Me:** maybe one Read Me document **in the Importer** (never in the Panel, 2026-11-21) for BruControl users. It
    waits until the Import is done (Rule 14.3).

11.4 **Hover Help is the same as the Skynet Panel Help** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "The Hover Help will be the exact same as the
Skynet Panel Help, with BruControl comments added for the Import Help"). A dialog's balloons (Rule 2.38) say the same thing as the Help
page of that dialog, in the same words, with no BruControl comments (Rule 11.3). The Importer's own hover help is the same, with the
BruControl comments added (on hold with the Importer Help).
*Changed 2026-11-10 by Rule 11.8:* the Help and the Hover Help say the same for the same topic, **unless the Help expands on it**; the
most technical explanations go in the Help, not the Hover Help.

11.5 **Never mention Fritz in any Help** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10). No Help page, balloon or dialog note names a person, and no
"(Fritz, date)" note is written in Help. Who asked for something, and when, is kept in these Rules and their Change log (and may stay in
code comments). Where Help needs to say whose a drawing is, it says **Skynet** (the Skynet drawings, the Skynet Timer frames).

11.6 **OakBarn Brewery entries are few, and approved** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "Oakbarn Entries should be limited and approved").
"OakBarn Brewery" is written in Help or a balloon only where OakBarn Brewery has approved it. A dated "(OakBarn Brewery, date)" note is
not written in Help (as in Rule 11.5). Approved so far: the electrical warning (Rule 6.20) and the GitHub address (github.com/oakbarn). **The one exception to Rule 11.5
"for now":** the beer money button keeps its words **"Buy Fritz a beer"** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "\"Buy Fritz a beer\" is the one
exceotion for now"); Help 17 still names no person. **OakBarn Brewery may also be named where the Help is specifically about the OakBarn
Schema** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "All of those can remain when we are specifically dealing with the OakBarn Schema"): the OakBarn
Brewery Schema Template (Help 157, 158) and the OakBarn Brewery sample (Help 85). Anywhere else it says Skynet (Help 135: the Skynet
plain vessel; Help 99: no OakBarn Hop Warnings). **A Tartan Schema sample** may be added the same way, with permission ("With
permission, we may add Tartan Schema as well as a sample"); it is not added until that permission is given. **The same goes for any other user's Schema**
(OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "If we add another schema from another user, that name will also be allowed"): once added with that
user's permission, their name may be used in Help that is specifically about their Schema.
The others found on 2026-11-10 wait for OakBarn Brewery's word (thread "Set the Help format rules").

11.7 **Hover Help examples use the entries of their own dialog in the 3 Vessel 1 Pump sample** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "Have the
examples in the Hover Help use the Properties and Entries in the Dialog they are on in the # Vessel Schema as a General Rule"). A
balloon's example uses the real names and entries of the same dialog in the 3 Vessel 1 Pump sample, so what you read in the balloon is
what you see in the dialog. First done: the **Heater Properties** of a Vessel Build, with the **HLT element** built into **HLT_Vessel**
(`BM_8_DO@H_Element_HLT~element_BH`: Brewery Mega Port 8, the Brew House Tab, Hysteresis holding 150 °F with an On offset of 1, its probe
`BM1w1_1_HLT_BH`; in a Process `HLT_Vessel.BM_8_DO@H_Element_HLT~element_BH`). A test (test/helpformat.test.js) checks the example still matches
the sample. The other dialogs follow, one at a time.

11.8 **KISS: Keep It Simple, no clutter** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "Label for DDLB and other field 1 to 2 Words. Use Hover Help for
Bloviating, not on the Dialog. Plain English in Both Dialog, Dialog DDLB Choices and the Hover Help. If it needs a more geeky explanation
then maybe but always follow by plain English in Help and Hover Help. Make the Help and Hover Help be the same for the same topic unless
the Help can Expand More. Most technical Explanations in Help and Not Hover Help."). In both programs:
  1. **A field's label is 1 or 2 words**, the label of a dropdown too. Nothing else is written on the dialog to explain it (Rule 2.38).
  2. **Explanations go in the Hover Help**, not on the dialog. **Exception: a need-to-know note** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "Change
     the Rule but avoid mostly as Help is a Better Place but since this is sorta need to know, it follow my One clcik rule"): a short,
     plain English note that the brewer must see to be safe or to set up right may show on the dialog, so it is seen with no extra
     click (Rule 2.44). Use it rarely: one or two sentences, only for safety or setup, and the full explanation stays in the Hover Help
     and the Help. Example: under a greyed Self Priming of No, the priming note (Rule 18.32).
  3. **Plain English everywhere:** the dialog, its dropdown choices (short, Rule 2.38) and the Hover Help. A technical word may follow
     the plain words, in ( ) (Rule 2.37).
  4. **Plain English first, then the technical part.** Where a topic needs a more technical explanation, the plain English comes first,
     in both the Help and the Hover Help.
  5. **The same words for the same topic** in the Help and the Hover Help (Rule 11.4), unless the Help expands on it.
  6. **The most technical explanations go in the Help**, not the Hover Help. Example: how a heater's Hysteresis works has the same plain
     English explanation in the Hover Help and in the Help, using the dialog's own boxes and values (Rule 11.7); the Help then adds the
     technical, scientific explanation.
  7. **The Hysteresis Help is the model** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "Use the Hysteresis Help (Hover and Regular as a Model For
     Help"). Every Help topic and its Hover Help are written the same way: the Hover Help says in plain English what happens, step by
     step, with the dialog's own boxes and values from the 3 Vessel 1 Pump sample (Setpoint 150 °F, Offset (−) −1, 149 °F (150 −1));
     the Help page shows the same Hover Help words first, then a **technical side** part with the science, using the same signs; the
     electrical warning (Rule 6.20) ends it where wiring comes up. The approved Hysteresis words are the balloon on a Heating
     Element's **Current Method** while it is Hysteresis (after the electrical warning), and the **Hysteresis** part of Help 150.
  8. **No "how" the user cannot change:** see Rule 11.13.

11.9 **Step by Step guides** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-11: "Also need Section in Help That is a Step By Step with Pictures on How to do
something. First Step By Step in Add a Schema as I could not see an easy way to begin."). Help has a **Step by Step** section: it is
listed first, above every other page, in the Help page list (and in the page dropdown on a phone). A Step by Step guide:
  1. has a title that starts **Step by Step:** (that is what puts it in the section), and a Help page number like any other page;
  2. walks through one job from the very beginning, numbered **Step 1, Step 2 ...**, with a **picture of the real screen** at each step
     (a screenshot of the panel, in `media/help_pictures/`, named `Step_<Job>_NN_<What>.png`; the thing to press has a red box around it);
  3. follows the Help format (Rules 11.3 to 11.8): plain English, the names of the 3 Vessel sample, no person named;
  4. links to the full Help page of each part for more.
First guide: **Step by Step: Add a Schema** (Help 188). The same day, an easier way to begin: **☰ Menu > ➕ New Schema…** (just under 🗂 Schema)
and a big **➕ New Schema** button (with **❓ Step by step**) on the ☰ Menu > Schema tab; both open the same Add new Schema box as the
Schema dropdown's Add new Schema (the box itself is not changed, Rule 18.10). Both programs: the Importer uses the Panel's Help and Schema
list, so nothing else changes there.

11.10 **No outside links in Help unless OakBarn Brewery directs one; a broken Help link opens nothing** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-12,
Hover Help Blichmann RipTide Dialog 1 #2: "None Links outside of Help unless it is directed By me. If the Help Link in a Hover Help is
Broken or not set, it opens Bing and takes me to a Page on the WEB. Broken links will be sent to support@oakbarnbrewery.com with the
details of the Broken link, and a Pop Up Dialog saying that and a button to Send."):
- **Outside links:** a Help page links to a web page only when OakBarn Brewery directs it. Each one is listed in
  `docs/Outside_Links.md`; a test fails on any Help web link that is not on the list. Those links open in the default browser
  ("Outside links open in the default browser", under How Rules work).
- **A broken Help link:** a hot spot in a Hover Help (Rule 2.49) or a link between Help pages is checked before it opens. When its
  page or part is not there, or it has none set, **nothing opens and nothing goes to the web**: a pop-up says **This Help link is
  broken**, shows the details (where, the link, what is wrong, the page, the browser, the time), and has **✖ Close** and **✉ Send**.
  Send emails the details to **support@oakbarnbrewery.com** from the Brain when its email is set up (Settings > Sending codes);
  otherwise the computer's own mail program opens with them filled in.
- **Both programs:** the Panel and its Help window. The BruControl Import's balloons have no hot spots while its Help is on hold
  (Rule 11.3), so it has no Help links to break.

11.11 **Help in French; the screens stay English, forever** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "French Help Only forever"; "Ballons and
Hover Help French"):
- **Only the Help is translated:** the Help pages, the Hover Help balloons and the Help snippets in balloons. The screens, buttons,
  labels, menus, dropdown choices and messages stay English, in both programs, forever. A French Help page or balloon writes the name
  of a button, box or menu in English, exactly as it is on the screen (**Finish Build**, **Interface ID**), so what you read is what you see.
- **One exception: the safety buttons follow the Help language** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20: "Maybe the skynet over ride and STop
  Button label translate", option A, a change to this Rule): the **Override** button and the **Stop** buttons (a Process Widget's
  ■ Stop, Stop and Stop all on the Processes page, the Ask Before box's Stop, the PID Auto-tune's ■ Stop, the Recipe alerts' ■ Stop)
  show in the language picked in 🌐 Help language, so a brewer reads at once the button that stops or moves on a Process. French:
  Override = **Passer**, Stop = **Arrêt**, Stop all = **Tout arrêter**. The words are in `public/screenwords.js`; a new Help
  language adds its own. Only the Override button's own Label (**Override**) changes: a Label the user typed (**Water Override**) is
  the user's and stays as typed. A French Help page names such a button with both words, **Passer** (Override), and an English page
  says Override. Every other screen word stays English.
- **Picked by 🌐 Help language** at the top of the Help page list: **English** or **Français** (or a User Language, Rule 11.16). The browser remembers it (the Help
  window, the panel's own Help page and the balloons follow the same choice). English is the default.
- **French pages:** `help/fr/`, with the same file names as the English pages. They keep everything that is not words: each heading
  keeps the id of its English heading (`## Pour commencer {#getting-started}`) so links to a part of a page work in both languages, and
  the links, pictures, code and names are the same. The electrical warning (Rule 6.20) is in French, in red under the red triangle:
  "⚠ L'électricité peut tuer. OakBarn Brewery et Skynet ne sont pas électriciens et ne peuvent donner aucun conseil en électricité.
  Consultez un électricien qualifié."
- **English and French never drift apart:** whenever an English Help page changes, its French page is updated **in the same PR**. Each
  French page records which English text it was made from (`help/fr/_source.json`); a test (test/helpfrench.test.js) fails and names the
  page while a French page is missing or out of date. `node tools/help-french.js` lists them; `node tools/help-french.js --stamp <page>`
  marks one brought up to date.
- **Balloons:** each balloon (Hover Help) and each button's own tip shows in French when Français is picked. The French is in
  `public/hoverhelp-fr.json`, English text → French text; the Panel reads it only when French is picked. A balloon with something put in
  it (a name, a number) keeps that part as it is. A balloon change gets its French **in the same PR**: a test
  (test/hoverfrench.test.js) finds every balloon text in the Panel's code and fails, naming it, while one has no French or the French lost
  something that is not words ({0}, ⬢, ⬆, a red mark, a picture, the electrical warning). `node tools/hoverhelp-french.js` lists them.
- **On a Brain:** when an Admin edits an English page in the Help window, its French page shows a note that it may be out of date, with a
  link to the English page. A page not translated yet shows the English page with a note.
- **Machine translation:** the French was made by machine translation. Every French page ends with a note saying so, and that the
  English page is the one that counts if in doubt. A French-speaking brewer may review it.
- **Both programs:** the Skynet Panel's Help and balloons (the BruControl Import's Build page is the Panel's own page). The Importer's
  own pages keep English balloons for now: the Importer Help is on hold (Rule 11.3); when it is written it gets its French the same way.

11.12 **In OakBarn Brewery's markups, { } is an instruction, not text** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "notice that { are
instruction not verbatim text"; "Make that a Rule"):
- In a markup or PDF from OakBarn Brewery (the README, a Help page, Hover Help, a dialog), **text inside curly brackets { } is an
  instruction to Claude**. It is carried out, and never copied into the text.
- **Everything outside the brackets is his text** and goes in word for word, with only the spelling corrected (Rule 2.37).
- An instruction can be a change to make, a question to answer, or where text goes (for example **{Importer Sandbox ...}** moves the
  text inside it to the Importer Sandbox, Rule 11.3). When an instruction is unclear, Claude asks before building it.
- **Both programs:** the Skynet Panel and the BruControl Import.

11.13 **Background actions: "Skynet does this in the Background and needs no user input."** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13:
"Telling a user "how" when he cannot change it is TMI (too much information!)"; "Make that a Help Rule: For things in the Background
that a user cannot see or needs no user input on the code, needs a Simple "Skynet does this in the Background and needs no user
input." For something Like providing a file name to import, after you supply Skynet the File Name, no other user input is needed.
The action takes place in the background."):
- **Nothing to give:** when Skynet does something the user cannot see and needs no input for, Help and Hover Help say only:
  **"Skynet does this in the Background and needs no user input."** How it is done is never explained in Help; it goes in the Rules
  and the code notes. Example: a goLine number follows its line when lines are added or taken out (Rule 16.10, Help 22, Rule 11.13).
- **Something to give first:** when the user gives one thing and Skynet does the rest, Help says what to give, then that nothing more
  is needed. Example: an import: **"After you supply Skynet the File Name, no other user input is needed. The action takes place in
  the background."**
- **Both programs:** the Skynet Panel and the BruControl Import (its Help is on hold, Rule 11.3).

11.14 **Machine translation notice** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "when a different Language other than English is Chosen for the
Help pop a Dialog with the Caveat that the Translation was by Machine and not Human in English and the Language Chosen with an
Aknowlegement Button"). Every time a Help language other than English is picked (🌐 in the Help page list), a dialog says that the
Help in that language was translated by a machine, not a person, may have mistakes, and that the English page is the one to trust.
It says so in English and in the language picked, and closes only with its **Acknowledge** button (the button is English, like
every screen, Rule 11.11). Picking English shows nothing. A new Help language adds its text to `public/mtnotice.js`
(test/mtnotice.test.js checks every language in the list has it). Both programs (the BruControl Import uses the Panel's Help).

11.15 **Wiring guides** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "We will also need some step by step with graphic for hooking up Dacs, 10KNTC
Probes, SSRs, 1 wire circuit, PT100 and PT 1000 Probes. All come with the electricty Warning and that the User is resposible for
safety as these are simple methods and are very general in nature and cannot know a Users wiring or electrical outlay"; "Separate
ones and one for every thing that requires something besides a Pin/Port to work. We can use the Mega as the example and explain that
other boards are similar."). Every part that needs more than a bare Port to work gets its own Step by Step guide (Rule 11.9), titled
**Step by Step: Wire ...**. Each guide:
  1. opens with the electrical warning (Rule 6.20), then **"You are responsible for your own safety."**: the guide shows a simple,
     very general way to wire the part and cannot know the brewer's wiring, parts or electrical layout; read each part's data sheet;
     a Licensed Electrician does or checks anything on AC (wall) power;
  2. uses the **Arduino Mega 2560** as the example and says other boards are wired the same way with other Port names (Help 206),
     with an **Other boards** part for 3.3 V boards and the Arduino Opta;
  3. has a **Skynet drawing** of the wiring in place of a screenshot (`media/help_pictures/Step_Wire_<Part>_NN_<What>.svg`, MIT, never
     copied from another drawing, not in the Image Library), with the warning along its foot; the AC side is shown only as a box for
     the electrician;
  4. ends with the Device to add in Skynet, a check that it works, and **The technical side** (the Mega program's pin lists).
First six (Help 209-214): a DAC (0-10 V), a 10K NTC probe, an SSR, 1-Wire (DS18B20) probes, a PT100 and a PT1000 probe. Next 19
(Help 215-233): a relay board, a contactor, a motorized ball valve, a water solenoid valve, a gas solenoid and igniter, DC pump speed
(MOSFET), a thermocouple, an LM35 or TMP36, a flow meter, a pressure transducer, a 4-20 mA level transmitter, a 0-10 V sensor, an
ADS1115, a vessel scale (HX711), a stepper motor, a pH probe, an E-Stop, a fan, buzzer or LED, and switches and float switches. A guide
for anything on gas puts the gas warning before the electrical warning, on the page and on its drawing. Both programs (the BruControl
Import uses the Panel's Help).

11.16 **Help in any language by AI translation: the User Language** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20, Panel Updates entry 45: "Could
there be a method where the Help could be sent to an AI agent external to the Program to Translate to a different langauge and then
brought back into skynet"; "like 1 better"; "That way we keep french and then another is user. So there would be 3 choices of Help.
English, French, User Language."; "Right to LEFT will Not work but allow"):
- **Three choices** in 🌐 Help language: English, Français and **one User Language** (shown by its own name, 🌐 Deutsch). English and
  French ship with Skynet; the User Language stays on the Brain where it was imported (data/help_user/), so a Setup never touches it
  and Move Brain takes it along. Importing a different language replaces it; the old one goes to data/help_user_backups/ (Rule #1).
  More parts of the same language are added to it.
- **Export** (Admins, Help > **🌐 Languages**): the Help pages, every balloon, the words of the Help pictures (Rule 7.25), the
  Override and Stop words (Rule 11.11) and the notes around a page (not translated yet, may be out of date, machine translation, the
  electrical and gas warnings, the notice of Rule 11.14) as plain text files in **parts** (about 40 KB of English each, so one AI
  answer can hold it; a page is never cut in two). Each piece sits under a marker line the AI keeps; each part starts with
  instructions for the AI and the **Keep English** list. **Only new and changed** exports only what the User Language lacks or what
  changed since. No internet, key or cost inside Skynet: the user pastes the parts into any AI.
- **Import:** every piece is checked against its English: a page keeps the same headings, links, pictures, code, code blocks and ⚠
  paragraphs; a balloon keeps its {0} parts, ⬢ ⬆ ⟦ ⟧ marks, ⟪ ⟫ parts and ⚠ lines. A piece that fails stays English, and **one
  warning** lists them all; every good piece is kept (Don't restrict users). Skynet gives each heading its English id (as in French)
  and makes each red warning (Rule 6.20) the language's own warning sentence, or the English one when the AI gave none, so the
  warning is never lost.
- **Keep English words** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-20: "list them in English with the English Translation in English. When you get a
  language import back, put the English back and leave the translation as foreign ... Since these are fixed and not dynamic, it would
  work and the brain would know where."): the brewing words in `help/_keep_english.txt` (OakBarn Brewery fills it in; seeded with
  Strike, Sparge, Mash, Wort, Vorlauf ...) plus an Admin's own words on that Brain. On Export each one is written twice, ⁅Mash⁆ (Mash);
  on Import the word in the fixed ⁅ ⁆ slot is put back in English, whatever the AI did, so the page reads **Mash (Maische)**. A
  translated page says under it that these words stay English. Override and Stop are not on the list: they follow the Help language
  (Rule 11.11).
- **Right to left** (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu ...): taken like any other language, never blocked; it will not show right. Said
  once, in the Add Font to Brain warning below, not at Import.
- **Fonts:** the browser reading the Help draws it, and phones, PCs and Macs have most letters. The Skynet Language Fonts (Rule 9.24)
  and fonts an Admin adds are served by the Brain (/fonts/fonts.css) to the Help pages and balloons only, after the screen's own font,
  so they are used only for letters it lacks. An Import whose letters need a Skynet Language Font the Brain lacks says where to get it.
  **🔤 Add Font to Brain** (.woff2, .woff, .ttf, .otf; Pi or Windows Brain alike, no command line): its **first screen is the one
  warning**, with **▶ Next** and **Abandon**: "Fonts added here are not tested and may not work. Right-to-left languages (such as
  Arabic or Hebrew) will not work." Delete moves a font to data/help_user_backups/fonts (Rule #1). A font file name follows Rule 3.4.
- **Code stays English:** Process code, Device, Widget, Tab and file names, and the screens are never translated (Rule 11.11).
- **Machine translation** (Rule 11.14): the notice and the note under each page come in the User Language's own words.
- Still to decide: whether a good User Language can be sent in to ship in a Setup (German, Danish, Norwegian, Italian are coming).
  Both programs: the Panel's Help (the BruControl Import's Build page uses the Panel's Help). (Help 242, lib/helplang.js,
  public/helplang.js, test/helplang.test.js)

11.17 **A Help table's Name column never wraps** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-22, Panel Update 9, item 10a): in a Help table whose first
column is a name (a `code` or **bold** word alone in its cell, such as `skn_Boil_Temp`), that column is on one line; the other columns
wrap. Both programs: the BruControl Import's Build page uses the Panel's Help. (public/style.css `.hpTable`)

12.1 **Nothing is posted or announced anywhere without Fritz's word.** The announcement goes only to
a few BruControl friends. (2026-10-04)
*Replaced in part:* "never make the repo public" (2026-10-04). On 2026-10-22 Fritz said "Public is
fine" for the GitHub repo, which the Get Skynet pictures feature needs.

12.2 **Beer money donations can go to at most 2 PayPal accounts.** It is **locked now with only Fritz's
PayPal account**, in one file (lib/donation.js, owned by @oakbarn). It is unlocked only when Fritz gives the
second PayPal account (that may never happen); once that account is added it is locked again. Nobody can
add, change or delete a PayPal account from the panel, and the Prime Developers cannot either. (Fritz,
2026-11-02, thread "Expand Buy a Beer and Patron support")
*Replaced:* "The Beer money donation recipient is locked to Fritz's PayPal in one file and can never be
made editable again." (2026-10-04, PR #18)

12.3 **Patron payments are not Beer money.** They are split by percent between several PayPal accounts:
every Patron payment goes to one collecting account and a Prime Developer runs a Pay Out by percent
(Option A). The Patron accounts and percents are changed only by the Prime Developers as a group, on
GitHub, and **every** Prime Developer must approve (100%). Rule 12.2 covers Buy a Beer only. (Fritz, 2026-11-02, thread "Expand Buy a Beer and Patron support")

12.4 **The Patron Level** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "Set up Patron Level and we will adjust after seeing it in action"; "WE will
be building the Patron e mail system external to skynet. Patron level might unlock something on Skynet, but those brains would not
have any patron e mails on them"):
- A Patron gets a **Patron code** from OakBarn Brewery; an Admin pastes it in **Settings > Patron**. The Brain checks OakBarn Brewery's
  signature (lib/patron.js holds only the public half of the key; the private half never goes on GitHub or a Brain;
  tools/patron-code.js makes codes) and unlocks the Patron perks until the code's end date.
- A Patron code holds only the name to show, the level and the end date: **never an email address**. Patron emails (New Releases and
  the like, with their tick boxes) are OakBarn Brewery's own system outside Skynet; no Brain holds them.
- **Patron: $10 every 6 months** (Rule 12.3). Perks: **Request a Feature** (☰ Menu > ⭐ Request a Feature, sent from the Brain's own
  email account to support@oakbarnbrewery.com, or the user's mail program), **Email alert for new Releases** (outside Skynet), **Send
  your pump to OakBarn Brewery** (coming with My Pumps), and **Your Brewery Name** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-23, Panel Update 10, items
  4, 5g, 5h: "Brewery Name Becomes a Patron Perk. If Not a Patron Put in Skynet Panel"; picked on a card: built now, and a non-Patron's
  new Process gets a Copyright with no name): a Patron's Brewery Name (☰ Menu > Default settings; empty: the name on the Patron code)
  shows on the Menu Bar and in the Process Editor, and is the Copyright and **Created by** of every new Process (Rule 16.13). Not a
  Patron: the Menu Bar shows **Skynet Panel**, the Brewery Name box is greyed out (Rule 18.46) and keeps what was typed, and a new
  Process has **no Created by, MIT License or Copyright line** (changed 2026-11-23, Panel Update 11, OakBarn Brewery: "Skynet did not write it, so Skynet should not be attached to it. A better solution might be to avoid the lines for non patron"; it
  was Copyright © year with no name). A non-Patron who tries a perk sees a friendly note with the levels and
  perks and a link to oakbarnbrewery.com, each time. The levels and perks are a first try, to be adjusted.
Both programs (Settings is the same). (thread "Let users build their own Pump Templates", Help 198)
