18.11 **Cancel warns before throwing away changes.** In every dialog with ✖ Cancel and 💾 Save, if anything was changed and
Cancel is pressed, a warning asks whether to really discard the changes or go back and save. With no changes, Cancel just
closes (Rule 2.17). (Fritz, 2026-11-02)

18.12 **The drill-down: Pump Device Properties is the standard for every Device** (Fritz, 2026-11-03, thread "Set the
drill-down dialog standard for Devices"; his drawing [docs/Pump_Drill_Down_Format.png](Pump_Drill_Down_Format.png)). The Pump's
dialog is the first one changed to Rule 18 (Rule 18.10) and is **the starting standard for all Devices added**; every other
dialog will work the same way when Fritz commands it, one at a time. From the top:
1. The title (**Pump Device Properties** and its **?**), then 🗑 Delete, ✖ Cancel, 💾 Save (at the top, frozen while the rest scrolls; no bottom row, Rules 2.17, 2.51).
2. **Visible**, **Hidden Locked** and the 🔓 lock.
3. **Pump Properties ⬢**: the hexagon beside the heading opens the **Properties pop-up**: Visible, Hidden Locked, the lock, Tab,
   X Horizontal, Y Vertical, Width, Height, and 🗑 Delete, with ✖ Cancel and 💾 Save.
4. **Label ⬆ ⬢** (Rule 18.3): the arrow opens the 2 line String Entry Dialog, the hexagon the **Label pop-up** (Label, Visible,
   Font size, Font, Bold, Fore color, Back color, Alignment). Then **Show label**. A blank Label becomes the Name on Save, so a
   Label is never blank (Rules 1.13, 18.3).
5. **Name** (Rule 18.4), the Suggested Name and the Device Type it is made from.
6. The Device's own fields, the most used first, each extra in a pop-up: for the Pump, **Interface**, **Pin ⬢** (Invert,
   One-shot time, One-shot pulses OFF), **When tapped ⬢** (Tap target, Ask before changing) and Kind; **Picture ⬢** (On
   overlay, Picture when on), Cover, **Background picture (Image Path 1) ⬢** (the Graphic Dialog, Rule 18.8); **Text when
   on ⬆ ⬢** (Hide the text, its font size, colors, alignment, Look, Border) and **Text when off ⬆**.
7. Database and .API last (Rule 6.14).
A field shown both on the dialog and in a pop-up is the same setting: saving the pop-up updates the dialog. Nothing is saved
until 💾 Save on the dialog. (Help 115)

18.13 **Adding a Pump** (Fritz's Add Pump drawing, 2026-11-04, [docs/Add_Pump_Format.png](Add_Pump_Format.png)):
1. **Pumps > Pump, on / off (relay or SSR)**, then 2. **Pick the pump**: a list of the Skynet pump drawings (March 809 and 815,
   Chugger, Blichmann Riptide, Topsflo TD5, KegLand MKII), each with its picture. The pick is the Pump's Picture, with the green
   On overlay and Cover None to start.
3. The Add box is titled with the pump (e.g. **Blichmann Riptide**). Besides Rule 4.2's fields it has the **Label ⬢** (Label
   pop-up), **Label Visible**, **Cover**, **X (Horizontal)**, **Y (Vertical)**, Width and Height, and the **Device Type** greyed
   out, read only (Pump: it comes from the list it was picked in). X and Y typed here are kept.
4. Once ➕ Add Device is pressed, its Properties (Rule 18.12) show the **Interface (board)** and **Port** greyed out and set, **for
   good** (Fritz, 2026-11-05: it is physical wiring, so a user almost never changes it; the Device keeps its hidden key, Rule 3.10,
   and only its Name changes, with ✏ Change name). To wire it to another board or pin, delete it and add it again. **Tab, X, Y, Width and Height** on the dialog itself (they are in the Pump
   Properties ⬢ pop-up too); the **Device Type** greyed out, read only; and the Name with ✏ Change name once built (Rule 3.11).
The Add box follows Rule 4.2's order (1 Label, 2 Interface, 3 Port, 4 Tab, 5 Name); the pump starts on the 🔨 Build Tab and Finish Build ... moves it to the picked Tab (Rule 4.1).
(Help 115)

18.14 **"Add new ..." in a dialog pauses it and comes back** (Fritz, 2026-11-04, a general Rule): when **➕ Add new ...** (a new
Tab, Interface, Style, unit, picture ...) is picked in a dropdown of a dialog, the calling dialog **keeps what was entered so far
as temporary data and pauses**; the new thing is made in its own dialog; once that is saved the calling dialog **comes back with
the temporary data filled in again**, the dropdown **refreshed**, and **the new thing picked**. Cancel while making it makes
nothing and goes back to the calling dialog as it was. The first one built this way: ➕ Add new Tab… in the Add Device box
(Rule 4.1); ➕ Add new Interface… already works this way. Other dialogs are brought to it one at a time, when Fritz says (Rule 18.10).

18.15 **The opening pattern of every new Device dialog** (Fritz, 2026-11-04): **1 Label, 2 Interface, 3 Port, 4 Tab**, then
**5 the Suggested Name** made from them (Rule 4.2), before anything else. **Label Visible starts at No** (Fritz, 2026-11-04: the standard for every new Device dialog).
   **The standard for every new Device dialog** (Fritz, 2026-11-04): the **Label, Interface, Port and Tab are filled in first**;
   no other property shows until all four are done (only the greyed out Device Type). **➕ Add Device** can always be pressed:
   until all four are done it looks faded and pressing it says what is still missing (Fritz, 2026-11-04: "Add Device button
   does not work"; a greyed out button gave no reason on a phone). Then the hidden properties appear, with
   the **Name** (the Suggested Name) on top of them, then the rest (Cover for a pump, X, Y, Width, Height ...). The Label must be
   filled in (Label Visible off does not skip it). The Add Device box has it now.
   *Changed (Fritz, 2026-11-05):* **A Device or Widget must have a Label, and a Label can't be blank.** Some Devices and Widgets
   have their Label **filled in for you** with the pattern **Type_n**, n the next number not used yet: a **Motorized Ball Valve**
   starts as **mBV_1**, then mBV_2 ... (Fritz: "Pumps do NOT have Auto Fill, Valves do"); a **Temperature Probe** by its kind, as **tP_1W_1**, **tP_RTD_1**, **tP_10KNTC_1** ... (Rule 18.26); a **PWM output** as **PWM_1**, an **Analog output** as **4_20_1** or **0_10_1** (Rule 18.25). It can be changed like any Label. When the
   Label is filled in (by you or by the program) on a Build dialog, **the focus jumps to the next field** in the Enter order (the
   next one still empty). **Every Label is editable by the user**, filled in for you or not. Which Devices and Widgets fill in
   their Label is decided **dialog by dialog: Fritz says so when each dialog is built** (Fritz, 2026-11-05). Every other dialog that
makes a new Device (for now the RIMS tube and the Integrated Electric Kettle New Device box) gets it one at a time, when Fritz
says (Rule 18.10).

18.16 **Short field names, the rest in a tip** (Fritz, 2026-11-04, his Pump example): a field's name is short ("Label",
"Interface (board)"); the longer explanation is in its **tip**: hover the name (dotted underline) to see it, or tap it for a
small pop-up with Close. The Add Device box has it now; other dialogs get it one at a time (Rule 18.10). Since 2026-11-06
the hover shows at once and stays while the mouse rests on the name (Rule 2.38).

18.17 **Dropdowns of Interfaces and Tabs read "ID: Name"** (Fritz, 2026-11-04): an Interface as `BM: Brewery Mega`, a Tab as
`BH: Brew House`, everywhere they are picked.
*Replaced:* the Interface list showed the full name first, `Brewery Mega   (ID BM_)` (Fritz, 2026-10-27).

18.18 **Device Type shows its General Type first** (Fritz, 2026-11-04): where a Device Type is shown, it reads
`GeneralType@Type`, the same as in the Suggested Name (Rule 3.1; OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-11: "Any where in Skynet Change any DO:Pump
and any other devices where there is a Subgroup to Type to DO@Pump"; "All Get Updated to the new standard"): an On/Off Pump is `DO@Pump`,
a Pump on a PWM port `PWM@Pump`, a Heating Element `DO@H_Element` (`PWM@H_Element`, `AO@H_Element`). A new Device fills it in: a new On/Off Pump (a
Blichmann RipTide) reads `DO@Pump`. On a PWM or 0-10 V port a Pump, Fan, Motor, LED or Heating Element has the same Type ID as on an
On/Off port (Pump, Fan, Mtr, LED, H_Element; they were P_Pump, P_Fan, P_Mtr, P_LED, H_PWM, H_AO), since the General Type already says the
port; older Schemas are upgraded on load, names too (Rule 15.2). A Proportional Valve is `Valve_L` (low temperature) or `Valve_H` (high temperature): `PWM@Valve_L`, `AO@Valve_H` (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-11: "PWM@Valve_L or PWM@Valve_H and AO to follow"; were P_L_Vlv, P_H_Vlv).
The saved type stays as it was (digitalOut, typeCode Pump). General Types: **DO** (Digital Out), **PWM**,
**HYS** (Hysteresis) from Fritz; AO (Analog Out), DI (Digital In), AI (Analog In), TEMP, FLOW, SCALE, STEP (Stepper),
DUTY (Duty Cycle) and PID proposed, waiting on Fritz's OK. A type with no sub-type shows only its General Type.

18.19 **A Device dialog shows its Graphic with its Orientation** (Fritz, 2026-11-04, the Pump first): the Add box and the
Properties show the **Graphic** (the picture as it will be on the Tab, with its Cover) and an **Orientation** dropdown (a pump: **Right**, as
drawn, or **Left**, mirrored; Fritz's screens 7-9). Changing the Orientation flips the Graphic on the dialog and the Device on the Tab,
and its IPs follow (Rule 5.5); a pump's Inlet IP and Outlet IP stay where they are and the Hose or Pipe inside it is drawn again
(Rule 18.37). A **Skynet pump drawing's Graphic is set**: no path is offered (Rule 5.6), the Picture is shown
greyed out with its pump name. A **User pump** (its own picture) has **one path only**, its Image Path (an exception to Rule
7.10's three paths). Cover is for the Skynet pump drawings only (Rule 7.13). (Help 115)

18.20 **Focus and the Enter key in a dialog** (Fritz, 2026-11-04, his Blichmann Pump Sequence 1-9,
[docs/Blichmann_Pump_Sequence.png](Blichmann_Pump_Sequence.png)): the field with the focus has a **blue border**. Inside a dialog
**Tab** moves field to field and **Enter jumps to the next field** (from the last field to the Save button); Enter no longer
saves from a field. **Exception, a new Device:** until it is added, Enter (or picking from one of its dropdowns) jumps to the next
field of its sequence: 1 Label, 2 Interface, 3 Available Ports, 4 Tab, then Orientation (a Pump), then the **➕ Add Device**
button, where Enter adds it. The Name, Cover, X, Y, Width and Height are skipped by Enter (Tab or a click reaches them). The box
opens with the focus on the first empty field of the sequence. Arrow keys change a dropdown without jumping on. (Help 82) The Pump
Add box has its own order of focus (Rule 18.38).

18.21 **Pump Device Properties are Fritz's screen 9** (2026-11-04, [docs/Blichmann_Pump_Sequence.png](Blichmann_Pump_Sequence.png)):
the title is the pump (e.g. **Blichmann Riptide** ?) with the 🔓 lock, **Visible** and **Hidden Locked** on the title line; 🗑 Delete,
✖ Cancel, 💾 Save; **1. Label** ⬆ ⬢ and **Label Visible**; **2. Interface (board)** with **Available Ports** on the same line
(greyed out for good, Rule 18.13); **3. Tab**; **4. Name** and the Suggested Name; the **Graphic**; its **Path** (greyed out on a
Skynet pump drawing, editable on a User pump, Rule 18.19); **Orientation** (Right / Left); **Hose or Pipe** below it (Rule 5.27;
OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-11: every pump has 8 IPs; Hose or Pipe on a Skynet pump drawing only; 2026-11-16: no Inlet IP / Outlet IP
box, the pipe or hose joined sets them); **Cover** with **Toggle** (On/Off, Push
button, None: what a tap does) on the same line; just below it the **Overlay** (the On overlay, Rule 7.15; Fritz,
2026-11-04: "add an Overlay DDLB just below the Cover DDLB", in the Add box too), and on its line **Database and .API ⬢**:
the hexagon opens the Database and .API settings in a pop-up, in the Add box and the Properties (Fritz's screen 7); **X, Y, Width, Height**; the **Device
Type** (DO@Pump) greyed out last. A User pump has the same Properties. **Only these** belong to a Pump: the old Hidden Locked row,
Pump Properties ⬢, Pin ⬢ (Invert, One-shot), When tapped ⬢, Kind, Picture ⬢, Background picture ⬢ and Text when on / off are gone
from its dialog (what a Pump already has set is kept). The On / Off text is shown with an **Overlay** instead (Rule 7.13).
*Replaced:* for the Pump, Rule 18.12's list of fields (2026-11-03).
*Replaced (Rule 18.13):* the Interface and Port each had **✏ Change** to change them on purpose (2026-11-04).
*Changed (Fritz, 2026-11-08, Rule 18.32):* the Model ⬢, Power with Use, and Speed control with Speed % are added below the Overlay.

18.22 **Each Device and Widget has only its own Properties** (Fritz, 2026-11-04): besides the Universal Properties (Rule 1.21),
a Device or Widget may have a limited set of attributes and Properties, only the ones that fit it (the Pump: Rule 18.21). Other
dialogs are changed to their own set one at a time, on Fritz's say (Rule 18.10).

18.23 **Adding a Motorized Ball Valve: the Pump's drill-down without a Cover** (Fritz, 2026-11-05: "Create a Motorized Ball Valve
Add Dialog using the Pump Drill Down Format. Valves do not have covers but every thing else the same.", thread "Add Motorized Ball
Valve drill-down dialog", Help 128):
1. **Valves (or On/Off) > Motorized Ball Valve, open / closed (relay)**, then 2. **Pick the valve**, each with its picture:
   **Skynet Motorized Ball Valve** or **User Defined Motorized Ball Valve** (its own pictures). The two rows the lists had for them
   are now this one row (Rule 15.3).
   Its Label starts filled in as **mBV_n** (the next number), so the focus starts on the Interface (Rule 18.15).
3. The Add box is titled with the valve and works as the Pump's (Rules 4.2, 18.13, 18.15-18.17, 18.20): 1 Label ⬢ and Label
   Visible, 2 Interface with Available Ports, 3 Tab; then the Name, the **Graphic**, its **Path**, **Orientation** with **Toggle**
   on its line, **Overlay** with **Database and .API ⬢** on its line, **Tap water valve**, **On Close List** and **On Open List**
   on one line, X, Y, Width, Height, and the Device Type greyed out last. Fritz, 2026-11-05: "It should look and feel almost a
   copy of the Pump dialogs": two fields on one line in the Pump's dialogs are on one line here too. Enter goes Label,
   Interface, Ports, Tab, Orientation, ➕ Add Device. **No Cover** (Covers are for pumps, Rule 7.13).
4. Its Properties are the Pump's screen 9 (Rule 18.21) without the Cover, plus the valve's own set (Rule 18.22): **Tap water
   valve**, **On Close List** and **On Open List** on one line (a tap water valve shows its Tap Water flows instead, Rule 6.15).
   A tap water valve also has **Water Supply** (None / Pipe / Hose): a picture-only house water line on its TAP end, always flowing blue; it is not a normal Pipe (Rule 6.15 note, 2026-11-25).
5. Its Type ID is **Valve_E** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-11: "Change ON Off Motorized Valves to DO@Valve_E"; was eVlv, before that E_L_Vlv; the Device Type reads **DO@Valve_E**). Older valves are
   upgraded on load, the stored Type ID and the name (Rule 15.2). The other electric valves follow (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-11:
   "Valve_E_H and Valve_Sgas"): a High Temperature Electric Valve is **Valve_E_H** (**DO@Valve_E_H**, was E_H_Vlv) and a Solenoid Gas
   Valve is **Valve_Sgas** (**DO@Valve_Sgas**, was G_Vlv), upgraded on load the same way.
- **Skynet Motorized Ball Valve:** the Path is greyed out (set by its Template, Rule 5.6) and follows the Orientation; the
  **Orientation** (Horizontal, Vertical Left, Vertical Right, Front, 45 degrees) picks its Template (Rule 5.17), with that Template's
  Width and Height; **Toggle and Overlay work normally**, as on the Pump (Fritz, 2026-11-05: "Toggles and Overlays should work
  normally"): an exception to Rule 5.18's fixed tap behaviour and overlay for this valve only; its Templates list them as user
  settable. It starts with On/Off and the steady bolt (Rule 7.15).
- **User Defined Motorized Ball Valve:** **Path (closed)** with a ⬢ for its In and Out IP spots (Rule 5.22) and **Path (open)** (a
  valve shows open and closed, so the User pump's one-path exception is not used); Orientation Horizontal, Vertical, 45 degrees
  Left or Right; Toggle and Overlay can be picked.
- Gone from these dialogs, as for the Pump (what a valve already has set is kept): Pin ⬢ (Invert, One-shot), When tapped ⬢, Kind,
  Picture ⬢, Background picture ⬢, Text when on / off, Flip Horizontal / Vertical (the Orientation does it), Valve type and Service.
  The Motorized Butterfly Valve and the Proportional Valves keep their present dialogs until Fritz says (Rule 18.10).

18.24 **Adding a Heating Element: the Pump's drill-down without a Cover** (Fritz, 2026-11-05: "Same with Heating Element but
instead of the Electric Kettle, Basic have Vessel Device Template and Choose then Build", thread "Build Heating Element Add dialogs
like Pump", Help 137):
1. **Heating Element (or On/Off) > Heating element, on / off (relay, SSR or contactor)**, then 2. **Pick the heating element**, each
   with its picture: **Skynet Heating Element** (the Skynet element drawing, its Path set, Rule 5.6) or **User Defined Heating
   Element** (its own Path (off) and Path (on)).
3. The Add box is titled with the element and works as the Pump's and the Motorized Ball Valve's (Rules 4.2, 18.13, 18.15-18.17,
   18.20, 18.23): 1 Label ⬢ and Label Visible, 2 Interface with Available Ports, 3 Tab; then the Name, the **Graphic**, its **Path**,
   **Orientation** (Right / Left) with **Toggle** (Toggle or Push Button, Rule 2.46) on its line, **Overlay** (Glow to start; None shows nothing, Rule 7.8) with **Database and
   .API ⬢** on its line, X, Y, Width, Height, and the Device Type greyed out last (**HE**, Rule 3.1). **No Cover.** One click on it turns it
   ON or OFF at once (Rule 2.33, changed 2026-11-08). Label auto-fill (Fritz, 2026-11-05, Rule 18.15): a Heating Element's Label fills in as **hE_n** (**hE_1**, hE_2 ...), with no
   method in it, since its method can change (Rule 6.19, 2026-11-07); a heating PWM is **hE_PWM_1**, and the older control Devices
   keep **hE_PID_1**, **hE_HYS_1**, **hE_DutyC_1**, **hE_DeadB_1** (n the next number not used yet). *The hE_ start and the _n end wait on Fritz's OK.*
4. Its Properties are the Pump's screen 9 (Rule 18.21) without the Cover; the Interface and Port are greyed out for good (Rule 18.13).
5. **Vessel Device Template: Choose, then Build.** In the Heating Element list it takes the place of *Electric kettle, basic*
   (which stays in the full Add Device list, Devices: Skynet). **Choose** a Vessel Template that has an Element Port (the Vessel
   Widget, Rule 5.31, first), then the Heating Element is added as above; **Build** puts the Heating Element on the picked Tab
   (Rule 4.1) and a copy of the Vessel Template on the 🔨 Build Tab with its **Element Placed and linked** to the new Heating
   Element. The Vessel keeps no Devices of its own (Rule 5.7): the Heating Element is its own Device, which the Element spot links
   (Rule 5.31).
- Heating elements built into a RIMS tube or an Integrated kettle, and the PID, Hysteresis, Deadband and Duty Cycle heaters, keep
  their present dialogs until Fritz says (Rule 18.10).
18.25 **Adding a PWM or Analog output: the Pump's drill-down** (Fritz, 2026-11-05: "PWM Build Dialog", thread "Build PWM Add dialog
like Pump", Help 136): a **PWM output** and an **Analog output** (0-10 V, 4-20 mA), from the PWM / Analog out list or the Pump speed rows,
get the Pump's Add box and Properties (Rules 4.2, 18.13, 18.15-18.17, 18.20, 18.21):
1. The Add box is titled **Add PWM Output** or **Add Analog Output 0-10V**: 1 Label ⬢ and Label Visible, 2 Interface with Available
   Ports (only free PWM pins), the **Device Type** (PWM or AO to start; P_Pump, P_Fan ... can be picked, since this kind has more than
   one, Rule 4.2), 3 Tab; then the Name, the **Graphic**, its **Path** (one picture, the same on and off; optional, with none it shows
   its value), **Overlay** with **Database and .API ⬢** on its line (drawn while it is above 0 %), its own set, X, Y, Width, Height.
   Enter goes Label, Interface, Ports, Device Type, Tab, ➕ Add Device.
2. Its own set (Rule 18.22), two to a line as the Pump's: a PWM output **Start value (%)** with **Decimals**; an Analog output
   **Signal** with **Units**, **Low value** with **High value**, then **Decimals**.
3. **No Cover** (pumps only, Rule 7.13), **no Orientation** (it has no IPs) and **no Toggle** (a tap opens the box that sets its %).
4. Its Properties are the same, with the Interface and Port greyed out for good (Rule 18.13) and the Device Type last.
5. The Label starts filled in (Rule 18.15; Fritz, 2026-11-05: "PWM = _PWM_  4-20ma = _4_20_,  O-10v = 0_10"): a PWM output as
   **PWM_1**, PWM_2 ...; a 4-20 mA Analog output as **4_20_1** ...; a 0-10 V (or 0-5 V) Analog output as **0_10_1** ....
A Proportional Valve and a heating element's PWM keep their own dialogs until Fritz says (Rule 18.10).
18.26 **Adding a Temperature Probe: the Pump's drill-down without a Cover, Toggle or Overlay** (Fritz, 2026-11-05: "Build the Probe
Add Dialog Boxes using the Pump Drill down as the Template", thread "Build Probe Add dialogs like Pump", Help 138). For every
Temperature Probe Device: a plain probe, a **Thermowell** (Short, Medium, Long) and a **tee with a Temperature Probe** (Instrument Tee,
Long Tee, Rule 5.30). A probe built into a Skynet_Integrated_Device (RIMS tube, Integrated Electric Kettle) keeps its present dialog
1. **The kind of probe is picked first, as before** (Fritz, 2026-11-05: "Choosing the Probe Type First like it is is fine"): the
   list row of a plain probe (DS18B20, PT100 ...), or step 2a after picking a Thermowell or probe tee.
2. The Add box is titled with the probe (e.g. **Short Thermowell: DS18B20**) and works as the Pump's (Rules 4.2, 18.13, 18.15-18.17,
   18.20): 1 Label ⬢ and Label Visible, 2 Interface with its Port on the same line (**Probe #**, the OneWire probe number of a
   DS18B20, or **Available Ports**: the chip-select pin of an RTD or thermocouple board, the analog pin of an NTC, LM35 or TMP36),
   3 Tab; then the Name, and for a Thermowell or probe tee the **Graphic**, its **Path** (greyed out, the Skynet drawing, Rule 5.6) and
   **Orientation** (Rotate 0, 90, 180, 270) with **Flip** on its line; then the probe's own set (Rule 18.22): **Probe type** greyed
   out with a ⬢ for its settings (wires, reference resistor, thermocouple type, thermistor values, board voltage, Simulator
   settings), **Units** with **Decimals** on one line, **Calibration offset** with **Database and .API ⬢** on its line; X, Y, Width,
   Height, and the Device Type greyed out last (e.g. **TEMP@1W**). Enter goes Label, Interface, Port, Tab, Orientation,
   ➕ Add Device. **No Cover, Toggle or Overlay** (a probe is an input).
3. Its Label starts filled in by its kind of probe as **tP_Type_n**, n the next number for that kind, so the focus starts on the
   Interface (Rule 18.15). Fritz, 2026-11-05: "Probe 10KNTC = _10KNTC_, One Wire = _1W_, RTD = _RTD_. Other Thermoresistors follow
   10KNTC": **tP_1W_1** (DS18B20), **tP_RTD_1** (PT100 and PT1000), **tP_10KNTC_1**, **tP_50KNTC_1**, **tP_100KNTC_1** (the other
   thermistors like the 10K; another size is **tP_NTC_1**), and by their Type ID **tP_TC_1** (thermocouple), **tP_LM35_1**,
   **tP_TMP36_1**. *(The tP_ start and _n end follow the Heating Element's hE_; they wait on Fritz's OK.)*
4. Its Properties are the Pump's screen 9 (Rule 18.21) without Cover, Toggle and Overlay, plus the same own set and the **Reading
   now**. The Interface and Port are greyed out for good once added (Rule 18.13); so is the **Probe type**: to use another kind of
   probe, delete it and add it again.
- Gone from these dialogs (what a probe already has set is kept): the Probe type dropdown, Device (empty = any), the separate Flip
  Horizontal / Flip Vertical / Rotate rows (now Orientation and Flip), the Thermowell and probe tee notes (now the Graphic's tip).

18.27 **Adding a Picture Widget: the Pump's drill-down made to fit a Widget** (Fritz, 2026-11-05: "build a Picture Widget Build, I
will look at what you did and modify, but follow the look and sequences of the Pump drill Down", thread "Build Picture Widget dialog
like Pump", Help 74). A Widget has no Interface or Port (Rule 1.2) and is made on the 🔨 Build Tab first (Rule 4.1), so:
1. **Picture ➕** on the Edit layout bar, or **Add Widget > Pictures and text > Picture Widget**, opens the **Add Widget box**, titled
   **Picture Widget**, with ✖ Cancel and **➕ Add Widget** at the top and the bottom (Picture ➕ made a plain still picture before;
   those already on a Tab keep working).
2. The opening pattern (Rule 18.15 for a Widget): **1 Label** ⬢ and **Label Visible** (starts at No), **2 Picture** (the picture it
   shows, from the Picture list with the 🖼 icon picker), **3 Tab** greyed out as **🔨 Build Tab**. Nothing else shows until the
   Label and the Picture are done; ➕ Add Widget can always be pressed and says what is missing. Enter goes Label, Picture,
   ➕ Add Widget (Rule 18.20). Label auto-fill (Fritz, 2026-11-05, Rule 18.15): a Heating Element's Label fills in as **hE_n** (**hE_1**, hE_2 ...), with no
   method in it, since its method can change (Rule 6.19, 2026-11-07); a heating PWM is **hE_PWM_1**, and the older control Devices
   keep **hE_PID_1**, **hE_HYS_1**, **hE_DutyC_1**, **hE_DeadB_1** (n the next number not used yet). *The hE_ start and the _n end wait on Fritz's OK.*
3. Then **4 Name** (the Suggested Name **wgt_PIX_Label_TabID**, Rule 3.14, e.g. wgt_PIX_Kettle_Element_BR; it may be edited),
   the **Graphic**, **Turns on with** (Rule 7.11) with **Toggle** (On/Off, Push button, None: what a tap does) on its line,
   **Overlay** (greyed out while Turns on with is None) with a ⬢ for the second picture (Picture when on, optional, Rule 7.8) and
   the Back Colour, **Text on picture** ⬆, X, Y, Width, Height (140 x 120 to start), and the **Widget Type** (Picture) greyed out last.
4. **Picture Widget Properties** are the Pump's screen 9 (Rule 18.21) for a Widget: the lock, Visible and Hidden Locked in the
   title line; 🗑 Delete, ✖ Cancel, 💾 Save; 1 Label ⬆ ⬢ and Label Visible, 2 Picture, 3 Tab, 4 Name (✏ Change name once built,
   Rule 3.11), then the same fields as the Add box. The Label is never blank (a blank one becomes the Name on Save).
- Gone from its dialog (Rule 18.22; what an older Picture Widget already has set is kept): the Image block (Background #, Image
  Path 1-3), Hide value, Look, Digits, When tapped, Tap target and Ask before changing. Database and .API are not offered: a
  picture has no value (Rule 6.14).

18.28 **A blank Label (or Port): only Save waits for it** (Fritz, 2026-11-05: "If the Label Field is Blank ... A Pop Up Dialog that
States the Label Cannot be Blank. Dialog self distructs after 5 seconds"; OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15, Blichmann RipTide Dialog 1:
"Best to be able to change Inter face and also the tab anytime"; "If a user wanted to use the 2 Lines for the label, why prevent";
"Rule 18.28 please". Help 140). In **every** Add / Build and Properties dialog that has a Label (every Device and Widget, Rule 18.15):
- While the **Label is blank**, the **Tab key and the mouse reach every other field and icon** of the dialog at any time (the ⬆
  two-line box, the ⬢, Label Visible, the Interface, the Port, the Tab, the ? Help ...).
- Only **Save / ➕ Add Device / ➕ Add Widget** and a box that gets no focus (greyed out or read only, like Device Type) wait for the
  Label: a click on them does nothing, a small pop-up says **"⚠ The Label cannot be blank."** and the focus goes back to the Label.
  The pop-up **goes away by itself after 2 seconds** (or when tapped; Rule 2.74, was 5 seconds).
- A field's **name** (its Hover Help) may be clicked or double-clicked too: a double-click on the Tab's name opens its Tab settings
  (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: a double-click on the Tab with a blank Label after Confirm gave the warning: fixed).
- **Enter** on a blank Label stays on it. A blank Label left for nothing (a click on empty space, a title, a greyed out box) gets
  the focus back.
- **The Cancel button is "hot"** (Fritz, 2026-11-05: "The Cancel Button is Hot is part of the Rule"): ✖ Cancel (and Esc) always
  work, even while the Label or the Port is blank (Rule 18.11 still asks first when something was changed).
- **Delete is "hot" too** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14: "I also tried to delete a Hose that had no label but the Delete button warned
  it needed one. Have Delete Delete without those types of issues"): a Delete button (Properties Delete, 🗑 Delete, 🗑 Delete Pipe /
  Hose, top or bottom) always works, in every dialog, even while the Label, the Port or any needed box (Rule 18.33) is blank. Both
  programs. *Changed (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-23: "getting the annoying Do you really want do delete nanny popup. Could a simple
  CTRL + Z restore a Delete ?"):* an item's Properties Delete no longer asks "Delete this item?": it goes at once, a toast says so,
  and **↩ Put back** (Ctrl+Z) brings it back (Rule 5.37). A Device with Clones still offers its choices (Rule 4.4).
- **The same for a Port** when the Device needs one (Fritz: "If the device needs a Port, the same Rule for a Port"): Save / ➕ Add
  waits for it with **"⚠ The Port cannot be blank."**, and a blank Port never keeps the focus ("If Port is Nul, it does not retain
  focus ... this allows for an Interface Change").
- A **needed box** (Rule 18.33) still keeps the focus until it is filled.
- **➕ Add new Interface…** (extends Rule 18.14, Fritz 2026-11-05: "If you choose to create a new Interface. that new Interface pops
  into the DDLB. If the new Interface is aborted, the default Interface is posted back to the DDLB"): the new Interface is picked in
  the Interface dropdown; if the new Interface is cancelled, the default Interface (the one that was there before) is put back.
- It is one shared helper (public/labelguard.js) that watches every dialog, so a new dialog with a Label gets it by itself.

18.29 **Valve Tees and Supply Manifolds: the Pump's drill-down** (Fritz, 2026-11-06: "The long tees with valves and all those other
intergraded ones you built need their property dialog and the Build look and feel like the Pump Drill down", thread "Add valve Tees
and supply manifolds", Help 146). The Valve Tee, Double and Triple Supply Manifold (Rule 5.35) get the Pump's Add box and Properties
(Rules 18.13-18.21), kept clean: every explanation is in the tip of the field's name (Rule 18.16; Fritz, 2026-11-06: "Dialogs should
be kept as clean as possible"):
1. The Add box is titled with the fitting (e.g. **Double Supply Manifold**): **1. Label ⬢** (filled in: valve_tee_n, manifold_2_n,
   manifold_3_n; ⬢ its look) and **Label Visible** (No to start); **2. Interface (board)** (one board for all its Motorized valves);
   **3. Valve 1**, **Valve 2**, **Valve 3**, each **Manual** or **Motorized**, a Motorized one with its **Available Ports** on the
   same line (two valves can't share a Port); **4. Tab** (➕ Add new Tab… and ➕ Add new Interface… work as Rule 18.14); then the
   **5. Name**, the **Graphic** (its valves as picked, with their numbers), its **Path** (greyed out, Rule 5.6), **Orientation**
   (Rule 5.35's three, with **Flip** on its line), X, Y, Width, Height, and the **Device Type** greyed out last (e.g. Fitting with V1 DO@Valve_E, V2 DO@M_L_Vlv).
   ➕ Add Device can always be pressed and says what is missing (Rule 18.15). Enter goes Label, Interface, each Valve and Port, Tab,
   Orientation, Flip, ➕ Add Device (Rule 18.20).
2. Its **Properties** are the same with 🗑 Delete, ✖ Cancel and 💾 Save and the 🔓 lock in the title line. A valve saved Motorized
   shows its **Port** greyed out, and the **Interface** is greyed out while any valve has a saved Port (Rule 18.13).
- *Replaced:* the Properties listed a note, Name, Label, a Valves heading, Flip Horizontal, Flip Vertical, Rotate and a Label and place
  heading (2026-11-06, PR #239).

18.30 **Widgets look like the Pump's drill-down** (Fritz, 2026-11-06: "Widgets follow Pump Drill Down look", "Widget look similar to the
Pump Drill Down"). Every Widget's Properties are brought to the Pump's screen 9 (Rule 18.21), as the Picture Widget's are (Rule 18.27).
Fritz's word is the command for all the Widgets (Rule 18.10); they are done one kind after another. First: the **Value, Time and
DateTime Widgets** (Rule 1.23), then the **Timer Widget** (Count, Start value, Reset value, Running at start with Database and .API ⬢,
Style; no pictures), the **Text Widget** (Text ⬆ ⬢ with its look, Fore color; its Label ⬢ has its own label attributes), the
**Override button** (1 Label, 2 Tab, 3 Name greyed out, Fore color ⬢ with its look), the **Sound Player** (Sound file, Repeat sound),
the **Switch, Push Button, Pulse Button and LED** (Device controlled with Database and .API ⬢, Picture ⬢ with the picture when on,
Text when on ⬢ with the text when off; the LED has no picture), the **Label Widget** (Fore color ⬢ with its look) and the **Manual Valve
and Tap Water Valve** (1 Label, Label Visible, 2 Name greyed out, Picture, its place; OPEN or CLOSED now stays on the dialog). The
Value, Time and DateTime Widgets: the lock, Visible and Hidden Locked in the title line; **1 Label ⬆ ⬢** and Label Visible, **2 Tab**,
**3 Name**; the Start value; a Value Widget's **Units ⬢** (Decimals, Step, Lowest, Highest); **Read only** with **Database and .API ⬢**
on its line; **Fore color ⬢** (Back color, Alignment); X, Y, Width, Height; and the **Widget Type** greyed out last. Every explanation
is in the hover help of the field's name (Rule 2.38). (Help 134)

18.31 **Every Device looks like the Pump's drill-down** (Fritz, 2026-11-07: "All dialogs for devices should follow the Pump Drill
down sample"; "Check All Devices and insure the Properties follow the PUMP Drill Down model", thread "Make every Device dialog match
Pump drill-down", Help 148). Fritz's word is the command for every Device dialog (Rule 18.10). The Devices that already had the
drill-down keep theirs (the Pump, Motorized Ball Valve, Heating Element, PWM / Analog out, Temperature Probes, Valve Tees and Supply
Manifolds, Vessel Device). **Every other Device's Properties** now have the same layout: a plain relay / SSR / contactor output, the
Skynet Motorized Butterfly Valve, the Skynet KLD20T and User Defined Proportional Valves, the heating element PWM, Duty Cycle,
Hysteresis, PID and Deadband, the digital inputs (Switch, Push, Toggle and Pulse buttons, Latching input, Pulse counter, Float,
Flow switch, Interlock), the analog inputs and sensors (Pressure, Level, pH), the Flow meter, the Steppers and the Vessel scale:
1. The lock, **Visible** and **Hidden Locked** in the title line; 🗑 Delete, ✖ Cancel, 💾 Save frozen at the top, no bottom row (Rules 2.17, 2.51).
2. **1. Label ⬆ ⬢** and **Label Visible**; **2. Interface** with its **Port** (or **Probe #**) on the same line, greyed out for
   good (Rule 18.13), with **Invert** and **One-shot** in its ⬢ where it has them (the Pump's Pin attributes); **3. Tab**;
   **4. Name** and the Suggested Name (Rule 3.1).
3. With pictures: the **Graphic**, **Path** (and **Path (on)** when it has a second picture), and **Overlay** with **Toggle**
   (an output) and **Database and .API ⬢** on its line. With no pictures: **Database and .API ⬢** on a line of its own.
4. Its own set (Rule 18.22): what that kind of Device needs (a PID's Input, Setpoint, Kp ...; a sensor's Signal, Units ...).
5. **Text attributes ⬢** (its Value or On / Off text and its look), **X, Y, Width, Height**, and the **Device Type** last.
- **A Device built into something** (a Vessel Device's Thermowell, Probe, Heating Element or Valve; a RIMS tube's or an Integrated
  kettle's element and probe, Rule 5.7) gets the same layout, with **3. Built into** (greyed out) in place of the Tab, no Graphic and
  no X, Y, Width, Height (it moves with what it is built into); a built in probe shows its Probe type ⬢, Units, Calibration offset and
  Reading now as a Temperature Probe does (Rule 18.26). Double-clicking the part's picture on the Vessel or its reading opens it.
  *Changed (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "If I double Tap on a Heater Image on a Saved Template, in edit mode, the Properties and
  attributes of a Heater show be display just like it was an independent Device"):* a **Vessel Device's** Heating Element,
  Thermowell or Probe opens **the same Properties as one of its own** (the Heating Element's or the Temperature Probe's, with its
  title, Toggle, Overlay, Heating method and so on), with **3. Built into** in place of the Tab and no Graphic, Orientation, X, Y,
  Width or Height (the vessel draws it). A double-click or a long press on its picture always opens the part, never the vessel.
  **The Vessel Device's own Properties** have a section for each **Heating Element** and for the **Thermowell / Probe**, showing
  its Label, Interface, Port, Name and main settings, with a button to its own Properties. With none built in, the section is
  still there, empty and greyed out.
  *Changed (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "Fix this Dialog"; "It can still have the Universal attributes plus the sub device
  sections (Heater, Probe just things you might change ... those fully editable include a whole different choice of Probe or
  Heating Element as those could be Physically changed on the Vessel after it was built"):* once a Vessel Device is **integrated**
  (built with the Vessel Device Builder, or built and saved on a Tab) its Properties have only **the Universal Properties** (Rule
  1.21: Name with ✏ Change name, Label, Visible, Hidden Locked, Label and place, Tab, X, Y, Lock), its **Type** greyed out, its Out
  flow color, and a section for each **Heating Element** and **Thermowell / Probe**. Those sections can change the Label, Heating
  method, Temperature Probe, Setpoint, Units and Calibration offset; their **Interface and Port (or Probe #) are greyed out for good**
  and **a part can't be swapped** (Rule 5.31).
  *Replaced* (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09, Rule 5.31: "none may be swapped for a different Device Port Combination ever"): "each can
  be swapped for another existing one or a new one ... when the new one is on another Port the old one is deleted; when it is on the
  same Port the old one stays on the Tab as a Device of its own." 
  Its **Size** stays (2026-11-09, OakBarn Brewery: "Both"): Gallons, Method, Diameter, Height, Calculated Volume (read only), Dead
  space and Safe Element Volume (Rule 19.2). No Graphic, Place sliders, one Interface for all parts, HERMS coil, Drain, Tangential,
  Sparge / Steam Slayer or IP rows: none of those can change after integration.
- What a Device already has set is kept (its look, pin settings and so on); only the dialog changed. Every explanation is in the
  hover help (Rule 2.38).
- **BruControl Import:** it has no Device dialogs of its own; the Devices it brings in open in these Properties in the Panel.
---

18.32 **DC pumps: Model, Power, Use, Speed and the pump's facts** (Fritz, 2026-11-08: "All of the Suggestions on the Pump MD are a
Go. I think that any of the Pumps can be controlled (On/Off or PWM if it can) and the voltage, Lift, GPM etc are all good info to
have at your fingertips", [docs/DC_Brewing_Pumps.md](DC_Brewing_Pumps.md), Help 163). Every Pump's Add box and Properties have,
below the Overlay:
- **Model** (the pump list in public/pumps.js; a Skynet pump drawing picks its own; **Other** for a pump not listed) with a **⬢**
  holding the **Pump facts**: **Power** (AC 120 V, AC 240 V, DC 12 V, DC 24 V), **Use** (**Hot & Cool**, or Cold for a glycol pump),
  Flow, Lift, Hottest liquid and **Self Priming** (Yes / No / Not known; OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "a Prperty of Self Priming   for
  a Riotide it is no"; a switch on a User Defined pump). For a model in the list the Pump facts are to look at only, with one **◀ Back**
  button; for Other they are typed in (Rule 18.40). Hottest liquid's Hover Help ends with the caveat that boiling liquids are not
  recommended to be pumped because of cavitation (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16). A fact is filled in only from the maker's own words:
  the RipTide's Hottest liquid stays Not known until Blichmann's own number is found (blichmannengineering.com now goes to MoreBeer,
  whose RipTide pages give none).
- **Inlet IP Fitting** and **Outlet IP Fitting** where Power was (Rule 18.40), each on its own line and each its own dropdown (OakBarn
  Brewery, 2026-11-17, all Pump dialogs: "Ports could be confused with Arduino Ports so use Inlet Fitting"; "Separate Outlet
  Fitting"). They are the End Fittings of the pump's In and Out IPs (Rule 5.40, Rule 2.57): the **IP Type In / Out** row is changed
  to **Inlet IP Fitting**, and **Outlet IP Fitting** is added (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "Remove IP TYPe  In/Out rows not a Take
  away but a Change.  Change IP TYPe  In/Out to Inlet Ip Fitting  and Add Outlet IP Fitting"; "Populate Both Changed ANd NEW WITH
  THE OLD IP TYPe  In/Out VALUE"): a saved pump shows its old IP Type In in Inlet IP Fitting and its old IP Type Out in Outlet IP
  Fitting. A dropdown, because a fitting can change an End Fitting; the list has every size of the old Ports list plus
  the sizes ticked in Default settings and those used in the Schema. A pump saved with the one **Ports** pick starts from it; its
  Ports pick is kept (Design Rule #1).
  *Replaced (2026-11-17):* one **Ports** dropdown for both ends, and the **IP Type In / IP Type Out** row (changed to Inlet IP Fitting; Outlet IP Fitting added).
- **Speed Control** (On/Off only, or PWM speed) with **Speed %** (0-100, empty = 100) on its line, for **PWM pumps only** (a DC pump,
  or one already set to PWM; OakBarn Brewery's drawing, 2026-11-11). An AC pump is On/Off only. A PWM pump needs a true PWM Port (Rule
  4.2's pin lists): its Add box lists only PWM Ports, and its Properties warn when the Port cannot.
- The electrical warning (Rule 6.20) is the start of the **Power** Hover Help, not a line in the dialog (OakBarn Brewery's drawing,
  2026-11-11).
- **KISS** (OakBarn Brewery's drawing, 2026-11-11, Rule 11.8): the Model a drawing picks shows by its own name, **Blichmann RipTide
  (AC)**, not "From the drawing (...)"; the Power the model gives shows as **AC 120 V (house power)**, not "From the model (...)".
- **Known values are filled in and greyed out** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-11: "If the data is Known, fill it in and Grey Out for Know
  values"; "For a User defined pump Useful"): the Model a Skynet pump drawing picks, the Power of that model, and in the ⬢ **Pump
  Facts** each fact the model knows (Flow, Lift, Hottest Liquid, Ports). A fact the model doesn't know, and every fact of a User
  Defined pump, stays a box to type in. A fact typed before stays the brewer's own (Rule #1). **Ports** is a dropdown (OakBarn
  Brewery, 2026-11-11: "This should be DDLB TC1.5 TC2 TC3/4 TC1/2 FPT1/2 FPT 3/4 FPT1 MPT1/2 MPT3/4 MPT1 Differnt BSP up to 1 Metrc";
  "Ports can Editable except for TC which would be Greyed"; "A user can add a TC Fitting and make it TC"): TC1.5, TC2, TC3/4,
  TC1/2, FPT1/2, FPT3/4, FPT1, MPT1/2, MPT3/4, MPT1, BSP1/4, BSP3/8, BSP1/2, BSP3/4, BSP1, DN8, DN10, DN15, DN20, DN25 (metric pipe
  matching 1/4" to 1"). It stays editable; only a Tri-Clamp port the model is known to have is filled in and greyed out. Its
  Hover Help gives the example: FPT1/2 or FPT1 pumps made TC1.5 with a Tri-Clamp fitting.
- **X (Horizontal), Y (Vertical), Width and Height** on one line, in small boxes (OakBarn Brewery's drawing, 2026-11-11). **Device
  Type** stays greyed out, and **Cancel** and **Add Device** stay at the bottom.
One click still turns a Pump On or Off (Rule 2.33); a PWM pump runs at its Speed % while On. A Process sets `Pump.speed = 60`.
Holding the mouse on a Pump shows its facts. New pump drawings are made only when OakBarn Brewery asks (Rule 7.7); the manual
BrewZilla 3 pump is a Pump Widget, built in its own thread.
- **BruControl Import:** it shares the Pump; an imported Pump starts On/Off only with no Model. Guessing a Cold pump from its name
  ("Cool", "Glycol") and joining a BruControl pump's on/off and PWM speed on one Port into one PWM Pump wait for the Importer review.

18.33 **OakBarn Brewery decides which boxes are mandatory** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "Fritz decides what is mandatory and cannot
be left as pick one or blank ... Volts is just good information to have but would not affect a drawing while Connection Type and size
might"; "label is always mandatory in any dialog"). In the Panel **and the BruControl Import**:
- A box is **mandatory** (it cannot be left blank or at **Pick one…**) only when OakBarn Brewery says so. A new box starts **optional**
  until OakBarn Brewery decides; a box is never made mandatory without asking.
- The **Label** is always mandatory, in every dialog (Rule 18.28). So are the Name (Rule 18.4) and the Port (Rule 18.28).
- An optional dropdown reads **Pick one… (optional)**, an optional number box *(optional)*; only a blank mandatory box is marked red.
- **The test** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "If something is needed for something to work (like a Hall Effect Flow Meter), that field
  cannot become blank ... Watts do not help the Program or Arduino to work, so it is just Handy Information. Volts, Amps, Watts might
  be good info for a User to look at, but they do not affect the Program or an Arduino"): a box is mandatory when the program or the
  board needs it to work. Handy information (Volts, Amps, Watts, a model) is optional. OakBarn Brewery still OKs each one.
- A box needed by **some types only** (like a Tilt's Color) is greyed out for the types that don't use it. For a type that needs it,
  leaving it blank brings up a pop-up, so the box is filled in or the Build is abandoned (Cancel, or ◀ Back in the Importer).
- **The Panel and the Importer follow the same list** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "They would also be mandatory in the Skynet Panel").
  The Importer may be more flexible only where it must be to import something, and only as an Importer exception written here.
- **Mandatory now** (2026-11-09), in the Importer's item pages and in the Panel wherever the Panel has the same box:
  - every **Label** (and Name and Port);
  - Temperature Probes: **Probe type**;
  - Valves: **Connection Type** and **Size**;
  - Flow Meters: **Meter type**, and **Pulses per Gallon or Liter** for a meter that counts pulses (Hall effect, Turbine, Oval gear).
    Panel: a Flow Meter's **Pulses per unit**;
  - pH Meters: **Signal to the board**;
  - Pressure Sensors: **Sensor type**, and **Highest pressure it reads** (not for a Pressure switch). Panel: an Analog input's **Value at
    highest signal**;
  - Hydrometers: **Hydrometer type**, and a Tilt's **Color** or any other kind's **Hardware ID** (Rule 6.25);
  - Volume Meters: **How it measures**, and **Most it reads** for an Ultrasonic, Pressure or Float level sensor;
  - Floats: **Contact** (Normally Open or Normally Closed);
  - Digital Inputs: **Input type**.
- **Optional** (handy information): Pump model and Power; Watts and Volts; Valve type and Voltage; pH meter type; Float type.
- In the Panel a mandatory number box that is blank gets Rule 18.28's pop-up as soon as anything else but its Label, Interface or Port
  is clicked (fill it in or Cancel). The Panel's other boxes on this list are dropdowns or switches that are never blank, or are picked
  when the Device is added.

18.34 **The Pump dialog is the model: Label Hover Help, Title Case, Label Attributes** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10, the Blichmann
Riptide Add box: "Since the 3 Vessel is the Model, these all apply globally to the Skynet Panel and Importer"):
- **Title Case** ("Titles and Attribute Labels follow Pascal Camel Code Style"): every dialog's field names, headings and pop-up
  titles start each word with a capital (Fore Color, Font Size, Label Attributes); small joining words (and, of, the ...) stay
  small, and what is in ( ) is left as it is. A long sentence is not a name: it belongs in Hover Help (Rule 11.8).
- **The Label's Hover Help** of a Pump is OakBarn Brewery's own text, **word for word, with its pictures** (the Label Visible
  switch and the Red Pump with its Label), the same as Help 115 "The Label" (Rule 11.4). Only the spelling is fixed (Rule 2.37).
  Second pass, 2026-11-11 ("You did not put the Hover Help for label correctly"): no rewording, no shortening. A balloon may hold
  pictures (help_pictures, as in Help) and a bold heading. Every other Device's balloon starts "How do you refer to this Device?".
- **Label Visible** of a Pump: "The Label may be shown on the Tab, for example Red Pump above the Pump Device." with the Red Pump
  picture.
- **The Add box** has the ⬆ beside the Label too, with the ⬢.
- **The second part of the Pump Add box** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-11, "Second Blichmann Pump Build Dialog"): repeated fields keep
  the same layout and Hover Help as the first part, with what was entered there. Once the Interface and Port are **Confirmed** (Rule 18.35)
  the **Interface and Available Ports** line is greyed out (it can't change after the Device is made; Cancel to start again); **Label and Tab** can still be edited
  and the Suggested Name follows them; the focus goes to **Orientation**, the first box that was not on the first part. **Graphic**
  Hover Help ends "The Picture itself cannot be changed." **Cover**: "User Add" (OakBarn Brewery's drawing, 2026-11-11; was "Pick
  Cover Color", before that "User cover (pick its color below)") pops up the Color Picker and shows the **Color (RGB)** line just
  below (Rule 2.48); a color must be picked, or **◀ Back** sets the Cover back to None (no cover).
- **The ⬆ and ⬢ have their own balloons** (what they open), and **Available Ports** has its own balloon, apart from the Interface's.
- **Label Attributes**: no clutter (Visible, Font Size); **Font Size** shows the size the Label has now, not a blank; **Alignment**
  is **Left**, **Centered** or **Right**, with no "Default (Centered)" choice. A Label with no alignment of its own (nor from its
  Tab Style) is really Centered. The same three choices on the Timer's Label and the Value look.
- **The 3 Vessel 1 Pump sample's Tab is BH: Brew House** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-10: "BH follows Pascal Camel Code better"): Tab
  ID BH, so every name on it ends _BH (BM_22_DO@Pump_Pump_BH, BM_8_DO@H_Element_HLT~element_BH ...), in its Processes, Help and Hover Help too.
  Name examples in Help and Hover Help end _BH. A New Schema's hot-side Tab starts as Brew House (BH). Pipe ids (p_Brewhouse_1 ...)
  are meaningless keys and stay as they are (Rule 2 of the Design Rules).

18.35 **Review the Interface and Port before they are set** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-12, Hover Help Blichmann RipTide Dialog 1:
"Add New Review Dialog with the Interface and Port List Boxes here Greyed Out. Check before A Confirm Button is Clicked. Add a
Confirm Button and a Back Button."; "Do Not Lock the Interface or Port until the Confirm Button is Clicked and the device is saved."):
- In the Add box of a Device with the Pump's drill-down (Pump, Motorized Ball Valve, Temperature Probe, PWM / Analog out, Heating
  Element), once the **Interface** and **Port** are picked a **Review** pop-up shows them greyed out with this statement, and **no
  Hover Help** on it: "You MUST Confirm the Interface and Port Number. Once Confirmed, they cannot be changed. If a Change is needed
  now, Click the Back Button." Its buttons are **◀ Back** and **✔ Confirm**.
- **◀ Back** (or Esc) goes back to the Port; nothing is greyed out. Picking another Interface or Port asks again. **➕ Add Device**
  pressed before the Review brings the Review up.
- **✔ Confirm** greys out the Interface and Available Ports line in the Add box; the rest of the box opens once the Label and Tab are
  filled in too. They are set for good only when **➕ Add Device** saves the Device; **Cancel** before that keeps nothing.
- **➕ Add Device's own Hover Help** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-12, Dialog 1 #2: "The Hover Help for the Add Device should be the same
  with Just that the Label or Port needs to be set first"): while it waits, its balloon is the line that says what is missing
  ("Type a Label first", "Pick the Port first" ...), a blank line, then the same balloon as that box (Label, Interface, Available
  Ports or Tab).
- **The Pump's Tab and Device Type Hover Help** (the same PDF) are OakBarn Brewery's own text too, in the Add box and in Pump Device
  Properties (Dialog 2), the same as Help 115 The Tab and The Device Type. After each Suggested Name Format line comes the same
  standard text as the Interface balloon (what the name tells you, and Predictive Text). The BruControl comparison he wrote with the
  Device Type is for the Importer only: it waits in the Importer Sandbox (Rule 11.3).
- The **Hover Help** of the Pump's Interface and of every Available Ports is OakBarn Brewery's own text (Rule 18.34, word for word,
  the electrical warning in red, Rule 6.20), the same as Help 115 The Port and The Interface. Its examples use **Port 15**
  (BM_15_DO@Pump_Red~Pump_BH): Port 6 is used elsewhere on the 3 Vessel sample. The waiting ➕ Add Device button's balloon keeps
  "Pick the Port first (Available Ports)" and adds his longer help below it, one blank line between.
- **Both programs:** the BruControl Import brings in Devices that are already wired, so it has no Add box and no Review; it shares
  the balloons (public/app.js) when it uses the Panel's Build page.

18.36 **A default is the number in the box** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13, Default settings markup: "Empty = 10 and like is a real
Who's on First Issue. Just put 10 in the Slot and no comments like Empty = 10 / Empty = Nul"):
- A box with a Skynet default shows **that number in the box** (Pulse 100, Lockout 3000, a new Tab the screen's size, Dial tick marks 6,
  Pump speed 100 ...). The user sees what is used and changes it there.
- **No "(empty = ...)" in a label**, ever. A box left empty is **Null** (Rule 1.32).
- When an empty box means something that is not a number ("none", "no limit", "itself", "the Name"), that goes in the box's
  **Hover Help** as "Empty: ...", not in its label.
Both programs: the BruControl Import's Build page uses the same dialogs.

18.37 **Blichmann Riptide Dialogs 3** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-14, PDF "Blichmann Riptide Dialogs 3", the model, Rule 18.34):
1. **Every tap pop-up of Hover Help** (the small pop-up a tap or click on a field's name opens, Rule 18.16) has its title and
   **✖ Close** frozen at the top while it scrolls, and no Close at the bottom ("Close Button Frozen at top of All Hover Help. Get Rid
   of Bottom Close Buttons"). Every dialog, not only the Pump's. A pop-up with pictures is wider.
2. **Switching a pump's Orientation leaves its IPs where they are** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "flipping IPs would need lots of
   pipe or hose joins to move ... internal redraw is the way to go"). The Inlet IP
   and Outlet IP stay on the same spots on the Tab, so the pipes and hoses joined to them never move; only the Hose or Pipe drawn
   inside the pump is drawn again to reach them (Rule 5.27). Example 2 (Left, Inlet Bottom Right, Outlet Top Left) switched to Right
   keeps Inlet Bottom Right, Outlet Top Left. The Orientation Hover Help says so.
3. **The Pump Hover Help is OakBarn Brewery's text and pictures, word for word** (only the spelling fixed, Rule 2.37): the Interface's
   first paragraph, the whole Name balloon (its "Update to Suggest Name Button" names the real buttons, 🏷 Suggested Names > 💾 Convert for all and 💾 Update to Suggested for one: OakBarn Brewery, "Yes"), the Inlet IP balloon (the 8 IPs picture, Example 1 and Example 2, and "Pipes or Hose snap
   connect to an IP ... within 10 px"), the Hose or Pipe balloon, and the 8 IPs picture on top of the Graphic balloon and the Right /
   Left pictures on top of the Orientation balloon. The pictures are in `media/help_pictures` (the Media Setup). Help 115 has the same
   text (Hover Help = Panel Help).
Both programs: the BruControl Import's Build page uses the same Pump dialogs and tap pop-ups.

18.38 **Blichmann RipTide Dialog 1: the order of focus** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15, "Blichmann Riptide Dialog 1 Final", the model,
Rule 18.34). In the Pump Add box, until the Interface and Port are Confirmed (Rule 18.35). **All** = the Enter key, the Tab key or
the mouse; **TMF** = the Tab key or the mouse only; **NF** = no focus:
1. **Label**: All. It has the focus when the box opens.
2. **⬆** (two-line box): TMF.
3. **⬢** (Label attributes): TMF.
4. **Label Visible**: TMF.
5. **Interface**: TMF ("Best to be able to change Inter face and also the tab anytime ... not go to them but require the tab cycle or
   mouse"). Picking a new Interface goes on to its Port.
6. **Port**: All.
7. **Tab**: TMF. Never jumped to.
8. **Device Type**: NF.
- The **Enter key** goes only between the Label and the Port. Enter on a blank Label stays on it; with the Label filled in, Enter
  goes to the Port. With both filled in, Enter on the Port asks for the Review (Confirm or Back, Rule 18.35). From a TMF field,
  Enter goes to the next All field (the Port, or from the Tab back to the Label).
- The **Tab key** cycles through 1 to 7, the last back to the first. The **? Help**, **✖ Cancel** and **➕ Add Device** are not in
  the cycle: they are for the mouse.
- A blank Label or Port never stops the Tab key or the mouse (Rule 18.28). Once Confirmed, the rest of the box opens with the focus
  on the Orientation (Rule 18.20).
- The Pump first; the other Device dialogs follow once the Pump dialog, the model, is done. Both programs: the BruControl Import's
  Build page uses the same dialog.

18.39 **The Add Interface pop-up follows the Blichmann RipTide model** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15, Add Interface markup: "Rule #1
Follow Blicmann RipTide Model"; "I was able to get to this on the BHlickmann Dialog 1 so it must be fixed before Blickman Dialog 1 is
finished"). Both programs (the BruControl Import's Build page uses the same pop-up). Help 76.
- **Hover Help on every name, each its own**: Name, Interface ID, Board, Connection (with its rating, Rule 6.3), USB Port or Network
  address, and each Board setting (Rule 6.27). The **Interface ID** Hover Help is the Pump's Interface Hover Help (Dialog 1) with this
  Interface's own ID (in red in the example name) and Name put in as they are typed; with no Name and no ID it is Dialog 1's, word
  for word. The ID is suggested as Rule 3.2 says.
- **Board**: boards only (Arduino Mega, ESP32, Raspberry Pi). A board the BruControl Import could not tell shows "(pick the board)"
  and must be picked before Save.
- **Connection**: the choices follow the Board. Arduino Mega: USB, Ethernet (with W5100 or W5500 Shield), WiFi (through an ESP32
  bridge). ESP32: USB, Ethernet, WiFi (built in). Raspberry Pi: Ethernet (or the Brain itself), WiFi (built in). **No Simulator**: it
  belongs to the panel (Rule 10.10), not to a board. A pretend board (a Skynet Schema Template's Mega) stays pretend until its USB
  Port or Network address is filled in.
- **USB Port**: plain words in its Hover Help ("a number between 1 and 256, used to connect the Arduino to the Brain"), with a link to
  the technical side (Help 76). Skynet suggests the first USB port it finds that no other Interface uses. On Windows the number alone
  is typed (7 = COM7).
- **The USB Port may be skipped** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-24: "When Building a New schema and adding a Board, be able to skip the
  USB Port and allow the Build to continue and add the Board"): the USB Port list ends with **None for now** (just before 🔄 Look
  again), and a blank Network address is allowed too. The board is added anyway, so the build goes on and Devices can be put on it.
  Until it has a USB Port or Network address the Brain opens nothing for it and the Devices page shows it **not connected** ("No USB
  Port yet: ⚙ Change on the Devices page to pick it"). One warning only, the note when it is added; no pop-up. ⚙ Change fills it in
  later. Skynet still suggests a free port when it finds one. Both programs (the BruControl Import's Build page uses the same pop-up).
- **The focus**: the Name and the USB Port (or Network address) are **All** (Enter, Tab key, mouse); the Interface ID, Board,
  Connection and Board settings are Tab key or mouse only. Enter goes from the Name to the USB Port; Enter on a filled-in USB Port
  with a Name adds (or saves) it. The Tab key cycles through the boxes only, last back to first; the ? Help, ✖ Cancel and Add are for
  the mouse. Opened from the New Device box (➕ Add new Interface…), it comes back to that box with its own keys as they were.
- No Simulator note at the bottom (OakBarn Brewery: "Remove").
- **The model's buttons** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "You did not follow the Model. Frozen at Top and none on Bottom"): the title,
  ✖ Cancel and Add are frozen at the top (Rule 2.51); no row of buttons at the bottom.
- **Picking another Connection keeps the suggested Interface ID** ("Change of Connection Type removes suggested Interface ID").
- **USB Port** Hover Help says that in Simulator mode nothing goes over the USB Port, and how to test the real connection.
- **Network address** Hover Help (Ethernet and WiFi each its own) starts "If you do not understand Networks and protocols, call a
  friend to help." and explains, in plain words, what the address is, that a WiFi name (SSID) and password go into the program on the
  board (never into Skynet), how to find the address and reserve it in the router, and that it is the same on Windows, Mac, Linux and a
  Raspberry Pi (Help 76, The Network address).
- **Lost Comm** Hover Help: after a blank line, "You are the Safety" in bold red with the red safety triangle. **Diagnostic Logging**:
  Skynet's caveat (no help with communication problems) at the bottom, after a blank line, in normal text.
- More common boards are added once the Skynet firmware is set (Sandbox/Panel_Updates entry 11).
- **A suggested Network address** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16: "it is possible for Skynet to suggest a Network address based on the
  Brian's IP address"; "Ok we need to make at least the Hint and Discuss the Fixed address and to best to hook in the Board or Power
  it on (ESP 32)"): a new Ethernet or WiFi Interface starts with an address on the Brain's own home network (the Brain's first three
  numbers and a last one no other Interface or the Brain uses, 60 first; 192.168.1.60 when the Brain's address is not known). Its
  Hover Help says to plug in or power on the board first, that the address is only a suggestion, and to make it fixed in the board's
  program or reserved in the router (Help 76). A **Search** button that finds boards on the network waits in Sandbox/Panel_Updates
  entry 17: it needs the Skynet firmware to answer a search.

18.40 **Blichmann RipTide Dialog 2 #3** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-16, PDF "Blichmann_Riptide_Dialog_2_3", the model, Rule 18.34).
The Pump Add box (Dialog 2) and Pump Device Properties:
- *Taken out 2026-11-18 (Rule 18.46: a greyed box has no Hover Help, only the ⛔):* **Greyed out Interface and Available Ports**: once they are Confirmed (the Add box) or set (Properties), both Hover Helps start by
  saying the Interface and Port combination is saved and can not be changed ("Hover Help after Uodated and Greyed out need to basically

  box comes back with everything typed (Rule 4.7; "Do not want to save yet because any changes to the Tab might affect Suggested Name").
- **Pump Profile**: always one marked Default, no (none) choice (Rule 2.42).
- **Cover** and **Overlay** Hover Help have a picture: the pump with and without a cover ("Need Graphic in Hover help with and without
  cover Pump"), and every Overlay choice on a pump that is On ("Needs a Graphic with all of the Choices depicted").
- **Database and .API**: the name on the dialog line has its own Hover Help, and every box in its ⬢ pop-up has its own short name and

- **Model** Hover Help: "The Pump Model you choose from Available Common Brewery Pumps. Its Properties can be displayed with the ⬢."
- **Model ⬢ (Pump facts)**: to look at only, with **◀ Back** in place of Keep ("Change Keep to Back and no Edits Just View and Ports
  move"). **Power** and **Use** moved into it ("Move to Facts"); Use can not be changed, period. **Ports** moved to the dialog, where
  Power was; its Hover Help starts "Match YOUR Pump fittings" and has a bullet for each kind of port.

18.41 **The Motorized Ball Valve dialogs follow the Blichmann Model** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-18: "Under the Valves/ Equipment
Motorized Ball Valve (Open/Close (relay) fix all dialogs Now (exception) to the Blickmann Model Standard"; "Build it now with the
bring up to Blickmann Model Standard"; a Rule 14.4 exception). Every dialog of Valves/Equipment > Motorized Ball Valve, open / closed
(relay), the Skynet one and the User Defined one, works as the Pump dialogs do (Rules 2.51, 18.34-18.40):
- **2. Pick the valve**: the User Defined row says **➕ New User Defined Motorized Ball Valve** (OakBarn Brewery: "if there are no user
  defined valves, how can you pick one?"). The row makes a new valve; it never picks a saved one (a valve already on a Tab is shown
  again with ⧉ Clone Device). The same for **➕ New User Defined Proportional Valve** in the Valves and PWM lists. The BruControl
  Import's valve list names what an imported valve IS, so it keeps "User Defined ..." without ➕ New.
- **The Add box and the Valve Device Properties**: the title and buttons frozen at the top, no row of buttons at the bottom (Rule
  2.51), as wide as the pump dialog so the title line (lock, Visible, Hidden Locked) stays on one line; **X, Y, Width and Height on
  one line**, with Layer Order under the Tab, as on the pump.
- **Its ⬢ and ⬆ pop-ups** (Label, Label Attributes, Pin attributes, Database and .API, In and Out IP spots): title, ✖ Cancel and
  💾 Keep frozen at the top, no bottom row (Rule 2.51).
- **The order of focus** of Rule 18.38 (Enter only between the Label and the Port, the Tab key cycles the box's own fields, the
  Interface and Tab never jumped to, the Review before the Interface and Port are set). Its Label starts filled in (mBV_1, Rule
  18.15), so the focus starts on the Port, the next All field.
- **Always one Default Valve Profile** (as the Default Pump Profile, Rule 18.40): Skynet makes "Default Valve Profile" (the vertical
  ball valve, motor right, and the Lightning Bolt Overlay) when none is marked Default; its Default can not be turned off and it can
  not be deleted until another is marked Default. The User Defined valve's Add box always shows the **Valve Profile** list with the
  Default picked, and no (none).
- **Label Visible** Hover Help speaks of a valve ("Mash Valve above the Valve Device"), not a pump.
- **Its Hover Help** is adapted from the Pump's (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-18: "Adapt it", Rule 18.42).
Both programs: the BruControl Import's Build page uses the same valve dialogs. Help 128.

18.42 **Hover Help not written yet is adapted from the Blichmann RipTide's** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-18: "Adapt it"; "Make that a
rule. Adapt from Blickmann for any Hover Help not found, Do in same style with graphics and laymans Language"). Both programs.
- Where OakBarn Brewery has written a box's Hover Help, it is used **word for word** (Rules 18.34, 18.37; only the spelling is fixed).
- Where a box has **no Hover Help of OakBarn Brewery's own**, it is adapted from the Pump (Blichmann RipTide) Hover Help of the same
  box: the **same style and order**, the same Suggested Name read part by part, **plain words** (Rule 2.37), and **pictures** like the
  Pump's (help_pictures, Skynet's own drawings, a row in docs/Media_Licenses.csv, Rule 9.12). Only what is about a pump is changed, for
  example Red Pump -> Mash Valve, DO@Pump -> DO@Valve_E, the SSR -> a Relay or SSR, 120 VAC -> the Device's own power.
- The French is added in the same PR (Rule 11.11), and the Help page of that Device gets the same text (Hover Help = Panel Help, Rule 11.4).
- First done: the **Motorized Ball Valve** (Rule 18.41): Label (with Mash_Valve_Label.png), Label Visible, Interface (with
  Valve_Daisy_Chain.png), Available Ports, Tab, Name and Device Type. Help 128.

18.43 **Valves: the 3 Vessel valve pictures first, one picture, Horizontal or Vertical Left or Right** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-18:
"the Graphics of the valves the ones used in 3 vessel look much better so make those the first choice. And There are only valves, not
opened and closed the overlay for on is enough Horizonital or Vetical, Left or Right. for all Valves"; "We will likely get rid of most
of the Motorized Ball Valve Pictures for the one used on the 3 vessel."). Both programs.
- **First choice**: Motorized_TC15_Ball_Valve_Horizontal.svg and Motorized_TC15_Ball_Valve_Vertical.svg (the 3 Vessel valves) are the
  first pictures offered: the Skynet Motorized Ball Valve and KLD20T Horizontal picture, the Add list rows, a new User Defined valve,
  a new proportional valve, the Default Valve Profile, a valve on a Vessel port, and the top of the valve pictures in the On/Off list.
- **One picture**: a valve has one picture; the Overlay shows it open. Path (open), Picture when open and Graphic when open are not
  offered on a new valve or profile. A valve or profile that already has an open picture keeps it and still shows the box (Never Take Away).
- **Orientation**: Horizontal, Vertical Left or Vertical Right (a User Defined valve: Horizontal or Vertical). Front, Front Elbow and
  45 degrees are not offered to a new valve; a valve already set that way keeps it and still shows that choice (Never Take Away).
  *Changed 2026-11-25 (OakBarn Brewery, PDF "Panel Update 14", picked "Change the Rules"):* "Orientation only two Choices":
  **Horizontal** and **Vertical** (motor left), and "Add the two Flip Boxes": **Flip Horizontal** and **Flip Vertical** on the
  Orientation's line, on the Skynet and User Defined Motorized valves (the Toggle moves to its own line). "All Pictures Horizontal Start as
  Left to Right Flow"; "All Pictures Vertical Start as Bottom to Top Flow"; "Other Valves Follow this pattern" (Manual Valves and Hose
  Bibs, Rule 18.52). Vertical Right is Vertical with Flip Horizontal; a User Defined Horizontal Flipped is Horizontal with Flip Vertical: a
  valve saved that way is shown so when its Properties open, with the same look and IPs (its Template becomes the set's Vertical one). A
  flipped Skynet side-view valve keeps its box hugging the valve (Rule 5.29). A valve that is not made from a Template but has a Skynet
  side-view picture takes the Skynet Vertical picture on Vertical (before, Vertical did not turn it). Tap Water Flows: Rule 5.10.
- **Vertical Left and Vertical Right switch the picture** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-18: "That is the way the picture should be switched so it
  is needed"; "Add it"): Vertical Left shows Motorized_TC15_Ball_Valve_Vertical_Left.svg (the 3 Vessel valve mirrored, motor left),
  Vertical Right shows it flipped (motor right), the same on the Skynet Motorized Ball Valve and the KLD20T.
- **User Defined valve: one picture, four looks** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, Panel Updates 6, sandbox entry 32: "Can a User
  Provide a single Image and Skynet create other needed so a User Creates Dialog looks and acts like a Skynet one except for the
  addition Picture Path? ... flip Vertical Flip Left Right Rotate"; "90 degrees to make horizontal vertical"; "Not to concerned with
  the quality of a Users image but we can provide guidelines on what works best"; "Go with A KISS"). The user gives one picture
  (its Path), drawn Horizontal (pipe left to right, motor on top). Its Orientation offers **Horizontal** (as drawn), **Horizontal
  Flipped** (mirrored top to bottom, motor below), **Vertical Left** (turned 90 degrees, motor left) and **Vertical Right** (turned
  and mirrored left to right, motor right); the Valve Profile offers the same four. The picture file is never changed, only drawn
  turned or mirrored, and the In and Out IPs follow the look (the In end, left on the picture, is at the bottom when upright). Plain
  Vertical (the picture upright as drawn) and the 45s show only on a valve that already sits that way (Never Take Away). Help 128 has
  a short guide on what picture works best (plain background, straight on, no writing); picture quality is not checked. Both
  programs (the BruControl Import's Build page shares the dialog). **No own picture for a look** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "C.
  and Regardless These are not backgrounds but Device images without any path available to a user"): the looks are Device images
  Skynet draws from the one Path. They are not background pictures (Rule 7.10 does not count them), have no path of their own, and
  the user never sees or sets one.
- **Unused valve pictures retired** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-18: "Valve pictures: Discard any not used"): pictures no Template, sample
  Schema, default Schema or Skynet feature uses are moved to Delete/ (Help 129): Valve_Motor_Ball_ClosedH, _ClosedV_LC, _ClosedV_RC,
  Valve_Motor_Butterfly_ClosedV_R (Vertical Right flips V_L) and Valve_Manual_ClosedV_L, _ClosedV_R. A picture still used by a
  Template (Valve_Motor_Ball_ClosedFront for a valve already set to Front) stays. Help 36, 88, 117, 128, 129, 131.

     first) or **Push Button** (open only while it is held down on its Tab, closed when let go; holding it is the confirmation).

     Command may read it (.API Read) or ask for it (.API Read & Control). Asked for from outside, it is asked **by hand**, the same as a
     Process line (Rule 5.15): the Tab shows "Open it by hand", and it changes when someone turns it and clicks it on its Tab; its .state

18.50 **Panel Update Final 4: how every Widget dialog follows the Model** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-18, PDF "Panel Update Final 4",
the Hose Bib Widget dialog beside the Blichmann RipTide's: "1. Good 2. Good"; "Final 4 will just be some guidance Rules"). A guidance
Rule: it says how a Widget dialog is matched to the Model in the "Recheck dialogs" pass (Rule 18.47); it changes no dialog now. Both
programs (the BruControl Import's Build page shares the Panel's dialogs).
1. **The Model** ("The Blickmann and the Hose Bib are now the Model. Follow the way you updated from the Blickman to the Hose Bid and
   Reference the Hose Bib for Widgets."): a Device dialog follows the Blichmann RipTide; a **Widget dialog follows the Hose Bib**, made
   from the Blichmann the same way the Hose Bib was (Rules 18.48, 18.49): no Interface or Available Ports, no Model, **2. Tab** with
   Layer Order under it, 3. Name with Change Name and the Suggested Name, the Graphic block (below), .confirmation where it has one,
   X Y Width Height on one line, and the **Widget Type** last where a Device has its Device Type.
2. **A Widget with no Graphic** ("If a Widget has no Graphic, Graphics are gone as attributes but Background and Fore and Back colors
   are added to a Widget That does not have a Graphic."): it has no Graphic box and no picture attributes; it gets its **Background**
   and **Fore color** and **Back color** instead.
3. **Which Widgets have the Graphic properties** ("Generally Switch Widgets. Pump Widgets, and anything like them and the Graphic
   Widget have the Graphic Properties. Other Widgets do not unless they have IPs or have Confirmation."): the Switch Widgets, the Pump
   Widgets (the Manual Pump) and Widgets like them, and the **Graphic Widget** (the Picture Widget). Any other Widget has them only when
   it has IPs (the Hose Bib, the Manual Valve) or .confirmation.
4. **Backgrounds** ("The Graphic Widget can have the 3 Backgrounds with the .path_n attributes, All Other widgets get 1 from Skynet
   unless it is a User Widget, but it only gets one path only. Skynet ones have no path except the Graphic Widget."):
   - **The Graphic Widget**: up to 3 Backgrounds, .path, .path_2 and .path_3 (.backpath, .backpath_2, .backpath_3, Rules 7.10, 7.23),
     with .background picking which one shows.
   - **Every other Widget**: one Background from Skynet. It is set, so a Skynet Widget has **no path** box.
   - **A User Widget** (the user's own picture): **one path only**, as a User pump (Rule 7.10's exception).
   - **A new Skynet Device or Widget** (one BruControl never had): one path and one attribute, `.path_image` and `.path_audio` (Rule 7.26, Panel Update 8).
5. **No pipe parts** ("No IPs, No Hose/Pipe No Ips Fittings No Cover No Overlay except for Switches which have an Overlay."): a Widget
   without IPs has no IPs, no Hose or Pipe, no IP Fittings, no Cover and no Overlay. **A Switch has an Overlay.** A Widget with IPs (the
   Hose Bib, the Manual Pump) keeps its own, as the Model does.
