- **Older Widgets** (gGlobal Widget, older Alarm, Manual vessel, Clone): the Hose Bib order; their Background picture (#4) with a ⬢
  for the older Background boxes, text look and Database and .API in ⬢ lines.
- **Picture Widget** Properties: 2. Tab, 3. Name, Graphic, Picture, **Background** (None, 1, 2 or 3, #3) with its 3 paths in its ⬢.
- **Drawn things** (Vessels, Vessel Widgets, IPs, Pipes, Hoses, TC and pipe fittings, Tab_Fittings, Manifolds, Equipment, Integrated
  Devices): the title line, 1. Label (Label look in its ⬢), Label Visible, 2. Tab, Layer Order, 3. Name, X Y Width Height, the Type
  last (Device Type on an Integrated Device). The RIMS tube and electric kettle Add box: 1. Label, Label Visible, 2. Interface, then
  its parts, ➕ Add Device. Manual Pump: Confirmation under the Overlay.
Help 64, 65, 74, 76, 148.

18.51 **Every dialog uses the Model's rows, in the Model's places** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "How does the PWM look anything like
the Blickmann Model. Redo all the dialogs to for the Blickman and Hose Bib Model. Same Layout, same fields for the same things"; "We redo
it and make the Model Work"). The Model wins: a dialog is fitted to the Model, never the Model to a dialog. Both programs. Every Device
Properties and Add box (the Pump itself is the Model) and every Widget Properties (the Hose Bib is the Model; the Picture Widget and the
Alarm Widgets keep their own Picture and Alarm boxes, Rules 18.27, 18.50) has these rows, in this order, each in the same place:
- the title line (lock, Visible, Hidden Locked), **State**, **1. Label** ⬆ ⬢, **Label Visible**, **2. Interface** with **Available
  Ports** on its line (a Widget: none), **3. Tab** (or 3. Built into), **Layer Order**, **4. Name** with Change Name and the Suggested
  Name (a Widget: 3. Name), a **Profile**;
- **Graphic**: every Device and Widget has one: its Skynet drawing (Pump, Valve, Heating Element, Thermowell) or it as it is drawn on
  its Tab. The Model has no Path or Picture row: a picture Path is in the Graphic's ⬢ (nothing taken away);
- a Widget's **Background**, **Fore color** and **Back color** (Rule 18.50 #2), then **Orientation**, **Hose or Pipe**, **Cover** with
  **Toggle** on its line (no Cover: **Toggle** on its own line in the Cover's place; a Toggle no longer rides on the Overlay or the
  Orientation line);
- **Overlay** with **Database and .API** ⬢ on its line; with no Overlay, Database and .API is its own ⬢ line in the Overlay's place
  (no longer on Calibration Offset, Read Only or Running at Start);
- **Model** ⬢, **Inlet IP Fitting**, **Outlet IP Fitting**, then its own settings, where the Pump has Speed Control;
- **X Y Width Height** on one line, the **Device Type** (or Widget Type) last.
A row the Model has that a dialog's Device or Widget does not have is left out (Rule 18.47). Help 148.

18.52 **A Hose Bib and the Manual Valves are laid out like a Motorized Valve** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, word for word: "The Hose
Bib Graphic should be more like a Motorized Valve with the Vertical and Horizontal. I want the Inlet at the Top or Bottom in addition.
Treat the Handle as the "motor". This should be done for Manual Ball Valves and Manual Butterfly valves as well as in a Rael would, the
can (and will be placed like that, Manual Ball Valves do not need left right as they are the same. A butterfly graphic might be
different left right, I would need to see if it makes a difference. Vertical Left Right does matter because the handle "motor" can be
Left or Right.. and besides a Hose bib, a Butterfly valve could have a Different inlet Outlet Top Bottom. Again for a Butterfly valve
I would Have to see it."). Both programs (the BruControl Import's Build page shares the dialogs).
*Changed 2026-11-25 (Panel Update 14, Rule 18.43):* Left / Right and Inlet are replaced by **Flip Horizontal** and **Flip Vertical**
beside the Orientation. A Manual Valve or Hose Bib unflipped stands as drawn (Horizontal) or turned a quarter left with the handle to the
left (Vertical); a Hose Bib unflipped has its Inlet (TAP) on the left (Horizontal, Left to Right) or at the bottom with the handle to the
left (Vertical, Bottom to Top). The Flips mirror it as it looks on the Tab. A Manual Ball or Butterfly Valve's Flip Horizontal is not greyed
("Manual Valve Picture Flips Horizontal ... the graphic would show the handle in the opposite direction"). A front view has no Orientation
and no Flips. Saved as mvFlipH / mvFlipV; a valve saved with Left / Right and Inlet keeps the same look (the Flips are worked out from
them). Items 1 to 4 below are the old way, kept for the record.
1. **Hose Bib**: Orientation, Left / Right and a new **Inlet** box on one line. Horizontal: Left / Right puts the Inlet (the wall
   side) on the Right (as drawn) or the Left (mirrored); Inlet is greyed out (⛔ on hover, Rule 18.46). Vertical: **Inlet** is **Top**
   or **Bottom** and **Left / Right** is the side the handle (the "motor") points to, so it has all 4 Vertical looks. A Hose Bib saved
   before keeps its look: Vertical Left = Inlet Top, Vertical Right = Inlet Bottom. Its one IP, its 8 spots and its inside Hose or Pipe
   (Rules 18.45, 18.49) are unchanged and go with the picture.
2. **Manual Ball Valve** (Plain and Side view): it looks the same mirrored, so on Horizontal **Left / Right** is greyed out; its value
   stays as it was (Design Rule #1, nothing taken away). Vertical: Left / Right is the side the handle points to.
3. **Manual Butterfly Valve**: the Skynet drawings look the same mirrored and upside down (shown to OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19), so it
   is the same as the Manual Ball Valve: Horizontal Left / Right greyed, Vertical handle Left or Right, no Top / Bottom. If a Butterfly
   drawing with a one-sided lever is made, an Inlet Top / Bottom like the Hose Bib's can be added.
4. A User's own picture keeps Left / Right on Horizontal (it may not look the same mirrored).
5. A turned or mirrored Manual Valve's **Label** stays upright and below it on the Tab (before, it turned with the picture).
6. **Inlet IP** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, "Yes"): a Hose Bib has a second IP, on the outer face of its wall side's pipe thread, that
   turns with the picture (on Vertical it is at the Top or the Bottom). Its hose outlet IP, 8 spots and inside Hose or Pipe are as
   before. It never cuts a pipe it is dropped on (Rule 5.26).
7. **Tap flow** (Panel Updates entry 35, OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, word for word: "A Pipe on the inlet side of a Hose bib has slow
   when the hose bib is open. A Pipe on the Hose Bib that has a Valve one the other end has to have that valve fot Tap to flow";
   "Remember I what I said about flow and if another valve is on that side, it must be open?"): with nothing on its Inlet it always
   has water (the house plumbing is not drawn). With a pipe on its Inlet, open, water flows in along that pipe toward it, tap water
   Blue (Rule 5.21), as far as a plain IP end, an open end in the air, another source or an open valve whose other side has nothing
   joined (the house supply). A closed valve on that side means no water: no flow on the Inlet pipe and none out of the hose either.
   On the hose side a closed valve at the far end stops the flow, as on every pipe.
Help 141, 87 (and French).

18.53 **Every pop-up is on top** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "On HoseBib Dialog (and Maybe Others) the Change Name Pop Up is at a
lower layer than the Dialog and not on top so cannot read it. So Popups need to be temporary Layer 1"; "All pop ups should be on
top"). A pop-up is the short message box (for example "The Name will be ... when you press 💾 Save" or what is wrong with a typed
Name), a notice bar (a Brain notice, a Flame Out notice, a Manual Valve's Done bar, the Not Official bar), the Undo note, the Build
kept on the Brain note, the Sound is off button, the Job pick bar and a Vessel's small pop-up. While it shows it is **Layer 1 over
everything, every open dialog too**, and its buttons can be clicked; when it goes away nothing under it has changed. A pop-up that is
a dialog of its own (Discard changes?, Change name on a Tab, a Picker) opens on top of the dialog it came from, as before. The small
⚠ boxes of Rule 18.28, the Color Picker and Hover Help were already on top and stay as they are. Every new pop-up follows this Rule.
The technical side: public/ontop.js.

## 19. Vessel Rules

Fritz (2026-11-05): "Vessels will have their own Rules." "Vessels on a Tab are Exception to the Rule and Only Apply to Vessel
Devices or Vessel Widgets." Where a Vessel Rule and a general Rule differ, the Vessel Rule wins for **Vessel Widgets and Vessel
Devices only**; everything else keeps the general Rules (2.20, 1.21, 5.31). (thread "Size Vessels by gallons with a Master Sizer",
Help 135)

19.1 **Gallons.** Every Vessel has a **Gallons** field (Liters when its Units are Metric). **A Vessel Template starts at 10
gallons**, Skynet and User Templates alike, and it is an editable field. **Gallons is one of the first fields of a new build from a
Template** (right after the Label in the Properties that open on the Build Tab).

19.2 **Size follows the Method: Proportional or Diameter.**
- **Proportional:** Fritz's plain vessel is the **One Gallon start: 197 x 237 pixels** (Fritz, 2026-11-05). Its Width to Height is
  the shape, and the Gallons field sizes it in proportion to that 1 gallon start.
- **Diameter:** a **Diameter** and a **Height** field (inches; cm for Metric). It is drawn by its **real size** (OakBarn Brewery,
  2026-11-09: "if we use the size rather than the gallons it will draw better in proportion"; "Advertized gallons could also be
  wrong"): the volume a cylinder of that Diameter and Height holds sizes it, never the Gallons typed. **Calculated Volume** shows that
  volume, read only. Every Vessel also keeps **Dead space** and **Safe Element Volume** (the least liquid that covers its Heating
  Element).
- **Size follows volume:** twice the gallons is the cube root of 2 (about 1.26) times as wide and as tall. 10 gallons is 424 x 511.
  (Fritz, 2026-11-05: "I think the way you have done it will work.")

19.3 **The Master Vessel Sizer** is a Tab attribute (Tab settings). Any one Vessel on the Tab can be assigned. **Only the Master's
size fields are active**, in a Process or on the screen (grab points, Width, Height); it is the only one that can be resized, and
**every Vessel on that Tab follows** at the same scale. Changing the Master's own Gallons resizes only the Master; another Vessel's
Gallons or Method resizes only that Vessel, at the Master's scale. **No Master Vessel Sizer picked: no Vessel can be resized**
(a new build is still drawn at its Gallons). A resized Vessel keeps the middle of its bottom where it was; its IPs, fittings and
End Caps go with it (pipes per Rule 5.19). The Master shows 📏 in Edit layout.

19.4 **Not Placed is hidden, even on a Build screen.** A spot that is Not Placed (Rule 5.31) is hidden on every Tab, the Build Tab
and Edit layout included, and its slider is hidden in the Vessel's Properties. A **👁 Show All** button in the Build or Edit dialog
(Vessel Widget Properties) shows the hidden items (their sliders, and faint marks on the vessel) until it is pressed again (🙈 Hide
Not Placed) or the dialog closes.

19.5 **The Vessel Device Builder** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-08: "time to Build the Vessel Device Template. We will Build in the
Skynet Panel First and bring it over to the Importer"; then the full design: "This replaces the Interview on The Importer"; "the end
result will be the same look and feel Skynet Panel or Importer"; thread "Build the Vessel Device Builder", Help 166).
**Vessel > 🔨 Build a Vessel Device** on the Edit layout bar (and Add Widget > Vessels) is the same interview in both programs
(the questions are in one shared file, public/vesselbuilder.js):
1. **The Question Dialog first:** Label (never blank), **General Type** (HLT, Mash Tun, Brew Kettle, All In One, Whirlpool,
   Fermentor, Bright Tank; **Other** lets the user type one, kept in the list as **USER: Hop Pot Strainer**), the Tab, Units,
   **Volume**, **Height** and **Diameter** (both empty = the plain vessel shape, Rule 19.2), **Bottom Drain** (None, Center Low,
   Center Bottom Drain), **Tangential Inlet** (None, Left, Right), **Sparge Arm / Steam Slayer** (None, Right (High), Left (High)),
   **Thermowell / Probe** (None, Center, Left, Right, Back Left, Back Center, Back Right), **Heating Element** (None, Left, Right,
   Back Left, Back Center, Back Right; a second one may be added) and **HERMS Coil** (None, Left, Right).
2. A Thermowell / Probe and a Heating Element **make no IP of their own**: they go on a spot, and on an IP they close it like an
   End Cap (its IP is hidden). Two can't share a spot.
3. **🔨 Build** puts the vessel on **one side of the 🔨 Build Tab** with its Heating Element, Thermowell and HERMS coil shown and
   the IPs of its Drain, Tangential, Sparge / Steam Slayer and HERMS; every spot not used is Not Placed (Rule 19.4). The
   **Vessel Builder** panel is on **the other side**, with a dialog only for what was chosen.
4. **Heater and Probe pickers:** a dropdown of the existing Heating Elements (or Temperature Probes) not built into anything, and
   **➕ Add new**, which runs the usual Add dialogs. The one picked is **built into the vessel** (Rule 5.31) and keeps its name and
   Port; its readout sits on the vessel like the Three Vessel sample's HLT and its picture gets a hot spot. Until one is picked the
   spot shows faintly, closed, and its hot spot opens the picker.
5. **The Drain, Tangential and Sparge Arm pieces** (2026-11-09): each one chosen has a row on the Vessel Builder panel; it opens
   **up to 3 pieces**, from the vessel out: **None, Valve, Elbow, Tee, Priming Tee** (a Tangential Inlet and a Sparge Arm have
   no Priming Tee). None ends it, so the pieces after it are greyed out. An Elbow turns the run; the Priming Tee always points up,
   so it goes only in a level run. Each piece is joined to the one before by a short pipe the size of the vessel's opening. A
   **Valve** is picked from the Motorized valves not on a pipe yet, **➕ Add New Motorized Ball Valve** (the usual Add dialogs),
   or **➕ Add Manual Valve Widget** (Plain, Manual Ball Valve side view, or Manual Butterfly Valve; turned for an up and down
   run; a Confirmation Widget, Rule 1.28). Only valves get a hot spot. The **Sparge Arm** is drawn inside the vessel from its
   IP toward the other side. *To come:* the **Steam Slayer** (its pieces, a 2" to 1.5" Reducer, then the Steam Slayer), the
   **Integrate** button that saves a **Vessel Device Template** for the Add Vessel list, the standard Templates, and the BruControl
   Import using the same interview (a prebuilt Template may be picked first).
6. **Pick** (2026-11-09, Rule 5.31 changed): the Drain, Tangential, Sparge Arm / Steam Slayer, Thermowell / Probe and Heating
   Element questions have **Pick (double-click the spot on the vessel)**: a blank vessel opens with small dots on the preset IPs; a
   double-click marks the spot, **↶ Undo** takes it off, **💾 Save** keeps it. Near a preset IP it takes that IP, anywhere else it
   makes a User IP. The HERMS Coil has no Pick but has the two crossed choices (Rule 5.31).
7. **The Priming Tee** (2026-11-09: "Basically an Instrument Tee with a Manual Valve on the Short side always pointing up"): a TC Pipe
   Fittings Widget (Elbows, Tees ...), openings at the run ends only; it can Flip Horizontal but never turns or flips upside down.
   The Drain and Tangential pieces will offer it.
8. **Both programs** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-09: "When updating the Vessel Device builder do both unless I say only for Importer
   or Only for Skynet"): every change to the builder goes into the Skynet Panel and the BruControl Import. In the Importer, the
   **Your vessels** step has **🔨 Build** on each vessel: it opens the builder on the Importer's Build page with the questions
   filled in from that vessel's row (public/vesselbuilder.js vbFromImport). The Heating Element and Probe pickers list the
   imported ones, the row's own first. A part already built into a vessel (the Three Vessel sample's too) is never listed.
9. **14. Fermentor Control** (2026-11-10, Rule 6.30): None, Heat & Cool, Heat only or Cool only (a Thermowell / Probe is a must).
   After 🔨 Build the panel has a **Heat** row and a **Cooling** row: pick one not built into anything, or **➕ Add new** (Heat mat,
   Heat wrap, Ceramic heat emitter, Heating Element, Light; Freezer or fridge, Glycol pump, Glycol valve). They are built in
   without a spot, beside the vessel. Then the Fermentor Control is made, named after the vessel's Label. In the Importer, a
   Fermentor Control the Import already made on that probe is built in instead of a second one. Help 182.
Once **✅ Finish Build ... > Move to Tab** has put it on a Tab and the layout is saved, its IPs and parts are locked (Rule 5.31).

19.6 **The Equipment Profile Interview** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "WE also need to create an interview to build an Equipment
Profile. 1. Ask How many Vessels 2. Type of each 3. Then Chose an Vessel Device or Widget, and able to choose to build a new Vessel
Device 4. How Many Pumps (Types, Covers, Overlays, Labels and Names, Normal attributes) 5. How many Motorized Valves 6. And so On";
Help 196). **☰ Menu > Equipment Profile > Add new ...** starts with **Answer a few questions (the Interview)**. Plain questions,
one page at a time, with **◀ Back**, **Next ▶** and **✖ Cancel** (nothing is made): Start (Name, Tab or a new Tab, Interface),
how many Vessels, the type of each, pick or build each one (that type's Vessel Templates first, the plain Skynet Vessel Widget,
**🔨 Build a new Vessel Device**, which opens the Vessel Device Builder, Rule 19.5, after the Interview; Label, Size, Dead space),
how many Pumps and each one (Type, Cover, Overlay, Label, Label Visible, Toggle), how many Motorized Valves and each one, Manual
Valves, **And so on** (recirculation, chiller, Supply Manifold), the profile's numbers, and **Review**. Every answer starts from
the Default settings (Rule 2.42). **🔨 Build** makes the profile, gives it to the Tab and puts everything on the 🔨 Build Tab
(Rule 4.1); each pump and motorized valve is a real Device on the next free Port (Rule 4.2), named by Rule 3.1.
1. **It replaces the Vessel tab** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13: "Yes"). A vessel's size, dead space, heater and probe are in its
   Properties on the Tab. The list of a profile made before Templates and its **Put on Tab** are gone (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "Remove old"; Help 34).
2. **The profile is all of the brewery's physical hardware** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "A Brewery has a set of equipment.
   Generally all of the Schema could be made of the same Equipment Profile."; "The reason to \"import\" and equipment Profiles is to
   create a new Schema with its own Text Widgets, and Processes."; "An equipment profile would be all the Brewery Hardware, including
   the Interfaces, Ports and Wiring. All of the actual Physical Real World things that are set in concrete (sometimes literally)").
   The profile keeps its vessels, IPs, pipes, hoses, fittings, pumps, valves, chillers and Widgets with IPs **and the Interfaces
   (boards), their Ports and wiring**, each with **all of its Properties and its Name** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "Yes all the
   Properties would come"). Its main use is **starting a new Schema from the profile**, which then gets its own Text
   Widgets and Processes. Not decided yet (OakBarn Brewery: "could go either way ... I have to be further along to answer that
   properly"): whether a profile put on a Tab of a Schema that already has its own boards always brings the boards too.
   Each pump and motorized valve keeps its **slot** (a meaningless key, Design Rule 2), and pipes point at the slot.
   **Hardware already there** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "If there is Hardware on a Tab that is the same as the Equipment Profile,
   if it is imported, the existing one one the Tab are deleted and replaced by the Equipment Profile. So the Equipment Profile need
   User Input to add."; then "A Same Tab", which replaced "I would think pasting an Equipment Profile into a Tab that has the same
   interface to be Prohibited"):
   - **On the Tab it is pasted to:** hardware that is the same as the profile's (the same board and Port, or the same slot) is
     **replaced** by the profile's. Nothing happens until the user says so: a list shows what will be replaced ("These 6 will be
     replaced: ...") with **Replace** and **Cancel**, and **↩ Undo** shows after (Rule 2.53). The profile's numbers (Efficiency ...)
     replace the Tab's the same way, shown in the same list ("Brewhouse efficiency 74 % → 72 %"). A replaced Device keeps its
     hidden key (Rule 3.10), so the Processes that use it keep working.
   - **On another Tab of the Schema:** when one of the profile's boards is already used on another Tab, the paste is **not allowed**:
     it stops, nothing is added, and a plain note names the board and the Tab and says why (one board is never split by a paste, and
     its ID never changes, Rule 3.2).
   A Port is never given to two Devices (Rule 6.1). A slot another Schema has not given a Port stays in the profile (Design Rule 1); a Device deleted where it was given a Port takes its slot out.
   **Built (2026-11-17):** the profile keeps the hardware of a Tab saved into it with **💾 Save as a profile ...** (no hidden key goes
   into it; changed 2026-11-19, Rule 2.62: was "every time that Tab is saved"). The
   ➡ Transfer buttons of the Equipment Profile view (below) paste **All**, **Vessels** (each vessel with everything on it) or
   **Manifold** (OakBarn Brewery: "Yes All of the manifold. Just Not the Vessesls") onto the Tab picked beside them; the pieces land on the
   🔨 Build Tab (OakBarn Brewery: "2. Build Tab") and Finish Build > Move to Tab puts them there in the same spots. A pipe end whose
   piece did not come stays **open** (OakBarn Brewery: "Open so a Vessel could be attached"). A board the Schema does not have comes
   with the paste; a piece whose Name is used elsewhere gets _2. ↩ Undo puts it all back. **🗂 New Schema from this profile ...** (also
   Add new Schema > Start from > An Equipment Profile) makes a Schema whose one Tab uses the profile, with every board and Device already
   wired and nothing else (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "I thought how I would build my Brewery as an Equipment Profile and then create
   my first Schema as a Keg Cleaning Schema. It would need to use the already wired Arduino and assigned Ports and Pins"). The board
   block above is inside one Schema only: a new Schema always takes the boards. Help 28 and 188.
   **The Equipment Profile view** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "The one in Skynet now does not make sense for what the Equipment Profile
   will be used for"; "Make it with your recommendations and I will test"; "IT Is NOT a Tab  but a PROFILE"): Open shows the profile
   itself, drawn from what the profile holds, look only. **A profile is not a Tab, and it holds only the real world hardware**
   (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "Equipment Profile only includes real world things (like Widgets with IPs) and no other Widgets like
   Text Boxes or such.  No Switches."; "Yes and immersion Chillers   any widget with an IP Can be added.    Text Widgets and Like CANNOT
   be added"; "That is because if a Widget has an IP, it is a real world thing.   Plate chillers  on so on."): **the test is the IP: a
   Widget with an IP is a real world thing, so it can be in a profile** (plate chillers and so on; an immersion chiller goes with the
   vessel it sits in), and so is every Device on a board with its Port. **A Switch that is a real world thing is a Special Widget like
   a Manual Valve, so it is in the profile** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "Ok a switch  that is a real world thing is a Special widget
   like a Manual Valve.  So yes."). Text Widgets, Switches that are not real world things, Processes, Timers and the like
   **cannot be added**: Skynet never puts them in a profile, so nothing is hidden in the view;
   they are not there. A frozen bar (Rule 2.51) holds
   **Move** (a dropdown: Entire Profile, Just Vessels, Just Manifold), **To Tab** (a dropdown that starts on **🔨 Build Tab** each time
   the profile opens) and one **➡ Transfer** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-22, Panel Update 9, item 17, "Tab to Move to DDLB. Always when
   opened goes to Build Tab but the user may select"; one dropdown, not three check boxes, by Rule 2.6, Fritz picked A; it was three
   Transfer buttons, 2026-11-17), then Delete · Save ·
   Undo · Close. Under it the profile's Properties, which go with every Transfer and Paste (OakBarn Brewery: "Equipment Profile
   Properties are ones transferred like Effenicy"): they are copied onto the Tab as its own numbers, and a Tab that has numbers shows
   the ones that change in the Replace list (Rule 2.62). Beside the Properties: **🧮 Check the volumes**, **📈 Efficiency** (the
   Efficiency of the Tab picked in To Tab, Rule 17.13) and **🗂 New Schema
   from this profile ...**. **The old Equipment Profile screen is gone** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-17: "Remove old"; before the first
   Public Production, the Old Ways policy): its form, Equipment list, Paste onto a Tab dialog, Made before Templates list and the
   Settings button. ☰ Menu > Equipment Profile keeps each Tab's row (since 2026-11-19, Rule 2.62: its own numbers, ⚙ Numbers,
   📈 Efficiency, 💾 Save as a profile ..., 🔌 Give ... a Port, and 🔒 when lock_Equipment locked it) and the Open list, which opens the
   profile view.
   *Replaced (2026-11-17):* "Each pump and motorized valve on the profile's Tab is a slot of the profile ...: its look and place,
   never its Interface, Port or Name. ... A Schema that picks the profile and has no Device for a slot is asked for the Interface;
   each slot gets the next free Port (Tab row: 🔌 Give ... their Ports)" (2026-11-13: "I may have a 3 Vessel 3 Pump Layout that I want
   in more than a singles Schema, but rather Than having to rebuild it, just select from a DDLB").
3. **Both programs:** the BruControl Import has no Equipment Profiles, so the Interview is in the Skynet Panel only. The Import's
   Build page is not changed.

19.7 **The Stove Top Vessel: a Widget with IPs and a hose hang top, drawn for its Height and Width** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-13:
"We need stove top Vessel with the Hose hang top and size attributes H_w and Gallons and make the Graphic Dynamic top"; 2026-11-15:
"Stove Top is widget with IPs with Top IP to hang a hose. 2 different ones. 1 no Outlets, 2. Outlet at Bottom with the conector types
like a Pipe"; "Center Bottom on Stove Top Widget and it gets IP"; thread "Build the Stove Top Vessel", Help 199).
- **Two of them, next to Add equipment:** **Stove Top Vessel** (no outlets) and **Stove Top Vessel, Bottom Outlet** (one IP at the
  center of the bottom). Both are Widgets with IPs and **no Devices**. They are the only choices there besides the Skynet equipment
  Widgets: the older Electric heated vessel, Gas heated vessel, Unheated mash tun, Cooling coil and Plate chiller are gone (OakBarn
  Brewery, 2026-11-13: "remove for now. We will build several Vessel Template Devices where these would be").
- **Hose hang top:** its top third is one big IP, as on every vessel (Rules 5.28 and 5.34): a Quick Disconnect hose dropped there, or
  a Process line `Hose_1.connect = Stove_Top_Vessel_1`, hangs over the rim into the pot.
- **Size (Vessel Rules):** Units, **Gallons** (5 to start), **Height**, **Width** (across the pot) and a read only **Calculated
  Volume**. Both Height and Width typed: drawn by its real size and shape (as the Diameter method, Rule 19.2). Either empty: a stock pot
  as tall as it is wide, sized by its Gallons. It follows the Tab's Master Vessel Sizer (Rule 19.3) and can be the Master.
- **Its picture is drawn by Skynet for its box** (the "Graphic Dynamic"): pot body, rim and two side handles, flat grey #808080 with a
  black outline and no text (the Label is its only text). A Graphic picked by the user is used instead.
- **The Bottom Outlet IP** has a **Bottom Outlet IP Type**: Tri-Clamp, NPT, BSP or Quick Disconnect, like a pipe end (Rule 5.40). It
  starts as the Default pipe IP Type, is drawn as its type under the pot, and is the size of the pipe or hose joined to it (a pipe end
  on it draws no second connector).
- **Both programs:** the BruControl Import's Build page is the Panel's own, so it has both. BruControl has no stove top pot, so an
  import never makes one.

19.8 **The Ice Water Can: cold water for a Sump Pump, drawn for its box** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-15: "Also need a Sump Pump widget
similar to a Manual Valve as most brewers just use them by plugging them in and not controlled by the Skynet"; "we have a sump pump in
chilled water that recycles back to a large trash can with Ice and Water"; "the Iced Water Is pass through a Plate Chiller to Cool Tap
Water. That tap water is sent to another Plate Chiller for the WORT ... The Ice Water is retuned to the Large Ice Bath and the Waste tap
water from the WORT PLate chiller is used on the lawn"; thread "Add a manual Sump Pump widget", Help 201).
- **Ice Water Can, in Add equipment:** a big trash can (or tub or cooler) of ice and water. A Widget with **no Devices and no IPs of
  its own**. Name `Ice_Water_Can_1` (as the Stove Top Vessel's, Rule 19.7); Label starts **Ice Water**.
- **Hose hang top:** its top third is one big IP, as on every vessel (Rules 5.28 and 5.34): a Quick Disconnect hose dropped there, or
  a Process line `Hose_1.connect = Ice_Water_Can_1`, hangs over the rim and brings the water back.
- **A pump inside it draws from it:** a running pump whose inlet sits inside the can, with nothing joined to that inlet (the **Sump
  Pump by hand**, Rule 5.15a), pulls the can's water. Its flow takes the can's **Out flow color** (Rule 5.21), which starts **Blue**
  because the water is cold.
- **Its picture is drawn by Skynet for its box:** a grey can a little wider at the top, rim, two side handles, blue water and ice
  cubes, no text (the Label is its only text). A Graphic picked by the user is used instead. No Gallons: it is not brewing liquid,
  so it is sized by dragging and does not follow the Master Vessel Sizer.
- **Both programs:** the BruControl Import's Build page is the Panel's own, so it has it. BruControl has no ice bath, so an import
  never makes one.

19.9 **📐 My Size: a vessel drawn to the user's own Height and Diameter** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, PDF "Panel Update 5" #8: "if
a User Choses a Vessel can we resize proportionally and create an SVG as a User Vessel Template"). In a Vessel Template's settings
(☰ Menu > Vessel Templates, a plain vessel), **📐 My Size** asks a name, the **Height** and the **Diameter**. Skynet draws that
vessel's picture stretched to that shape as an SVG of the user's own in the User Graphic folder, makes a **User Vessel Template**
with it (sized by Diameter, with that Height and Diameter) and opens it. The Skynet Template is not changed. **Both programs:** the
BruControl Import's Build page shares the ☰ Menu Templates, so it has it; an import makes no templates.

19.10 **Material: Copper, Stainless or Hose** (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19, PDF "Panel Update 5" #9, option B: "i LIKE b"; "After
fix, the chillzilla is not needed. It is Not a Chillzilla and Chillzilla is brand but other counterflows look very similar";
"Don't need it. It is a Duplicate of the Imersion in copper").
1. A HERMS coil, an Immersion chiller and a Counterflow chiller have a **Material** dropdown: **As drawn**, **Copper** or
   **Stainless (SS)**; a Counterflow chiller also **Hose** (green, with brass ends). The picture is drawn in that color. It is on
   the Add box, the Properties and the Equipment Template.
2. New Skynet Equipment Templates **HERMS Coil Same Side** and **Immersion Chiller Same Side**: In and Out IPs on the same side
   (Top Left and Bottom Left; any corner or Left / Right may be picked). A HERMS coil's In and Out may now be on any corner.
3. The **Chillzilla** Equipment Template is taken out: Chillzilla is a brand, and it is the Counterflow (Hose) or the Immersion
   chiller in Copper. Before the first Public Production, so no old way is kept; a Chillzilla already on a Tab stays as it is.
   Its file is moved to `Delete/templates/vessel/` (Rule 15.3), and on a Brain an older Setup put it on, the Official Skynet check
   moves it to backups/retired_files_<date> by itself, so the check does not call it "added" (OakBarn Brewery, 2026-11-19: "504 not
   officail templates/vessel/Chillzilla.json added").
**Both programs:** the BruControl Import's Build page shares the dialogs and Templates; BruControl has no chillers or coils to
import.

- 2026-11-21: `clear` is no longer a Process command (OakBarn Brewery: "Anything not needed from Brucontrol like clear is not needed"). It did nothing; it is gone from the Process reader, the editor colors and Suggest list, and Help 22. An import drops a `clear` line (Importing Norms section 4).
- 2026-11-22: The Process reader keeps only Skynet's words (OakBarn Brewery: "enabled is gone, displayname is label. We still have the countdown and countup on timers just different, target is setpoint and hiddenlock is of little use"; "A name attribute is inherent in any Skynet item but it is not an attribute"). A Process writes `Name.attribute` with a dot; `"Name" attribute` without one stops with "Put a dot between a name and its attribute". `.displayname` (use `.label`), `.enabled` on a Heating Element or Fermentor Control (use `.state`), a Timer's `.type` (use `.countdown`), `.target` for a Setpoint (use `.setpoint`; a stepper's `.target` stays) and the word `hiddenlocked` each stop with the Skynet word. Saving a Process no longer rewrites old lines; only the Importer does (lib/modernize.js, Importing Norms 2 to 4). `.hidden` / `.hiddenlock` (the Hidden Lock switch) stay. Help 5, 16, 20, 21, 22, 72, 77, 150, 161, 186 (and French). Checked against the BruControl Import program: it converts these lines before they reach the Panel.
